concepts.label: Narcissistic Personality Disorder
concepts.title: Narcissistic Personality Disorder
concepts.definition: A pattern of grandiosity, need for admiration, and lack of empathy. (ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/books/NBK556001/)

concepts.label: Sigma-1 Receptor
concepts.title: Sigma-1 Receptor
concepts.definition: A sigma receptor that regulates neuroinflammation, neurotransmitters, neurogenesis, ENDOPLASMIC RETICULUM stress and MITOCHONDRIA function.

concepts.label: Ganglionic Eminence
concepts.title: Ganglionic Eminence
concepts.definition: A transitory embryonic structure that appears during the 5th week post-fertilization. The ganglionic eminence plays an important in the development of the nervous system by guiding tangential cell and axon migration during embryonic development and give rise to BASAL GANGLIA and cortical GABAergic and thalamic and olfactory INTERNEURONS.

concepts.label: GluK2 Kainate Receptor
concepts.title: GluK2 Kainate Receptor
concepts.definition: A high-affinity KAINATE and GLUTAMATE receptor that functions as ligand-gated ion channel in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSYEM and plays an essential role in NEURONAL PLASTICITY.

concepts.label: GluK3 Kainate Receptor
concepts.title: GluK3 Kainate Receptor
concepts.definition: A high-affinity KAINATE and GLUTAMATE receptor that functions as ligand-gated ion channel in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSYEM and modulates excitatory synaptic transmission.

concepts.label: Psychological Growth
concepts.title: Psychological Growth
concepts.definition: A process of actively learning and adapting to new ways to function following a challenging life crisis.

concepts.label: Coping Skills
concepts.title: Coping Skills
concepts.definition: Various techniques for actively managing a stressful event or situation.

concepts.label: Emotional Exhaustion
concepts.title: Emotional Exhaustion
concepts.definition: A state of feeling emotionally overextended and drained.

concepts.label: Media Exposure
concepts.title: Media Exposure
concepts.definition: The extent to which individuals encounter messages and content via COMMUNICATION MEDIA.

concepts.label: Role Conflict
concepts.title: Role Conflict
concepts.definition: A state of tension or distress that occurs when fulfilling roles of one status making it difficult to fulfill the roles of another.

concepts.label: Subjective Stress
concepts.title: Subjective Stress
concepts.definition: Perceptions of PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS based on the individual's own personal values, beliefs and past and current experiences and circumstances.

concepts.label: Ejaculatory Dysfunction
concepts.title: Ejaculatory Dysfunction
concepts.definition: The inability in males to ejaculate, or to have a normal time to EJACULATION.

concepts.label: Hearing Loss, Hidden
concepts.title: Hearing Loss, Hidden
concepts.definition: Hearing loss that is difficult to diagnose by standard hearing tests as it most often pertains to difficulties in hearing only in certain situations such as in noisy environments.

concepts.label: Gender-Affirming Care
concepts.title: Gender-Affirming Care
concepts.definition: A supportive healthcare, consisting of medical, surgical, mental health, and non-medical services for TRANSGENDER PERSONS and GENDER-NONCONFORMING PERSONS. Medical and psychosocial gender affirming healthcare practices may lower rates of adverse mental health outcomes, build SELF ESTEEM, and improve overall QUALITY OF LIFE for transgender and gender diverse youth (http[已隐藏本地路径]

concepts.label: Time Pressure
concepts.title: Time Pressure
concepts.definition: Sense of time urgency to complete a task. This sense of time urgency creates psychological pressure affecting performance (http[已隐藏本地路径]

concepts.label: Cognitive Flexibility
concepts.title: Cognitive Flexibility
concepts.definition: The ability to effectively adapt one's cognitive and behavioral strategies in response to changing task or environmental demands. (from Clinical Psychology Review August 2021,102061).

concepts.label: Emotional Eating
concepts.title: Emotional Eating
concepts.definition: Eating behaviors caused by PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; ANXIETY; BOREDOM; or other negative emotions rather than physical HUNGER.

concepts.label: Dimensionality Reduction
concepts.title: Dimensionality Reduction
concepts.definition: A machine learning process used to reduce the number of attributes or features of data (called dimensionality) thereby simplifying understanding of the dataset without a loss in data integrity.

concepts.label: Reinforcement Machine Learning
concepts.title: Reinforcement Machine Learning
concepts.definition: A machine learning training method in which an agent in an uncertain environment is rewarded for optimal behaviors and punished for undesired behaviors, allowing the agent to learn from trial-and-error.

concepts.label: Long Short Term Memory
concepts.title: Long Short Term Memory
concepts.definition: A form of recurrent computer neural networks which allows for important information to be retained and less important information to be erased. These kinds of networks are used for tasks such as language translation, anomaly detection, speech and handwriting recognition, and time series prediction.

concepts.label: Recurrent Neural Networks
concepts.title: Recurrent Neural Networks
concepts.definition: A type of neural network where the output from the previous step is fed as input to the current step with the help of a hidden layer which tracks data sequences. Recurrent neural network is often used when the data is sequential, and weights need to be treated same across all the layers such as in time series data and speech recognition. Variation of recurrent neural network include bidirectional neural network and long short-term memory.

concepts.label: Hidden Markov Models
concepts.title: Hidden Markov Models
concepts.definition: Finite learnable stochastic models often used in MACHINE LEARNING consisting of two processes: a MARKOV CHAIN and an event observed and analyzed in a state unknown or hidden to the observer. Hidden Markov Models are often used in BIOINFORMATICS, time series analysis and speech and handwriting recognition.

concepts.label: Claustrophobia
concepts.title: Claustrophobia
concepts.definition: Persistent and irrational fear of enclosed places (e.g., elevators, closets, tunnels) or of being confined (e.g., in an airplane or the backseat of a car). Situations where enclosure or confinement may be encountered are often avoided or else endured with intense anxiety or distress. The focus of fear is typically on panic symptoms triggered in these situations, such as feelings of being unable to breathe, choking, sweating, and fears of losing control. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology, accessed 11/8/2023)

concepts.label: Phobia, School
concepts.title: Phobia, School
concepts.definition: Overwhelming and persistent reluctance to go to school, which usually occurs during the primary school years and is often a symptom of an educational, social, or emotional problem. (From APA Dictionary of Psychology)

concepts.label: Body Satisfaction
concepts.title: Body Satisfaction
concepts.definition: The subjective perception and evaluation of one’s own body in terms of different aspects such as size, shape, musculature or muscle tone, weight, and fitness.

concepts.label: Coccidioidal Meningitis
concepts.title: Coccidioidal Meningitis
concepts.definition: Meningitis caused by a fungus of the genus COCCIDIOIDES, endemic to the SOUTHWESTERN UNITED STATES, south-central Washington State, and parts of Mexico and Central and South America.

concepts.label: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease
concepts.title: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody-Associated Disease
concepts.definition: A disease in which serum antibodies are directed against MYELIN-OLIGODENDROCYTE GLYCOPROTEIN. MOGAD is typically associated with ACUTE DISSEMINATED ENCEPHALOMYELITIS; NEUROMYELITIS OPTICA; or TRANSVERSE MYELITIS.
aliases: Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Antibody Associated Disease
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Autoantibody Associated Disease
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein Immunoglobulin G Associated Disorder
Myelin Oligodendrocyte Glycoprotein-Immunoglobulin G Associated Disorder

concepts.label: Periodization
concepts.title: Periodization
concepts.definition: A systematic training calendar designed to provide variations in performance targeting, while maximizing results and reducing the potential for overtraining. Term only applies to EXERCISE.

concepts.label: Mesolimbic System
concepts.title: Mesolimbic System
concepts.definition: One of the main brain dopaminergic circuits, which connects the MIDBRAIN with the LIMBIC SYSTEM, going from the VENTRAL TEGMENTAL AREA to the NUCLEUS ACCUMBENS, connecting with other structures such as the AMYGDALA and the PREFRONTAL CORTEX.

concepts.label: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
concepts.title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder
concepts.definition: Uncontrolled anxiety or excessive worry that exceeds the realistic scope of life situations and endures for at least a month or longer.

concepts.label: Nociplastic Pain
concepts.title: Nociplastic Pain
concepts.definition: Pain originating from the disrupted function of pain-related sensory pathways in both the peripheral and central nervous system (CNS), leading to heightened sensitivity.

concepts.label: Grief Therapy
concepts.title: Grief Therapy
concepts.definition: Treatment that helps a person work through a greater than normal reaction to a loss, such as the death of a loved one.  Therapy may be individual or group therapy.

concepts.label: Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome
concepts.title: Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome
concepts.definition: Disease that affects linguistic, VISUAL SPATIAL PROCESSING; EXECUTIVE FUNCTION, and MOOD regulation. Cerebellar Cognitive Affective Syndrome is associated with acquired lesions in the CEREBELLUM particularly in the posterior lobe and the vermis.

concepts.label: Chemsex
concepts.title: Chemsex
concepts.definition: The use of drugs to enhance or sustain sexual activity primarily but not exclusively by men who have sex with men.

concepts.label: Sense of Agency
concepts.title: Sense of Agency
concepts.definition: Perception or feeling of control over one's own actions thereby influencing the course of events and outcomes. SELF-EFFICACY on the other hand is beliefs or expectations in self-ability to achieve intended goals or to produce a given effect in specific tasks.

concepts.label: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction
concepts.title: Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction
concepts.definition: A therapeutic intervention designed to improve PSYCHOLOGICAL WELL-BEING through reduced ANXIETY; PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; DEPRESSIVE SYMPTOMS; DISTRESS and improved mood by increased mindfulness.

concepts.label: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy
concepts.title: Mindfulness-Based Cognitive Therapy
concepts.definition: A therapeutic intervention designed to treat people with DEPRESSION through use of elements of MINDFULNESS-BASED STRESS REDUCTION and other cognitive behavioral therapy.

concepts.label: Climate Anxiety
concepts.title: Climate Anxiety
concepts.definition: Persistent and difficult to control psychological distress over CLIMATE CHANGE.

concepts.label: CRF Receptor, Type 1
concepts.title: CRF Receptor, Type 1
concepts.definition: Corticotropin Releasing Hormone Receptor 1 is a G protein coupled receptor that binds corticotropin-releasing hormone, a peptide that plays a key role in activating signal transduction pathways involved in the stress response.

concepts.label: Treatment Expectations
concepts.title: Treatment Expectations
concepts.definition: Outcome anticipated or expected due to various qualities of a healthcare treatment.

concepts.label: Outcome Expectations
concepts.title: Outcome Expectations
concepts.definition: Believed or anticipated consequences of a person’s behavior.

concepts.label: Atrophic Maxilla
concepts.title: Atrophic Maxilla
concepts.definition: Loss of the MAXILLA bone mass and/or height due to natural edentulous maxilla (JAW, EDENTULOUS) or previous dental extractions. It may require a reconstruction via BONE TRANSPLANTATION and/or ALVEOLOPLASTY prior to a DENTAL IMPLANTATION.

concepts.label: Foveomacular Retinitis
concepts.title: Foveomacular Retinitis
concepts.definition: A photochemical injury to retina tissues, usually at the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. It is commonly associated with sungazing, eclipse viewing, welding, or using a laser pointer without proper eye protection resulting in subjective visual disturbances (e.g., floaters) and reduced VISUAL ACUITY.

concepts.label: Medical Interpreting
concepts.title: Medical Interpreting
concepts.definition: The facilitation of verbal communication to assist in the healthcare process, by converting a message in one language to the same message in another language.

concepts.label: Vestibular Migraine
concepts.title: Vestibular Migraine
concepts.definition: Vertigo or major dizziness associated with abnormal brain activity in migraine affecting the VESTIBULAR SYSTEM.

concepts.label: Dual-Task Tests
concepts.title: Dual-Task Tests
concepts.definition: Tests in which two tasks are performed simultaneously. Dual-Task Exercises can be used to show the performance differences of subjects in MULTITASKING BEHAVIOR.

concepts.label: Auditory Acuity
concepts.title: Auditory Acuity
concepts.definition: The ability to hear and distinguish one SOUND from another. These are typically assessed using whisper tests, tuning fork tests, or BONE CONDUCTION tests.

concepts.label: Blood-Spinal Cord Barrier
concepts.title: Blood-Spinal Cord Barrier
concepts.definition: A specialized transport barrier between the PARENCHYMAL TISSUE of the SPINAL CORD and the surrounding BLOOD VESSELS.

concepts.label: Carotid Webs
concepts.title: Carotid Webs
concepts.definition: The presence of one or more thin flap-like membranes arising from the posterior wall of the INTERNAL CAROTID ARTERY bulb. While carotid webs can be asymptomatic, they may also be associated with TRANSIENT ISCHEMIC ATTACKS, and STROKE.

concepts.label: Force Potentiation
concepts.title: Force Potentiation
concepts.definition: A phenomenon where a muscle's force output is temporarily enhanced due to its previous contraction history.

concepts.label: Neurodevelopment
concepts.title: Neurodevelopment
concepts.definition: A developmental process in which NEURONS extend and form SYNAPSES.

concepts.label: Pseudobulbar Affect
concepts.title: Pseudobulbar Affect
concepts.definition: A condition that is characterized by episodes of sudden uncontrollable and inappropriate laughing or crying. It can result from certain neurological conditions or injuries that may impact the way the brain controls emotions.

concepts.label: Acetylcholine
concepts.title: Acetylcholine
concepts.definition: A neurotransmitter found at neuromuscular junctions, autonomic ganglia, parasympathetic effector junctions, a subset of sympathetic effector junctions, and at many sites in the central nervous system.

concepts.label: Achievement
concepts.title: Achievement
concepts.definition: Success in bringing an effort to the desired end; the degree or level of success attained in some specified area (esp. scholastic) or in general.

concepts.label: Acids, Acyclic
concepts.title: Acids, Acyclic
concepts.definition: Carboxylic acids that have open-chain molecular structures as opposed to ring-shaped structures.

concepts.label: Vestibulocochlear Nerve
concepts.title: Vestibulocochlear Nerve
concepts.definition: The 8th cranial nerve. The vestibulocochlear nerve has a cochlear part (COCHLEAR NERVE) which is concerned with hearing and a vestibular part (VESTIBULAR NERVE) which mediates the sense of balance and head position. The fibers of the cochlear nerve originate from neurons of the SPIRAL GANGLION and project to the cochlear nuclei (COCHLEAR NUCLEUS). The fibers of the vestibular nerve arise from neurons of Scarpa's ganglion and project to the VESTIBULAR NUCLEI.

concepts.label: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Diseases
concepts.title: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes of the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE, including the branches of COCHLEAR NERVE and VESTIBULAR NERVE. Common examples are VESTIBULAR NEURITIS, cochlear neuritis, and ACOUSTIC NEUROMA. Clinical signs are varying degree of HEARING LOSS; VERTIGO; and TINNITUS.

concepts.label: Acoustic Stimulation
concepts.title: Acoustic Stimulation
concepts.definition: Use of sound to elicit a response in the nervous system.

concepts.label: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
concepts.title: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome
concepts.definition: An acquired defect of cellular immunity associated with infection by the human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), a CD4-positive T-lymphocyte count under 200 cells/microliter or less than 14% of total lymphocytes, and increased susceptibility to opportunistic infections and malignant neoplasms. Clinical manifestations also include emaciation (wasting) and dementia. These elements reflect criteria for AIDS as defined by the CDC in 1993.

concepts.label: Acrodynia
concepts.title: Acrodynia
concepts.definition: A condition seen primarily in childhood, most often resulting from chronic exposure to MERCURY COMPOUNDS which may result in encephalopathy and POLYNEUROPATHY. Clinical features include pain, swelling and pinkish discoloration of the fingers and toes, weakness in the extremities, extreme irritability, HYPERESTHESIA, and alterations in level of consciousness. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p603)

concepts.label: Acromegaly
concepts.title: Acromegaly
concepts.definition: A condition caused by prolonged exposure to excessive HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE in adults. It is characterized by bony enlargement of the FACE; lower jaw (PROGNATHISM); hands; FEET; HEAD; and THORAX. The most common etiology is a GROWTH HORMONE-SECRETING PITUITARY ADENOMA. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1992, Ch36, pp79-80)

concepts.label: Acting Out
concepts.title: Acting Out
concepts.definition: Expressing unconscious emotional conflicts or feelings, often of hostility or love, through overt behavior.

concepts.label: Actinomycetales Infections
concepts.title: Actinomycetales Infections
concepts.definition: Infections with bacteria of the order ACTINOMYCETALES.

concepts.label: Action Potentials
concepts.title: Action Potentials
concepts.definition: Abrupt changes in the membrane potential that sweep along the CELL MEMBRANE of excitable cells in response to excitation stimuli.

concepts.label: Actuarial Analysis
concepts.title: Actuarial Analysis
concepts.definition: The application of probability and statistical methods to calculate the risk of occurrence of any event, such as onset of illness, recurrent disease, hospitalization, disability, or death. It may include calculation of the anticipated money costs of such events and of the premiums necessary to provide for payment of such costs.

concepts.label: Acute-Phase Proteins
concepts.title: Acute-Phase Proteins
concepts.definition: Proteins that are secreted into the blood in increased or decreased quantities by hepatocytes in response to trauma, inflammation, or disease. These proteins can serve as inhibitors or mediators of the inflammatory processes. Certain acute-phase proteins have been used to diagnose and follow the course of diseases or as tumor markers.

concepts.label: Adaptation, Biological
concepts.title: Adaptation, Biological
concepts.definition: Changes in biological features that help an organism cope with its ENVIRONMENT. These changes include physiological (ADAPTATION, PHYSIOLOGICAL), phenotypic and genetic changes.

concepts.label: Adaptation, Physiological
concepts.title: Adaptation, Physiological
concepts.definition: The non-genetic biological changes of an organism in response to challenges in its ENVIRONMENT.

concepts.label: Adaptation, Psychological
concepts.title: Adaptation, Psychological
concepts.definition: A state of harmony between internal needs and external demands and the processes used in achieving this condition. (From APA Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed).

concepts.label: Adenocarcinoma
concepts.title: Adenocarcinoma
concepts.definition: A malignant epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

concepts.label: Adenoma
concepts.title: Adenoma
concepts.definition: A benign epithelial tumor with a glandular organization.

concepts.label: Adenoma, Basophil
concepts.title: Adenoma, Basophil
concepts.definition: A small tumor of the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland whose cells stain with basic dyes. It may give rise to excessive secretion of ACTH, resulting in CUSHING SYNDROME. (Dorland, 27th ed)

concepts.label: Adenoma, Chromophobe
concepts.title: Adenoma, Chromophobe
concepts.definition: A benign tumor of the anterior pituitary in which the cells do not stain with acidic or basic dyes.

concepts.label: Adenoma, Acidophil
concepts.title: Adenoma, Acidophil
concepts.definition: A benign tumor, usually found in the anterior lobe of the pituitary gland, whose cells stain with acid dyes. Such pituitary tumors may give rise to excessive secretion of growth hormone, resulting in gigantism or acromegaly. A specific type of acidophil adenoma may give rise to nonpuerperal galactorrhea. (Dorland, 27th ed)

concepts.label: Adenosine Triphosphatases
concepts.title: Adenosine Triphosphatases
concepts.definition: A group of enzymes which catalyze the hydrolysis of ATP. The hydrolysis reaction is usually coupled with another function such as transporting Ca(2+) across a membrane. These enzymes may be dependent on Ca(2+), Mg(2+), anions, H+, or DNA.

concepts.label: Adie Syndrome
concepts.title: Adie Syndrome
concepts.definition: A syndrome characterized by a TONIC PUPIL that occurs in combination with decreased lower extremity reflexes. The affected pupil will respond more briskly to accommodation than to light (light-near dissociation) and is supersensitive to dilute pilocarpine eye drops, which induce pupillary constriction. Pathologic features include degeneration of the ciliary ganglion and postganglionic parasympathetic fibers that innervate the pupillary constrictor muscle. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p279)

concepts.label: Adjustment Disorders
concepts.title: Adjustment Disorders
concepts.definition: Maladaptive reactions to identifiable psychosocial stressors occurring within a short time after onset of the stressor. They are manifested by either impairment in social or occupational functioning or by symptoms (depression, anxiety, etc.) that are in excess of a normal and expected reaction to the stressor.

concepts.label: Adolescent Behavior
concepts.title: Adolescent Behavior
concepts.definition: Any observable response or action of an adolescent.

concepts.label: Adolescent Psychiatry
concepts.title: Adolescent Psychiatry
concepts.definition: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders in individuals 13-18 years.

concepts.label: Psychology, Adolescent
concepts.title: Psychology, Adolescent
concepts.definition: Field of psychology involving the study of normal and abnormal behavior of adolescents. It includes mental processes as well as observable responses.

concepts.label: Adrenal Gland Diseases
concepts.title: Adrenal Gland Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes of the ADRENAL GLANDS.

concepts.label: Adrenocortical Hyperfunction
concepts.title: Adrenocortical Hyperfunction
concepts.definition: Excess production of ADRENAL CORTEX HORMONES such as ALDOSTERONE; HYDROCORTISONE; DEHYDROEPIANDROSTERONE; and/or ANDROSTENEDIONE. Hyperadrenal syndromes include CUSHING SYNDROME; HYPERALDOSTERONISM; and VIRILISM.

concepts.label: Adrenal Insufficiency
concepts.title: Adrenal Insufficiency
concepts.definition: Conditions in which the production of adrenal CORTICOSTEROIDS falls below the requirement of the body. Adrenal insufficiency can be caused by defects in the ADRENAL GLANDS, the PITUITARY GLAND, or the HYPOTHALAMUS.

concepts.label: Adrenal Glands
concepts.title: Adrenal Glands
concepts.definition: A pair of glands located at the cranial pole of each of the two KIDNEYS. Each adrenal gland is composed of two distinct endocrine tissues with separate embryonic origins, the ADRENAL CORTEX producing STEROIDS and the ADRENAL MEDULLA producing NEUROTRANSMITTERS.

concepts.label: Adrenal Medulla
concepts.title: Adrenal Medulla
concepts.definition: The inner portion of the adrenal gland. Derived from ECTODERM, adrenal medulla consists mainly of CHROMAFFIN CELLS that produces and stores a number of NEUROTRANSMITTERS, mainly adrenaline (EPINEPHRINE) and NOREPINEPHRINE. The activity of the adrenal medulla is regulated by the SYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM.

concepts.label: Adrenergic alpha-Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic alpha-Agonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that selectively bind to and activate alpha adrenergic receptors.

concepts.label: Adrenergic alpha-Antagonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic alpha-Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate alpha-adrenergic receptors thereby blocking the actions of endogenous or exogenous adrenergic agonists. Adrenergic alpha-antagonists are used in the treatment of hypertension, vasospasm, peripheral vascular disease, shock, and pheochromocytoma.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-Agonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that selectively bind to and activate beta-adrenergic receptors.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-Antagonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate beta-adrenergic receptors thereby blocking the actions of beta-adrenergic agonists. Adrenergic beta-antagonists are used for treatment of hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, angina pectoris, glaucoma, migraine headaches, and anxiety.

concepts.label: Adrenergic Fibers
concepts.title: Adrenergic Fibers
concepts.definition: Nerve fibers liberating catecholamines at a synapse after an impulse.

concepts.label: Adrenergic Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic Agonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to and activate adrenergic receptors.

concepts.label: Adrenoleukodystrophy
concepts.title: Adrenoleukodystrophy
concepts.definition: An X-linked recessive disorder characterized by the accumulation of saturated very long chain fatty acids in the LYSOSOMES of ADRENAL CORTEX and the white matter of CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. This disease occurs almost exclusively in the males. Clinical features include the childhood onset of ATAXIA; NEUROBEHAVIORAL MANIFESTATIONS; HYPERPIGMENTATION; ADRENAL INSUFFICIENCY; SEIZURES; MUSCLE SPASTICITY; and DEMENTIA. The slowly progressive adult form is called adrenomyeloneuropathy. The defective gene ABCD1 is located at Xq28, and encodes the adrenoleukodystrophy protein (ATP-BINDING CASSETTE TRANSPORTERS).

concepts.label: Affect
concepts.title: Affect
concepts.definition: The feeling-tone accompaniment of an idea or mental representation. It is the most direct psychic derivative of instinct and the psychic representative of the various bodily changes by means of which instincts manifest themselves.

concepts.label: Affective Disorders, Psychotic
concepts.title: Affective Disorders, Psychotic
concepts.definition: Disorders in which the essential feature is a severe disturbance in mood (depression, anxiety, elation, and excitement) accompanied by psychotic symptoms such as delusions, hallucinations, gross impairment in reality testing, etc.

concepts.label: Affective Symptoms
concepts.title: Affective Symptoms
concepts.definition: Mood or emotional responses dissonant with or inappropriate to the behavior and/or stimulus.

concepts.label: Afferent Pathways
concepts.title: Afferent Pathways
concepts.definition: Nerve structures through which impulses are conducted from a peripheral part toward a nerve center.

concepts.label: Aftercare
concepts.title: Aftercare
concepts.definition: The care and treatment of a convalescent patient, especially that of a patient after surgery.

concepts.label: Afterimage
concepts.title: Afterimage
concepts.definition: Continuation of visual impression after cessation of stimuli causing the original image.

concepts.label: Ageusia
concepts.title: Ageusia
concepts.definition: Complete or severe loss of the subjective sense of taste, frequently accompanied by OLFACTION DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Aggression
concepts.title: Aggression
concepts.definition: Behavior which may be manifested by destructive and attacking action which is verbal or physical, by covert attitudes of hostility or by obstructionism.

concepts.label: Agnosia
concepts.title: Agnosia
concepts.definition: Loss of the ability to comprehend the meaning or recognize the importance of various forms of stimulation that cannot be attributed to impairment of a primary sensory modality. Tactile agnosia is characterized by an inability to perceive the shape and nature of an object by touch alone, despite unimpaired sensation to light touch, position, and other primary sensory modalities.

concepts.label: Agonistic Behavior
concepts.title: Agonistic Behavior
concepts.definition: Any behavior associated with conflict between two individuals.

concepts.label: Agoraphobia
concepts.title: Agoraphobia
concepts.definition: Obsessive, persistent, intense fear of places or situations from which escape might be difficult or embarrassing.

concepts.label: Agraphia
concepts.title: Agraphia
concepts.definition: Loss or impairment of the ability to write (letters, syllables, words, or phrases) due to an injury to a specific cerebral area or occasionally due to emotional factors. This condition rarely occurs in isolation, and often accompanies APHASIA. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p485; APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994)

concepts.label: Air Pollution
concepts.title: Air Pollution
concepts.definition: The presence of contaminants or pollutant substances in the air (AIR POLLUTANTS) that interfere with human health or welfare, or produce other harmful environmental effects. The substances may include GASES; PARTICULATE MATTER; or volatile ORGANIC CHEMICALS.

concepts.label: Akinetic Mutism
concepts.title: Akinetic Mutism
concepts.definition: A syndrome characterized by a silent and inert state without voluntary motor activity despite preserved sensorimotor pathways and vigilance. Bilateral FRONTAL LOBE dysfunction involving the anterior cingulate gyrus and related brain injuries are associated with this condition. This may result in impaired abilities to communicate and initiate motor activities. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p348; Fortschr Neurol Psychiatr 1995 Feb;63(2):59-67)

concepts.label: Alcohol Amnestic Disorder
concepts.title: Alcohol Amnestic Disorder
concepts.definition: A mental disorder associated with chronic ethanol abuse (ALCOHOLISM) and nutritional deficiencies characterized by short term memory loss, confabulations, and disturbances of attention. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1139)

concepts.label: Alcohol Deterrents
concepts.title: Alcohol Deterrents
concepts.definition: Substances interfering with the metabolism of ethyl alcohol, causing unpleasant side effects thought to discourage the drinking of alcoholic beverages. Alcohol deterrents are used in the treatment of alcoholism.

concepts.label: Alcohol Drinking
concepts.title: Alcohol Drinking
concepts.definition: Behaviors associated with the ingesting of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES, including social drinking.

concepts.label: Alcohol Withdrawal Delirium
concepts.title: Alcohol Withdrawal Delirium
concepts.definition: An acute organic mental disorder induced by cessation or reduction in chronic alcohol consumption. Clinical characteristics include CONFUSION; DELUSIONS; vivid HALLUCINATIONS; TREMOR; agitation; insomnia; and signs of autonomic hyperactivity (e.g., elevated blood pressure and heart rate, dilated pupils, and diaphoresis). This condition may occasionally be fatal. It was formerly called delirium tremens. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1175)

concepts.label: Alcoholic Intoxication
concepts.title: Alcoholic Intoxication
concepts.definition: An acute brain syndrome which results from the excessive ingestion of ETHANOL or ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES.

concepts.label: Alcoholics Anonymous
concepts.title: Alcoholics Anonymous
concepts.definition: An organization of self-proclaimed alcoholics who meet frequently to reinforce their practice of abstinence.

concepts.label: Alcoholism
concepts.title: Alcoholism
concepts.definition: A primary, chronic disease with genetic, psychosocial, and environmental factors influencing its development and manifestations. The disease is often progressive and fatal. It is characterized by impaired control over drinking, preoccupation with the drug alcohol, use of alcohol despite adverse consequences, and distortions in thinking, most notably denial. Each of these symptoms may be continuous or periodic. (Morse & Flavin for the Joint Commission of the National Council on Alcoholism and Drug Dependence and the American Society of Addiction Medicine to Study the Definition and Criteria for the Diagnosis of Alcoholism: in JAMA 1992;268:1012-4)

concepts.label: Alcohols
concepts.title: Alcohols
concepts.definition: Alkyl compounds containing a hydroxyl group. They are classified according to relation of the carbon atom: primary alcohols, R-CH2OH; secondary alcohols, R2-CHOH; tertiary alcohols, R3-COH. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

concepts.label: Algorithms
concepts.title: Algorithms
concepts.definition: A procedure consisting of a sequence of algebraic formulas and/or logical steps to calculate or determine a given task.

concepts.label: alpha-Fetoproteins
concepts.title: alpha-Fetoproteins
concepts.definition: The first alpha-globulins to appear in mammalian sera during FETAL DEVELOPMENT and the dominant serum proteins in early embryonic life.

concepts.label: Alpha-Globulins
concepts.title: Alpha-Globulins
concepts.definition: Serum proteins that have the most rapid migration during ELECTROPHORESIS. This subgroup of globulins is divided into faster and slower alpha(1)- and alpha(2)-globulins.

concepts.label: Alpha Rhythm
concepts.title: Alpha Rhythm
concepts.definition: Brain waves characterized by a relatively high voltage or amplitude and a frequency of 8-13 Hz. They constitute the majority of waves recorded by EEG registering the activity of the parietal and occipital lobes when the individual is awake, but relaxed with the eyes closed.

concepts.label: alpha-Galactosidase
concepts.title: alpha-Galactosidase
concepts.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of terminal, non-reducing alpha-D-galactose residues in alpha-galactosides including galactose oligosaccharides, galactomannans, and galactolipids.

concepts.label: Complementary Therapies
concepts.title: Complementary Therapies
concepts.definition: Therapeutic practices which are not currently considered an integral part of conventional allopathic medical practice. They may lack biomedical explanations but as they become better researched some (PHYSICAL THERAPY MODALITIES; DIET; ACUPUNCTURE) become widely accepted whereas others (humors, radium therapy) quietly fade away, yet are important historical footnotes. Therapies are termed as Complementary when used in addition to conventional treatments and as Alternative when used instead of conventional treatment.

concepts.label: Altruism
concepts.title: Altruism
concepts.definition: Belief or practice of selfless concern for others.

concepts.label: Alzheimer Disease
concepts.title: Alzheimer Disease
concepts.definition: A degenerative disease of the BRAIN characterized by the insidious onset of DEMENTIA. Impairment of MEMORY, judgment, attention span, and problem solving skills are followed by severe APRAXIAS and a global loss of cognitive abilities. The condition primarily occurs after age 60, and is marked pathologically by severe cortical atrophy and the triad of SENILE PLAQUES; NEUROFIBRILLARY TANGLES; and NEUROPIL THREADS. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1049-57)

concepts.label: Amblyopia
concepts.title: Amblyopia
concepts.definition: A nonspecific term referring to impaired vision. Major subcategories include stimulus deprivation-induced amblyopia and toxic amblyopia. Stimulus deprivation-induced amblyopia is a developmental disorder of the visual cortex. A discrepancy between visual information received by the visual cortex from each eye results in abnormal cortical development. STRABISMUS and REFRACTIVE ERRORS may cause this condition. Toxic amblyopia is a disorder of the OPTIC NERVE which is associated with ALCOHOLISM, tobacco SMOKING, and other toxins and as an adverse effect of the use of some medications.

concepts.label: Amides
concepts.title: Amides
concepts.definition: Organic compounds containing the -CO-NH2 radical. Amides are derived from acids by replacement of -OH by -NH2 or from ammonia by the replacement of H by an acyl group. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

concepts.label: Oxidoreductases Acting on CH-NH Group Donors
concepts.title: Oxidoreductases Acting on CH-NH Group Donors
concepts.definition: Enzymes catalyzing the dehydrogenation of secondary amines, introducing a C=N double bond as the primary reaction. In some cases this is later hydrolyzed.
aliases: Oxidoreductases Acting on CH NH Group Donors

concepts.label: Amines
concepts.title: Amines
concepts.definition: A group of compounds derived from ammonia by substituting organic radicals for the hydrogens. (From Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

concepts.label: Amino Acid Metabolism, Inborn Errors
concepts.title: Amino Acid Metabolism, Inborn Errors
concepts.definition: Disorders affecting amino acid metabolism. The majority of these disorders are inherited and present in the neonatal period with metabolic disturbances (e.g., ACIDOSIS) and neurologic manifestations. They are present at birth, although they may not become symptomatic until later in life.

concepts.label: Amino Acid Oxidoreductases
concepts.title: Amino Acid Oxidoreductases
concepts.definition: A class of enzymes that catalyze oxidation-reduction reactions of amino acids.

concepts.label: Amino Acids
concepts.title: Amino Acids
concepts.definition: Organic compounds that generally contain an amino (-NH2) and a carboxyl (-COOH) group. Twenty alpha-amino acids are the subunits which are polymerized to form proteins.

concepts.label: Amino Acids, Cyclic
concepts.title: Amino Acids, Cyclic
concepts.definition: A class of amino acids characterized by a closed ring structure.

concepts.label: Amino Acids, Dicarboxylic
concepts.title: Amino Acids, Dicarboxylic
concepts.definition: MeSH 已登记该主题词，但此条目未提供范围说明；需继续补全定义。

concepts.label: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
concepts.title: Amino Acids, Peptides, and Proteins
concepts.definition: Amino acids and chains of amino acids connected by peptide linkages.

concepts.label: Amino Alcohols
concepts.title: Amino Alcohols
concepts.definition: Compounds possessing both a hydroxyl (-OH) and an amino group (-NH2).

concepts.label: Renal Aminoacidurias
concepts.title: Renal Aminoacidurias
concepts.definition: A group of inherited kidney disorders characterized by the abnormally elevated levels of AMINO ACIDS in URINE. Genetic mutations of transport proteins result in the defective reabsorption of free amino acids at the PROXIMAL RENAL TUBULES. Renal aminoaciduria are classified by the specific amino acid or acids involved.

concepts.label: Aminobutyrates
concepts.title: Aminobutyrates
concepts.definition: Derivatives of BUTYRIC ACID that contain one or more amino groups attached to the aliphatic structure. Included under this heading are a broad variety of acid forms, salts, esters, and amides that include the aminobutryrate structure.

concepts.label: Amnesia
concepts.title: Amnesia
concepts.definition: Pathologic partial or complete loss of the ability to recall past experiences (AMNESIA, RETROGRADE) or to form new memories (AMNESIA, ANTEROGRADE). This condition may be of organic or psychologic origin. Organic forms of amnesia are usually associated with dysfunction of the DIENCEPHALON or HIPPOCAMPUS. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp426-7)

concepts.label: Amnesia, Retrograde
concepts.title: Amnesia, Retrograde
concepts.definition: Loss of the ability to recall information that had been previously encoded in memory prior to a specified or approximate point in time. This process may be organic or psychogenic in origin. Organic forms may be associated with CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA; CEREBROVASCULAR ACCIDENTS; SEIZURES; DEMENTIA; and a wide variety of other conditions that impair cerebral function. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp426-9)

concepts.label: Amphetamines
concepts.title: Amphetamines
concepts.definition: Analogs or derivatives of AMPHETAMINE. Many are sympathomimetics and central nervous system stimulators causing excitation, vasopressin, bronchodilation, and to varying degrees, anorexia, analepsis, nasal decongestion, and some smooth muscle relaxation.

concepts.label: Amygdala
concepts.title: Amygdala
concepts.definition: Almond-shaped group of basal nuclei anterior to the INFERIOR HORN OF THE LATERAL VENTRICLE of the TEMPORAL LOBE. The amygdala is part of the limbic system.

concepts.label: Amyloid
concepts.title: Amyloid
concepts.definition: A fibrous protein complex that consists of proteins folded into a specific cross beta-pleated sheet structure. This fibrillar structure has been found as an alternative folding pattern for a variety of functional proteins. Deposits of amyloid in the form of AMYLOID PLAQUES are associated with a variety of degenerative diseases. The amyloid structure has also been found in a number of functional proteins that are unrelated to disease.

concepts.label: Amyloidosis
concepts.title: Amyloidosis
concepts.definition: A group of sporadic, familial and/or inherited, degenerative, and infectious disease processes, linked by the common theme of abnormal protein folding and deposition of AMYLOID. As the amyloid deposits enlarge they displace normal tissue structures, causing disruption of function. Various signs and symptoms depend on the location and size of the deposits.

concepts.label: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
concepts.title: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis
concepts.definition: A degenerative disorder affecting upper MOTOR NEURONS in the brain and lower motor neurons in the brain stem and SPINAL CORD. Disease onset is usually after the age of 50 and the process is usually fatal within 3 to 6 years. Clinical manifestations include progressive weakness, atrophy, FASCICULATION, hyperreflexia, DYSARTHRIA, dysphagia, and eventual paralysis of respiratory function. Pathologic features include the replacement of motor neurons with fibrous ASTROCYTES and atrophy of anterior SPINAL NERVE ROOTS and corticospinal tracts. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1089-94)
aliases: Motor Neuron Disease, Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis

concepts.label: Central Nervous System Stimulants
concepts.title: Central Nervous System Stimulants
concepts.definition: A loosely defined group of drugs that tend to increase behavioral alertness, agitation, or excitation. They work by a variety of mechanisms, but usually not by direct excitation of neurons. The many drugs that have such actions as side effects to their main therapeutic use are not included here.

concepts.label: Analgesia
concepts.title: Analgesia
concepts.definition: Methods of PAIN relief that may be used with or in place of ANALGESICS.

concepts.label: Pain Insensitivity, Congenital
concepts.title: Pain Insensitivity, Congenital
concepts.definition: A syndrome characterized by indifference to PAIN despite the ability to distinguish noxious from non-noxious stimuli. Absent corneal reflexes and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY may be associated. Familial forms with autosomal recessive and autosomal dominant patterns of inheritance have been described. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1343)

concepts.label: Analgesics
concepts.title: Analgesics
concepts.definition: Compounds capable of relieving pain without the loss of CONSCIOUSNESS.

concepts.label: Analysis of Variance
concepts.title: Analysis of Variance
concepts.definition: A statistical technique that isolates and assesses the contributions of categorical independent variables to variation in the mean of a continuous dependent variable.

concepts.label: Anastomosis, Surgical
concepts.title: Anastomosis, Surgical
concepts.definition: Surgical union or shunt between ducts, tubes or vessels. It may be end-to-end, end-to-side, side-to-end, or side-to-side.

concepts.label: Anatomy
concepts.title: Anatomy
concepts.definition: A branch of biology dealing with the structure of organisms.

concepts.label: Anecdotes as Topic
concepts.title: Anecdotes as Topic
concepts.definition: Works about brief accounts or narratives of an incident or event.

concepts.label: Anencephaly
concepts.title: Anencephaly
concepts.definition: A malformation of the nervous system caused by failure of the anterior neuropore to close. Infants are born with intact spinal cords, cerebellums, and brainstems, but lack formation of neural structures above this level. The skull is only partially formed but the eyes are usually normal. This condition may be associated with folate deficiency. Affected infants are only capable of primitive (brain stem) reflexes and usually do not survive for more than two weeks. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p247)

concepts.label: Anesthesia
concepts.title: Anesthesia
concepts.definition: A state characterized by loss of feeling or sensation. This depression of nerve function is usually the result of pharmacologic action and is induced to allow performance of surgery or other painful procedures.

concepts.label: Anesthesia and Analgesia
concepts.title: Anesthesia and Analgesia
concepts.definition: Medical methods of either relieving pain caused by a particular condition or removing the sensation of pain during a surgery or other medical procedure.

concepts.label: Anesthesia, Conduction
concepts.title: Anesthesia, Conduction
concepts.definition: Injection of an anesthetic to inhibit nerve transmission in a specific part of the body.

concepts.label: Anesthetics
concepts.title: Anesthetics
concepts.definition: Agents capable of inducing a total or partial loss of sensation, especially tactile sensation and pain. They may act to induce general ANESTHESIA, in which an unconscious state is achieved, or may act locally to induce numbness or lack of sensation at a targeted site.

concepts.label: Aneurysm
concepts.title: Aneurysm
concepts.definition: Pathological outpouching or sac-like dilatation in the wall of any blood vessel (ARTERIES or VEINS) or the heart (HEART ANEURYSM). It indicates a thin and weakened area in the wall which may later rupture. Aneurysms are classified by location, etiology, or other characteristics.

concepts.label: Anger
concepts.title: Anger
concepts.definition: A strong emotional feeling of displeasure aroused by being interfered with, injured or threatened.

concepts.label: Angina Pectoris
concepts.title: Angina Pectoris
concepts.definition: The symptom of paroxysmal pain consequent to MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA usually of distinctive character, location and radiation. It is thought to be provoked by a transient stressful situation during which the oxygen requirements of the MYOCARDIUM exceed that supplied by the CORONARY CIRCULATION.

concepts.label: Angiography
concepts.title: Angiography
concepts.definition: Radiography of blood vessels after injection of a contrast medium.

concepts.label: Fabry Disease
concepts.title: Fabry Disease
concepts.definition: An X-linked inherited metabolic disease caused by a deficiency of lysosomal ALPHA-GALACTOSIDASE A. It is characterized by intralysosomal accumulation of globotriaosylceramide and other GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS in blood vessels throughout the body leading to multi-system complications including renal, cardiac, cerebrovascular, and skin disorders.

concepts.label: Angiomatosis
concepts.title: Angiomatosis
concepts.definition: A condition with multiple tumor-like lesions caused either by congenital or developmental malformations of BLOOD VESSELS, or reactive vascular proliferations, such as in bacillary angiomatosis. Angiomatosis is considered non-neoplastic.

concepts.label: Animals
concepts.title: Animals
concepts.definition: Unicellular or multicellular, heterotrophic organisms, that have sensation and the power of voluntary movement. Under the older five kingdom paradigm, Animalia was one of the kingdoms. Under the modern three domain model, Animalia represents one of the many groups in the domain EUKARYOTA.

concepts.label: Animal Communication
concepts.title: Animal Communication
concepts.definition: Communication between animals involving the giving off by one individual of some chemical or physical signal, that, on being received by another, influences its behavior.

concepts.label: Animal Diseases
concepts.title: Animal Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases that occur in VERTEBRATE animals.

concepts.label: Animal Structures
concepts.title: Animal Structures
concepts.definition: Organs and other anatomical structures of non-human vertebrate and invertebrate animals.

concepts.label: Animal Population Groups
concepts.title: Animal Population Groups
concepts.definition: Animals grouped according to ecological, morphological or genetic populations.

concepts.label: Animals, Domestic
concepts.title: Animals, Domestic
concepts.definition: Animals which have become adapted through breeding in captivity to a life intimately associated with humans. They include animals domesticated by humans to live and breed in a tame condition on farms or ranches for economic reasons, including LIVESTOCK (specifically CATTLE; SHEEP; HORSES; etc.), POULTRY; and those raised or kept for pleasure and companionship, e.g., PETS; or specifically DOGS; CATS; etc.

concepts.label: Animals, Laboratory
concepts.title: Animals, Laboratory
concepts.definition: Animals used or intended for use in research, testing, or teaching.

concepts.label: Anomia
concepts.title: Anomia
concepts.definition: A language dysfunction characterized by the inability to name people and objects that are correctly perceived. The individual is able to describe the object in question, but cannot provide the name. This condition is associated with lesions of the dominant hemisphere involving the language areas, in particular the TEMPORAL LOBE. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p484)

concepts.label: Anomie
concepts.title: Anomie
concepts.definition: A state of social disorganization and demoralization in society which is largely the result of disharmony between cultural goals and the means for attaining them. This may be reflected in the behavior of the individual in many ways - non-conformity, social withdrawal, deviant behavior, etc.

concepts.label: Anorexia
concepts.title: Anorexia
concepts.definition: The lack or loss of APPETITE accompanied by an aversion to food and the inability to eat. It is the defining characteristic of the disorder ANOREXIA NERVOSA.

concepts.label: Anorexia Nervosa
concepts.title: Anorexia Nervosa
concepts.definition: An eating disorder that is characterized by the lack or loss of APPETITE, known as ANOREXIA. Other features include excess fear of becoming OVERWEIGHT; BODY IMAGE disturbance; significant WEIGHT LOSS; and refusal to maintain minimal normal weight.

concepts.label: Olfaction Disorders
concepts.title: Olfaction Disorders
concepts.definition: Impaired ability to smell. This may be caused by OLFACTORY NERVE DISEASES; PARANASAL SINUS DISEASES; viral RESPIRATORY TRACT INFECTIONS; CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA; SMOKING; and other conditions.

concepts.label: Hypoxia
concepts.title: Hypoxia
concepts.definition: Sub-optimal OXYGEN levels in the ambient air of living organisms.

concepts.label: Anterior Horn Cells
concepts.title: Anterior Horn Cells
concepts.definition: MOTOR NEURONS in the anterior (ventral) horn of the SPINAL CORD which project to SKELETAL MUSCLES.

concepts.label: Haplorhini
concepts.title: Haplorhini
concepts.definition: A suborder of PRIMATES consisting of six families: CEBIDAE (some New World monkeys), ATELIDAE (some New World monkeys), CERCOPITHECIDAE (Old World monkeys), HYLOBATIDAE (gibbons and siamangs), CALLITRICHINAE (marmosets and tamarins), and HOMINIDAE (humans and great apes).

concepts.label: Anthropology
concepts.title: Anthropology
concepts.definition: The science devoted to the comparative study of man.

concepts.label: Anthropology, Cultural
concepts.title: Anthropology, Cultural
concepts.definition: Study of social phenomena which characterize the learned, shared, and transmitted social activities of particular ethnic groups with focus on the causes, consequences, and complexities of human social and cultural variability.

concepts.label: Anthropology, Physical
concepts.title: Anthropology, Physical
concepts.definition: The comparative science dealing with the physical characteristics of humans as related to their origin, evolution, and development in the total environment.

concepts.label: Anthropometry
concepts.title: Anthropometry
concepts.definition: The technique that deals with the measurement of the size, weight, and proportions of the human or other primate body.

concepts.label: Anti-Ulcer Agents
concepts.title: Anti-Ulcer Agents
concepts.definition: Various agents with different action mechanisms used to treat or ameliorate PEPTIC ULCER or irritation of the gastrointestinal tract. This has included ANTIBIOTICS to treat HELICOBACTER INFECTIONS; HISTAMINE H2 ANTAGONISTS to reduce GASTRIC ACID secretion; and ANTACIDS for symptomatic relief.

concepts.label: Anticonvulsants
concepts.title: Anticonvulsants
concepts.definition: Drugs used to prevent SEIZURES or reduce their severity.

concepts.label: Antidepressive Agents
concepts.title: Antidepressive Agents
concepts.definition: Mood-stimulating drugs used primarily in the treatment of affective disorders and related conditions. Several MONOAMINE OXIDASE INHIBITORS are useful as antidepressants apparently as a long-term consequence of their modulation of catecholamine levels. The tricyclic compounds useful as antidepressive agents (ANTIDEPRESSIVE AGENTS, TRICYCLIC) also appear to act through brain catecholamine systems. A third group (ANTIDEPRESSIVE AGENTS, SECOND-GENERATION) is a diverse group of drugs including some that act specifically on serotonergic systems.

concepts.label: Antidepressive Agents, Tricyclic
concepts.title: Antidepressive Agents, Tricyclic
concepts.definition: Substances that contain a fused three-ring moiety and are used in the treatment of depression. These drugs block the uptake of norepinephrine and serotonin into axon terminals and may block some subtypes of serotonin, adrenergic, and histamine receptors. However, the mechanism of their antidepressant effects is not clear because the therapeutic effects usually take weeks to develop and may reflect compensatory changes in the central nervous system.

concepts.label: Antigens
concepts.title: Antigens
concepts.definition: Substances that are recognized by the immune system and induce an immune reaction.

concepts.label: Antigens, Surface
concepts.title: Antigens, Surface
concepts.definition: Antigens on surfaces of cells, including infectious or foreign cells or viruses. They are usually protein-containing groups on cell membranes or walls and may be isolated.

concepts.label: Antisocial Personality Disorder
concepts.title: Antisocial Personality Disorder
concepts.definition: A personality disorder whose essential feature is a pervasive pattern of disregard for, and violation of, the rights of others that begins in childhood or early adolescence and continues into adulthood. The individual must be at least age 18 and must have a history of some symptoms of CONDUCT DISORDER before age 15. (From DSM-IV, 1994).

concepts.label: Anxiety
concepts.title: Anxiety
concepts.definition: Feelings or emotions of dread, apprehension, and impending disaster but not disabling as with ANXIETY DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Anxiety Disorders
concepts.title: Anxiety Disorders
concepts.definition: Persistent and disabling ANXIETY.

concepts.label: Anxiety, Castration
concepts.title: Anxiety, Castration
concepts.definition: Anxiety due to fantasized injuries to or loss of the genitals.

concepts.label: Anxiety, Separation
concepts.title: Anxiety, Separation
concepts.definition: Anxiety experienced by an individual upon separation from a person or object of particular significance to the individual.

concepts.label: Aortic Bodies
concepts.title: Aortic Bodies
concepts.definition: Small clusters of chemoreceptive and supporting cells located near the ARCH OF THE AORTA; the PULMONARY ARTERIES; and the CORONARY ARTERIES. The aortic bodies sense PH; CARBON DIOXIDE; and OXYGEN concentrations in the BLOOD and participate in the control of RESPIRATION. The aortic bodies should not be confused with the PARA-AORTIC BODIES in the abdomen (which are sometimes also called aortic bodies).

concepts.label: Aortic Valve Stenosis
concepts.title: Aortic Valve Stenosis
concepts.definition: A pathological constriction that can occur above (supravalvular stenosis), below (subvalvular stenosis), or at the AORTIC VALVE. It is characterized by restricted outflow from the LEFT VENTRICLE into the AORTA.

concepts.label: Aphasia
concepts.title: Aphasia
concepts.definition: A cognitive disorder marked by an impaired ability to comprehend or express language in its written or spoken form. This condition is caused by diseases which affect the language areas of the dominant hemisphere. Clinical features are used to classify the various subtypes of this condition. General categories include receptive, expressive, and mixed forms of aphasia.

concepts.label: Aphasia, Broca
concepts.title: Aphasia, Broca
concepts.definition: An aphasia characterized by impairment of expressive LANGUAGE (speech, writing, signs) and relative preservation of receptive language abilities (i.e., comprehension). This condition is caused by lesions of the motor association cortex in the FRONTAL LOBE (BROCA AREA and adjacent cortical and white matter regions).

concepts.label: Aphasia, Wernicke
concepts.title: Aphasia, Wernicke
concepts.definition: Impairment in the comprehension of speech and meaning of words, both spoken and written, and of the meanings conveyed by their grammatical relationships in sentences. It is caused by lesions that primarily affect Wernicke's area, which lies in the posterior perisylvian region of the temporal lobe of the dominant hemisphere. (From Brain & Bannister, Clinical Neurology, 7th ed, p141; Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science, 3d ed, p846)

concepts.label: Aphonia
concepts.title: Aphonia
concepts.definition: Complete loss of phonation due to organic disease of the larynx or to nonorganic (i.e., psychogenic) causes.

concepts.label: Apnea
concepts.title: Apnea
concepts.definition: A transient absence of spontaneous respiration.

concepts.label: Appetite
concepts.title: Appetite
concepts.definition: Natural recurring desire for food. Alterations may be induced by APPETITE DEPRESSANTS or APPETITE STIMULANTS.

concepts.label: Appetite Depressants
concepts.title: Appetite Depressants
concepts.definition: Agents that are used to suppress appetite.

concepts.label: Feeding and Eating Disorders
concepts.title: Feeding and Eating Disorders
concepts.definition: A group of disorders characterized by physiological and/or psychological disturbances in appetite or food intake.

concepts.label: Appetitive Behavior
concepts.title: Appetitive Behavior
concepts.definition: Animal searching behavior. The variable introductory phase of an instinctive behavior pattern or sequence, e.g., looking for food, or sequential courtship patterns prior to mating.

concepts.label: Apraxias
concepts.title: Apraxias
concepts.definition: A group of cognitive disorders characterized by the inability to perform previously learned skills that cannot be attributed to deficits of motor or sensory function. The two major subtypes of this condition are ideomotor (see APRAXIA, IDEOMOTOR) and ideational apraxia, which refers to loss of the ability to mentally formulate the processes involved with performing an action. For example, dressing apraxia may result from an inability to mentally formulate the act of placing clothes on the body. Apraxias are generally associated with lesions of the dominant PARIETAL LOBE and supramarginal gyrus. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp56-7)

concepts.label: Aptitude
concepts.title: Aptitude
concepts.definition: The ability to acquire general or special types of knowledge or skill.

concepts.label: Aptitude Tests
concepts.title: Aptitude Tests
concepts.definition: Primarily non-verbal tests designed to predict an individual's future learning ability or performance.

concepts.label: Arachnoid
concepts.title: Arachnoid
concepts.definition: A delicate membrane enveloping the brain and spinal cord. It lies between the PIA MATER and the DURA MATER. It is separated from the pia mater by the subarachnoid cavity which is filled with CEREBROSPINAL FLUID.

concepts.label: Arachnoiditis
concepts.title: Arachnoiditis
concepts.definition: Acute or chronic inflammation of the arachnoid membrane of the meninges most often involving the spinal cord or base of the brain. This term generally refers to a persistent inflammatory process characterized by thickening of the ARACHNOID membrane and dural adhesions. Associated conditions include prior surgery, infections, trauma, SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE, and chemical irritation. Clinical features vary with the site of inflammation, but include cranial neuropathies, radiculopathies, and myelopathies. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1997, Ch48, p25)

concepts.label: Arbovirus Infections
concepts.title: Arbovirus Infections
concepts.definition: Infections caused by arthropod-borne viruses, general or unspecified.

concepts.label: Arcuate Nucleus of Hypothalamus
concepts.title: Arcuate Nucleus of Hypothalamus
concepts.definition: A nucleus located in the middle hypothalamus in the most ventral part of the THIRD VENTRICLE near the entrance of the infundibular recess. Its small cells are in close contact with the EPENDYMA.

concepts.label: Arenaviridae Infections
concepts.title: Arenaviridae Infections
concepts.definition: Virus diseases caused by the ARENAVIRIDAE.

concepts.label: Arginase
concepts.title: Arginase
concepts.definition: A ureahydrolase that catalyzes the hydrolysis of arginine or canavanine to yield L-ornithine (ORNITHINE) and urea. Deficiency of this enzyme causes HYPERARGININEMIA. EC 3.5.3.1.

concepts.label: Argininosuccinate Lyase
concepts.title: Argininosuccinate Lyase
concepts.definition: An enzyme of the urea cycle which splits argininosuccinate to fumarate plus arginine. Its absence leads to the metabolic disease ARGININOSUCCINIC ACIDURIA in man. EC 4.3.2.1.

concepts.label: Argininosuccinate Synthase
concepts.title: Argininosuccinate Synthase
concepts.definition: An enzyme of the urea cycle that catalyzes the formation of argininosuccinic acid from citrulline and aspartic acid in the presence of ATP. Absence or deficiency of this enzyme causes the metabolic disease CITRULLINEMIA in humans. EC 6.3.4.5.

concepts.label: Arnold-Chiari Malformation
concepts.title: Arnold-Chiari Malformation
concepts.definition: A group of congenital malformations involving the brainstem, cerebellum, upper spinal cord, and surrounding bony structures. Type II is the most common, and features compression of the medulla and cerebellar tonsils into the upper cervical spinal canal and an associated MENINGOMYELOCELE. Type I features similar, but less severe malformations and is without an associated meningomyelocele. Type III has the features of type II with an additional herniation of the entire cerebellum through the bony defect involving the foramen magnum, forming an ENCEPHALOCELE. Type IV is a form a cerebellar hypoplasia. Clinical manifestations of types I-III include TORTICOLLIS; opisthotonus; HEADACHE; VERTIGO; VOCAL CORD PARALYSIS; APNEA; NYSTAGMUS, CONGENITAL; swallowing difficulties; and ATAXIA. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p261; Davis, Textbook of Neuropathology, 2nd ed, pp236-46)

concepts.label: Arousal
concepts.title: Arousal
concepts.definition: Cortical vigilance or readiness of tone, presumed to be in response to sensory stimulation via the reticular activating system.

concepts.label: Art
concepts.title: Art
concepts.definition: Processes and results of aesthetic expression.

concepts.label: Art Therapy
concepts.title: Art Therapy
concepts.definition: The use of art as an adjunctive therapy in the treatment of neurological, mental, or behavioral disorders.

concepts.label: Arterial Occlusive Diseases
concepts.title: Arterial Occlusive Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes which result in the partial or complete obstruction of ARTERIES. They are characterized by greatly reduced or absence of blood flow through these vessels. They are also known as arterial insufficiency.

concepts.label: Arteriosclerosis
concepts.title: Arteriosclerosis
concepts.definition: Thickening and loss of elasticity of the walls of ARTERIES of all sizes. There are many forms classified by the types of lesions and arteries involved, such as ATHEROSCLEROSIS with fatty lesions in the ARTERIAL INTIMA of medium and large muscular arteries.

concepts.label: Arteriovenous Fistula
concepts.title: Arteriovenous Fistula
concepts.definition: An abnormal direct communication between an artery and a vein without passing through the CAPILLARIES. An A-V fistula usually leads to the formation of a dilated sac-like connection, arteriovenous aneurysm. The locations and size of the shunts determine the degree of effects on the cardiovascular functions such as BLOOD PRESSURE and HEART RATE.

concepts.label: Arteriovenous Malformations
concepts.title: Arteriovenous Malformations
concepts.definition: Abnormal formation of blood vessels that shunt arterial blood directly into veins without passing through the CAPILLARIES. They usually are crooked, dilated, and with thick vessel walls. A common type is the congenital arteriovenous fistula. The lack of blood flow and oxygen in the capillaries can lead to tissue damage in the affected areas.

concepts.label: Arteritis
concepts.title: Arteritis
concepts.definition: INFLAMMATION of any ARTERIES.

concepts.label: Arthroplasty
concepts.title: Arthroplasty
concepts.definition: Surgical reconstruction of a joint to relieve pain or restore motion.

concepts.label: Articulation Disorders
concepts.title: Articulation Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders of the quality of speech characterized by the substitution, omission, distortion, and addition of phonemes.

concepts.label: Artificial Intelligence
concepts.title: Artificial Intelligence
concepts.definition: Theory and development of COMPUTER SYSTEMS which perform tasks that normally require human intelligence. Such tasks may include speech recognition, LEARNING; VISUAL PERCEPTION; MATHEMATICAL COMPUTING; reasoning, PROBLEM SOLVING, DECISION-MAKING, and translation of language.

concepts.label: Arylsulfatases
concepts.title: Arylsulfatases
concepts.definition: Enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of a phenol sulfate to yield a phenol and sulfate. Arylsulfatase A, B, and C have been separated. A deficiency of arylsulfatases is one of the causes of metachromatic leukodystrophy (LEUKODYSTROPHY, METACHROMATIC). EC 3.1.6.1.

concepts.label: Aspergillosis
concepts.title: Aspergillosis
concepts.definition: Infections with fungi of the genus ASPERGILLUS.

concepts.label: Aspirations, Psychological
concepts.title: Aspirations, Psychological
concepts.definition: Strong desires to accomplish something. This usually pertains to greater values or high ideals.

concepts.label: Assertiveness
concepts.title: Assertiveness
concepts.definition: Strongly insistent, self-assured, and demanding behavior.

concepts.label: Association
concepts.title: Association
concepts.definition: A functional relationship between psychological phenomena of such nature that the presence of one tends to evoke the other; also, the process by which such a relationship is established.

concepts.label: Association Learning
concepts.title: Association Learning
concepts.definition: The principle that items experienced together enter into a connection, so that one tends to reinstate the other.

concepts.label: Asthenia
concepts.title: Asthenia
concepts.definition: Clinical sign or symptom manifested as debility, or lack or loss of strength and energy.

concepts.label: Astrocytes
concepts.title: Astrocytes
concepts.definition: A class of large neuroglial (macroglial) cells in the central nervous system - the largest and most numerous neuroglial cells in the brain and spinal cord. Astrocytes (from star cells) are irregularly shaped with many long processes, including those with end feet which form the glial (limiting) membrane and directly and indirectly contribute to the BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER. They regulate the extracellular ionic and chemical environment, and reactive astrocytes (along with MICROGLIA) respond to injury.

concepts.label: Ataxia
concepts.title: Ataxia
concepts.definition: Impairment of the ability to perform smoothly coordinated voluntary movements. This condition may affect the limbs, trunk, eyes, pharynx, larynx, and other structures. Ataxia may result from impaired sensory or motor function. Sensory ataxia may result from posterior column injury or PERIPHERAL NERVE DISEASES. Motor ataxia may be associated with CEREBELLAR DISEASES; CEREBRAL CORTEX diseases; THALAMIC DISEASES; BASAL GANGLIA DISEASES; injury to the RED NUCLEUS; and other conditions.

concepts.label: Ataxia Telangiectasia
concepts.title: Ataxia Telangiectasia
concepts.definition: An autosomal recessive inherited disorder characterized by choreoathetosis beginning in childhood, progressive CEREBELLAR ATAXIA; TELANGIECTASIS of CONJUNCTIVA and SKIN; DYSARTHRIA; B- and T-cell immunodeficiency, and RADIOSENSITIVITY to IONIZING RADIATION. Affected individuals are prone to recurrent sinobronchopulmonary infections, lymphoreticular neoplasms, and other malignancies. Serum ALPHA-FETOPROTEINS are usually elevated. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p688) The gene for this disorder (ATM) encodes a cell cycle checkpoint protein kinase and has been mapped to chromosome 11 (11q22-q23).

concepts.label: Athetosis
concepts.title: Athetosis
concepts.definition: A dyskinesia characterized by an inability to maintain the fingers, toes, tongue, or other body parts in a stable position, resulting in continuous slow, sinusoidal, and flowing involuntary movements. This condition is frequently accompanied by CHOREA, where it is referred to as choreoathetosis. Athetosis may occur as a manifestation of BASAL GANGLIA DISEASES or DRUG TOXICITY. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p76)

concepts.label: Atrophy
concepts.title: Atrophy
concepts.definition: Decrease in the size of a cell, tissue, organ, or multiple organs, associated with a variety of pathological conditions such as abnormal cellular changes, ischemia, malnutrition, or hormonal changes.

concepts.label: Attention
concepts.title: Attention
concepts.definition: Focusing on certain aspects of current experience to the exclusion of others. It is the act of heeding or taking notice or concentrating.

concepts.label: Attention Deficit Disorder with Hyperactivity
concepts.title: Attention Deficit Disorder with Hyperactivity
concepts.definition: A behavior disorder originating in childhood in which the essential features are signs of developmentally inappropriate inattention, impulsivity, and hyperactivity. Although most individuals have symptoms of both inattention and hyperactivity-impulsivity, one or the other pattern may be predominant. The disorder is more frequent in males than females. Onset is in childhood. Symptoms often attenuate during late   adolescence although a minority experience the full complement of symptoms into mid-adulthood. (From DSM-V)

concepts.label: Attitude
concepts.title: Attitude
concepts.definition: An enduring, learned predisposition to behave in a consistent way toward a given class of objects, or a persistent mental and/or neural state of readiness to react to a certain class of objects, not as they are but as they are conceived to be.

concepts.label: Attitude of Health Personnel
concepts.title: Attitude of Health Personnel
concepts.definition: Attitudes of personnel toward their patients, other professionals, toward the medical care system, etc.

concepts.label: Attitude to Computers
concepts.title: Attitude to Computers
concepts.definition: The attitude and behavior associated with an individual using the computer.

concepts.label: Attitude to Death
concepts.title: Attitude to Death
concepts.definition: Conceptual response of the person to the various aspects of death, which are based on individual psychosocial and cultural experience.

concepts.label: Attitude to Health
concepts.title: Attitude to Health
concepts.definition: Public attitudes toward health, disease, and the medical care system.

concepts.label: Audiovisual Aids
concepts.title: Audiovisual Aids
concepts.definition: Auditory and visual instructional materials.

concepts.label: Audiometry
concepts.title: Audiometry
concepts.definition: The testing of the acuity of the sense of hearing to determine the thresholds of the lowest intensity levels at which an individual can hear a set of tones. The frequencies between 125 and 8000 Hz are used to test air conduction thresholds and the frequencies between 250 and 4000 Hz are used to test bone conduction thresholds.

concepts.label: Audiometry, Evoked Response
concepts.title: Audiometry, Evoked Response
concepts.definition: A form of electrophysiologic audiometry in which an analog computer is included in the circuit to average out ongoing or spontaneous brain wave activity. A characteristic pattern of response to a sound stimulus may then become evident. Evoked response audiometry is known also as electric response audiometry.

concepts.label: Auditory Cortex
concepts.title: Auditory Cortex
concepts.definition: The region of the cerebral cortex that receives the auditory radiation from the MEDIAL GENICULATE BODY.

concepts.label: Auditory Diseases, Central
concepts.title: Auditory Diseases, Central
concepts.definition: Disorders of hearing or auditory perception due to pathological processes of the AUDITORY PATHWAYS in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. These include CENTRAL HEARING LOSS and AUDITORY PERCEPTUAL DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Auditory Fatigue
concepts.title: Auditory Fatigue
concepts.definition: Loss of sensitivity to sounds as a result of auditory stimulation, manifesting as a temporary shift in auditory threshold. The temporary threshold shift, TTS, is expressed in decibels.

concepts.label: Auditory Pathways
concepts.title: Auditory Pathways
concepts.definition: NEURAL PATHWAYS and connections within the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM, beginning at the hair cells of the ORGAN OF CORTI, continuing along the eighth cranial nerve, and terminating at the AUDITORY CORTEX.

concepts.label: Auditory Perception
concepts.title: Auditory Perception
concepts.definition: The process whereby auditory stimuli are selected, organized, and interpreted by the organism.

concepts.label: Auditory Perceptual Disorders
concepts.title: Auditory Perceptual Disorders
concepts.definition: Acquired or developmental cognitive disorders of AUDITORY PERCEPTION characterized by a reduced ability to perceive information contained in auditory stimuli despite intact auditory pathways. Affected individuals have difficulty with speech perception, sound localization, and comprehending the meaning of inflections of speech.

concepts.label: Auditory Threshold
concepts.title: Auditory Threshold
concepts.definition: The audibility limit of discriminating sound intensity and pitch.

concepts.label: Authoritarianism
concepts.title: Authoritarianism
concepts.definition: The personality pattern or syndrome consisting of behavioral and attitudinal characteristics reflecting a preoccupation with the factors of power and authority in interpersonal relationships.

concepts.label: Autistic Disorder
concepts.title: Autistic Disorder
concepts.definition: A disorder beginning in childhood. It is marked by the presence of markedly abnormal or impaired development in social interaction and communication and a markedly restricted repertoire of activity and interest. Manifestations of the disorder vary greatly depending on the developmental level and chronological age of the individual. (DSM-V)

concepts.label: Autogenic Training
concepts.title: Autogenic Training
concepts.definition: Technique based on muscle relaxation during self-hypnotic exercises. It is used in conjunction with psychotherapy.

concepts.label: Autoimmune Diseases
concepts.title: Autoimmune Diseases
concepts.definition: Disorders that are characterized by the production of antibodies that react with host tissues or immune effector cells that are autoreactive to endogenous peptides.

concepts.label: Automatism
concepts.title: Automatism
concepts.definition: Automatic, mechanical, and apparently undirected behavior which is outside of conscious control.

concepts.label: Automobile Driving
concepts.title: Automobile Driving
concepts.definition: The effect of environmental or physiological factors on the driver and driving ability. Included are driving fatigue, and the effect of drugs, disease, and physical disabilities on driving.

concepts.label: Autonomic Agents
concepts.title: Autonomic Agents
concepts.definition: Agents affecting the function of, or mimicking the actions of, the autonomic nervous system and thereby having an effect on such processes as respiration, circulation, digestion, body temperature regulation, certain endocrine gland secretions, etc.

concepts.label: Autonomic Fibers, Postganglionic
concepts.title: Autonomic Fibers, Postganglionic
concepts.definition: Nerve fibers which project from cell bodies of AUTONOMIC GANGLIA to SYNAPSES on target organs.

concepts.label: Autonomic Fibers, Preganglionic
concepts.title: Autonomic Fibers, Preganglionic
concepts.definition: NERVE FIBERS which project from the central nervous system to AUTONOMIC GANGLIA. In the sympathetic division most preganglionic fibers originate with neurons in the intermediolateral column of the SPINAL CORD, exit via ventral roots from upper thoracic through lower lumbar segments, and project to the paravertebral ganglia; there they either terminate in SYNAPSES or continue through the SPLANCHNIC NERVES to the prevertebral ganglia. In the parasympathetic division the fibers originate in neurons of the BRAIN STEM and sacral spinal cord. In both divisions the principal transmitter is ACETYLCHOLINE but peptide cotransmitters may also be released.

concepts.label: Autonomic Nervous System
concepts.title: Autonomic Nervous System
concepts.definition: The ENTERIC NERVOUS SYSTEM; PARASYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM; and SYMPATHETIC NERVOUS SYSTEM taken together.
