concepts.title: Cognition
concepts.definition: Intellectual or mental process whereby an organism obtains knowledge.

concepts.label: Cognition Disorders
concepts.title: Cognition Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders characterized by disturbances in mental processes related to learning, thinking, reasoning, and judgment.

concepts.label: Cognitive Dissonance
concepts.title: Cognitive Dissonance
concepts.definition: Motivational state produced by inconsistencies between simultaneously held cognitions or between a cognition and behavior; e.g., smoking enjoyment and believing smoking is harmful are dissonant.

concepts.label: Coitus
concepts.title: Coitus
concepts.definition: The sexual union of a male and a female, a term used for human only.

concepts.label: Coitus Interruptus
concepts.title: Coitus Interruptus
concepts.definition: A contraceptive method whereby coitus is purposely interrupted in order to prevent EJACULATION of SEMEN into the VAGINA.

concepts.label: Colic
concepts.title: Colic
concepts.definition: A clinical syndrome with intermittent abdominal pain characterized by sudden onset and cessation that is commonly seen in infants. It is usually associated with obstruction of the INTESTINES; of the CYSTIC DUCT; or of the URINARY TRACT.

concepts.label: Collagen
concepts.title: Collagen
concepts.definition: A polypeptide substance comprising about one third of the total protein in mammalian organisms. It is the main constituent of SKIN; CONNECTIVE TISSUE; and the organic substance of bones (BONE AND BONES) and teeth (TOOTH).

concepts.label: Collective Bargaining
concepts.title: Collective Bargaining
concepts.definition: The process of negotiation between representatives of an employee organization, association or union, and representatives of the employer.

concepts.label: Coloboma
concepts.title: Coloboma
concepts.definition: Congenital anomaly in which some of the structures of the eye are absent due to incomplete fusion of the fetal intraocular fissure during gestation.
aliases: Coloboma Of Iris, Choroid, And Retina

concepts.label: Color Vision Defects
concepts.title: Color Vision Defects
concepts.definition: Defects of color vision are mainly hereditary traits but can be secondary to acquired or developmental abnormalities in the CONES (RETINA). Severity of hereditary defects of color vision depends on the degree of mutation of the ROD OPSINS genes (on X CHROMOSOME and CHROMOSOME 3) that code the photopigments for red, green and blue.

concepts.label: Color Perception
concepts.title: Color Perception
concepts.definition: Mental processing of chromatic signals (COLOR VISION) from the eye by the VISUAL CORTEX where they are converted into symbolic representations. Color perception involves numerous neurons, and is influenced not only by the distribution of wavelengths from the viewed object, but also by its background color and brightness contrast at its boundary.

concepts.label: Coma
concepts.title: Coma
concepts.definition: A profound state of unconsciousness associated with depressed cerebral activity from which the individual cannot be aroused. Coma generally occurs when there is dysfunction or injury involving both cerebral hemispheres or the brain stem RETICULAR FORMATION.

concepts.label: Combat Disorders
concepts.title: Combat Disorders
concepts.definition: Neurotic reactions to unusual, severe, or overwhelming military stress.

concepts.label: Commerce
concepts.title: Commerce
concepts.definition: The interchange of goods or commodities, especially on a large scale, between different countries or between populations within the same country. It includes trade (the buying, selling, or exchanging of commodities, whether wholesale or retail) and business (the purchase and sale of goods to make a profit). (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed, p411, p2005 & p283)

concepts.label: Commitment of Persons with Psychiatric Disorders
concepts.title: Commitment of Persons with Psychiatric Disorders
concepts.definition: Legal process required for the institutionalization of a patient with severe psychiatric problems.
aliases: Commitment of Persons with Mental Illness

concepts.label: Communicable Diseases
concepts.title: Communicable Diseases
concepts.definition: An illness caused by an infectious agent or its toxins that occurs through the direct or indirect transmission of the infectious agent or its products from an infected individual or via an animal, vector or the inanimate environment to a susceptible animal or human host.

concepts.label: Communication
concepts.title: Communication
concepts.definition: The exchange or transmission of ideas, attitudes, or beliefs between individuals or groups.

concepts.label: Communications Media
concepts.title: Communications Media
concepts.definition: The means of interchanging or transmitting and receiving information. Historically the media were written: books, journals, newspapers, and other publications; in the modern age the media include, in addition, radio, television, computers, and information networks.

concepts.label: Communication Disorders
concepts.title: Communication Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders of verbal and nonverbal communication caused by receptive or expressive LANGUAGE DISORDERS, cognitive dysfunction (e.g., MENTAL RETARDATION), psychiatric conditions, and HEARING DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Community Health Services
concepts.title: Community Health Services
concepts.definition: Diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive health services provided for individuals in the community.

concepts.label: Community Mental Health Services
concepts.title: Community Mental Health Services
concepts.definition: Diagnostic, therapeutic and preventive mental health services provided for individuals in the community.

concepts.label: Community Psychiatry
concepts.title: Community Psychiatry
concepts.definition: Branch of psychiatry concerned with the provision and delivery of a coordinated program of mental health care to a specified population. The foci included in this concept are: all social, psychological and physical factors related to etiology, prevention, and maintaining positive mental health in the community.

concepts.label: Competitive Behavior
concepts.title: Competitive Behavior
concepts.definition: The direct struggle between individuals for environmental necessities or for a common goal.

concepts.label: Comprehensive Health Care
concepts.title: Comprehensive Health Care
concepts.definition: Providing for the full range of personal health services for diagnosis, treatment, follow-up and rehabilitation of patients.

concepts.label: Compulsive Behavior
concepts.title: Compulsive Behavior
concepts.definition: The behavior of performing an act persistently and repetitively without it leading to reward or pleasure. The act is usually a small, circumscribed behavior, almost ritualistic, yet not pathologically disturbing. Examples of compulsive behavior include twirling of hair, checking something constantly, not wanting pennies in change, straightening tilted pictures, etc.

concepts.label: Compulsive Personality Disorder
concepts.title: Compulsive Personality Disorder
concepts.definition: Disorder characterized by an emotionally constricted manner that is unduly conventional, serious, formal, and stingy, by preoccupation with trivial details, rules, order, organization, schedules, and lists, by stubborn insistence on having things one's own way without regard for the effects on others, by poor interpersonal relationships, and by indecisiveness due to fear of making mistakes.

concepts.label: Computer Simulation
concepts.title: Computer Simulation
concepts.definition: Computer-based representation of physical systems and phenomena such as chemical processes.

concepts.label: Computing Methodologies
concepts.title: Computing Methodologies
concepts.definition: Computer-assisted analysis and processing of problems in a particular area.

concepts.label: Concept Formation
concepts.title: Concept Formation
concepts.definition: A cognitive process involving the formation of ideas generalized from the knowledge of qualities, aspects, and relations of objects.

concepts.label: Conditioning, Psychological
concepts.title: Conditioning, Psychological
concepts.definition: Simple form of learning involving the formation, strengthening, or weakening of an association between a stimulus and a response.

concepts.label: Conditioning, Classical
concepts.title: Conditioning, Classical
concepts.definition: Learning that takes place when a conditioned stimulus is paired with an unconditioned stimulus.

concepts.label: Conditioning, Eyelid
concepts.title: Conditioning, Eyelid
concepts.definition: Reflex closure of the eyelid occurring as a result of classical conditioning.

concepts.label: Conditioning, Operant
concepts.title: Conditioning, Operant
concepts.definition: Learning situations in which the sequence responses of the subject are instrumental in producing reinforcement. When the correct response occurs, which involves the selection from among a repertoire of responses, the subject is immediately reinforced.

concepts.label: Confidentiality
concepts.title: Confidentiality
concepts.definition: The privacy of information and its protection against unauthorized disclosure.

concepts.label: Conflict, Psychological
concepts.title: Conflict, Psychological
concepts.definition: The internal individual struggle resulting from incompatible or opposing needs, drives, or external and internal demands. In group interactions, competitive or opposing action of incompatibles: antagonistic state or action (as of divergent ideas, interests, or persons). (from Merriam-Webster's Collegiate Dictionary, 10th ed)

concepts.label: Confusion
concepts.title: Confusion
concepts.definition: A mental state characterized by bewilderment, emotional disturbance, lack of clear thinking, and perceptual disorientation.

concepts.label: Congresses as Topic
concepts.title: Congresses as Topic
concepts.definition: Works about conferences, conventions or formal meetings usually attended by delegates representing a special field of interest.

concepts.label: Connective Tissue
concepts.title: Connective Tissue
concepts.definition: Tissue that supports and binds other tissues. It consists of CONNECTIVE TISSUE CELLS embedded in a large amount of EXTRACELLULAR MATRIX.

concepts.label: Connective Tissue Cells
concepts.title: Connective Tissue Cells
concepts.definition: A group of cells that includes FIBROBLASTS, cartilage cells, ADIPOCYTES, smooth muscle cells, and bone cells.

concepts.label: Connective Tissue Diseases
concepts.title: Connective Tissue Diseases
concepts.definition: A heterogeneous group of disorders, some hereditary, others acquired, characterized by abnormal structure or function of one or more of the elements of connective tissue, i.e., collagen, elastin, or the mucopolysaccharides.

concepts.label: Consanguinity
concepts.title: Consanguinity
concepts.definition: The magnitude of INBREEDING in humans.

concepts.label: Conscience
concepts.title: Conscience
concepts.definition: The cognitive and affective processes which constitute an internalized moral governor over an individual's moral conduct.

concepts.label: Consciousness
concepts.title: Consciousness
concepts.definition: Sense of awareness of self and of the environment.

concepts.label: Consciousness Disorders
concepts.title: Consciousness Disorders
concepts.definition: Organic mental disorders in which there is impairment of the ability to maintain awareness of self and environment and to respond to environmental stimuli. Dysfunction of the cerebral hemispheres or brain stem RETICULAR FORMATION may result in this condition.

concepts.label: Consensus Statements as Topic
concepts.title: Consensus Statements as Topic
concepts.definition: Works that are about the concept of consensus statements or consensus development conferences, such as their general design or a means of scientific communication.

concepts.label: Constipation
concepts.title: Constipation
concepts.definition: Infrequent or difficult evacuation of FECES. These symptoms are associated with a variety of causes, including low DIETARY FIBER intake, emotional or nervous disturbances, systemic and structural disorders, drug-induced aggravation, and infections.

concepts.label: Consumer Organizations
concepts.title: Consumer Organizations
concepts.definition: Organized groups of users of goods and services.

concepts.label: Community Participation
concepts.title: Community Participation
concepts.definition: Involvement of members of the community in the affairs of that community.

concepts.label: Consumer Behavior
concepts.title: Consumer Behavior
concepts.definition: Behavior associated with the procurement of goods, services, or experiences.

concepts.label: Consummatory Behavior
concepts.title: Consummatory Behavior
concepts.definition: An act which constitutes the termination of a given instinctive behavior pattern or sequence.

concepts.label: Contingent Negative Variation
concepts.title: Contingent Negative Variation
concepts.definition: A negative shift of the cortical electrical potentials that increases over time. It is associated with an anticipated response to an expected stimulus and is an electrical event indicative of a state of readiness or expectancy.

concepts.label: Continuity of Patient Care
concepts.title: Continuity of Patient Care
concepts.definition: Health care provided on a continuing basis from the initial contact, following the patient through all phases of medical care.

concepts.label: Contraception
concepts.title: Contraception
concepts.definition: Prevention of CONCEPTION by blocking fertility temporarily, or permanently (STERILIZATION, REPRODUCTIVE). Common means of reversible contraception include NATURAL FAMILY PLANNING METHODS; CONTRACEPTIVE AGENTS; or CONTRACEPTIVE DEVICES.

concepts.label: Contraception Behavior
concepts.title: Contraception Behavior
concepts.definition: Behavior patterns of those practicing CONTRACEPTION.

concepts.label: Contractile Proteins
concepts.title: Contractile Proteins
concepts.definition: Proteins which participate in contractile processes. They include MUSCLE PROTEINS as well as those found in other cells and tissues. In the latter, these proteins participate in localized contractile events in the cytoplasm, in motile activity, and in cell aggregation phenomena.

concepts.label: Contusions
concepts.title: Contusions
concepts.definition: Injuries resulting in hemorrhage, usually manifested in the skin.

concepts.label: Conversion Disorder
concepts.title: Conversion Disorder
concepts.definition: A disorder whose predominant feature is a loss or alteration in physical functioning that suggests a physical disorder but that is actually a direct expression of a psychological conflict or need.

concepts.label: Convulsants
concepts.title: Convulsants
concepts.definition: Substances that act in the brain stem or spinal cord to produce tonic or clonic convulsions, often by removing normal inhibitory tone. They were formerly used to stimulate respiration or as antidotes to barbiturate overdose. They are now most commonly used as experimental tools.

concepts.label: Seizures, Febrile
concepts.title: Seizures, Febrile
concepts.definition: Seizures that occur during a febrile episode. It is a common condition, affecting 2-5% of children aged 3 months to five years. An autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance has been identified in some families. The majority are simple febrile seizures (generally defined as generalized onset, single seizures with a duration of less than 30 minutes). Complex febrile seizures are characterized by focal onset, duration greater than 30 minutes, and/or more than one seizure in a 24 hour period. The likelihood of developing epilepsy (i.e., a nonfebrile seizure disorder) following simple febrile seizures is low. Complex febrile seizures are associated with a moderately increased incidence of epilepsy. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p784)

concepts.label: Convulsive Therapy
concepts.title: Convulsive Therapy
concepts.definition: Convulsions induced in order to treat MENTAL DISORDERS. It is used primarily in the treatment of severe affective disorders and SCHIZOPHRENIA.

concepts.label: Cooperative Behavior
concepts.title: Cooperative Behavior
concepts.definition: The interaction of two or more persons or organizations directed toward a common goal which is mutually beneficial. An act or instance of working or acting together for a common purpose or benefit, i.e., joint action. (From Random House Dictionary Unabridged, 2d ed)

concepts.label: Coprophagia
concepts.title: Coprophagia
concepts.definition: Eating of excrement by animal species.

concepts.label: Copulation
concepts.title: Copulation
concepts.definition: Sexual union of a male and a female in non-human species.

concepts.label: Copying Processes
concepts.title: Copying Processes
concepts.definition: Reproduction of data in a new location or other destination, leaving the source data unchanged, although the physical form of the result may differ from that of the source.

concepts.label: Corneal Diseases
concepts.title: Corneal Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases of the cornea.

concepts.label: Coronary Disease
concepts.title: Coronary Disease
concepts.definition: An imbalance between myocardial functional requirements and the capacity of the CORONARY VESSELS to supply sufficient blood flow. It is a form of MYOCARDIAL ISCHEMIA (insufficient blood supply to the heart muscle) caused by a decreased capacity of the coronary vessels.

concepts.label: Corpora Allata
concepts.title: Corpora Allata
concepts.definition: Paired or fused ganglion-like bodies in the head of insects. The bodies secrete hormones important in the regulation of metamorphosis and the development of some adult tissues.

concepts.label: Tectum Mesencephali
concepts.title: Tectum Mesencephali
concepts.definition: The dorsal portion or roof of the midbrain which is composed of two pairs of bumps, the INFERIOR COLLICULI and the SUPERIOR COLLICULI. These four colliculi are also called the quadrigeminal bodies (TECTUM MESENCEPHALI). They are centers for sensorimotor integration.

concepts.label: Corpus Callosum
concepts.title: Corpus Callosum
concepts.definition: Broad plate of dense myelinated fibers that reciprocally interconnect regions of the cortex in all lobes with corresponding regions of the opposite hemisphere. The corpus callosum is located deep in the longitudinal fissure.

concepts.label: Corpus Striatum
concepts.title: Corpus Striatum
concepts.definition: Striped GRAY MATTER and WHITE MATTER consisting of the NEOSTRIATUM and paleostriatum (GLOBUS PALLIDUS). It is located in front of and lateral to the THALAMUS in each cerebral hemisphere. The gray substance is made up of the CAUDATE NUCLEUS and the lentiform nucleus (the latter consisting of the GLOBUS PALLIDUS and PUTAMEN). The WHITE MATTER is the INTERNAL CAPSULE.

concepts.label: Cortical Synchronization
concepts.title: Cortical Synchronization
concepts.definition: EEG phase synchronization of the cortical brain region (CEREBRAL CORTEX).

concepts.label: Counseling
concepts.title: Counseling
concepts.definition: The giving of advice and assistance to individuals with educational or personal problems.

concepts.label: Countertransference
concepts.title: Countertransference
concepts.definition: Conscious or unconscious emotional reaction of the therapist to the patient which may interfere with treatment. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Courtship
concepts.title: Courtship
concepts.definition: Activities designed to attract the attention or favors of another.

concepts.label: Cranial Nerve Diseases
concepts.title: Cranial Nerve Diseases
concepts.definition: Disorders of one or more of the twelve cranial nerves. With the exception of the optic and olfactory nerves, this includes disorders of the brain stem nuclei from which the cranial nerves originate or terminate.

concepts.label: Cranial Nerve Neoplasms
concepts.title: Cranial Nerve Neoplasms
concepts.definition: Benign and malignant neoplasms that arise from one or more of the twelve cranial nerves.

concepts.label: Cranial Nerves
concepts.title: Cranial Nerves
concepts.definition: Twelve pairs of nerves that carry general afferent, visceral afferent, special afferent, somatic efferent, and autonomic efferent fibers.

concepts.label: Creativity
concepts.title: Creativity
concepts.definition: The ability to generate new ideas or images.

concepts.label: Cri-du-Chat Syndrome
concepts.title: Cri-du-Chat Syndrome
concepts.definition: An infantile syndrome characterized by a cat-like cry, failure to thrive, microcephaly, MENTAL RETARDATION, spastic quadriparesis, micro- and retrognathia, glossoptosis, bilateral epicanthus, hypertelorism, and tiny external genitalia. It is caused by a deletion of the short arm of chromosome 5 (5p-).
aliases: Deletion of Short Arm of Chromosome 5 Syndrome

concepts.label: Crime
concepts.title: Crime
concepts.definition: A violation of the criminal law, i.e., a breach of the conduct code specifically sanctioned by the state, which through its administrative agencies prosecutes offenders and imposes and administers punishments. The concept includes unacceptable actions whether prosecuted or going unpunished.

concepts.label: Criminal Psychology
concepts.title: Criminal Psychology
concepts.definition: The branch of psychology which investigates the psychology of crime with particular reference to the personality factors of the criminal.

concepts.label: Criminology
concepts.title: Criminology
concepts.definition: The study of crime and criminals with special reference to the personality factors and social conditions leading toward, or away from crime.

concepts.label: Crisis Intervention
concepts.title: Crisis Intervention
concepts.definition: Brief therapeutic approach which is ameliorative rather than curative of acute psychiatric emergencies. Used in contexts such as emergency rooms of psychiatric or general hospitals, or in the home or place of crisis occurrence, this treatment approach focuses on interpersonal and intrapsychic factors and environmental modification. (APA Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 7th ed)

concepts.label: Critical Period, Psychological
concepts.title: Critical Period, Psychological
concepts.definition: A specific stage in animal and human development during which certain types of behavior normally are shaped and molded for life.

concepts.label: Crowding
concepts.title: Crowding
concepts.definition: An excessive number of individuals, human or animal, in relation to available space.

concepts.label: Crying
concepts.title: Crying
concepts.definition: To utter an inarticulate, characteristic sound in order to communicate or express a feeling, or desire for attention.

concepts.label: Cryptococcosis
concepts.title: Cryptococcosis
concepts.definition: Fungal infection caused by genus CRYPTOCOCCUS.

concepts.label: Cues
concepts.title: Cues
concepts.definition: Signals for an action; that specific portion of a perceptual field or pattern of stimuli to which a subject has learned to respond.

concepts.label: Culture
concepts.title: Culture
concepts.definition: A collective expression for all behavior patterns acquired and socially transmitted through symbols. Culture includes customs, traditions, and language.

concepts.label: Curriculum
concepts.title: Curriculum
concepts.definition: A course of study offered by an educational institution.

concepts.label: Cushing Syndrome
concepts.title: Cushing Syndrome
concepts.definition: A condition caused by prolonged exposure to excess levels of cortisol (HYDROCORTISONE) or other GLUCOCORTICOIDS from endogenous or exogenous sources. It is characterized by upper body OBESITY; OSTEOPOROSIS; HYPERTENSION; DIABETES MELLITUS; HIRSUTISM; AMENORRHEA; and excess body fluid. Endogenous Cushing syndrome or spontaneous hypercortisolism is divided into two groups, those due to an excess of ADRENOCORTICOTROPIN and those that are ACTH-independent.

concepts.label: Cyclothymic Disorder
concepts.title: Cyclothymic Disorder
concepts.definition: An affective disorder characterized by periods of depression and hypomania. These may be separated by periods of normal mood.

concepts.label: Cystathionine beta-Synthase
concepts.title: Cystathionine beta-Synthase
concepts.definition: A multifunctional pyridoxal phosphate enzyme. In the second stage of cysteine biosynthesis it catalyzes the reaction of homocysteine with serine to form cystathionine with the elimination of water. Deficiency of this enzyme leads to HYPERHOMOCYSTEINEMIA and HOMOCYSTINURIA. EC 4.2.1.22.

concepts.label: Cysticercosis
concepts.title: Cysticercosis
concepts.definition: Infection with CYSTICERCUS, the larval form of the various tapeworms of the genus Taenia (usually T. solium in man). In humans they penetrate the intestinal wall and invade subcutaneous tissue, brain, eye, muscle, heart, liver, lung, and peritoneum. Brain involvement results in NEUROCYSTICERCOSIS.

concepts.label: Cysts
concepts.title: Cysts
concepts.definition: Any fluid-filled closed cavity or sac that is lined by an EPITHELIUM. Cysts can be of normal, abnormal, non-neoplastic, or neoplastic tissues.

concepts.label: Cytoplasm
concepts.title: Cytoplasm
concepts.definition: The part of a cell that contains the CYTOSOL and small structures excluding the CELL NUCLEUS; MITOCHONDRIA; and large VACUOLES. (Glick, Glossary of Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 1990)

concepts.label: Cytoplasmic Granules
concepts.title: Cytoplasmic Granules
concepts.definition: Condensed areas of cellular material that may be bounded by a membrane.

concepts.label: Cytoplasmic Streaming
concepts.title: Cytoplasmic Streaming
concepts.definition: The movement of CYTOPLASM within a CELL. It serves as an internal transport system for moving essential substances throughout the cell, and in single-celled organisms, such as the AMOEBA, it is responsible for the movement (CELL MOVEMENT) of the entire cell.

concepts.label: Cytoskeletal Proteins
concepts.title: Cytoskeletal Proteins
concepts.definition: Major constituent of the cytoskeleton found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells. They form a flexible framework for the cell, provide attachment points for organelles and formed bodies, and make communication between parts of the cell possible.

concepts.label: Cytoskeleton
concepts.title: Cytoskeleton
concepts.definition: The network of filaments, tubules, and interconnecting filamentous bridges which give shape, structure, and organization to the cytoplasm.

concepts.label: Dairy Products
concepts.title: Dairy Products
concepts.definition: Raw and processed or manufactured milk and milk-derived products. These are usually from cows (bovine) but are also from goats, sheep, reindeer, and water buffalo.

concepts.label: Dance Therapy
concepts.title: Dance Therapy
concepts.definition: The use of dancing for therapeutic purposes.

concepts.label: Dandy-Walker Syndrome
concepts.title: Dandy-Walker Syndrome
concepts.definition: A congenital abnormality of the central nervous system marked by failure of the midline structures of the cerebellum to develop, dilation of the fourth ventricle, and upward displacement of the transverse sinuses, tentorium, and torcula. Clinical features include occipital bossing, progressive head enlargement, bulging of anterior fontanelle, papilledema, ataxia, gait disturbances, nystagmus, and intellectual compromise. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, pp294-5)

concepts.label: Dangerous Behavior
concepts.title: Dangerous Behavior
concepts.definition: Actions which have a high risk of being harmful or injurious to oneself or others.

concepts.label: Data Collection
concepts.title: Data Collection
concepts.definition: Systematic gathering of data for a particular purpose from various sources, including questionnaires, interviews, observation, existing records, and electronic devices. The process is usually preliminary to statistical analysis of the data.

concepts.label: Data Display
concepts.title: Data Display
concepts.definition: The visual representation of data via a manufactured system.

concepts.label: Data Interpretation, Statistical
concepts.title: Data Interpretation, Statistical
concepts.definition: Application of statistical procedures to analyze specific observed or assumed facts from a particular study.

concepts.label: De Lange Syndrome
concepts.title: De Lange Syndrome
concepts.definition: A syndrome characterized by growth retardation, severe MENTAL RETARDATION, short stature, a low-pitched growling cry, brachycephaly, low-set ears, webbed neck, carp mouth, depressed nasal bridge, bushy eyebrows meeting at the midline, hirsutism, and malformations of the hands. The condition may occur sporadically or be associated with an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance or duplication of the long arm of chromosome 3. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p231)

concepts.label: Deafness
concepts.title: Deafness
concepts.definition: A general term for the complete loss of the ability to hear from both ears.

concepts.label: Hearing Loss, Sudden
concepts.title: Hearing Loss, Sudden
concepts.definition: Sensorineural hearing loss which develops suddenly over a period of hours or a few days. It varies in severity from mild to total deafness. Sudden deafness can be due to head trauma, vascular diseases, infections, or can appear without obvious cause or warning.

concepts.label: Death
concepts.title: Death
concepts.definition: Irreversible cessation of all bodily functions, manifested by absence of spontaneous breathing and total loss of cardiovascular and cerebral functions.

concepts.label: Death, Sudden
concepts.title: Death, Sudden
concepts.definition: The abrupt cessation of all vital bodily functions, manifested by the permanent loss of total cerebral, respiratory, and cardiovascular functions.

concepts.label: Decerebrate State
concepts.title: Decerebrate State
concepts.definition: A condition characterized by abnormal posturing of the limbs that is associated with injury to the brainstem. This may occur as a clinical manifestation or induced experimentally in animals. The extensor reflexes are exaggerated leading to rigid extension of the limbs accompanied by hyperreflexia and opisthotonus. This condition is usually caused by lesions which occur in the region of the brainstem that lies between the red nuclei and the vestibular nuclei. In contrast, decorticate rigidity is characterized by flexion of the elbows and wrists with extension of the legs and feet. The causative lesion for this condition is located above the red nuclei and usually consists of diffuse cerebral damage. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p358)

concepts.label: Decision Making
concepts.title: Decision Making
concepts.definition: The process of making a selective intellectual judgment when presented with several complex alternatives consisting of several variables, and usually defining a course of action or an idea.

concepts.label: Decision Support Techniques
concepts.title: Decision Support Techniques
concepts.definition: Mathematical or statistical procedures used as aids in making a decision. They are frequently used in medical decision-making.

concepts.label: Decompression Sickness
concepts.title: Decompression Sickness
concepts.definition: A condition occurring as a result of exposure to a rapid fall in ambient pressure. Gases, nitrogen in particular, come out of solution and form bubbles in body fluid and blood. These gas bubbles accumulate in joint spaces and the peripheral circulation impairing tissue oxygenation causing disorientation, severe pain, and potentially death.

concepts.label: Defense Mechanisms
concepts.title: Defense Mechanisms
concepts.definition: Unconscious process used by an individual or a group of individuals in order to cope with impulses, feelings or ideas which are not acceptable at their conscious level; various types include reaction formation, projection and self reversal.

concepts.label: Deficiency Diseases
concepts.title: Deficiency Diseases
concepts.definition: A condition produced by dietary or metabolic deficiency. The term includes all diseases caused by an insufficient supply of essential nutrients, i.e., protein (or amino acids), vitamins, and minerals. It also includes an inadequacy of calories. (From Dorland, 27th ed; Stedman, 25th ed)

concepts.label: Vestibular Nucleus, Lateral
concepts.title: Vestibular Nucleus, Lateral
concepts.definition: Vestibular nucleus lying immediately superior to the inferior vestibular nucleus and composed of large multipolar nerve cells. Its upper end becomes continuous with the superior vestibular nucleus.

concepts.label: Deja Vu
concepts.title: Deja Vu
concepts.definition: A subjective feeling that an experience which is occurring for the first time has been experienced before.

concepts.label: Delirium
concepts.title: Delirium
concepts.definition: A disorder characterized by CONFUSION; inattentiveness; disorientation; ILLUSIONS; HALLUCINATIONS; agitation; and in some instances autonomic nervous system overactivity. It may result from toxic/metabolic conditions or structural brain lesions. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp411-2)

concepts.label: Delivery of Health Care
concepts.title: Delivery of Health Care
concepts.definition: The concept concerned with all aspects of providing and distributing health services to a patient population.

concepts.label: Delta Rhythm
concepts.title: Delta Rhythm
concepts.definition: Brain waves seen on EEG characterized by a high amplitude and a frequency of 4 Hz and below. They are considered the deep sleep waves observed during sleep in dreamless states, infancy, and in some brain disorders.

concepts.label: Delusions
concepts.title: Delusions
concepts.definition: A false belief regarding the self or persons or objects outside the self that persists despite the facts, and is not considered tenable by one's associates.

concepts.label: Dementia
concepts.title: Dementia
concepts.definition: An acquired organic mental disorder with loss of intellectual abilities of sufficient severity to interfere with social or occupational functioning. The dysfunction is multifaceted and involves memory, behavior, personality, judgment, attention, spatial relations, language, abstract thought, and other executive functions. The intellectual decline is usually progressive, and initially spares the level of consciousness.

concepts.label: Demography
concepts.title: Demography
concepts.definition: Statistical interpretation and description of a population with reference to distribution, composition, or structure.

concepts.label: Demyelinating Diseases
concepts.title: Demyelinating Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases characterized by loss or dysfunction of myelin in the central or peripheral nervous system.

concepts.label: Dendrites
concepts.title: Dendrites
concepts.definition: Extensions of the nerve cell body. They are short and branched and receive stimuli from other NEURONS.

concepts.label: Denervation
concepts.title: Denervation
concepts.definition: The resection or removal of the nerve to an organ or part.

concepts.label: Denial, Psychological
concepts.title: Denial, Psychological
concepts.definition: Refusal to admit the truth or reality of a situation or experience.

concepts.label: Densitometry
concepts.title: Densitometry
concepts.definition: The measurement of the density of a material by measuring the amount of light or radiation passing through (or absorbed by) the material.

concepts.label: Dental Implantation
concepts.title: Dental Implantation
concepts.definition: The grafting or inserting of a prosthetic device of alloplastic material into the oral tissue beneath the mucosal or periosteal layer or within the bone. Its purpose is to provide support and retention to a partial or complete denture.

concepts.label: Dental Implantation, Endosseous
concepts.title: Dental Implantation, Endosseous
concepts.definition: Insertion of an implant into the bone of the mandible or maxilla. The implant has an exposed head which protrudes through the mucosa and is a prosthodontic abutment.

concepts.label: Dental Occlusion
concepts.title: Dental Occlusion
concepts.definition: The relationship of all the components of the masticatory system in normal function. It has special reference to the position and contact of the maxillary and mandibular teeth for the highest efficiency during the excursive movements of the jaw that are essential for mastication. (From Jablonski, Dictionary of Dentistry, 1992, p556, p472)

concepts.label: Dental Occlusion, Centric
concepts.title: Dental Occlusion, Centric
concepts.definition: Contact between opposing teeth during a person's habitual bite.

concepts.label: Dentist-Patient Relations
concepts.title: Dentist-Patient Relations
concepts.definition: The psychological relations between the dentist and patient.

concepts.label: Dentistry
concepts.title: Dentistry
concepts.definition: The profession concerned with the teeth, oral cavity, and associated structures, and the diagnosis and treatment of their diseases including prevention and the restoration of defective and missing tissue.

concepts.label: Dependency, Psychological
concepts.title: Dependency, Psychological
concepts.definition: The tendency of an individual or individuals to rely on others for advice, guidance, or support.

concepts.label: Dependent Personality Disorder
concepts.title: Dependent Personality Disorder
concepts.definition: A personality disorder characterized by a pervasive and excessive need to be taken care of that leads to submissive and clinging behavior and fears of separation, beginning by early adulthood and present in a variety of contexts. (From DSM-IV, 1994)

concepts.label: Depersonalization
concepts.title: Depersonalization
concepts.definition: State in which an individual perceives or experiences a sensation of unreality concerning the self or the environment; it is seen in disorders such as schizophrenia, affection disorders, organic mental disorders, and personality disorders. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Depression
concepts.title: Depression
concepts.definition: Depressive states usually of moderate intensity in contrast with MAJOR DEPRESSIVE DISORDER present in neurotic and psychotic disorders.

concepts.label: Major Depressive Disorder
concepts.title: Major Depressive Disorder
concepts.definition: Disorder in which five (or more) of the following symptoms have been present during the same 2-week period and represent a change from previous functioning; at least one of the symptoms is either (1) depressed mood or (2) loss of interest or pleasure. Symptoms include: depressed mood most of the day, nearly every day; markedly diminished interest or pleasure in activities most of the day, nearly every day; significant weight loss when not dieting or weight gain; Insomnia or hypersomnia nearly every day; psychomotor agitation or retardation nearly every day; fatigue or loss of energy nearly every day; feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt; diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness, nearly every day; or recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation without a specific plan, or a suicide attempt. (DSM-5)

concepts.label: Depressive Disorder
concepts.title: Depressive Disorder
concepts.definition: An affective disorder manifested by either a dysphoric mood or loss of interest or pleasure in usual activities. The mood disturbance is prominent and relatively persistent.

concepts.label: Depth Perception
concepts.title: Depth Perception
concepts.definition: Perception of three-dimensionality.

concepts.label: Dermatoglyphics
concepts.title: Dermatoglyphics
concepts.definition: The study of the patterns of ridges of the skin of the fingers, palms, toes, and soles.

concepts.label: Dermatomyositis
concepts.title: Dermatomyositis
concepts.definition: A subacute or chronic inflammatory disease of muscle and skin, marked by proximal muscle weakness and a characteristic skin rash. The illness occurs with approximately equal frequency in children and adults. The skin lesions usually take the form of a purplish rash (or less often an exfoliative dermatitis) involving the nose, cheeks, forehead, upper trunk, and arms. The disease is associated with a complement mediated intramuscular microangiopathy, leading to loss of capillaries, muscle ischemia, muscle-fiber necrosis, and perifascicular atrophy. The childhood form of this disease tends to evolve into a systemic vasculitis. Dermatomyositis may occur in association with malignant neoplasms. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1405-6)

concepts.label: Desensitization, Psychologic
concepts.title: Desensitization, Psychologic
concepts.definition: A behavior therapy technique in which deep muscle relaxation is used to inhibit the effects of graded anxiety-evoking stimuli.

concepts.label: Diabetes Insipidus
concepts.title: Diabetes Insipidus
concepts.definition: A disease that is characterized by frequent urination, excretion of large amounts of dilute URINE, and excessive THIRST. Etiologies of diabetes insipidus include deficiency of antidiuretic hormone (also known as ADH or VASOPRESSIN) secreted by the NEUROHYPOPHYSIS, impaired KIDNEY response to ADH, and impaired hypothalamic regulation of thirst.

concepts.label: Diabetes Mellitus
concepts.title: Diabetes Mellitus
concepts.definition: A heterogeneous group of disorders characterized by HYPERGLYCEMIA and GLUCOSE INTOLERANCE.

concepts.label: Diabetes Mellitus, Type 1
concepts.title: Diabetes Mellitus, Type 1
concepts.definition: A subtype of DIABETES MELLITUS that is characterized by INSULIN deficiency. It is manifested by the sudden onset of severe HYPERGLYCEMIA, rapid progression to DIABETIC KETOACIDOSIS, and DEATH unless treated with insulin. The disease may occur at any age, but is most common in childhood or adolescence.

concepts.label: Diabetic Neuropathies
concepts.title: Diabetic Neuropathies
concepts.definition: Peripheral, autonomic, and cranial nerve disorders that are associated with DIABETES MELLITUS. These conditions usually result from diabetic microvascular injury involving small blood vessels that supply nerves (VASA NERVORUM). Relatively common conditions which may be associated with diabetic neuropathy include third nerve palsy (see OCULOMOTOR NERVE DISEASES); MONONEUROPATHY; mononeuropathy multiplex; diabetic amyotrophy; a painful POLYNEUROPATHY; autonomic neuropathy; and thoracoabdominal neuropathy. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1325)

concepts.label: Diagnosis
concepts.title: Diagnosis
concepts.definition: The determination of the nature of a disease or condition, or the distinguishing of one disease or condition from another. Assessment may be made through physical examination, laboratory tests, or the likes. Computerized programs may be used to enhance the decision-making process.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Techniques, Cardiovascular
concepts.title: Diagnostic Techniques, Cardiovascular
concepts.definition: Methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases or dysfunction of the cardiovascular system or its organs or demonstration of their physiological processes.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Techniques, Otological
concepts.title: Diagnostic Techniques, Otological
concepts.definition: Methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases of the ear or of hearing disorders or demonstration of hearing acuity or loss.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Techniques, Ophthalmological
concepts.title: Diagnostic Techniques, Ophthalmological
concepts.definition: Methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases of the eye or of vision disorders.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Techniques, Neurological
concepts.title: Diagnostic Techniques, Neurological
concepts.definition: Methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases of the nervous system, central and peripheral, or demonstration of neurologic function or dysfunction.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Techniques, Obstetrical and Gynecological
concepts.title: Diagnostic Techniques, Obstetrical and Gynecological
concepts.definition: Methods and procedures for the diagnosis of conditions related to pregnancy, labor, and the puerperium and of diseases of the female genitalia. It includes also demonstration of genital and pregnancy physiology.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Techniques, Radioisotope
concepts.title: Diagnostic Techniques, Radioisotope
concepts.definition: Any diagnostic evaluation using radioactive (unstable) isotopes. This diagnosis includes many nuclear medicine procedures as well as radioimmunoassay tests.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Techniques, Respiratory System
concepts.title: Diagnostic Techniques, Respiratory System
concepts.definition: Methods and procedures for the diagnosis of diseases of the respiratory tract or its organs. It includes RESPIRATORY FUNCTION TESTS.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Imaging
concepts.title: Diagnostic Imaging
concepts.definition: Any visual display of structural or functional patterns of organs or tissues for diagnostic evaluation. It includes measuring physiologic and metabolic responses to physical and chemical stimuli, as well as ultramicroscopy.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Services
concepts.title: Diagnostic Services
concepts.definition: Organized services for the purpose of providing diagnosis to promote and maintain health.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Tests, Routine
concepts.title: Diagnostic Tests, Routine
concepts.definition: Diagnostic procedures, such as laboratory tests and x-rays, routinely performed on all individuals or specified categories of individuals in a specified situation, e.g., patients being admitted to the hospital. These include routine tests administered to neonates.

concepts.label: Diastole
concepts.title: Diastole
concepts.definition: Post-systolic relaxation of the HEART, especially the HEART VENTRICLES.

concepts.label: Diencephalon
concepts.title: Diencephalon
concepts.definition: The paired caudal parts of the PROSENCEPHALON from which the THALAMUS; HYPOTHALAMUS; EPITHALAMUS; and SUBTHALAMUS are derived.

concepts.label: Diet
concepts.title: Diet
concepts.definition: Regular course of eating and drinking adopted by a person or animal.

concepts.label: Diet Therapy
concepts.title: Diet Therapy
concepts.definition: Adjusting the quantity and quality of food intake to improve health status of an individual. This term does not include the methods of food intake (NUTRITIONAL SUPPORT).

concepts.label: Differential Threshold
concepts.title: Differential Threshold
concepts.definition: The smallest difference which can be discriminated between two stimuli or one which is barely above the threshold.

concepts.label: Digestive System
concepts.title: Digestive System
concepts.definition: A group of organs stretching from the MOUTH to the ANUS, serving to breakdown foods, assimilate nutrients, and eliminate waste. In humans, the digestive system includes the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT and the accessory glands (LIVER; BILIARY TRACT; PANCREAS).

concepts.label: Digestive System Diseases
concepts.title: Digestive System Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases in any part of the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT or the accessory organs (LIVER; BILIARY TRACT; PANCREAS).

concepts.label: Digestive System Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Digestive System Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: Properties and processes of the DIGESTIVE SYSTEM as a whole or of any of its parts.

concepts.label: Dihydropteridine Reductase
concepts.title: Dihydropteridine Reductase
concepts.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the reduction of 6,7-dihydropteridine to 5,6,7,8-tetrahydropteridine in the presence of NADP+. Defects in the enzyme are a cause of PHENYLKETONURIA II. Formerly listed as EC 1.6.99.7.

concepts.label: Diplopia
concepts.title: Diplopia
concepts.definition: A visual symptom in which a single object is perceived by the visual cortex as two objects rather than one. Disorders associated with this condition include REFRACTIVE ERRORS; STRABISMUS; OCULOMOTOR NERVE DISEASES; TROCHLEAR NERVE DISEASES; ABDUCENS NERVE DISEASES; and diseases of the BRAIN STEM and OCCIPITAL LOBE.

concepts.label: Behavioral Disciplines and Activities
concepts.title: Behavioral Disciplines and Activities
concepts.definition: The specialties in psychiatry and psychology, their diagnostic techniques and tests, their therapeutic methods, and psychiatric and psychological services.

concepts.label: Discrimination, Psychological
concepts.title: Discrimination, Psychological
concepts.definition: Differential response to different stimuli.

concepts.label: Discrimination Learning
concepts.title: Discrimination Learning
concepts.definition: Learning that is manifested in the ability to respond differentially to various stimuli.

concepts.label: Disease Models, Animal
concepts.title: Disease Models, Animal
concepts.definition: Naturally-occurring or experimentally-induced animal diseases with pathological processes analogous to human diseases.

concepts.label: Disease Outbreaks
concepts.title: Disease Outbreaks
concepts.definition: Sudden increase in the incidence of a disease. The concept includes EPIDEMICS and PANDEMICS.

concepts.label: Disease Susceptibility
concepts.title: Disease Susceptibility
concepts.definition: A constitution or condition of the body which makes the tissues react in special ways to certain extrinsic stimuli and thus tends to make the individual more than usually susceptible to certain diseases.

concepts.label: Displacement, Psychological
concepts.title: Displacement, Psychological
concepts.definition: The process by which an emotional or behavioral response that is appropriate for one situation appears in another situation for which it is inappropriate.

concepts.label: Dissociative Disorders
concepts.title: Dissociative Disorders
concepts.definition: Sudden temporary alterations in the normally integrative functions of consciousness.

concepts.label: Distance Perception
concepts.title: Distance Perception
concepts.definition: The act of knowing or the recognition of a distance by recollective thought, or by means of a sensory process which is under the influence of a set of prior experiences.

concepts.label: Diving
concepts.title: Diving
concepts.definition: An activity in which the organism plunges into water. It includes scuba and bell diving. Diving as natural behavior of animals goes here, as well as diving in decompression experiments with humans or animals.

concepts.label: Divorce
concepts.title: Divorce
concepts.definition: Legal dissolution of an officially recognized marriage relationship.

concepts.label: Dizziness
concepts.title: Dizziness
concepts.definition: An imprecise term which may refer to a sense of spatial disorientation, motion of the environment, or lightheadedness.

concepts.label: DNA Virus Infections
concepts.title: DNA Virus Infections
concepts.definition: Diseases caused by DNA VIRUSES.

concepts.label: Dominance-Subordination
concepts.title: Dominance-Subordination
concepts.definition: Relationship between individuals when one individual threatens or becomes aggressive and the other individual remains passive or attempts to escape.

concepts.label: Dominance, Cerebral
concepts.title: Dominance, Cerebral
concepts.definition: Dominance of one cerebral hemisphere over the other in cerebral functions.

concepts.label: Dihydroxyphenylalanine
concepts.title: Dihydroxyphenylalanine
concepts.definition: A beta-hydroxylated derivative of phenylalanine. The D-form of dihydroxyphenylalanine has less physiologic activity than the L-form and is commonly used experimentally to determine whether the pharmacological effects of LEVODOPA are stereospecific.

concepts.label: Dopamine
concepts.title: Dopamine
concepts.definition: One of the catecholamine NEUROTRANSMITTERS in the brain. It is derived from TYROSINE and is the precursor to NOREPINEPHRINE and EPINEPHRINE. Dopamine is a major transmitter in the extrapyramidal system of the brain, and important in regulating movement. A family of receptors (RECEPTORS, DOPAMINE) mediate its action.

concepts.label: Dorsomedial Hypothalamic Nucleus
concepts.title: Dorsomedial Hypothalamic Nucleus
concepts.definition: An aggregation of cells in the middle hypothalamus dorsal to the ventromedial nucleus and bordering the THIRD VENTRICLE.

concepts.label: Double Bind Interaction
concepts.title: Double Bind Interaction
concepts.definition: Simultaneous communication of conflicting messages in which the response to either message evokes rejection or disapproval. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Double-Blind Method
concepts.title: Double-Blind Method
concepts.definition: A method of studying a drug or procedure in which both the subjects and investigators are kept unaware of who is actually getting which specific treatment.

concepts.label: Down Syndrome
concepts.title: Down Syndrome
concepts.definition: A chromosome disorder associated either with an extra CHROMOSOME 21 or an effective TRISOMY for chromosome 21. Clinical manifestations include HYPOTONIA, short stature, BRACHYCEPHALY, upslanting palpebral fissures, epicanthus, Brushfield spots on the iris, protruding tongue, small ears, short, broad hands, fifth finger clinodactyly, single transverse palmar crease, and moderate to severe INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY. Cardiac and gastrointestinal malformations, a marked increase in the incidence of LEUKEMIA, and the early onset of ALZHEIMER DISEASE are also associated with this condition. Pathologic features include the development of NEUROFIBRILLARY TANGLES in neurons and the deposition of AMYLOID BETA-PROTEIN, similar to the pathology of ALZHEIMER DISEASE. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p213)

concepts.label: Dreams
concepts.title: Dreams
concepts.definition: A series of thoughts, images, or emotions occurring during sleep which are dissociated from the usual stream of consciousness of the waking state.

concepts.label: Drinking Behavior
concepts.title: Drinking Behavior
concepts.definition: Behaviors associated with the ingesting of water and other liquids; includes rhythmic patterns of drinking (time intervals - onset and duration), frequency and satiety.

concepts.label: Drive
concepts.title: Drive
concepts.definition: A state of internal activity of an organism that is a necessary condition before a given stimulus will elicit a class of responses; e.g., a certain level of hunger (drive) must be present before food will elicit an eating response.

concepts.label: Drug Administration Routes
concepts.title: Drug Administration Routes
concepts.definition: The various ways of administering a drug or other chemical to a site in a patient or animal from where the chemical is absorbed into the blood and delivered to the target tissue.

concepts.label: Drug and Narcotic Control
concepts.title: Drug and Narcotic Control
concepts.definition: Control of drug and narcotic use by international agreement, or by institutional systems for handling prescribed drugs. This includes regulations concerned with the manufacturing, dispensing, approval (DRUG APPROVAL), and marketing of drugs.

concepts.label: Drug Therapy
concepts.title: Drug Therapy
concepts.definition: The use of DRUGS to treat a DISEASE or its symptoms. One example is the use of ANTINEOPLASTIC AGENTS to treat CANCER.

concepts.label: Pharmaceutical Preparations
concepts.title: Pharmaceutical Preparations
concepts.definition: Drugs intended for human or veterinary use, presented in their finished dosage form. Included here are materials used in the preparation and/or formulation of the finished dosage form.

concepts.label: Duane Retraction Syndrome
concepts.title: Duane Retraction Syndrome
concepts.definition: A syndrome characterized by marked limitation of abduction of the eye, variable limitation of adduction and retraction of the globe, and narrowing of the palpebral fissure on attempted adduction. The condition is caused by aberrant innervation of the lateral rectus by fibers of the OCULOMOTOR NERVE.

concepts.label: Dura Mater
concepts.title: Dura Mater
concepts.definition: The outermost of the three MENINGES, a fibrous membrane of connective tissue that covers the brain and the spinal cord.

concepts.label: Dwarfism
concepts.title: Dwarfism
concepts.definition: A genetic or pathological condition that is characterized by short stature and undersize. Abnormal skeletal growth usually results in an adult who is significantly below the average height.

concepts.label: Dwarfism, Pituitary
concepts.title: Dwarfism, Pituitary
concepts.definition: A form of dwarfism caused by complete or partial GROWTH HORMONE deficiency, resulting from either the lack of GROWTH HORMONE-RELEASING FACTOR from the HYPOTHALAMUS or from the mutations in the growth hormone gene (GH1) in the PITUITARY GLAND. It is also known as Type I pituitary dwarfism. Human hypophysial dwarf is caused by a deficiency of HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE during development.

concepts.label: Dysarthria
concepts.title: Dysarthria
concepts.definition: Disorders of speech articulation caused by imperfect coordination of pharynx, larynx, tongue, or face muscles. This may result from CRANIAL NERVE DISEASES; NEUROMUSCULAR DISEASES; CEREBELLAR DISEASES; BASAL GANGLIA DISEASES; BRAIN STEM diseases; or diseases of the corticobulbar tracts (see PYRAMIDAL TRACTS). The cortical language centers are intact in this condition. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p489)

concepts.label: Dysautonomia, Familial
concepts.title: Dysautonomia, Familial
concepts.definition: An autosomal disorder of the peripheral and autonomic nervous systems limited to individuals of Ashkenazic Jewish descent. Clinical manifestations are present at birth and include diminished lacrimation, defective thermoregulation, orthostatic hypotension (HYPOTENSION, ORTHOSTATIC), fixed pupils, excessive SWEATING, loss of pain and temperature sensation, and absent reflexes. Pathologic features include reduced numbers of small diameter peripheral nerve fibers and autonomic ganglion neurons. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1348; Nat Genet 1993;4(2):160-4)
aliases: Dominant Hereditary Sensory Neuropathy, Type III
HSAN (Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy) Type III
Hereditary Sensory Neuropathy, Dominant, Type III
Hereditary Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy Type III
Hereditary-Sensory and Autonomic Neuropathy Type III
Neuropathy, Hereditary Sensory And Autonomic, Type III
Neuropathy, Hereditary and Autonomic, Type III
Type III Hereditary Sensory Neuropathy, Dominant

concepts.label: Dysgeusia
concepts.title: Dysgeusia
concepts.definition: A condition characterized by alterations of the sense of taste which may range from mild to severe, including gross distortions of taste quality.

concepts.label: Dyskinesia, Drug-Induced
concepts.title: Dyskinesia, Drug-Induced
concepts.definition: Abnormal movements, including HYPERKINESIS; HYPOKINESIA; TREMOR; and DYSTONIA, associated with the use of certain medications or drugs. Muscles of the face, trunk, neck, and extremities are most commonly affected. Tardive dyskinesia refers to abnormal hyperkinetic movements of the muscles of the face, tongue, and neck associated with the use of neuroleptic agents (see ANTIPSYCHOTIC AGENTS). (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1199)

concepts.label: Dyslexia
concepts.title: Dyslexia
concepts.definition: A cognitive disorder characterized by an impaired ability to comprehend written and printed words or phrases despite intact vision. This condition may be developmental or acquired. Developmental dyslexia is marked by reading achievement that falls substantially below that expected given the individual's chronological age, measured intelligence, and age-appropriate education. The disturbance in reading significantly interferes with academic achievement or with activities of daily living that require reading skills. (From DSM-IV)

concepts.label: Dyslexia, Acquired
concepts.title: Dyslexia, Acquired
concepts.definition: A receptive visual aphasia characterized by the loss of a previously possessed ability to comprehend the meaning or significance of handwritten words, despite intact vision. This condition may be associated with posterior cerebral artery infarction (INFARCTION, POSTERIOR CEREBRAL ARTERY) and other BRAIN DISEASES.

concepts.label: Dysostoses
concepts.title: Dysostoses
concepts.definition: Defective bone formation involving individual bones, singly or in combination.

concepts.label: Dyspareunia
concepts.title: Dyspareunia
concepts.definition: Recurrent genital pain occurring during, before, or after SEXUAL INTERCOURSE in either the male or the female.

concepts.label: Dystonia
concepts.title: Dystonia
concepts.definition: An attitude or posture due to the co-contraction of agonists and antagonist muscles in one region of the body. It most often affects the large axial muscles of the trunk and limb girdles. Conditions which feature persistent or recurrent episodes of dystonia as a primary manifestation of disease are referred to as DYSTONIC DISORDERS. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p77)

concepts.label: Dystonia Musculorum Deformans
concepts.title: Dystonia Musculorum Deformans
concepts.definition: A condition characterized by focal DYSTONIA that progresses to involuntary spasmodic contractions of the muscles of the legs, trunk, arms, and face. The hands are often spared, however, sustained axial and limb contractions may lead to a state where the body is grossly contorted. Onset is usually in the first or second decade. Familial patterns of inheritance, primarily autosomal dominant with incomplete penetrance, have been identified. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1078)

concepts.label: Ear
concepts.title: Ear
concepts.definition: The hearing and equilibrium system of the body. It consists of three parts: the EXTERNAL EAR, the MIDDLE EAR, and the INNER EAR. Sound waves are transmitted through this organ where vibration is transduced to nerve signals that pass through the ACOUSTIC NERVE to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. The inner ear also contains the vestibular organ that maintains equilibrium by transducing signals to the VESTIBULAR NERVE.

concepts.label: Ear Diseases
concepts.title: Ear Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes of the ear, the hearing, and the equilibrium system of the body.

concepts.label: Ear, Middle
concepts.title: Ear, Middle
concepts.definition: The space and structures directly internal to the TYMPANIC MEMBRANE and external to the inner ear (LABYRINTH). Its major components include the AUDITORY OSSICLES and the EUSTACHIAN TUBE that connects the cavity of middle ear (tympanic cavity) to the upper part of the throat.

concepts.label: Earache
concepts.title: Earache
concepts.definition: Pain in the ear.

concepts.label: Echoencephalography
concepts.title: Echoencephalography
concepts.definition: Use of reflected ultrasound in the diagnosis of intracranial pathologic processes.

concepts.label: Echolalia
concepts.title: Echolalia
concepts.definition: Involuntary (parrot-like), meaningless repetition of a recently heard word, phrase, or song. This condition may be associated with transcortical APHASIA; SCHIZOPHRENIA; or other disorders. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p485)

concepts.label: Echolocation
concepts.title: Echolocation
concepts.definition: An auditory orientation mechanism involving the emission of high frequency sounds which are reflected back to the emitter (animal).

concepts.label: Eclampsia
concepts.title: Eclampsia
concepts.definition: Onset of HYPERREFLEXIA; SEIZURES; or COMA in a previously diagnosed pre-eclamptic patient (PRE-ECLAMPSIA).

concepts.label: Ecology
concepts.title: Ecology
concepts.definition: The branch of science concerned with the interrelationship of organisms and their ENVIRONMENT, especially as manifested by natural cycles and rhythms, community development and structure, interactions between different kinds of organisms, geographic distributions, and population alterations. (Webster's, 3d ed)

concepts.label: Economics
concepts.title: Economics
concepts.definition: The science of utilization, distribution, and consumption of services and materials.

concepts.label: Health Care Economics and Organizations
concepts.title: Health Care Economics and Organizations
concepts.definition: The economic aspects of health care, its planning, and delivery. It includes government agencies and organizations in the private sector.

concepts.label: Ectodermal Dysplasia
concepts.title: Ectodermal Dysplasia
concepts.definition: A group of hereditary disorders involving tissues and structures derived from the embryonic ectoderm. They are characterized by the presence of abnormalities at birth and involvement of both the epidermis and skin appendages. They are generally nonprogressive and diffuse. Various forms exist, including anhidrotic and hidrotic dysplasias, FOCAL DERMAL HYPOPLASIA, and aplasia cutis congenita.

concepts.label: Education
concepts.title: Education
concepts.definition: Acquisition of knowledge as a result of instruction in a formal course of study.

concepts.label: Education of Persons with Intellectual Disabilities
concepts.title: Education of Persons with Intellectual Disabilities
concepts.definition: The teaching or training of those individuals with subnormal intellectual functioning.

concepts.label: Education, Nonprofessional
concepts.title: Education, Nonprofessional
concepts.definition: Education and training outside that for the professions.

concepts.label: Education, Special
concepts.title: Education, Special
concepts.definition: Education of the individual who markedly deviates intellectually, physically, socially, or emotionally from those considered to be normal, thus requiring special instruction.

concepts.label: Educational Status
concepts.title: Educational Status
concepts.definition: Educational attainment or level of education of an individual.

concepts.label: Efferent Pathways
concepts.title: Efferent Pathways
concepts.definition: Nerve structures through which impulses are conducted from a nerve center toward a peripheral site. Such impulses are conducted via efferent neurons (NEURONS, EFFERENT), such as MOTOR NEURONS, autonomic neurons, and hypophyseal neurons.

concepts.label: Efficiency
concepts.title: Efficiency
concepts.definition: Ratio of output to effort and or resources, or the ratio of effort and or resources produced to energy expended.

concepts.label: Ego
concepts.title: Ego
concepts.definition: The conscious portion of the personality structure which serves to mediate between the demands of the primitive instinctual drives, (the id), of internalized parental and social prohibitions or the conscience, (the superego), and of reality.

concepts.label: Eidetic Imagery
concepts.title: Eidetic Imagery
concepts.definition: A visual image which is recalled in accurate detail. It is a sort of projection of an image on a mental screen.

concepts.label: Ejaculation
concepts.title: Ejaculation
concepts.definition: The emission of SEMEN to the exterior, resulting from the contraction of muscles surrounding the male internal urogenital ducts.

concepts.label: Elapid Venoms
concepts.title: Elapid Venoms
concepts.definition: Venoms from snakes of the family Elapidae, including cobras, kraits, mambas, coral, tiger, and Australian snakes. The venoms contain polypeptide toxins of various kinds, cytolytic, hemolytic, and neurotoxic factors, but fewer enzymes than viper or crotalid venoms. Many of the toxins have been characterized.

concepts.label: Elastin
concepts.title: Elastin
concepts.definition: MeSH 已登记该主题词，但此条目未提供范围说明；需继续补全定义。

concepts.label: Electric Stimulation
concepts.title: Electric Stimulation
concepts.definition: Use of electric potential or currents to elicit biological responses.

concepts.label: Transcutaneous Electric Nerve Stimulation
concepts.title: Transcutaneous Electric Nerve Stimulation
concepts.definition: The use of specifically placed small electrodes to deliver electrical impulses across the SKIN to relieve PAIN. It is used less frequently to produce ANESTHESIA.

concepts.label: Electroconvulsive Therapy
concepts.title: Electroconvulsive Therapy
concepts.definition: Electrically induced CONVULSIONS primarily used in the treatment of severe AFFECTIVE DISORDERS and SCHIZOPHRENIA.

concepts.label: Electrodiagnosis
concepts.title: Electrodiagnosis
concepts.definition: Diagnosis of disease states by recording the spontaneous electrical activity of tissues or organs or by the response to stimulation of electrically excitable tissue.

concepts.label: Electroencephalography
concepts.title: Electroencephalography
concepts.definition: Recording of electric currents developed in the brain by means of electrodes applied to the scalp, to the surface of the brain, or placed within the substance of the brain.

concepts.label: Electronics
concepts.title: Electronics
concepts.definition: The study, control, and application of the conduction of ELECTRICITY through gases or vacuum, or through semiconducting or conducting materials. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

concepts.label: Electronystagmography
concepts.title: Electronystagmography
concepts.definition: Recording of nystagmus based on changes in the electrical field surrounding the eye produced by the difference in potential between the cornea and the retina.

concepts.label: Electrooculography
concepts.title: Electrooculography
concepts.definition: Recording of the average amplitude of the resting potential arising between the cornea and the retina in light and dark adaptation as the eyes turn a standard distance to the right and the left. The increase in potential with light adaptation is used to evaluate the condition of the retinal pigment epithelium.

concepts.label: Electrophysiology
concepts.title: Electrophysiology
concepts.definition: The study of the generation and behavior of electrical charges in living organisms particularly the nervous system and the effects of electricity on living organisms.

concepts.label: Electroshock
concepts.title: Electroshock
concepts.definition: Induction of a stress reaction in experimental subjects by means of an electrical shock; applies to either convulsive or non-convulsive states.

concepts.label: Electric Stimulation Therapy
concepts.title: Electric Stimulation Therapy
concepts.definition: Application of electric current in treatment without the generation of perceptible heat. It includes electric stimulation of nerves or muscles, passage of current into the body, or use of interrupted current of low intensity to raise the detection threshold of the skin to pain.

concepts.label: Eliminative Behavior, Animal
concepts.title: Eliminative Behavior, Animal
concepts.definition: Behavior associated with the elimination of feces and urine from the body.

concepts.label: Embryo, Mammalian
concepts.title: Embryo, Mammalian
concepts.definition: The entity of a developing mammal (MAMMALS), generally from the cleavage of a ZYGOTE to the end of embryonic differentiation of basic structures. For the human embryo, this represents the first two months of intrauterine development preceding the stages of the FETUS.

concepts.label: Embryonic Structures
concepts.title: Embryonic Structures
concepts.definition: The anatomical parts that make up an organism in the early stages of development.

concepts.label: Emergency Medical Services
concepts.title: Emergency Medical Services
concepts.definition: Services specifically designed, staffed, and equipped for the emergency care of patients.

concepts.label: Emergency Services, Psychiatric
concepts.title: Emergency Services, Psychiatric
concepts.definition: Organized services to provide immediate psychiatric care to patients with acute psychological disturbances.

concepts.label: Emotions
concepts.title: Emotions
concepts.definition: Those affective states which can be experienced and have arousing and motivational properties.

concepts.label: Empathy
concepts.title: Empathy
concepts.definition: An individual's objective and insightful awareness of the feelings and behavior of another person. It should be distinguished from sympathy, which is usually nonobjective and noncritical. It includes caring, which is the demonstration of an awareness of and a concern for the good of others. (From Bioethics Thesaurus, 1992)

concepts.label: Empty Sella Syndrome
concepts.title: Empty Sella Syndrome
concepts.definition: A condition when the SELLA TURCICA is not filled with pituitary tissue. The pituitary gland is either compressed, atrophied, or removed. There are two types: (1) primary empty sella is due a defect in the sella diaphragm leading to arachnoid herniation into the sellar space; (2) secondary empty sella is associated with the removal or treatment of PITUITARY NEOPLASMS.

concepts.label: Empyema
concepts.title: Empyema
concepts.definition: Presence of pus in a hollow organ or body cavity.

concepts.label: Encephalitis
concepts.title: Encephalitis
concepts.definition: Inflammation of the BRAIN due to infection, autoimmune processes, toxins, and other conditions. Viral infections (see ENCEPHALITIS, VIRAL) are a relatively frequent cause of this condition.

concepts.label: Encephalitis, California
concepts.title: Encephalitis, California
concepts.definition: A viral infection of the brain caused by serotypes of California encephalitis virus (ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS, CALIFORNIA) transmitted to humans by the mosquito AEDES triseriatus. The majority of cases are caused by the LA CROSSE VIRUS. This condition is endemic to the midwestern United States and primarily affects children between 5-10 years of age. Clinical manifestations include FEVER; VOMITING; HEADACHE; and abdominal pain followed by SEIZURES, altered mentation, and focal neurologic deficits. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1996, Ch26, p13)

concepts.label: Encephalitis, Arbovirus
concepts.title: Encephalitis, Arbovirus
concepts.definition: Infections of the brain caused by arthropod-borne viruses (i.e., arboviruses) primarily from the families TOGAVIRIDAE; FLAVIVIRIDAE; BUNYAVIRIDAE; REOVIRIDAE; and RHABDOVIRIDAE. Life cycles of these viruses are characterized by ZOONOSES, with birds and lower mammals serving as intermediate hosts. The virus is transmitted to humans by the bite of mosquitoes (CULICIDAE) or TICKS. Clinical manifestations include fever, headache, alterations of mentation, focal neurologic deficits, and COMA. (From Clin Microbiol Rev 1994 Jan;7(1):89-116; Walton, Brain's Diseases of the Nervous System, 10th ed, p321)

concepts.label: Encephalitis, Japanese
concepts.title: Encephalitis, Japanese
concepts.definition: A mosquito-borne encephalitis caused by the Japanese B encephalitis virus (ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS, JAPANESE) occurring throughout Eastern Asia and Australia. The majority of infections occur in children and are subclinical or have features limited to transient fever and gastrointestinal symptoms. Inflammation of the brain, spinal cord, and meninges may occur and lead to transient or permanent neurologic deficits (including a POLIOMYELITIS-like presentation); SEIZURES; COMA; and death. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p751; Lancet 1998 Apr 11;351(9109):1094-7)

concepts.label: Encephalomyelitis, Acute Disseminated
concepts.title: Encephalomyelitis, Acute Disseminated
concepts.definition: An acute or subacute inflammatory process of the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM characterized histologically by multiple foci of perivascular demyelination. Symptom onset usually occurs several days after an acute viral infection or immunization, but it may coincide with the onset of infection or rarely no antecedent event can be identified. Clinical manifestations include CONFUSION, somnolence, FEVER, nuchal rigidity, and involuntary movements. The illness may progress to COMA and eventually be fatal. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p921)

concepts.label: Encephalitis, St. Louis
concepts.title: Encephalitis, St. Louis
concepts.definition: A viral encephalitis caused by the St. Louis encephalitis virus (ENCEPHALITIS VIRUS, ST. LOUIS), a FLAVIVIRUS. It is transmitted to humans and other vertebrates primarily by mosquitoes of the genus CULEX. The primary animal vectors are wild birds and the disorder is endemic to the midwestern and southeastern United States. Infections may be limited to an influenza-like illness or present as an ASEPTIC MENINGITIS or ENCEPHALITIS. Clinical manifestations of the encephalitic presentation may include SEIZURES, lethargy, MYOCLONUS, focal neurologic signs, COMA, and DEATH. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p750)

concepts.label: Encephalitis, Tick-Borne
concepts.title: Encephalitis, Tick-Borne
concepts.definition: Encephalitis caused by neurotropic viruses that are transmitted via the bite of TICKS. In Europe, the diseases are caused by ENCEPHALITIS VIRUSES, TICK-BORNE, which give rise to Russian spring-summer encephalitis, central European encephalitis, louping ill encephalitis, and related disorders. Powassan encephalitis occurs in North America and Russia and is caused by the Powassan virus. ASEPTIC MENINGITIS and rarely encephalitis may complicate COLORADO TICK FEVER which is endemic to mountainous regions of the western United States. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1996, Ch26, pp14-5)

concepts.label: Encephalocele
concepts.title: Encephalocele
concepts.definition: Brain tissue herniation through a congenital or acquired defect in the skull. The majority of congenital encephaloceles occur in the occipital or frontal regions. Clinical features include a protuberant mass that may be pulsatile. The quantity and location of protruding neural tissue determines the type and degree of neurologic deficit. Visual defects, psychomotor developmental delay, and persistent motor deficits frequently occur.

concepts.label: Encephalomalacia
concepts.title: Encephalomalacia
concepts.definition: Softening or loss of brain tissue following CEREBRAL INFARCTION; cerebral ischemia (see BRAIN ISCHEMIA), infection, CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA, or other injury. The term is often used during gross pathologic inspection to describe blurred cortical margins and decreased consistency of brain tissue following infarction. Multicystic encephalomalacia refers to the formation of multiple cystic cavities of various sizes in the cerebral cortex of neonates and infants following injury, most notably perinatal hypoxia-ischemic events. (From Davis et al., Textbook of Neuropathology, 2nd ed, p665; J Neuropathol Exp Neurol, 1995 Mar;54(2):268-75)

concepts.label: Encephalomyelitis
concepts.title: Encephalomyelitis
concepts.definition: A general term indicating inflammation of the BRAIN and SPINAL CORD, often used to indicate an infectious process, but also applicable to a variety of autoimmune and toxic-metabolic conditions. There is significant overlap regarding the usage of this term and ENCEPHALITIS in the literature.

concepts.label: Encephalomyelitis, Autoimmune, Experimental
concepts.title: Encephalomyelitis, Autoimmune, Experimental
concepts.definition: An experimental animal model for central nervous system demyelinating disease.
