concepts.definition: The sciences dealing with processes observable in nature.

concepts.label: Physical Stimulation
concepts.title: Physical Stimulation
concepts.definition: Act of eliciting a response from a person or organism through physical contact.

concepts.label: Physician-Patient Relations
concepts.title: Physician-Patient Relations
concepts.definition: The interactions between physician and patient.

concepts.label: Physician's Role
concepts.title: Physician's Role
concepts.definition: The expected function of a member of the medical profession.

concepts.label: Physics
concepts.title: Physics
concepts.definition: The study of those aspects of energy and matter in terms of elementary principles and laws. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

concepts.label: Physiology
concepts.title: Physiology
concepts.definition: The biological science concerned with the life-supporting properties, functions, and processes of living organisms or their parts.

concepts.label: Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: The functions and properties of living organisms, including both the physical and chemical factors and processes, supporting life in single- or multi-cell organisms from their origin through the progression of life.

concepts.label: Pia Mater
concepts.title: Pia Mater
concepts.definition: The innermost layer of the three meninges covering the brain and spinal cord. It is the fine vascular membrane that lies under the ARACHNOID and the DURA MATER.

concepts.label: Pica
concepts.title: Pica
concepts.definition: The persistent eating of non-nutritive substances for a period of at least one month.

concepts.label: Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome
concepts.title: Obesity Hypoventilation Syndrome
concepts.definition: HYPOVENTILATION syndrome in very obese persons with excessive ADIPOSE TISSUE around the ABDOMEN and DIAPHRAGM. It is characterized by diminished to absent ventilatory chemoresponsiveness; chronic HYPOXIA; HYPERCAPNIA; POLYCYTHEMIA; and long periods of sleep during day and night (HYPERSOMNOLENCE). It is a condition often related to OBSTRUCTIVE SLEEP APNEA but can occur separately.

concepts.label: Picornaviridae Infections
concepts.title: Picornaviridae Infections
concepts.definition: Virus diseases caused by the PICORNAVIRIDAE.

concepts.label: Pigmentation Disorders
concepts.title: Pigmentation Disorders
concepts.definition: Diseases affecting PIGMENTATION, including SKIN PIGMENTATION.

concepts.label: Pigments, Biological
concepts.title: Pigments, Biological
concepts.definition: Any normal or abnormal coloring matter in PLANTS; ANIMALS or micro-organisms.

concepts.label: Piloerection
concepts.title: Piloerection
concepts.definition: Involuntary erection or bristling of hairs.

concepts.label: Pineal Gland
concepts.title: Pineal Gland
concepts.definition: A light-sensitive neuroendocrine organ attached to the roof of the THIRD VENTRICLE of the brain. The pineal gland secretes MELATONIN, other BIOGENIC AMINES and NEUROPEPTIDES.

concepts.label: Pinealoma
concepts.title: Pinealoma
concepts.definition: Neoplasms which originate from pineal parenchymal cells that tend to enlarge the gland and be locally invasive. The two major forms are pineocytoma and the more malignant pineoblastoma. Pineocytomas have moderate cellularity and tend to form rosette patterns. Pineoblastomas are highly cellular tumors containing small, poorly differentiated cells. These tumors occasionally seed the neuroaxis or cause obstructive HYDROCEPHALUS or Parinaud's syndrome. GERMINOMA; CARCINOMA, EMBRYONAL; GLIOMA; and other neoplasms may arise in the pineal region with germinoma being the most common pineal region tumor. (From DeVita et al., Cancer: Principles and Practice of Oncology, 5th ed, p2064; Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p670)

concepts.label: Pitch Discrimination
concepts.title: Pitch Discrimination
concepts.definition: The ability to differentiate sound frequency or pitch.

concepts.label: Pitch Perception
concepts.title: Pitch Perception
concepts.definition: A dimension of auditory sensation varying with cycles per second of the sound stimulus.

concepts.label: Pituitary Apoplexy
concepts.title: Pituitary Apoplexy
concepts.definition: The sudden loss of blood supply to the PITUITARY GLAND, leading to tissue NECROSIS and loss of function (PANHYPOPITUITARISM). The most common cause is hemorrhage or INFARCTION of a PITUITARY ADENOMA. It can also result from acute hemorrhage into SELLA TURCICA due to HEAD TRAUMA; INTRACRANIAL HYPERTENSION; or other acute effects of central nervous system hemorrhage. Clinical signs include severe HEADACHE; HYPOTENSION; bilateral visual disturbances; UNCONSCIOUSNESS; and COMA.

concepts.label: Pituitary Diseases
concepts.title: Pituitary Diseases
concepts.definition: Disorders involving either the ADENOHYPOPHYSIS or the NEUROHYPOPHYSIS. These diseases usually manifest as hypersecretion or hyposecretion of PITUITARY HORMONES. Neoplastic pituitary masses can also cause compression of the OPTIC CHIASM and other adjacent structures.

concepts.label: Pituitary Gland
concepts.title: Pituitary Gland
concepts.definition: A small, unpaired gland situated in the SELLA TURCICA. It is connected to the HYPOTHALAMUS by a short stalk which is called the INFUNDIBULUM.

concepts.label: Pituitary Gland, Anterior
concepts.title: Pituitary Gland, Anterior
concepts.definition: The anterior glandular lobe of the pituitary gland, also known as the adenohypophysis. It secretes the ADENOHYPOPHYSEAL HORMONES that regulate vital functions such as GROWTH; METABOLISM; and REPRODUCTION.

concepts.label: Pituitary Gland, Posterior
concepts.title: Pituitary Gland, Posterior
concepts.definition: Neural tissue of the pituitary gland, also known as the neurohypophysis. It consists of the distal AXONS of neurons that produce VASOPRESSIN and OXYTOCIN in the SUPRAOPTIC NUCLEUS and the PARAVENTRICULAR NUCLEUS. These axons travel down through the MEDIAN EMINENCE, the hypothalamic infundibulum of the PITUITARY STALK, to the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

concepts.label: Pituitary Hormone Release Inhibiting Hormones
concepts.title: Pituitary Hormone Release Inhibiting Hormones
concepts.definition: Polypeptide hormones produced in the hypothalamus which inhibit the release of pituitary hormones. Used for PHRIH in general or for which there is no specific heading.

concepts.label: Pituitary Hormone-Releasing Hormones
concepts.title: Pituitary Hormone-Releasing Hormones
concepts.definition: Peptides, natural or synthetic, that stimulate the release of PITUITARY HORMONES. They were first isolated from the extracts of the HYPOTHALAMUS; MEDIAN EMINENCE; PITUITARY STALK; and NEUROHYPOPHYSIS. In addition, some hypophysiotropic hormones control pituitary cell differentiation, cell proliferation, and hormone synthesis. Some can act on more than one pituitary hormone.

concepts.label: Pituitary Neoplasms
concepts.title: Pituitary Neoplasms
concepts.definition: Neoplasms which arise from or metastasize to the PITUITARY GLAND. The majority of pituitary neoplasms are adenomas, which are divided into non-secreting and secreting forms. Hormone producing forms are further classified by the type of hormone they secrete. Pituitary adenomas may also be characterized by their staining properties (see ADENOMA, BASOPHIL; ADENOMA, ACIDOPHIL; and ADENOMA, CHROMOPHOBE). Pituitary tumors may compress adjacent structures, including the HYPOTHALAMUS, several CRANIAL NERVES, and the OPTIC CHIASM. Chiasmal compression may result in bitemporal HEMIANOPSIA.

concepts.label: Platyhelminths
concepts.title: Platyhelminths
concepts.definition: A phylum of acoelomate, bilaterally symmetrical flatworms, without a definite anus. It includes three classes: Cestoda, Turbellaria, and Trematoda.

concepts.label: Play and Playthings
concepts.title: Play and Playthings
concepts.definition: Spontaneous or voluntary recreational activities pursued for enjoyment and accessories or equipment used in the activities; includes games, toys, etc.

concepts.label: Play Therapy
concepts.title: Play Therapy
concepts.definition: A treatment technique utilizing play as a medium for expression and communication between patient and therapist.

concepts.label: Pleasure-Pain Principle
concepts.title: Pleasure-Pain Principle
concepts.definition: The psychoanalytic concept that man instinctively seeks to avoid pain and discomfort and strives for gratification and pleasure.

concepts.label: Pneumocephalus
concepts.title: Pneumocephalus
concepts.definition: Presence of air or gas within the intracranial cavity (e.g., epidural space, subdural space, intracerebral, etc.) which may result from traumatic injuries, fistulous tract formation, erosions of the skull from NEOPLASMS or infection, NEUROSURGICAL PROCEDURES, and other conditions.

concepts.label: Pneumococcal Infections
concepts.title: Pneumococcal Infections
concepts.definition: Infections with bacteria of the species STREPTOCOCCUS PNEUMONIAE.

concepts.label: Pneumoencephalography
concepts.title: Pneumoencephalography
concepts.definition: Radiographic visualization of the cerebral ventricles by injection of air or other gas.

concepts.label: Pneumoradiography
concepts.title: Pneumoradiography
concepts.definition: Radiography using air, oxygen, or some other gas as a contrast medium.

concepts.label: Poisoning
concepts.title: Poisoning
concepts.definition: A condition or physical state produced by the ingestion, injection, inhalation of or exposure to a deleterious agent.

concepts.label: Policy Making
concepts.title: Policy Making
concepts.definition: The decision process by which individuals, groups or institutions establish policies pertaining to plans, programs or procedures.

concepts.label: Poliomyelitis
concepts.title: Poliomyelitis
concepts.definition: An acute infectious disease of humans, particularly children, caused by any of three serotypes of human poliovirus (POLIOVIRUS). Usually the infection is limited to the gastrointestinal tract and nasopharynx, and is often asymptomatic. The central nervous system, primarily the spinal cord, may be affected, leading to rapidly progressive paralysis, coarse FASCICULATION and hyporeflexia. Motor neurons are primarily affected. Encephalitis may also occur. The virus replicates in the nervous system, and may cause significant neuronal loss, most notably in the spinal cord. A rare related condition, nonpoliovirus poliomyelitis, may result from infections with nonpoliovirus enteroviruses. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp764-5)

concepts.label: Poliomyelitis, Bulbar
concepts.title: Poliomyelitis, Bulbar
concepts.definition: A form of paralytic poliomyelitis affecting neurons of the MEDULLA OBLONGATA of the brain stem. Clinical features include impaired respiration, HYPERTENSION, alterations of vasomotor control, and dysphagia. Weakness and atrophy of the limbs and trunk due to spinal cord involvement is usually associated. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p765)

concepts.label: Politics
concepts.title: Politics
concepts.definition: Activities concerned with governmental policies, functions, etc.

concepts.label: Polycyclic Compounds
concepts.title: Polycyclic Compounds
concepts.definition: Compounds which contain two or more rings in their structure.

concepts.label: Polymers
concepts.title: Polymers
concepts.definition: Compounds formed by the joining of smaller, usually repeating, units linked by covalent bonds. These compounds often form large macromolecules (e.g., BIOPOLYMERS; PLASTICS).

concepts.label: Polymorphism, Genetic
concepts.title: Polymorphism, Genetic
concepts.definition: The regular and simultaneous occurrence in a single interbreeding population of two or more discontinuous genotypes. The concept includes differences in genotypes ranging in size from a single nucleotide site (POLYMORPHISM, SINGLE NUCLEOTIDE) to large nucleotide sequences visible at a chromosomal level.

concepts.label: Polymyalgia Rheumatica
concepts.title: Polymyalgia Rheumatica
concepts.definition: A syndrome in the elderly characterized by proximal joint and muscle pain, high erythrocyte sedimentation rate, and a self-limiting course. Pain is usually accompanied by evidence of an inflammatory reaction. Women are affected twice as commonly as men and Caucasians more frequently than other groups. The condition is frequently associated with GIANT CELL ARTERITIS and some theories pose the possibility that the two diseases arise from a single etiology or even that they are the same entity.

concepts.label: Polyneuropathies
concepts.title: Polyneuropathies
concepts.definition: Diseases of multiple peripheral nerves simultaneously. Polyneuropathies usually are characterized by symmetrical, bilateral distal motor and sensory impairment with a graded increase in severity distally. The pathological processes affecting peripheral nerves include degeneration of the axon, myelin or both. The various forms of polyneuropathy are categorized by the type of nerve affected (e.g., sensory, motor, or autonomic), by the distribution of nerve injury (e.g., distal vs. proximal), by nerve component primarily affected (e.g., demyelinating vs. axonal), by etiology, or by pattern of inheritance.

concepts.label: Polyradiculopathy
concepts.title: Polyradiculopathy
concepts.definition: Disease or injury involving multiple SPINAL NERVE ROOTS. Polyradiculitis refers to inflammation of multiple spinal nerve roots.

concepts.label: Polyradiculoneuropathy
concepts.title: Polyradiculoneuropathy
concepts.definition: Diseases characterized by injury or dysfunction involving multiple peripheral nerves and nerve roots. The process may primarily affect myelin or nerve axons. Two of the more common demyelinating forms are acute inflammatory polyradiculopathy (GUILLAIN-BARRE SYNDROME) and POLYRADICULONEUROPATHY, CHRONIC INFLAMMATORY DEMYELINATING. Polyradiculoneuritis refers to inflammation of multiple peripheral nerves and spinal nerve roots.

concepts.label: Polyribosomes
concepts.title: Polyribosomes
concepts.definition: A multiribosomal structure representing a linear array of RIBOSOMES held together by messenger RNA; (RNA, MESSENGER); They represent the active complexes in cellular protein synthesis and are able to incorporate amino acids into polypeptides both in vivo and in vitro. (From Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

concepts.label: Pons
concepts.title: Pons
concepts.definition: The front part of the hindbrain (RHOMBENCEPHALON) that lies between the MEDULLA and the midbrain (MESENCEPHALON) ventral to the cerebellum. It is composed of two parts, the dorsal and the ventral. The pons serves as a relay station for neural pathways between the CEREBELLUM to the CEREBRUM.

concepts.label: Population Characteristics
concepts.title: Population Characteristics
concepts.definition: Qualities and characterization of various types of populations within a social or geographic group, with emphasis on demography, health status, and socioeconomic factors.

concepts.label: Postoperative Complications
concepts.title: Postoperative Complications
concepts.definition: Pathologic processes that affect patients after a surgical procedure. They may or may not be related to the disease for which the surgery was done, and they may or may not be direct results of the surgery.

concepts.label: Posture
concepts.title: Posture
concepts.definition: The position or physical attitude of the body.

concepts.label: Power, Psychological
concepts.title: Power, Psychological
concepts.definition: The exertion of a strong influence or control over others in a variety of settings--administrative, social, academic, etc.

concepts.label: Practice, Psychological
concepts.title: Practice, Psychological
concepts.definition: Performance of an act one or more times, with a view to its fixation or improvement; any performance of an act or behavior that leads to learning.

concepts.label: Prader-Willi Syndrome
concepts.title: Prader-Willi Syndrome
concepts.definition: An autosomal dominant disorder caused by deletion of the proximal long arm of the paternal chromosome 15 (15q11-q13) or by inheritance of both of the pair of chromosomes 15 from the mother (UNIPARENTAL DISOMY) which are imprinted (GENETIC IMPRINTING) and hence silenced. Clinical manifestations include MENTAL RETARDATION; MUSCULAR HYPOTONIA; HYPERPHAGIA; OBESITY; short stature; HYPOGONADISM; STRABISMUS; and HYPERSOMNOLENCE. (Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, p229)

concepts.label: Predatory Behavior
concepts.title: Predatory Behavior
concepts.definition: Instinctual behavior pattern in which food is obtained by killing and consuming other species.

concepts.label: Pregnancy
concepts.title: Pregnancy
concepts.definition: The status during which female mammals carry their developing young (EMBRYOS or FETUSES) in utero before birth, beginning from FERTILIZATION to BIRTH.

concepts.label: Pregnancy Complications
concepts.title: Pregnancy Complications
concepts.definition: Conditions or pathological processes associated with pregnancy. They can occur during or after pregnancy, and range from minor discomforts to serious diseases that require medical interventions. They include diseases in pregnant females, and pregnancies in females with diseases.

concepts.label: Pregnancy in Adolescence
concepts.title: Pregnancy in Adolescence
concepts.definition: Pregnancy in human adolescent females under the age of 19.

concepts.label: Prejudice
concepts.title: Prejudice
concepts.definition: A preconceived judgment made without factual basis.

concepts.label: Premarital Examinations
concepts.title: Premarital Examinations
concepts.definition: Medical tests taken by couples planning to be married in order to determine presence of genetic and contagious diseases.

concepts.label: Premenstrual Syndrome
concepts.title: Premenstrual Syndrome
concepts.definition: A combination of distressing physical, psychologic, or behavioral changes that occur during the luteal phase of the menstrual cycle. Symptoms of PMS are diverse (such as pain, water-retention, anxiety, cravings, and depression) and they diminish markedly 2 or 3 days after the initiation of menses.

concepts.label: Preoptic Area
concepts.title: Preoptic Area
concepts.definition: Region of hypothalamus between the ANTERIOR COMMISSURE and OPTIC CHIASM.

concepts.label: Presbycusis
concepts.title: Presbycusis
concepts.definition: Gradual bilateral hearing loss associated with aging that is due to progressive degeneration of cochlear structures and central auditory pathways. Hearing loss usually begins with the high frequencies then progresses to sounds of middle and low frequencies.

concepts.label: Pressoreceptors
concepts.title: Pressoreceptors
concepts.definition: Receptors in the vascular system, particularly the aorta and carotid sinus, which are sensitive to stretch of the vessel walls.

concepts.label: Preventive Health Services
concepts.title: Preventive Health Services
concepts.definition: Services designed for HEALTH PROMOTION.

concepts.label: Preventive Medicine
concepts.title: Preventive Medicine
concepts.definition: A medical specialty primarily concerned with prevention of disease (PRIMARY PREVENTION) and the promotion and preservation of health in the individual.

concepts.label: Preventive Psychiatry
concepts.title: Preventive Psychiatry
concepts.definition: A discipline concerned with the prevention of mental illness and the promotion of mental health.

concepts.label: Primary Health Care
concepts.title: Primary Health Care
concepts.definition: Care which provides integrated, accessible health care services by clinicians who are accountable for addressing a large majority of personal health care needs, developing a sustained partnership with patients, and practicing in the context of family and community. (JAMA 1995;273(3):192)

concepts.label: Primates
concepts.title: Primates
concepts.definition: An order of mammals consisting of more than 300 species that include LEMURS; LORISIDAE; TARSIERS; MONKEYS; and HOMINIDS. They are characterized by a relatively large brain when compared with other terrestrial mammals, forward-facing eyes, the presence of a CALCARINE SULCUS, and specialized MECHANORECEPTORS in the hands and feet which allow the perception of light touch.

concepts.label: Prions
concepts.title: Prions
concepts.definition: Small proteinaceous infectious particles which resist inactivation by procedures that modify NUCLEIC ACIDS and contain an abnormal isoform of a cellular protein which is a major and necessary component. The abnormal (scrapie) isoform is PrPSc (PRPSC PROTEINS) and the cellular isoform PrPC (PRPC PROTEINS). The primary amino acid sequence of the two isoforms is identical. Human diseases caused by prions include CREUTZFELDT-JAKOB SYNDROME; GERSTMANN-STRAUSSLER SYNDROME; and INSOMNIA, FATAL FAMILIAL.

concepts.label: Proactive Inhibition
concepts.title: Proactive Inhibition
concepts.definition: The state or process hypothesized to account for poorer learning rate for elements later in a series as compared to the learning rate for elements coming earlier in a series.

concepts.label: Probability
concepts.title: Probability
concepts.definition: The study of chance processes or the relative frequency characterizing a chance process.

concepts.label: Probability Learning
concepts.title: Probability Learning
concepts.definition: Usually refers to the use of mathematical models in the prediction of learning to perform tasks based on the theory of probability applied to responses; it may also refer to the frequency of occurrence of the responses observed in the particular study.

concepts.label: Problem Solving
concepts.title: Problem Solving
concepts.definition: A learning situation involving more than one alternative from which a selection is made in order to attain a specific goal.

concepts.label: Professional Practice
concepts.title: Professional Practice
concepts.definition: The use of one's knowledge in a particular profession. It includes, in the case of the field of biomedicine, professional activities related to health care and the actual performance of the duties related to the provision of health care.

concepts.label: Professional Staff Committees
concepts.title: Professional Staff Committees
concepts.definition: Committees of professional personnel who have responsibility for determining policies, procedures, and controls related to professional matters in health facilities.

concepts.label: Professional-Family Relations
concepts.title: Professional-Family Relations
concepts.definition: The interactions between the professional person and the family.

concepts.label: Professional-Patient Relations
concepts.title: Professional-Patient Relations
concepts.definition: Interactions between health personnel and patients.

concepts.label: Prognosis
concepts.title: Prognosis
concepts.definition: A prediction of the probable outcome of a disease based on a individual's condition and the usual course of the disease as seen in similar situations.

concepts.label: Programmed Instructions as Topic
concepts.title: Programmed Instructions as Topic
concepts.definition: Works about instruction in which learners progress at their own rate using workbooks, textbooks, or electromechanical devices that provide information in discrete steps, test learning at each step, and provide immediate feedback about achievement. (ERIC, Thesaurus of ERIC Descriptors, 1996).

concepts.label: Projection
concepts.title: Projection
concepts.definition: A defense mechanism, operating unconsciously, whereby that which is emotionally unacceptable in the self is rejected and attributed (projected) to others.

concepts.label: Projective Techniques
concepts.title: Projective Techniques
concepts.definition: Techniques to reveal personality attributes by responses to relatively unstructured or ambiguous stimuli.

concepts.label: Pronation
concepts.title: Pronation
concepts.definition: Applies to movements of the forearm in turning the palm backward or downward. When referring to the foot, a combination of eversion and abduction movements in the tarsal and metatarsal joints (turning the foot up and in toward the midline of the body).

concepts.label: Propaganda
concepts.title: Propaganda
concepts.definition: The deliberate attempt to influence attitudes and beliefs for furthering one's cause or damaging an opponent's cause.

concepts.label: Proprioception
concepts.title: Proprioception
concepts.definition: Sensory functions that transduce stimuli received by proprioceptive receptors in joints, tendons, muscles, and the INNER EAR into neural impulses to be transmitted to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. Proprioception provides sense of stationary positions and movements of one's body parts, and is important in maintaining KINESTHESIA and POSTURAL BALANCE.

concepts.label: Prosthodontics
concepts.title: Prosthodontics
concepts.definition: A dental specialty concerned with the restoration and maintenance of oral function by the replacement of missing TEETH and related structures by artificial devices or DENTAL PROSTHESES.

concepts.label: Sex Work
concepts.title: Sex Work
concepts.definition: The act or practice of engaging in sexual relations for money or other benefit.

concepts.label: Protein Conformation
concepts.title: Protein Conformation
concepts.definition: The characteristic 3-dimensional shape of a protein, including the secondary, supersecondary (motifs), tertiary (domains) and quaternary structure of the peptide chain. PROTEIN STRUCTURE, QUATERNARY describes the conformation assumed by multimeric proteins (aggregates of more than one polypeptide chain).

concepts.label: Protein Kinases
concepts.title: Protein Kinases
concepts.definition: A family of enzymes that catalyze the conversion of ATP and a protein to ADP and a phosphoprotein.

concepts.label: Protein Precursors
concepts.title: Protein Precursors
concepts.definition: MeSH 已登记该主题词，但此条目未提供范围说明；需继续补全定义。

concepts.label: Proteins
concepts.title: Proteins
concepts.definition: Linear POLYPEPTIDES that are synthesized on RIBOSOMES and may be further modified, crosslinked, cleaved, or assembled into complex proteins with several subunits. The specific sequence of AMINO ACIDS determines the shape the polypeptide will take, during PROTEIN FOLDING, and the function of the protein.

concepts.label: Proteolipids
concepts.title: Proteolipids
concepts.definition: Protein-lipid combinations abundant in brain tissue, but also present in a wide variety of animal and plant tissues. In contrast to lipoproteins, they are insoluble in water, but soluble in a chloroform-methanol mixture. The protein moiety has a high content of hydrophobic amino acids. The associated lipids consist of a mixture of GLYCEROPHOSPHATES; CEREBROSIDES; and SULFOGLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS; while lipoproteins contain PHOSPHOLIPIDS; CHOLESTEROL; and TRIGLYCERIDES.

concepts.label: Protozoan Infections
concepts.title: Protozoan Infections
concepts.definition: Infections with unicellular organisms formerly members of the subkingdom Protozoa.

concepts.label: Pseudorabies
concepts.title: Pseudorabies
concepts.definition: A highly contagious herpesvirus infection affecting the central nervous system of swine, cattle, dogs, cats, rats, and other animals.

concepts.label: Pseudotumor Cerebri
concepts.title: Pseudotumor Cerebri
concepts.definition: A condition marked by raised intracranial pressure and characterized clinically by HEADACHES; NAUSEA; PAPILLEDEMA, peripheral constriction of the visual fields, transient visual obscurations, and pulsatile TINNITUS. OBESITY is frequently associated with this condition, which primarily affects women between 20 and 44 years of age. Chronic PAPILLEDEMA may lead to optic nerve injury (see OPTIC NERVE DISEASES) and visual loss (see BLINDNESS).

concepts.label: Psychiatric Status Rating Scales
concepts.title: Psychiatric Status Rating Scales
concepts.definition: Standardized procedures utilizing rating scales or interview schedules carried out by health personnel for evaluating the degree of mental illness.

concepts.label: Psychiatry
concepts.title: Psychiatry
concepts.definition: The medical science that deals with the origin, diagnosis, prevention, and treatment of mental disorders.

concepts.label: Psychoacoustics
concepts.title: Psychoacoustics
concepts.definition: The science pertaining to the interrelationship of psychologic phenomena and the individual's response to the physical properties of sound.

concepts.label: Psychoanalysis
concepts.title: Psychoanalysis
concepts.definition: The separation or resolution of the psyche into its constituent elements. The term has two separate meanings: 1. a procedure devised by Sigmund Freud, for investigating mental processes by means of free association, dream interpretation and interpretation of resistance and transference manifestations; and 2. a theory of psychology developed by Freud from his clinical experience with hysterical patients. (From Campbell, Psychiatric Dictionary, 1996).

concepts.label: Psychoanalytic Interpretation
concepts.title: Psychoanalytic Interpretation
concepts.definition: Utilization of Freudian theories to explain various psychologic aspects of art, literature, biographical material, etc.

concepts.label: Psychoanalytic Theory
concepts.title: Psychoanalytic Theory
concepts.definition: Conceptual system developed by Freud and his followers in which unconscious motivations are considered to shape normal and abnormal personality development and behavior.

concepts.label: Psychoanalytic Therapy
concepts.title: Psychoanalytic Therapy
concepts.definition: A form of psychiatric treatment, based on Freudian principles, which seeks to eliminate or diminish the undesirable effects of unconscious conflicts by making the patient aware of their existence, origin, and inappropriate expression in current emotions and behavior.

concepts.label: Psychodrama
concepts.title: Psychodrama
concepts.definition: Primarily a technique of group psychotherapy which involves a structured, directed, and dramatized acting out of the patient's personal and emotional problems.

concepts.label: Psycholinguistics
concepts.title: Psycholinguistics
concepts.definition: A discipline concerned with relations between messages and the characteristics of individuals who select and interpret them; it deals directly with the processes of encoding (phonetics) and decoding (psychoacoustics) as they relate states of messages to states of communicators.

concepts.label: Psychological Phenomena
concepts.title: Psychological Phenomena
concepts.definition: Mechanisms and underlying psychological principles of mental processes and their applications.

concepts.label: Psychological Techniques
concepts.title: Psychological Techniques
concepts.definition: Methods used in the diagnosis and treatment of behavioral, personality, and mental disorders.

concepts.label: Psychological Tests
concepts.title: Psychological Tests
concepts.definition: Standardized tests designed to measure abilities (as in intelligence, aptitude, and achievement tests) or to evaluate personality traits.

concepts.label: Psychological Theory
concepts.title: Psychological Theory
concepts.definition: Principles applied to the analysis and explanation of psychological or behavioral phenomena.

concepts.label: Psychology
concepts.title: Psychology
concepts.definition: The science dealing with the study of mental processes and behavior in man and animals.

concepts.label: Psychology, Applied
concepts.title: Psychology, Applied
concepts.definition: The science which utilizes psychologic principles to derive more effective means in dealing with practical problems.

concepts.label: Psychology, Clinical
concepts.title: Psychology, Clinical
concepts.definition: The branch of psychology concerned with psychological methods of recognizing and treating behavior disorders.

concepts.label: Psychology, Comparative
concepts.title: Psychology, Comparative
concepts.definition: The branch of psychology concerned with similarities or differences in the behavior of different animal species or of different races or peoples.

concepts.label: Psychology, Educational
concepts.title: Psychology, Educational
concepts.definition: The branch of psychology concerned with psychological aspects of teaching and the formal learning process in school.

concepts.label: Psychology, Experimental
concepts.title: Psychology, Experimental
concepts.definition: The branch of psychology which seeks to learn more about the fundamental causes of behavior by studying various psychologic phenomena in controlled experimental situations.

concepts.label: Psychology, Industrial
concepts.title: Psychology, Industrial
concepts.definition: The branch of applied psychology concerned with the application of psychologic principles and methods to industrial problems including selection and training of workers, working conditions, etc.

concepts.label: Psychology, Medical
concepts.title: Psychology, Medical
concepts.definition: A branch of psychology in which there is collaboration between psychologists and physicians in the management of medical problems. It differs from clinical psychology, which is concerned with the diagnosis and treatment of behavior disorders.

concepts.label: Psychology, Military
concepts.title: Psychology, Military
concepts.definition: The branch of applied psychology concerned with psychological aspects of selection, assignment, training, morale, etc., of Armed Forces personnel.

concepts.label: Psychology, Social
concepts.title: Psychology, Social
concepts.definition: The branch of psychology concerned with the effects of group membership upon the behavior, attitudes, and beliefs of an individual.

concepts.label: Psychometrics
concepts.title: Psychometrics
concepts.definition: Assessment of psychological variables by the application of mathematical procedures.

concepts.label: Psychomotor Agitation
concepts.title: Psychomotor Agitation
concepts.definition: A feeling of restlessness associated with increased motor activity. This may occur as a manifestation of nervous system drug toxicity or other conditions.

concepts.label: Psychomotor Disorders
concepts.title: Psychomotor Disorders
concepts.definition: Abnormalities of motor function that are associated with organic and non-organic cognitive disorders.

concepts.label: Psychomotor Performance
concepts.title: Psychomotor Performance
concepts.definition: The coordination of a sensory or ideational (cognitive) process and a motor activity.

concepts.label: Psychoneuroimmunology
concepts.title: Psychoneuroimmunology
concepts.definition: The field concerned with the interrelationship between the brain, behavior and the immune system. Neuropsychologic, neuroanatomic and psychosocial studies have demonstrated their role in accentuating or diminishing immune/allergic responses.

concepts.label: Psychopathology
concepts.title: Psychopathology
concepts.definition: The study of significant causes and processes in the development of mental illness.

concepts.label: Psychopharmacology
concepts.title: Psychopharmacology
concepts.definition: The study of the effects of drugs on mental and behavioral activity.

concepts.label: Psychophysics
concepts.title: Psychophysics
concepts.definition: The science dealing with the correlation of the physical characteristics of a stimulus, e.g., frequency or intensity, with the response to the stimulus, in order to assess the psychologic factors involved in the relationship.

concepts.label: Psychophysiologic Disorders
concepts.title: Psychophysiologic Disorders
concepts.definition: A group of disorders characterized by physical symptoms that are affected by emotional factors and involve a single organ system, usually under AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM control. (American Psychiatric Glossary, 1988)

concepts.label: Psychophysiology
concepts.title: Psychophysiology
concepts.definition: The study of the physiological basis of human and animal behavior.

concepts.label: Psychoses, Alcoholic
concepts.title: Psychoses, Alcoholic
concepts.definition: A group of mental disorders associated with organic brain damage and caused by poisoning from alcohol.

concepts.label: Psychoses, Substance-Induced
concepts.title: Psychoses, Substance-Induced
concepts.definition: Psychotic organic mental disorders resulting from the toxic effect of drugs and chemicals or other harmful substance.

concepts.label: Psychosexual Development
concepts.title: Psychosexual Development
concepts.definition: The stages of development of the psychological aspects of sexuality from birth to adulthood; i.e., oral, anal, genital, and latent periods.

concepts.label: Psychosocial Deprivation
concepts.title: Psychosocial Deprivation
concepts.definition: The absence of appropriate stimuli in the physical or social environment which are necessary for the emotional, social, and intellectual development of the individual.

concepts.label: Psychosomatic Medicine
concepts.title: Psychosomatic Medicine
concepts.definition: A system of medicine which aims at discovering the exact nature of the relationship between the emotions and bodily function, affirming the principle that the mind and body are one.

concepts.label: Psychosurgery
concepts.title: Psychosurgery
concepts.definition: Treatment of chronic, severe and intractable psychiatric disorders by surgical removal or interruption of certain areas or pathways in the brain, especially in the prefrontal lobes.

concepts.label: Psychotherapy
concepts.title: Psychotherapy
concepts.definition: A generic term for the treatment of mental illness or emotional disturbances primarily by verbal or nonverbal communication.

concepts.label: Psychotherapy, Brief
concepts.title: Psychotherapy, Brief
concepts.definition: Any form of psychotherapy designed to produce therapeutic change within a minimal amount of time, generally not more than 20 sessions.

concepts.label: Psychotherapy, Group
concepts.title: Psychotherapy, Group
concepts.definition: A form of therapy in which two or more patients participate under the guidance of one or more psychotherapists for the purpose of treating emotional disturbances, social maladjustments, and psychotic states.

concepts.label: Psychotherapy, Multiple
concepts.title: Psychotherapy, Multiple
concepts.definition: The use of more than one therapist at one time in individual or group psychotherapy.

concepts.label: Psychotherapy, Rational-Emotive
concepts.title: Psychotherapy, Rational-Emotive
concepts.definition: The replacement of illogical and unrealistic ideas with more realistic and adaptive ones through direct intervention and confrontation by the therapist.

concepts.label: Psychotic Disorders
concepts.title: Psychotic Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders in which there is a loss of ego boundaries or a gross impairment in reality testing with delusions or prominent hallucinations. (From DSM-IV, 1994)

concepts.label: Psychotropic Drugs
concepts.title: Psychotropic Drugs
concepts.definition: A loosely defined grouping of drugs that have effects on psychological function. Here the psychotropic agents include the antidepressive agents, hallucinogens, and tranquilizing agents (including the antipsychotics and anti-anxiety agents).

concepts.label: Public Health
concepts.title: Public Health
concepts.definition: Branch of medicine concerned with the prevention and control of disease and disability, and the promotion of physical and mental health of the population on the international, national, state, or municipal level.

concepts.label: Public Opinion
concepts.title: Public Opinion
concepts.definition: The attitude of a significant portion of a population toward any given proposition, based upon a measurable amount of factual evidence, and involving some degree of reflection, analysis, and reasoning.

concepts.label: Public Relations
concepts.title: Public Relations
concepts.definition: Relations of an individual, association, organization, hospital, or corporation with the publics which it must take into consideration in carrying out its functions. Publics may include consumers, patients, pressure groups, departments, etc.

concepts.label: Publications
concepts.title: Publications
concepts.definition: Copies of a work or document distributed to the public by sale, rental, lease, or lending. (From ALA Glossary of Library and Information Science, 1983, p181)

concepts.label: Publishing
concepts.title: Publishing
concepts.definition: The business or profession of the commercial production and issuance of literature (Webster's 3d). It includes the publisher, publication processes, editing and editors. Production may be by conventional printing methods or by electronic publishing.

concepts.label: Puerperal Disorders
concepts.title: Puerperal Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders or diseases associated with PUERPERIUM, the six-to-eight-week period immediately after PARTURITION in humans.

concepts.label: Pulmonary Stretch Receptors
concepts.title: Pulmonary Stretch Receptors
concepts.definition: Stretch receptors found in the bronchi and bronchioles. Pulmonary stretch receptors are sensors for a reflex which stops inspiration. In humans, the reflex is protective and is probably not activated during normal respiration.

concepts.label: Pulmonary Valve Stenosis
concepts.title: Pulmonary Valve Stenosis
concepts.definition: The pathologic narrowing of the orifice of the PULMONARY VALVE. This lesion restricts blood outflow from the RIGHT VENTRICLE to the PULMONARY ARTERY. When the trileaflet valve is fused into an imperforate membrane, the blockage is complete.

concepts.label: Punishment
concepts.title: Punishment
concepts.definition: The application of an unpleasant stimulus or penalty for the purpose of eliminating or correcting undesirable behavior.

concepts.label: Pupil Disorders
concepts.title: Pupil Disorders
concepts.definition: Conditions which affect the structure or function of the pupil of the eye, including disorders of innervation to the pupillary constrictor or dilator muscles, and disorders of pupillary reflexes.

concepts.label: Purine-Pyrimidine Metabolism, Inborn Errors
concepts.title: Purine-Pyrimidine Metabolism, Inborn Errors
concepts.definition: Dysfunctions in the metabolism of PURINES or PYRIMIDINES resulting from inborn genetic mutations that are inherited or acquired in utero.

concepts.label: Purkinje Cells
concepts.title: Purkinje Cells
concepts.definition: The output neurons of the cerebellar cortex.

concepts.label: Purpura
concepts.title: Purpura
concepts.definition: Purplish or brownish red discoloration, easily visible through the epidermis, caused by hemorrhage into the tissues. When the size of the discolorization is >2-3 cm it is generally called Ecchymoses (ECCHYMOSIS).

concepts.label: Putamen
concepts.title: Putamen
concepts.definition: The largest and most lateral of the BASAL GANGLIA lying between the lateral medullary lamina of the GLOBUS PALLIDUS and the EXTERNAL CAPSULE. It is part of the neostriatum and forms part of the LENTIFORM NUCLEUS along with the GLOBUS PALLIDUS.

concepts.label: Pyramidal Tracts
concepts.title: Pyramidal Tracts
concepts.definition: Fibers that arise from cells within the cerebral cortex, pass through the medullary pyramid, and descend in the spinal cord. Many authorities say the pyramidal tracts include both the corticospinal and corticobulbar tracts.

concepts.label: Pyridines
concepts.title: Pyridines
concepts.definition: Compounds with a six membered aromatic ring containing NITROGEN. The saturated version is PIPERIDINES.

concepts.label: Pyridinium Compounds
concepts.title: Pyridinium Compounds
concepts.definition: Derivatives of PYRIDINE containing a cation C5H5NH or radical C5H6N.

concepts.label: Pyruvate Carboxylase
concepts.title: Pyruvate Carboxylase
concepts.definition: A biotin-dependent enzyme belonging to the ligase family that catalyzes the addition of CARBON DIOXIDE to pyruvate. It is occurs in both plants and animals. Deficiency of this enzyme causes severe psychomotor retardation and ACIDOSIS, LACTIC in infants. EC 6.4.1.1.

concepts.label: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex
concepts.title: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase Complex
concepts.definition: A multienzyme complex responsible for the formation of ACETYL COENZYME A from pyruvate. The enzyme components are PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE (LIPOAMIDE); dihydrolipoamide acetyltransferase; and LIPOAMIDE DEHYDROGENASE. Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex is subject to three types of control: inhibited by acetyl-CoA and NADH; influenced by the energy state of the cell; and inhibited when a specific serine residue in the pyruvate decarboxylase is phosphorylated by ATP. PYRUVATE DEHYDROGENASE (LIPOAMIDE)-PHOSPHATASE catalyzes reactivation of the complex. (From Concise Encyclopedia Biochemistry and Molecular Biology, 3rd ed)

concepts.label: Q-Sort
concepts.title: Q-Sort
concepts.definition: A personality assessment technique in which the subject or observer indicates the degree to which a standardized set of descriptive statements actually describes the subject. The term reflects sorting procedures occasionally used with this technique.

concepts.label: Quackery
concepts.title: Quackery
concepts.definition: The fraudulent misrepresentation of the diagnosis and treatment of disease.

concepts.label: Quadriplegia
concepts.title: Quadriplegia
concepts.definition: Severe or complete loss of motor function in all four limbs which may result from BRAIN DISEASES; SPINAL CORD DISEASES; PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM DISEASES; NEUROMUSCULAR DISEASES; or rarely MUSCULAR DISEASES. The locked-in syndrome is characterized by quadriplegia in combination with cranial muscle paralysis. Consciousness is spared and the only retained voluntary motor activity may be limited eye movements. This condition is usually caused by a lesion in the upper BRAIN STEM which injures the descending cortico-spinal and cortico-bulbar tracts.

concepts.label: Quality Assurance, Health Care
concepts.title: Quality Assurance, Health Care
concepts.definition: Activities and programs intended to assure or improve the quality of care in either a defined medical setting or a program. The concept includes the assessment or evaluation of the quality of care; identification of problems or shortcomings in the delivery of care; designing activities to overcome these deficiencies; and follow-up monitoring to ensure effectiveness of corrective steps.

concepts.label: Quality of Health Care
concepts.title: Quality of Health Care
concepts.definition: The levels of excellence which characterize the health service or health care provided based on accepted standards of quality.

concepts.label: Quality of Life
concepts.title: Quality of Life
concepts.definition: A generic concept reflecting concern with the modification and enhancement of life attributes, e.g., physical, political, moral, social environment as well as health and disease.

concepts.label: Surveys and Questionnaires
concepts.title: Surveys and Questionnaires
concepts.definition: Collections of data obtained from voluntary subjects. The information usually takes the form of answers to questions, or suggestions.

concepts.label: Race Relations
concepts.title: Race Relations
concepts.definition: Cultural contacts between people of different races.

concepts.label: Radial Nerve
concepts.title: Radial Nerve
concepts.definition: A major nerve of the upper extremity. In humans the fibers of the radial nerve originate in the lower cervical and upper thoracic spinal cord (usually C5 to T1), travel via the posterior cord of the brachial plexus, and supply motor innervation to extensor muscles of the arm and cutaneous sensory fibers to extensor regions of the arm and hand.

concepts.label: Radiation
concepts.title: Radiation
concepts.definition: Emission or propagation of acoustic waves (SOUND), ELECTROMAGNETIC ENERGY waves (such as LIGHT; RADIO WAVES; GAMMA RAYS; or X-RAYS), or a stream of subatomic particles (such as ELECTRONS; NEUTRONS; PROTONS; or ALPHA PARTICLES).

concepts.label: Radiation Effects
concepts.title: Radiation Effects
concepts.definition: The effects of ionizing and nonionizing radiation upon living organisms, organs and tissues, and their constituents, and upon physiologic processes. It includes the effect of irradiation on food, drugs, and chemicals.

concepts.label: Radiation Injuries
concepts.title: Radiation Injuries
concepts.definition: Harmful effects of non-experimental exposure to ionizing or non-ionizing radiation in VERTEBRATES.

concepts.label: Radiculopathy
concepts.title: Radiculopathy
concepts.definition: Disease involving a spinal nerve root (see SPINAL NERVE ROOTS) which may result from compression related to INTERVERTEBRAL DISK DISPLACEMENT; SPINAL CORD INJURIES; SPINAL DISEASES; and other conditions. Clinical manifestations include radicular pain, weakness, and sensory loss referable to structures innervated by the involved nerve root.

concepts.label: Radiography
concepts.title: Radiography
concepts.definition: Examination of any part of the body for diagnostic purposes by means of X-RAYS or GAMMA RAYS, recording the image on a sensitized surface (such as photographic film).

concepts.label: Radiologic Health
concepts.title: Radiologic Health
concepts.definition: Health concerns associated with the effects of radiation on the environment and on public and personal health.

concepts.label: Radionuclide Imaging
concepts.title: Radionuclide Imaging
concepts.definition: The production of an image obtained by cameras that detect the radioactive emissions of an injected radionuclide as it has distributed differentially throughout tissues in the body. The image obtained from a moving detector is called a scan, while the image obtained from a stationary camera device is called a scintiphotograph.

concepts.label: Rage
concepts.title: Rage
concepts.definition: Fury; violent, intense anger.

concepts.label: Random Allocation
concepts.title: Random Allocation
concepts.definition: A process involving chance used in therapeutic trials or other research endeavor for allocating experimental subjects, human or animal, between treatment and control groups, or among treatment groups. It may also apply to experiments on inanimate objects.

concepts.label: Ranvier's Nodes
concepts.title: Ranvier's Nodes
concepts.definition: Regularly spaced gaps in the myelin sheaths of peripheral axons. Ranvier's nodes allow saltatory conduction, that is, jumping of impulses from node to node, which is faster and more energetically favorable than continuous conduction.

concepts.label: Raphe Nuclei
concepts.title: Raphe Nuclei
concepts.definition: Collections of small neurons centrally scattered among many fibers from the level of the TROCHLEAR NUCLEUS in the midbrain to the hypoglossal area in the MEDULLA OBLONGATA.

concepts.label: Rationalization
concepts.title: Rationalization
concepts.definition: A defense mechanism operating unconsciously, in which the individual attempts to justify or make consciously tolerable, by plausible means, feelings, behavior, and motives that would otherwise be intolerable.

concepts.label: Reaction Time
concepts.title: Reaction Time
concepts.definition: The time from the onset of a stimulus until a response is observed.

concepts.label: Reactive Inhibition
concepts.title: Reactive Inhibition
concepts.definition: Tendency toward a lessened strength of response due to practice or activity. It is independent of the effect of reward and is a direct function of time interval since the last response and the number of preceding responses.

concepts.label: Reading
concepts.title: Reading
concepts.definition: Acquiring information from text.

concepts.label: Reality Testing
concepts.title: Reality Testing
concepts.definition: The individual's objective evaluation of the external world and the ability to differentiate adequately between it and the internal world; considered to be a primary ego function.

concepts.label: Reality Therapy
concepts.title: Reality Therapy
concepts.definition: Method of psychotherapeutic treatment based on assumption of patients' personal responsibility for their own behavior. The therapist actively guides patients to accurate self-perception for fulfillment of needs of self-worth and respect for others. (From APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Mental Recall
concepts.title: Mental Recall
concepts.definition: The process whereby a representation of past experience is elicited.

concepts.label: Receptors, Adrenergic
concepts.title: Receptors, Adrenergic
concepts.definition: Cell-surface proteins that bind epinephrine and/or norepinephrine with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes. The two major classes of adrenergic receptors, alpha and beta, were originally discriminated based on their cellular actions but now are distinguished by their relative affinity for characteristic synthetic ligands. Adrenergic receptors may also be classified according to the subtypes of G-proteins with which they bind; this scheme does not respect the alpha-beta distinction.

concepts.label: Receptors, Adrenergic, alpha
concepts.title: Receptors, Adrenergic, alpha
concepts.definition: One of the two major pharmacological subdivisions of adrenergic receptors that were originally defined by the relative potencies of various adrenergic compounds. The alpha receptors were initially described as excitatory receptors that post-junctionally stimulate SMOOTH MUSCLE contraction. However, further analysis has revealed a more complex picture involving several alpha receptor subtypes and their involvement in feedback regulation.

concepts.label: Receptors, Adrenergic, beta
concepts.title: Receptors, Adrenergic, beta
concepts.definition: One of two major pharmacologically defined classes of adrenergic receptors. The beta adrenergic receptors play an important role in regulating CARDIAC MUSCLE contraction, SMOOTH MUSCLE relaxation, and GLYCOGENOLYSIS.

concepts.label: Receptors, Cholecystokinin
concepts.title: Receptors, Cholecystokinin
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind cholecystokinin (CCK) with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Cholecystokinin receptors are activated by GASTRIN as well as by CCK-4; CCK-8; and CCK-33. Activation of these receptors evokes secretion of AMYLASE by pancreatic acinar cells, acid and PEPSIN by stomach mucosal cells, and contraction of the PYLORUS and GALLBLADDER. The role of the widespread CCK receptors in the central nervous system is not well understood.

concepts.label: Receptors, Cholinergic
concepts.title: Receptors, Cholinergic
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind acetylcholine with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Cholinergic receptors are divided into two major classes, muscarinic and nicotinic, based originally on their affinity for nicotine and muscarine. Each group is further subdivided based on pharmacology, location, mode of action, and/or molecular biology.

concepts.label: Receptors, Cyclic AMP
concepts.title: Receptors, Cyclic AMP
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind cyclic AMP with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. The best characterized cyclic AMP receptors are those of the slime mold Dictyostelium discoideum. The transcription regulator CYCLIC AMP RECEPTOR PROTEIN of prokaryotes is not included nor are the eukaryotic cytoplasmic cyclic AMP receptor proteins which are the regulatory subunits of CYCLIC AMP-DEPENDENT PROTEIN KINASES.

concepts.label: Receptors, Dopamine
concepts.title: Receptors, Dopamine
concepts.definition: Cell-surface proteins that bind dopamine with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

concepts.label: Receptors, Cell Surface
concepts.title: Receptors, Cell Surface
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind signalling molecules external to the cell with high affinity and convert this extracellular event into one or more intracellular signals that alter the behavior of the target cell (From Alberts, Molecular Biology of the Cell, 2nd ed, pp693-5). Cell surface receptors, unlike enzymes, do not chemically alter their ligands.

concepts.label: Receptors, Opioid
concepts.title: Receptors, Opioid
concepts.definition: Cell membrane proteins that bind opioids and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. The endogenous ligands for opioid receptors in mammals include three families of peptides, the enkephalins, endorphins, and dynorphins. The receptor classes include mu, delta, and kappa receptors. Sigma receptors bind several psychoactive substances, including certain opioids, but their endogenous ligands are not known.

concepts.label: Receptors, FSH
concepts.title: Receptors, FSH
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind FOLLICLE STIMULATING HORMONE with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells.

concepts.label: Receptors, GABA-A
concepts.title: Receptors, GABA-A
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins which bind GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID and contain an integral membrane chloride channel. Each receptor is assembled as a pentamer from a pool of at least 19 different possible subunits. The receptors belong to a superfamily that share a common CYSTEINE loop.
aliases: gamma Aminobutyric Acid Subtype A Receptors

concepts.label: Receptors, Gastrointestinal Hormone
concepts.title: Receptors, Gastrointestinal Hormone
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind gastrointestinal hormones with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Most gastrointestinal hormones also act as neurotransmitters so these receptors are also present in the central and peripheral nervous systems.

concepts.label: Receptors, LHRH
concepts.title: Receptors, LHRH
concepts.definition: Receptors with a 6-kDa protein on the surfaces of cells that secrete LUTEINIZING HORMONE or FOLLICLE STIMULATING HORMONE, usually in the adenohypophysis. LUTEINIZING HORMONE-RELEASING HORMONE binds to these receptors, is endocytosed with the receptor and, in the cell, triggers the release of LUTEINIZING HORMONE or FOLLICLE STIMULATING HORMONE by the cell. These receptors are also found in rat gonads. INHIBINS prevent the binding of GnRH to its receptors.
aliases: Follicle Stimulating Hormone Releasing Hormone Receptors

concepts.label: Receptors, Gonadotropin
concepts.title: Receptors, Gonadotropin
concepts.definition: Those protein complexes or molecular sites on the surfaces of gonadal and other sensitive cells that bind gonadotropins and thereby modify the functions of those cells; hCG, LH, and FOLLICLE STIMULATING HORMONE are the major specific gonadotropins.

concepts.label: Receptors, Histamine
concepts.title: Receptors, Histamine
concepts.definition: Cell-surface proteins that bind histamine and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Histamine receptors are widespread in the central nervous system and in peripheral tissues. Three types have been recognized and designated H1, H2, and H3. They differ in pharmacology, distribution, and mode of action.

concepts.label: Receptors, Histamine H1
concepts.title: Receptors, Histamine H1
concepts.definition: A class of histamine receptors discriminated by their pharmacology and mode of action. Most histamine H1 receptors operate through the inositol phosphate/diacylglycerol second messenger system. Among the many responses mediated by these receptors are smooth muscle contraction, increased vascular permeability, hormone release, and cerebral glyconeogenesis. (From Biochem Soc Trans 1992 Feb;20(1):122-5)

concepts.label: Receptors, Histamine H2
concepts.title: Receptors, Histamine H2
concepts.definition: A class of histamine receptors discriminated by their pharmacology and mode of action. Histamine H2 receptors act via G-proteins to stimulate ADENYLYL CYCLASES. Among the many responses mediated by these receptors are gastric acid secretion, smooth muscle relaxation, inotropic and chronotropic effects on heart muscle, and inhibition of lymphocyte function. (From Biochem Soc Trans 1992 Feb;20(1):122-5)

concepts.label: Receptors, LH
concepts.title: Receptors, LH
concepts.definition: Those protein complexes or molecular sites on the surfaces and cytoplasm of gonadal cells that bind luteinizing or chorionic gonadotropic hormones and thereby cause the gonadal cells to synthesize and secrete sex steroids. The hormone-receptor complex is internalized from the plasma membrane and initiates steroid synthesis.

concepts.label: Receptors, Muscarinic
concepts.title: Receptors, Muscarinic
concepts.definition: One of the two major classes of cholinergic receptors. Muscarinic receptors were originally defined by their preference for MUSCARINE over NICOTINE. There are several subtypes (usually M1, M2, M3....) that are characterized by their cellular actions, pharmacology, and molecular biology.

concepts.label: Receptors, Nicotinic
concepts.title: Receptors, Nicotinic
concepts.definition: One of the two major classes of cholinergic receptors. Nicotinic receptors were originally distinguished by their preference for NICOTINE over MUSCARINE. They are generally divided into muscle-type and neuronal-type (previously ganglionic) based on pharmacology, and subunit composition of the receptors.

concepts.label: Receptors, Pituitary Hormone
concepts.title: Receptors, Pituitary Hormone
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind pituitary hormones with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes influencing the behavior of cells. Since many pituitary hormones are also released by neurons as neurotransmitters, these receptors are also found in the nervous system.

concepts.label: Receptors, Prolactin
concepts.title: Receptors, Prolactin
concepts.definition: Labile proteins on or in prolactin-sensitive cells that bind prolactin initiating the cells' physiological response to that hormone. Mammary casein synthesis is one of the responses. The receptors are also found in placenta, liver, testes, kidneys, ovaries, and other organs and bind and respond to certain other hormones and their analogs and antagonists. This receptor is related to the growth hormone receptor.

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind PURINES with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. The best characterized classes of purinergic receptors in mammals are the P1 receptors, which prefer ADENOSINE, and the P2 receptors, which prefer ATP or ADP.

concepts.label: Sensory Receptor Cells
concepts.title: Sensory Receptor Cells
concepts.definition: Specialized afferent neurons capable of transducing sensory stimuli into NERVE IMPULSES to be transmitted to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. Sometimes sensory receptors for external stimuli are called exteroceptors; for internal stimuli are called interoceptors and proprioceptors.

concepts.label: Receptors, Serotonin
concepts.title: Receptors, Serotonin
concepts.definition: Cell-surface proteins that bind SEROTONIN and trigger intracellular changes which influence the behavior of cells. Several types of serotonin receptors have been recognized which differ in their pharmacology, molecular biology, and mode of action.

concepts.label: Receptors, Thyrotropin
concepts.title: Receptors, Thyrotropin
concepts.definition: Cell surface proteins that bind pituitary THYROTROPIN (also named thyroid stimulating hormone or TSH) and trigger intracellular changes of the target cells. TSH receptors are present in the nervous system and on target cells in the thyroid gland. Autoantibodies to TSH receptors are implicated in thyroid diseases such as GRAVES DISEASE and Hashimoto disease (THYROIDITIS, AUTOIMMUNE).

concepts.label: Recreation
concepts.title: Recreation
concepts.definition: Activity engaged in for pleasure.

concepts.label: Recruitment, Neurophysiological
concepts.title: Recruitment, Neurophysiological
concepts.definition: The spread of response if stimulation is prolonged. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Recruitment Detection, Audiologic
concepts.title: Recruitment Detection, Audiologic
concepts.definition: Tests for measuring loudness recruitment.

concepts.label: Hyperacusis
concepts.title: Hyperacusis
concepts.definition: An abnormally disproportionate increase in the sensation of loudness in response to auditory stimuli of normal volume. COCHLEAR DISEASES; VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE DISEASES; FACIAL NERVE DISEASES; STAPES SURGERY; and other disorders may be associated with this condition.

concepts.label: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve
concepts.title: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve
concepts.definition: Branches of the vagus (tenth cranial) nerve. The recurrent laryngeal nerves originate more caudally than the superior laryngeal nerves and follow different paths on the right and left sides. They carry efferents to all muscles of the larynx except the cricothyroid and carry sensory and autonomic fibers to the laryngeal, pharyngeal, tracheal, and cardiac regions.

concepts.label: Red Nucleus
concepts.title: Red Nucleus
concepts.definition: A pinkish-yellow portion of the midbrain situated in the rostral mesencephalic tegmentum. It receives a large projection from the contralateral half of the CEREBELLUM via the superior cerebellar peduncle and a projection from the ipsilateral MOTOR CORTEX.

concepts.label: Referral and Consultation
concepts.title: Referral and Consultation
concepts.definition: The practice of sending a patient to another program or practitioner for services or advice which the referring source is not prepared to provide.

concepts.label: Reflex
concepts.title: Reflex
concepts.definition: An involuntary movement or exercise of function in a part, excited in response to a stimulus applied to the periphery and transmitted to the brain or spinal cord.

concepts.label: Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy
concepts.title: Reflex Sympathetic Dystrophy
concepts.definition: A syndrome characterized by severe burning pain in an extremity accompanied by sudomotor, vasomotor, and trophic changes in bone without an associated specific nerve injury. This condition is most often precipitated by trauma to soft tissue or nerve complexes. The skin over the affected region is usually erythematous and demonstrates hypersensitivity to tactile stimuli and erythema. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1360; Pain 1995 Oct;63(1):127-33)
aliases: Complex Regional Pain Syndrome, Type I
Pain Syndrome Type I, Complex Regional
Pain Syndrome Type I, Regional, Complex
Type I Complex Regional Pain Syndrome

concepts.label: Reflex, Abdominal
concepts.title: Reflex, Abdominal
concepts.definition: Contractions of the abdominal muscles upon stimulation of the skin (superficial abdominal reflex) or tapping neighboring bony structures (deep abdominal reflex). The superficial reflex may be weak or absent, for example, after a stroke, a sign of upper (suprasegmental) motor neuron lesions. (Stedman, 25th ed & Best & Taylor's Physiological Basis of Medical Practice, 12th ed, p1073)

concepts.label: Reflex, Abnormal
concepts.title: Reflex, Abnormal
concepts.definition: An abnormal response to a stimulus applied to the sensory components of the nervous system. This may take the form of increased, decreased, or absent reflexes.

concepts.label: Reflex, Acoustic
concepts.title: Reflex, Acoustic
concepts.definition: Intra-aural contraction of tensor tympani and stapedius in response to sound.

concepts.label: Reflex, Monosynaptic
concepts.title: Reflex, Monosynaptic
concepts.definition: A reflex in which the AFFERENT NEURONS synapse directly on the EFFERENT NEURONS, without any INTERCALATED NEURONS. (Lockard, Desk Reference for Neuroscience, 2nd ed.)

concepts.label: Reflex, Oculocardiac
concepts.title: Reflex, Oculocardiac
concepts.definition: Change of heartbeat induced by pressure on the eyeball, manipulation of extraocular muscles, or pressure upon the tissue remaining in the orbital apex after enucleation.

concepts.label: Reflex, Pupillary
concepts.title: Reflex, Pupillary
concepts.definition: Constriction of the pupil in response to light stimulation of the retina. It refers also to any reflex involving the iris, with resultant alteration of the diameter of the pupil. (Cline et al., Dictionary of Visual Science, 4th ed)

concepts.label: Reflex, Stretch
concepts.title: Reflex, Stretch
concepts.definition: Reflex contraction of a muscle in response to stretching, which stimulates muscle proprioceptors.

concepts.label: Reflex, Vestibulo-Ocular
concepts.title: Reflex, Vestibulo-Ocular
concepts.definition: A reflex wherein impulses are conveyed from the cupulas of the SEMICIRCULAR CANALS and from the OTOLITHIC MEMBRANE of the SACCULE AND UTRICLE via the VESTIBULAR NUCLEI of the BRAIN STEM and the median longitudinal fasciculus to the OCULOMOTOR NERVE nuclei. It functions to maintain a stable retinal image during head rotation by generating appropriate compensatory EYE MOVEMENTS.

concepts.label: Refraction, Ocular
concepts.title: Refraction, Ocular
concepts.definition: Refraction of LIGHT effected by the media of the EYE.

concepts.label: Refractive Errors
concepts.title: Refractive Errors
concepts.definition: Deviations from the average or standard indices of refraction of the eye through its dioptric or refractive apparatus.

concepts.label: Refractory Period, Electrophysiological
concepts.title: Refractory Period, Electrophysiological
concepts.definition: The period of time following the triggering of an ACTION POTENTIAL when the CELL MEMBRANE has changed to an unexcitable state and is gradually restored to the resting (excitable) state. During the absolute refractory period no other stimulus can trigger a response. This is followed by the relative refractory period during which the cell gradually becomes more excitable and the stronger impulse that is required to illicit a response gradually lessens to that required during the resting state.

concepts.label: Refractory Period, Psychological
concepts.title: Refractory Period, Psychological
concepts.definition: A delayed response interval occurring when two stimuli are presented in close succession.

concepts.label: Refsum Disease
concepts.title: Refsum Disease
concepts.definition: An autosomal recessive familial disorder that usually presents in childhood with POLYNEUROPATHY; SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS; ICHTHYOSIS; ATAXIA; RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA; and CARDIOMYOPATHIES. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1991, Ch37, p58-9; Rev Med Interne 1996;17(5):391-8) This condition can be caused by mutation in the genes encoding peroxisomal phytanoyl-CoA hydroxylase or proteins associated peroxisomal membrane, leading to impaired catabolism of PHYTANIC ACID in PEROXISOMES.

concepts.label: Regeneration
concepts.title: Regeneration
concepts.definition: The physiological renewal, repair, or replacement of tissue.

concepts.label: Regression, Psychology
concepts.title: Regression, Psychology
concepts.definition: A return to earlier, especially to infantile, patterns of thought or behavior, or stage of functioning, e.g., feelings of helplessness and dependency in a patient with a serious physical illness. (From APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 1994).

concepts.label: Regression Analysis
concepts.title: Regression Analysis
concepts.definition: Procedures for finding the mathematical function which best describes the relationship between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables. In linear regression (see LINEAR MODELS) the relationship is constrained to be a straight line and LEAST-SQUARES ANALYSIS is used to determine the best fit. In logistic regression (see LOGISTIC MODELS) the dependent variable is qualitative rather than continuously variable and LIKELIHOOD FUNCTIONS are used to find the best relationship. In multiple regression, the dependent variable is considered to depend on more than a single independent variable.

concepts.label: Rehabilitation
concepts.title: Rehabilitation
concepts.definition: Restoration of human functions to the maximum degree possible in a person or persons suffering from disease or injury.

concepts.label: Correction of Hearing Impairment
concepts.title: Correction of Hearing Impairment
concepts.definition: Procedures for correcting HEARING DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Reinforcement, Psychology
concepts.title: Reinforcement, Psychology
concepts.definition: The strengthening of a conditioned response.

concepts.label: Reinforcement Schedule
concepts.title: Reinforcement Schedule
concepts.definition: A schedule prescribing when the subject is to be reinforced or rewarded in terms of temporal interval in psychological experiments. The schedule may be continuous or intermittent.

concepts.label: Reinforcement, Social
concepts.title: Reinforcement, Social
concepts.definition: The strengthening of a response with a social reward such as a nod of approval, a parent's love or attention.

concepts.label: Reinforcement, Verbal
concepts.title: Reinforcement, Verbal
concepts.definition: Use of word stimulus to strengthen a response during learning.

concepts.label: Rejection, Psychology
concepts.title: Rejection, Psychology
concepts.definition: Non-acceptance, negative attitudes, hostility or excessive criticism of the individual which may precipitate feelings of rejection.

concepts.label: Relaxation
concepts.title: Relaxation
concepts.definition: Activity which reduces the feelings of tension and the effects of STRESS, PHYSIOLOGICAL.

concepts.label: Relaxation Therapy
concepts.title: Relaxation Therapy
concepts.definition: Treatment to improve one's health condition by using techniques that can reduce PHYSIOLOGICAL STRESS; PSYCHOLOGICAL STRESS; or both.

concepts.label: Religion
concepts.title: Religion
concepts.definition: A set of beliefs concerning the nature, cause, and purpose of the universe, especially when considered as the creation of a superhuman agency. It usually involves devotional and ritual observances and often a moral code for the conduct of human affairs. (Random House Collegiate Dictionary, rev. ed.)

concepts.label: Religion and Psychology
concepts.title: Religion and Psychology
concepts.definition: The interrelationship of psychology and religion.

concepts.label: Religious Philosophies
concepts.title: Religious Philosophies
concepts.definition: Sets of beliefs on the nature of the universe or Man.

concepts.label: Remedial Teaching
concepts.title: Remedial Teaching
concepts.definition: Specialized instruction for students deviating from the expected norm.

concepts.label: Cumulative Trauma Disorders
concepts.title: Cumulative Trauma Disorders
concepts.definition: Harmful and painful condition caused by overuse or overexertion of some part of the musculoskeletal system, often resulting from work-related physical activities. It is characterized by inflammation, pain, or dysfunction of the involved joints, bones, ligaments, and nerves.

concepts.label: Repetitive Sequences, Nucleic Acid
concepts.title: Repetitive Sequences, Nucleic Acid
concepts.definition: Sequences of DNA or RNA that occur in multiple copies. There are several types: INTERSPERSED REPETITIVE SEQUENCES are copies of transposable elements (DNA TRANSPOSABLE ELEMENTS or RETROELEMENTS) dispersed throughout the genome. TERMINAL REPEAT SEQUENCES flank both ends of another sequence, for example, the long terminal repeats (LTRs) on RETROVIRUSES. Variations may be direct repeats, those occurring in the same direction, or inverted repeats, those opposite to each other in direction. TANDEM REPEAT SEQUENCES are copies which lie adjacent to each other, direct or inverted (INVERTED REPEAT SEQUENCES).

concepts.label: Repression, Psychology
concepts.title: Repression, Psychology
concepts.definition: The active mental process of keeping out and ejecting, banishing from consciousness, ideas or impulses that are unacceptable to it.

concepts.label: Repression-Sensitization
concepts.title: Repression-Sensitization
concepts.definition: Defense mechanisms involving approach and avoidance responses to threatening stimuli. The sensitizing process involves intellectualization in approaching or controlling the stimulus whereas repression involves unconscious denial in avoiding the stimulus.

concepts.label: Reproduction
concepts.title: Reproduction
concepts.definition: The total process by which organisms produce offspring. (Stedman, 25th ed)

concepts.label: Reproductive Techniques
concepts.title: Reproductive Techniques
concepts.definition: Methods pertaining to the generation of new individuals, including techniques used in selective BREEDING, cloning (CLONING, ORGANISM), and assisted reproduction (REPRODUCTIVE TECHNIQUES, ASSISTED).

concepts.label: Reproductive and Urinary Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Reproductive and Urinary Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: Physiology of the human and animal body, male or female, in the processes and characteristics of REPRODUCTION and the URINARY TRACT.
aliases: Reproductive and Urinary Tract Physiological Concepts
Reproductive and Urinary Tract Physiological Phenomena
Reproductive and Urinary Tract Physiological Phenomenon

concepts.label: Reproductive Control Agents
concepts.title: Reproductive Control Agents
concepts.definition: Substances used either in the prevention or facilitation of pregnancy.

concepts.label: Research
concepts.title: Research
concepts.definition: Critical and exhaustive investigation or experimentation, having for its aim the discovery of new facts and their correct interpretation, the revision of accepted conclusions, theories, or laws in the light of newly discovered facts, or the practical application of such new or revised conclusions, theories, or laws. (Webster, 3d ed)

concepts.label: Research Design
concepts.title: Research Design
concepts.definition: A plan for collecting and utilizing data so that desired information can be obtained with sufficient precision or so that an hypothesis can be tested properly.

concepts.label: Residence Characteristics
concepts.title: Residence Characteristics
concepts.definition: Elements of residence that characterize a population. They are applicable in determining need for and utilization of health services.

concepts.label: Residential Treatment
concepts.title: Residential Treatment
concepts.definition: A specialized residential treatment program for behavior disorders including substance abuse. It may include therapeutically planned group living and learning situations including teaching of adaptive skills to help patient functioning in the community. (From Kahn, A. P. and Fawcett, J. Encyclopedia of Mental Health, 1993, p320.)

concepts.label: Respiration Disorders
concepts.title: Respiration Disorders
concepts.definition: Diseases of the respiratory system in general or unspecified or for a specific respiratory disease not available.

concepts.label: Respiratory Center
concepts.title: Respiratory Center
concepts.definition: Part of the brain located in the MEDULLA OBLONGATA and PONS. It receives neural, chemical and hormonal signals, and controls the rate and depth of respiratory movements of the DIAPHRAGM and other respiratory muscles.

concepts.label: Respiratory Function Tests
concepts.title: Respiratory Function Tests
