concepts.definition: Measurement of the various processes involved in the act of respiration: inspiration, expiration, oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange, lung volume and compliance, etc.

concepts.label: Respiratory Insufficiency
concepts.title: Respiratory Insufficiency
concepts.definition: Failure to adequately provide oxygen to cells of the body and to remove excess carbon dioxide from them. (Stedman, 25th ed)

concepts.label: Respiratory Paralysis
concepts.title: Respiratory Paralysis
concepts.definition: Complete or severe weakness of the muscles of respiration. This condition may be associated with MOTOR NEURON DISEASES; PERIPHERAL NERVE DISEASES; NEUROMUSCULAR JUNCTION DISEASES; SPINAL CORD DISEASES; injury to the PHRENIC NERVE; and other disorders.

concepts.label: Respiratory System
concepts.title: Respiratory System
concepts.definition: The tubular and cavernous organs and structures, by means of which pulmonary ventilation and gas exchange between ambient air and the blood are brought about.

concepts.label: Respiratory Tract Diseases
concepts.title: Respiratory Tract Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases involving the RESPIRATORY SYSTEM.

concepts.label: Rest
concepts.title: Rest
concepts.definition: Freedom from activity.

concepts.label: Restless Legs Syndrome
concepts.title: Restless Legs Syndrome
concepts.definition: A disorder characterized by aching or burning sensations in the lower and rarely the upper extremities that occur prior to sleep or may awaken the patient from sleep.

concepts.label: Polymorphism, Restriction Fragment Length
concepts.title: Polymorphism, Restriction Fragment Length
concepts.definition: Variation occurring within a species in the presence or length of DNA fragment generated by a specific endonuclease at a specific site in the genome. Such variations are generated by mutations that create or abolish recognition sites for these enzymes or change the length of the fragment.

concepts.label: Retention, Psychology
concepts.title: Retention, Psychology
concepts.definition: The persistence to perform a learned behavior (facts or experiences) after an interval has elapsed in which there has been no performance or practice of the behavior.

concepts.label: Reticular Formation
concepts.title: Reticular Formation
concepts.definition: A region extending from the PONS & MEDULLA OBLONGATA through the MESENCEPHALON, characterized by a diversity of neurons of various sizes and shapes, arranged in different aggregations and enmeshed in a complicated fiber network.

concepts.label: Retina
concepts.title: Retina
concepts.definition: The ten-layered nervous tissue membrane of the eye. It is continuous with the OPTIC NERVE and receives images of external objects and transmits visual impulses to the brain. Its outer surface is in contact with the CHOROID and the inner surface with the VITREOUS BODY. The outer-most layer is pigmented, whereas the inner nine layers are transparent.

concepts.label: Retinal Degeneration
concepts.title: Retinal Degeneration
concepts.definition: A retrogressive pathological change in the retina, focal or generalized, caused by genetic defects, inflammation, trauma, vascular disease, or aging. Degeneration affecting predominantly the macula lutea of the retina is MACULAR DEGENERATION. (Newell, Ophthalmology: Principles and Concepts, 7th ed, p304)

concepts.label: Retinal Diseases
concepts.title: Retinal Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases involving the RETINA.

concepts.label: Retinal Ganglion Cells
concepts.title: Retinal Ganglion Cells
concepts.definition: Neurons of the innermost layer of the retina, the internal plexiform layer. They are of variable sizes and shapes, and their axons project via the OPTIC NERVE to the brain. A small subset of these cells act as photoreceptors with projections to the SUPRACHIASMATIC NUCLEUS, the center for regulating CIRCADIAN RHYTHM.

concepts.label: Retinal Pigments
concepts.title: Retinal Pigments
concepts.definition: Photosensitive protein complexes of varied light absorption properties which are expressed in the PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS. They are OPSINS conjugated with VITAMIN A-based chromophores. Chromophores capture photons of light, leading to the activation of opsins and a biochemical cascade that ultimately excites the photoreceptor cells.

concepts.label: Retinitis Pigmentosa
concepts.title: Retinitis Pigmentosa
concepts.definition: Hereditary, progressive degeneration of the retina due to death of ROD PHOTORECEPTORS initially and subsequent death of CONE PHOTORECEPTORS. It is characterized by deposition of pigment in the retina.

concepts.label: Retrocochlear Diseases
concepts.title: Retrocochlear Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes involving the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE; BRAINSTEM; or CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. When hearing loss is due to retrocochlear pathology, it is called retrocochlear hearing loss.

concepts.label: Retroviridae Infections
concepts.title: Retroviridae Infections
concepts.definition: Virus diseases caused by the RETROVIRIDAE.

concepts.label: Reversal Learning
concepts.title: Reversal Learning
concepts.definition: Any situation where an animal or human is trained to respond differentially to two stimuli (e.g., approach and avoidance) under reward and punishment conditions and subsequently trained under reversed reward values (i.e., the approach which was previously rewarded is punished and vice versa).

concepts.label: Review Literature as Topic
concepts.title: Review Literature as Topic
concepts.definition: Works about published materials which provide an examination of recent or current literature. These articles can cover a wide range of subject matter at various levels of completeness and comprehensiveness based on analyses of literature that may include research findings. The review may reflect the state of the art and may also include reviews as a literary form.

concepts.label: Reward
concepts.title: Reward
concepts.definition: An object or a situation that can serve to reinforce a response, to satisfy a motive, or to afford pleasure.

concepts.label: Reye Syndrome
concepts.title: Reye Syndrome
concepts.definition: A form of encephalopathy with fatty infiltration of the LIVER, characterized by brain EDEMA and VOMITING that may rapidly progress to SEIZURES; COMA; and DEATH. It is caused by a generalized loss of mitochondrial function leading to disturbances in fatty acid and CARNITINE metabolism.

concepts.label: Rheumatic Diseases
concepts.title: Rheumatic Diseases
concepts.definition: Disorders of connective tissue, especially the joints and related structures, characterized by inflammation, degeneration, or metabolic derangement.

concepts.label: Rhombencephalon
concepts.title: Rhombencephalon
concepts.definition: The posterior of the three primitive cerebral vesicles of an embryonic brain. It consists of myelencephalon, metencephalon, and isthmus rhombencephali from which develop the major BRAIN STEM components, such as MEDULLA OBLONGATA from the myelencephalon, CEREBELLUM and PONS from the metencephalon, with the expanded cavity forming the FOURTH VENTRICLE.

concepts.label: Ribosomal Proteins
concepts.title: Ribosomal Proteins
concepts.definition: Proteins found in ribosomes. They are believed to have a catalytic function in reconstituting biologically active ribosomal subunits.

concepts.label: Ribosomes
concepts.title: Ribosomes
concepts.definition: Multicomponent ribonucleoprotein structures found in the CYTOPLASM of all cells, and in MITOCHONDRIA, and PLASTIDS. They function in PROTEIN BIOSYNTHESIS via GENETIC TRANSLATION.

concepts.label: Ribs
concepts.title: Ribs
concepts.definition: A set of twelve curved bones which connect to the vertebral column posteriorly, and terminate anteriorly as costal cartilage. Together, they form a protective cage around the internal thoracic organs.

concepts.label: Riots
concepts.title: Riots
concepts.definition: A form of violent crowd behavior which expresses the emotional release of resentments and prejudices, usually relevant to grievances toward the social system.

concepts.label: Risk
concepts.title: Risk
concepts.definition: The probability that an event will occur. It encompasses a variety of measures of the probability of a generally unfavorable outcome.

concepts.label: Risk Factors
concepts.title: Risk Factors
concepts.definition: An aspect of personal behavior or lifestyle, environmental exposure, inborn or inherited characteristic, which, based on epidemiological evidence, is known to be associated with a health-related condition considered important to prevent.

concepts.label: Risk Management
concepts.title: Risk Management
concepts.definition: The process of minimizing risk to an organization by developing systems to identify and analyze potential hazards to prevent accidents, injuries, and other adverse occurrences, and by attempting to handle events and incidents which do occur in such a manner that their effect and cost are minimized. Effective risk management has its greatest benefits in application to insurance in order to avert or minimize financial liability. (From Slee & Slee: Health care terms, 2d ed)

concepts.label: Risk-Taking
concepts.title: Risk-Taking
concepts.definition: Undertaking a task involving a challenge for achievement or a desirable goal in which there is a lack of certainty or a fear of failure. It may also include the exhibiting of certain behaviors whose outcomes may present a risk to the individual or to those associated with him or her.

concepts.label: RNA Virus Infections
concepts.title: RNA Virus Infections
concepts.definition: Diseases caused by RNA VIRUSES.

concepts.label: ROC Curve
concepts.title: ROC Curve
concepts.definition: A graphic means for assessing the ability of a screening test to discriminate between healthy and diseased persons; may also be used in other studies, e.g., distinguishing stimuli responses as to a faint stimuli or nonstimuli.

concepts.label: Rod Cell Outer Segment
concepts.title: Rod Cell Outer Segment
concepts.definition: The portion of a retinal rod cell situated between the ROD INNER SEGMENT and the RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM. It contains a stack of photosensitive disk membranes laden with RHODOPSIN.

concepts.label: Rodentia
concepts.title: Rodentia
concepts.definition: A mammalian order which consists of 29 families and many genera.

concepts.label: Role
concepts.title: Role
concepts.definition: The expected and characteristic pattern of behavior exhibited by an individual as a member of a particular social group.

concepts.label: Role Playing
concepts.title: Role Playing
concepts.definition: The adopting or performing the role of another significant individual in order to gain insight into the behavior of that person.

concepts.label: Rorschach Test
concepts.title: Rorschach Test
concepts.definition: A projective test used to evaluate a broad range of personality variables including pathology of thought and perception. The subject's responses to inkblot prints are scored along with subjective interpretation by the test administrator.

concepts.label: Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
concepts.title: Rubinstein-Taybi Syndrome
concepts.definition: A chromosomal disorder characterized by MENTAL RETARDATION, broad thumbs, webbing of fingers and toes, beaked nose, short upper lip, pouting lower lip, agenesis of corpus callosum, large foramen magnum, keloid formation, pulmonary stenosis, vertebral anomalies, chest wall anomalies, sleep apnea, and megacolon. The disease has an autosomal dominant pattern of inheritance and is associated with deletions of the short arm of chromosome 16 (16p13.3).
aliases: Broad Thumbs and Great Toes, Characteristic Facies, and Mental Retardation

concepts.label: Running
concepts.title: Running
concepts.definition: An activity in which the body is propelled by moving the legs rapidly. Running is performed at a moderate to rapid pace and should be differentiated from JOGGING, which is performed at a much slower pace.

concepts.label: Saccharopine Dehydrogenases
concepts.title: Saccharopine Dehydrogenases
concepts.definition: Amine oxidoreductases that use either NAD+ (EC 1.5.1.7) or NADP+ (EC 1.5.1.8) as an acceptor to form L-LYSINE or NAD+ (EC 1.5.1.9) or NADP+ (EC 1.5.1.10) as an acceptor to form L-GLUTAMATE. Deficiency of this enzyme causes HYPERLYSINEMIAS.

concepts.label: Saccule and Utricle
concepts.title: Saccule and Utricle
concepts.definition: Two membranous sacs within the vestibular labyrinth of the INNER EAR. The saccule communicates with COCHLEAR DUCT through the ductus reuniens, and communicates with utricle through the utriculosaccular duct from which the ENDOLYMPHATIC DUCT arises. The utricle and saccule have sensory areas (acoustic maculae) which are innervated by the VESTIBULAR NERVE.

concepts.label: Sadism
concepts.title: Sadism
concepts.definition: A condition in which there is a derivation of pleasure from inflicting pain, discomfort or humiliation on another person or persons. The sexual significance of sadistic wishes or behavior may be conscious or unconscious.

concepts.label: Sandhoff Disease
concepts.title: Sandhoff Disease
concepts.definition: An autosomal recessive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by an accumulation of G(M2) GANGLIOSIDE in neurons and other tissues. It is caused by mutation in the common beta subunit of HEXOSAMINIDASE A and HEXOSAMINIDASE B. Thus this disease is also known as the O variant since both hexosaminidase A and B are missing. Clinically, it is indistinguishable from TAY-SACHS DISEASE.
aliases: Deficiency Disease, Hexosaminidase A and B
Hexosaminidase A and B Deficiency Disease

concepts.label: Sarcoma
concepts.title: Sarcoma
concepts.definition: A connective tissue neoplasm formed by proliferation of mesodermal cells; it is usually highly malignant.

concepts.label: Satiation
concepts.title: Satiation
concepts.definition: Full gratification of a need or desire followed by a state of relative insensitivity to that particular need or desire.

concepts.label: Satiety Response
concepts.title: Satiety Response
concepts.definition: Behavioral response associated with the achieving of gratification.

concepts.label: Scapegoating
concepts.title: Scapegoating
concepts.definition: Process in which the mechanisms of projection or displacement are utilized in focusing feelings of aggression, hostility, frustration, etc., upon another individual or group; the amount of blame being unwarranted.

concepts.label: Schistosomiasis
concepts.title: Schistosomiasis
concepts.definition: Infection with flukes (trematodes) of the genus SCHISTOSOMA. Three species produce the most frequent clinical diseases: SCHISTOSOMA HAEMATOBIUM (endemic in Africa and the Middle East), SCHISTOSOMA MANSONI (in Egypt, northern and southern Africa, some West Indies islands, northern 2/3 of South America), and SCHISTOSOMA JAPONICUM (in Japan, China, the Philippines, Celebes, Thailand, Laos). S. mansoni is often seen in Puerto Ricans living in the United States.

concepts.label: Schizoid Personality Disorder
concepts.title: Schizoid Personality Disorder
concepts.definition: A personality disorder manifested by a profound defect in the ability to form social relationships, no desire for social involvement, and an indifference to praise or criticism.

concepts.label: Schizophrenia
concepts.title: Schizophrenia
concepts.definition: A severe emotional disorder of psychotic depth characteristically marked by a retreat from reality with delusion formation, HALLUCINATIONS, emotional disharmony, and regressive behavior.

concepts.label: Schizophrenia, Catatonic
concepts.title: Schizophrenia, Catatonic
concepts.definition: A type of schizophrenia characterized by abnormality of motor behavior which may involve particular forms of stupor, rigidity, excitement or inappropriate posture.

concepts.label: Schizophrenia, Childhood
concepts.title: Schizophrenia, Childhood
concepts.definition: An obsolete concept, historically used for childhood mental disorders thought to be a form of schizophrenia. It was in earlier versions of DSM but is now included within the broad concept of PERVASIVE DEVELOPMENT DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Schizophrenia, Disorganized
concepts.title: Schizophrenia, Disorganized
concepts.definition: A type of schizophrenia characterized by frequent incoherence; marked loosening of associations, or grossly disorganized behavior and flat or grossly inappropriate affect that does not meet the criteria for the catatonic type; associated features include extreme social withdrawal, grimacing, mannerisms, mirror gazing, inappropriate giggling, and other odd behavior. (Dorland, 27th ed)

concepts.label: Schizophrenia, Paranoid
concepts.title: Schizophrenia, Paranoid
concepts.definition: A chronic form of schizophrenia characterized primarily by the presence of persecutory or grandiose delusions, often associated with hallucination.

concepts.label: Schizophrenic Language
concepts.title: Schizophrenic Language
concepts.definition: The artificial language of schizophrenic patients - neologisms (words of the patient's own making with new meanings).

concepts.label: Schizophrenic Psychology
concepts.title: Schizophrenic Psychology
concepts.definition: Study of mental processes and behavior of schizophrenics.

concepts.label: Schizotypal Personality Disorder
concepts.title: Schizotypal Personality Disorder
concepts.definition: A personality disorder in which there are oddities of thought (magical thinking, paranoid ideation, suspiciousness), perception (illusions, depersonalization), speech (digressive, vague, overelaborate), and behavior (inappropriate affect in social interactions, frequently social isolation) that are not severe enough to characterize schizophrenia.

concepts.label: Schwann Cells
concepts.title: Schwann Cells
concepts.definition: Neuroglial cells of the peripheral nervous system which form the insulating myelin sheaths of peripheral axons.

concepts.label: Sciatic Nerve
concepts.title: Sciatic Nerve
concepts.definition: A nerve which originates in the lumbar and sacral spinal cord (L4 to S3) and supplies motor and sensory innervation to the lower extremity. The sciatic nerve, which is the main continuation of the sacral plexus, is the largest nerve in the body. It has two major branches, the TIBIAL NERVE and the PERONEAL NERVE.

concepts.label: Sciatica
concepts.title: Sciatica
concepts.definition: A condition characterized by pain radiating from the back into the buttock and posterior/lateral aspects of the leg. Sciatica may be a manifestation of SCIATIC NEUROPATHY; RADICULOPATHY (involving the SPINAL NERVE ROOTS; L4, L5, S1, or S2, often associated with INTERVERTEBRAL DISK DISPLACEMENT); or lesions of the CAUDA EQUINA.

concepts.label: Science
concepts.title: Science
concepts.definition: The study of natural phenomena by observation, measurement, and experimentation.

concepts.label: Scleroproteins
concepts.title: Scleroproteins
concepts.definition: Simple proteins characterized by their insolubility and fibrous structure. Within the body, they perform a supportive or protective function.

concepts.label: Scotoma
concepts.title: Scotoma
concepts.definition: A localized defect in the visual field bordered by an area of normal vision. This occurs with a variety of EYE DISEASES (e.g., RETINAL DISEASES and GLAUCOMA); OPTIC NERVE DISEASES, and other conditions.

concepts.label: Scrapie
concepts.title: Scrapie
concepts.definition: A fatal disease of the nervous system in sheep and goats, characterized by pruritus, debility, and locomotor incoordination. It is caused by proteinaceous infectious particles called PRIONS.

concepts.label: Sea-Blue Histiocyte Syndrome
concepts.title: Sea-Blue Histiocyte Syndrome
concepts.definition: A congenital disease caused by an inborn error involving APOLIPOPROTEINS E leading to abnormal LIPID METABOLISM and the accumulation of GLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS, particularly SPHINGOMYELINS in the HISTIOCYTES. This disorder is characterized by SPLENOMEGALY and the sea-blue histiocytes in the spleen and bone marrow after May Grunwald staining.

concepts.label: Bodily Secretions
concepts.title: Bodily Secretions
concepts.definition: Endogenous substances produced through the activity of intact cells of glands, tissues, or organs.

concepts.label: Security Measures
concepts.title: Security Measures
concepts.definition: Regulations to assure protection of property and equipment.

concepts.label: Seizures
concepts.title: Seizures
concepts.definition: Clinical or subclinical disturbances of cortical function due to a sudden, abnormal, excessive, and disorganized discharge of brain cells. Clinical manifestations include abnormal motor, sensory and psychic phenomena. Recurrent seizures are usually referred to as EPILEPSY or seizure disorder.

concepts.label: Selection, Genetic
concepts.title: Selection, Genetic
concepts.definition: Differential and non-random reproduction of different genotypes, operating to alter the gene frequencies within a population.

concepts.label: Self-Assessment
concepts.title: Self-Assessment
concepts.definition: Appraisal of one's own personal qualities or traits.

concepts.label: Self Concept
concepts.title: Self Concept
concepts.definition: Persons' view of themselves.

concepts.label: Self Disclosure
concepts.title: Self Disclosure
concepts.definition: A willingness to reveal information about oneself to others.

concepts.label: Self Mutilation
concepts.title: Self Mutilation
concepts.definition: The act of injuring one's own body to the extent of cutting off or permanently destroying a limb or other essential part of a body.

concepts.label: Self Stimulation
concepts.title: Self Stimulation
concepts.definition: The act or process of inducing or increasing the level of arousal in oneself. It can be observed in various situations; for example, infants who are understimulated may explore their surroundings or babble to themselves.(http[已隐藏本地路径] accessed 12/30/2020)

concepts.label: Self-Help Groups
concepts.title: Self-Help Groups
concepts.definition: Organizations which provide an environment encouraging social interactions through group activities or individual relationships especially for the purpose of rehabilitating or supporting patients, individuals with common health problems, or the elderly. They include therapeutic social clubs.

concepts.label: Semantic Differential
concepts.title: Semantic Differential
concepts.definition: Analysis of word concepts by the association of polar adjectives, e.g., good-bad, with the concept, father. The adjectives are usually scaled in 7 steps. The subject's placement of the concept on the adjectival scale indicates the connotative meaning of the concept.

concepts.label: Trigeminal Ganglion
concepts.title: Trigeminal Ganglion
concepts.definition: The semilunar-shaped ganglion containing the cells of origin of most of the sensory fibers of the trigeminal nerve. It is situated within the dural cleft on the cerebral surface of the petrous portion of the temporal bone and gives off the ophthalmic, maxillary, and part of the mandibular nerves.

concepts.label: Sensation
concepts.title: Sensation
concepts.definition: The process in which specialized SENSORY RECEPTOR CELLS transduce peripheral stimuli (physical or chemical) into NERVE IMPULSES which are then transmitted to the various sensory centers in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

concepts.label: Sensation Disorders
concepts.title: Sensation Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders of the special senses (i.e., VISION; HEARING; TASTE; and SMELL) or somatosensory system (i.e., afferent components of the PERIPHERAL NERVOUS SYSTEM).

concepts.label: Sense Organs
concepts.title: Sense Organs
concepts.definition: Specialized organs adapted for the reception of stimuli by the NERVOUS SYSTEM.

concepts.label: Sensitivity and Specificity
concepts.title: Sensitivity and Specificity
concepts.definition: Binary classification measures to assess test results. Sensitivity or recall rate is the proportion of true positives. Specificity is the probability of correctly determining the absence of a condition. (From Last, Dictionary of Epidemiology, 2d ed)

concepts.label: Sensitivity Training Groups
concepts.title: Sensitivity Training Groups
concepts.definition: A group of people who meet in an unstructured setting to learn about themselves, interpersonal relationships, and group processes and about larger social systems.

concepts.label: Sensory Aids
concepts.title: Sensory Aids
concepts.definition: Devices and materials used to extend the functioning of the senses, most often including materials adapted for those  having visual or hearing impairments and also includes materials that have been translated from one sensory mode to another. (ERIC http[已隐藏本地路径] accessed 12/31/2020)

concepts.label: Sensory Deprivation
concepts.title: Sensory Deprivation
concepts.definition: The absence or restriction of the usual external sensory stimuli to which the individual responds.

concepts.label: Sensory Thresholds
concepts.title: Sensory Thresholds
concepts.definition: The minimum amount of stimulus energy necessary to elicit a sensory response.

concepts.label: Septal Nuclei
concepts.title: Septal Nuclei
concepts.definition: Neural nuclei situated in the septal region. They have afferent and cholinergic efferent connections with a variety of FOREBRAIN and BRAIN STEM areas including the HIPPOCAMPAL FORMATION, the LATERAL HYPOTHALAMUS, the tegmentum, and the AMYGDALA. Included are the dorsal, lateral, medial, and triangular septal nuclei, septofimbrial nucleus, nucleus of diagonal band, nucleus of anterior commissure, and the nucleus of stria terminalis.

concepts.label: Septum Pellucidum
concepts.title: Septum Pellucidum
concepts.definition: A triangular double membrane separating the anterior horns of the LATERAL VENTRICLES of the brain. It is situated in the median plane and bounded by the CORPUS CALLOSUM and the body and columns of the FORNIX (BRAIN).

concepts.label: Serial Learning
concepts.title: Serial Learning
concepts.definition: Learning to make a series of responses in exact order.

concepts.label: Serotonin
concepts.title: Serotonin
concepts.definition: A biochemical messenger and regulator, synthesized from the essential amino acid L-TRYPTOPHAN. In humans it is found primarily in the central nervous system, gastrointestinal tract, and blood platelets. Serotonin mediates several important physiological functions including neurotransmission, gastrointestinal motility, hemostasis, and cardiovascular integrity. Multiple receptor families (RECEPTORS, SEROTONIN) explain the broad physiological actions and distribution of this biochemical mediator.

concepts.label: Serotonin Antagonists
concepts.title: Serotonin Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate serotonin receptors, thereby blocking the actions of serotonin or SEROTONIN RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

concepts.label: Serum Globulins
concepts.title: Serum Globulins
concepts.definition: All blood proteins except albumin ( = SERUM ALBUMIN, which is not a globulin) and FIBRINOGEN (which is not in the serum). The serum globulins are subdivided into ALPHA-GLOBULINS; BETA-GLOBULINS; and GAMMA-GLOBULINS on the basis of their electrophoretic mobilities. (From Dorland, 28th ed)

concepts.label: Set, Psychology
concepts.title: Set, Psychology
concepts.definition: Readiness to think or respond in a predetermined way when confronted with a problem or stimulus situation.

concepts.label: Sex
concepts.title: Sex
concepts.definition: The totality of characteristics of reproductive structure, functions, PHENOTYPE, and GENOTYPE, differentiating the MALE from the FEMALE organism.

concepts.label: Sexual Behavior
concepts.title: Sexual Behavior
concepts.definition: Sexual activities of humans.

concepts.label: Sexual Behavior, Animal
concepts.title: Sexual Behavior, Animal
concepts.definition: Sexual activities of animals.

concepts.label: Sex Counseling
concepts.title: Sex Counseling
concepts.definition: Advice and support given to individuals to help them understand and resolve their sexual adjustment problems. It excludes treatment for PSYCHOSEXUAL DISORDERS or PSYCHOSEXUAL DYSFUNCTION.

concepts.label: Disorders of Sex Development
concepts.title: Disorders of Sex Development
concepts.definition: In gonochoristic organisms, congenital conditions in which development of chromosomal, gonadal, or anatomical sex is atypical. Effects from exposure to abnormal levels of GONADAL HORMONES in the maternal environment, or disruption of the function of those hormones by ENDOCRINE DISRUPTORS are included.

concepts.label: Sexual Dysfunction, Physiological
concepts.title: Sexual Dysfunction, Physiological
concepts.definition: Physiological disturbances in normal sexual performance in either the male or the female.

concepts.label: Sex Education
concepts.title: Sex Education
concepts.definition: Education which increases the knowledge of the functional, structural, and behavioral aspects of human reproduction.

concepts.label: Sex Offenses
concepts.title: Sex Offenses
concepts.definition: Any violation of established legal or moral codes in respect to sexual behavior.

concepts.label: Sexual Abstinence
concepts.title: Sexual Abstinence
concepts.definition: Refraining from SEXUAL INTERCOURSE.

concepts.label: Sexual Partners
concepts.title: Sexual Partners
concepts.definition: Married or single individuals who share sexual relations.

concepts.label: Sexually Transmitted Diseases
concepts.title: Sexually Transmitted Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases due to or propagated by sexual contact.

concepts.label: Shame
concepts.title: Shame
concepts.definition: An emotional attitude excited by realization of a shortcoming or impropriety.

concepts.label: Shared Paranoid Disorder
concepts.title: Shared Paranoid Disorder
concepts.definition: A condition in which closely related persons, usually in the same family, share the same delusions.

concepts.label: Sheep Diseases
concepts.title: Sheep Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases of domestic and mountain sheep of the genus Ovis.

concepts.label: Shock
concepts.title: Shock
concepts.definition: A pathological condition manifested by failure to perfuse or oxygenate vital organs.

concepts.label: Shy-Drager Syndrome
concepts.title: Shy-Drager Syndrome
concepts.definition: A progressive neurodegenerative condition of the central and autonomic nervous systems characterized by atrophy of the preganglionic lateral horn neurons of the thoracic spinal cord. This disease is generally considered a clinical variant of MULTIPLE SYSTEM ATROPHY. Affected individuals present in the fifth or sixth decade with ORTHOSTASIS and bladder dysfunction; and later develop FECAL INCONTINENCE; anhidrosis; ATAXIA; IMPOTENCE; and alterations of tone suggestive of basal ganglia dysfunction. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p536)
aliases: Idiopathic Orthostatic Hypotension, Shy Drager Type

concepts.label: Shyness
concepts.title: Shyness
concepts.definition: Discomfort and partial inhibition of the usual forms of behavior when in the presence of others.

concepts.label: Sibling Relations
concepts.title: Sibling Relations
concepts.definition: Interactions and relationships between sisters and/or brothers. The concept also applies to animal studies.

concepts.label: Sick Role
concepts.title: Sick Role
concepts.definition: Set of expectations that exempt persons from responsibility for their illness and exempt them from usual responsibilities.

concepts.label: Sign Language
concepts.title: Sign Language
concepts.definition: A system of hand gestures used for communication by those with HEARING LOSS or by people speaking different languages.

concepts.label: Signal Processing, Computer-Assisted
concepts.title: Signal Processing, Computer-Assisted
concepts.definition: Computer-assisted processing of electric, ultrasonic, or electronic signals to interpret function and activity.

concepts.label: Signs and Symptoms
concepts.title: Signs and Symptoms
concepts.definition: Clinical manifestations that can be either objective when observed by a physician, or subjective when perceived by the patient.

concepts.label: Signs and Symptoms, Digestive
concepts.title: Signs and Symptoms, Digestive
concepts.definition: Digestive system manifestations of diseases of the gastrointestinal system or of other organs.

concepts.label: Signs and Symptoms, Respiratory
concepts.title: Signs and Symptoms, Respiratory
concepts.definition: Respiratory system manifestations of diseases of the respiratory tract or of other organs.

concepts.label: Single Person
concepts.title: Single Person
concepts.definition: The unmarried man or woman.

concepts.label: Sinus Thrombosis, Intracranial
concepts.title: Sinus Thrombosis, Intracranial
concepts.definition: Formation or presence of a blood clot (THROMBUS) in the CRANIAL SINUSES, large endothelium-lined venous channels situated within the SKULL. Intracranial sinuses, also called cranial venous sinuses, include the superior sagittal, cavernous, lateral, petrous sinuses, and many others. Cranial sinus thrombosis can lead to severe HEADACHE; SEIZURE; and other neurological defects.

concepts.label: Size Perception
concepts.title: Size Perception
concepts.definition: The sensory interpretation of the dimensions of objects.

concepts.label: Skeleton
concepts.title: Skeleton
concepts.definition: The rigid framework of connected bones that gives form to the body, protects and supports its soft organs and tissues, and provides attachments for MUSCLES.

concepts.label: Skin Abnormalities
concepts.title: Skin Abnormalities
concepts.definition: Congenital structural abnormalities of the skin.

concepts.label: Skin Diseases
concepts.title: Skin Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases involving the DERMIS or EPIDERMIS.

concepts.label: Skin Diseases, Genetic
concepts.title: Skin Diseases, Genetic
concepts.definition: Diseases of the skin with a genetic component, usually the result of various inborn errors of metabolism.

concepts.label: Skin Manifestations
concepts.title: Skin Manifestations
concepts.definition: Dermatologic disorders attendant upon non-dermatologic disease or injury.

concepts.label: Skin Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Skin Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: The functions of the skin in the human and animal body. It includes the pigmentation of the skin.

concepts.label: Skull Fractures
concepts.title: Skull Fractures
concepts.definition: Fractures of the skull which may result from penetrating or nonpenetrating head injuries or rarely BONE DISEASES (see also FRACTURES, SPONTANEOUS). Skull fractures may be classified by location (e.g., SKULL FRACTURE, BASILAR), radiographic appearance (e.g., linear), or based upon cranial integrity (e.g., SKULL FRACTURE, DEPRESSED).

concepts.label: Sleep
concepts.title: Sleep
concepts.definition: A readily reversible suspension of sensorimotor interaction with the environment, usually associated with recumbency and immobility.

concepts.label: Sleep Apnea Syndromes
concepts.title: Sleep Apnea Syndromes
concepts.definition: Disorders characterized by multiple cessations of respirations during sleep that induce partial arousals and interfere with the maintenance of sleep. Sleep apnea syndromes are divided into central (see SLEEP APNEA, CENTRAL), obstructive (see SLEEP APNEA, OBSTRUCTIVE), and mixed central-obstructive types.

concepts.label: Sleep Deprivation
concepts.title: Sleep Deprivation
concepts.definition: The state of being deprived of sleep under experimental conditions, due to life events, or from a wide variety of pathophysiologic causes such as medication effect, chronic illness, psychiatric illness, or sleep disorder.

concepts.label: Sleep Wake Disorders
concepts.title: Sleep Wake Disorders
concepts.definition: Abnormal sleep-wake schedule or pattern associated with the CIRCADIAN RHYTHM which affect the length, timing, and/or rigidity of the sleep-wake cycle relative to the day-night cycle.

concepts.label: Sleep Stages
concepts.title: Sleep Stages
concepts.definition: Periods of sleep manifested by changes in EEG activity and certain behavioral correlates; they formerly included Stage 1: sleep onset, drowsy sleep; Stage 2: light sleep; Stages 3 and 4: delta sleep, light sleep, deep sleep, telencephalic sleep. In 2007, sleep stages were redefined by The American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) as: N1-N2 (sleep onset - light sleep), N3 (SLOW-WAVE SLEEP), and REM SLEEP.

concepts.label: Sleep, REM
concepts.title: Sleep, REM
concepts.definition: A stage of sleep characterized by rapid movements of the eye and low voltage fast pattern EEG. It is usually associated with dreaming.

concepts.label: Slow Virus Diseases
concepts.title: Slow Virus Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases of viral origin, characterized by incubation periods of months to years, insidious onset of clinical manifestations, and protracted clinical course. Though the disease process is protracted, viral multiplication may not be unusually slow. Conventional viruses produce slow virus diseases such as SUBACUTE SCLEROSING PANENCEPHALITIS, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (LEUKOENCEPHALOPATHY, PROGRESSIVE MULTIFOCAL), and AIDS. Diseases produced by unconventional agents were originally considered part of this group. They are now called PRION DISEASES.

concepts.label: Autacoids
concepts.title: Autacoids
concepts.definition: A chemically diverse group of substances produced by various tissues in the body that cause slow contraction of smooth muscle; they have other intense but varied pharmacologic activities.

concepts.label: Smell
concepts.title: Smell
concepts.definition: The ability to detect scents or odors, such as the function of OLFACTORY RECEPTOR NEURONS.

concepts.label: Smiling
concepts.title: Smiling
concepts.definition: A facial expression which may denote feelings of pleasure, affection, amusement, etc.

concepts.label: Smoke
concepts.title: Smoke
concepts.definition: Visible gaseous suspension of carbon and other particulate matter emitted from burning substances.

concepts.label: Smoking
concepts.title: Smoking
concepts.definition: Willful or deliberate act of inhaling and exhaling SMOKE from burning substances or agents held by hand.

concepts.label: Snake Venoms
concepts.title: Snake Venoms
concepts.definition: Solutions or mixtures of toxic and nontoxic substances elaborated by snake (Ophidia) salivary glands (Duvernoy's gland) for the purpose of killing prey or disabling predators and delivered by grooved or hollow fangs. They usually contain enzymes, toxins, and other factors.

concepts.label: Social Adjustment
concepts.title: Social Adjustment
concepts.definition: Adaptation of the person to the social environment. Adjustment may take place by adapting the self to the environment or by changing the environment. (From Campbell, Psychiatric Dictionary, 1996).

concepts.label: Social Behavior
concepts.title: Social Behavior
concepts.definition: Any behavior caused by or affecting another individual or group usually of the same species.

concepts.label: Social Behavior Disorders
concepts.title: Social Behavior Disorders
concepts.definition: Behaviors which are at variance with the expected social norm and which affect other individuals.

concepts.label: Social Change
concepts.title: Social Change
concepts.definition: A shift, alteration, modification, or evolution of human behavior and culture, which over time, results in measurable consequences on societal values and norms.

concepts.label: Social Conditions
concepts.title: Social Conditions
concepts.definition: The state of society as it exists or in flux. While it usually refers to society as a whole in a specified geographical or political region, it is applicable also to restricted strata of a society.

concepts.label: Social Conformity
concepts.title: Social Conformity
concepts.definition: Behavioral or attitudinal compliance with recognized social patterns or standards.

concepts.label: Social Control, Formal
concepts.title: Social Control, Formal
concepts.definition: Control which is exerted by the more stable organizations of society, such as established institutions and the law. They are ordinarily embodied in definite codes, usually written.

concepts.label: Social Control, Informal
concepts.title: Social Control, Informal
concepts.definition: Those forms of control which are exerted in less concrete and tangible ways, as through folkways, mores, conventions, and public sentiment.

concepts.label: Social Desirability
concepts.title: Social Desirability
concepts.definition: A personality trait rendering the individual acceptable in social or interpersonal relations. It is related to social acceptance, social approval, popularity, social status, leadership qualities, or any quality making him a socially desirable companion.

concepts.label: Psychological Distance
concepts.title: Psychological Distance
concepts.definition: The degree of a person's detachment from emotional involvement with people or situations.(APA Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms accessed 12/29/2020)

concepts.label: Social Dominance
concepts.title: Social Dominance
concepts.definition: Social structure of a group as it relates to the relative social rank of dominance status of its members. (APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Social Environment
concepts.title: Social Environment
concepts.definition: The aggregate of social and cultural institutions, forms, patterns, and processes that influence the life of an individual or community.

concepts.label: Social Facilitation
concepts.title: Social Facilitation
concepts.definition: Any enhancement of a motivated behavior in which individuals do the same thing with some degree of mutual stimulation and consequent coordination.

concepts.label: Social Identification
concepts.title: Social Identification
concepts.definition: The process by which an aspect of self image is developed based on in-group preference or ethnocentrism and a perception of belonging to a social or cultural group. (From APA, Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Social Isolation
concepts.title: Social Isolation
concepts.definition: The separation of individuals or groups resulting in the lack of or minimizing of social contact and/or communication. This separation may be accomplished by physical separation, by social barriers and by psychological mechanisms. In the latter, there may be interaction but no real communication.

concepts.label: Social Justice
concepts.title: Social Justice
concepts.definition: An interactive process whereby members of a community are concerned for the equality and rights of all.

concepts.label: Social Perception
concepts.title: Social Perception
concepts.definition: The perceiving of attributes, characteristics, and behaviors of one's associates or social groups.

concepts.label: Social Problems
concepts.title: Social Problems
concepts.definition: Situations affecting a significant number of people, that are believed to be sources of difficulty or threaten the stability of the community, and that require programs of amelioration.

concepts.label: Social Responsibility
concepts.title: Social Responsibility
concepts.definition: The obligations and accountability assumed in carrying out actions or ideas on behalf of others.

concepts.label: Social Sciences
concepts.title: Social Sciences
concepts.definition: Disciplines concerned with the interrelationships of individuals in a social environment including social organizations and institutions. Includes Sociology and Anthropology.

concepts.label: Social Support
concepts.title: Social Support
concepts.definition: Support systems that provide assistance and encouragement to individuals with physical or emotional disabilities in order that they may better cope. Informal social support is usually provided by friends, relatives, or peers, while formal assistance such as COMMUNITY SUPPORT is provided by churches, groups, etc.

concepts.label: Social Values
concepts.title: Social Values
concepts.definition: Abstract standards or empirical variables in social life which are believed to be important and/or desirable.

concepts.label: Social Welfare
concepts.title: Social Welfare
concepts.definition: Organized institutions which provide services to ameliorate conditions of need or social pathology in the community.

concepts.label: Social Work
concepts.title: Social Work
concepts.definition: The use of community resources, individual case work, or group work to promote the adaptive capacities of individuals in relation to their social and economic environments. It includes social service agencies.

concepts.label: Social Work, Psychiatric
concepts.title: Social Work, Psychiatric
concepts.definition: Use of all social work processes in the treatment of patients in a psychiatric or mental health setting.

concepts.label: Socialization
concepts.title: Socialization
concepts.definition: The training or molding of an individual through various relationships, educational agencies, and social controls, which enables him to become a member of a particular society.

concepts.label: Socioeconomic Factors
concepts.title: Socioeconomic Factors
concepts.definition: Social and economic factors that characterize the individual or group within the social structure.

concepts.label: Socioenvironmental Therapy
concepts.title: Socioenvironmental Therapy
concepts.definition: Therapy whose primary emphasis is on the physical and social structuring of the environment to promote interpersonal relationships which will be influential in reducing behavioral disturbances of patients.

concepts.label: Sociology
concepts.title: Sociology
concepts.definition: A social science dealing with group relationships, patterns of collective behavior, and social organization.

concepts.label: Sociology, Medical
concepts.title: Sociology, Medical
concepts.definition: The study of the social determinants and social effects of health and disease, and of the social structure of medical institutions or professions.

concepts.label: Sociometric Techniques
concepts.title: Sociometric Techniques
concepts.definition: Methods for quantitatively assessing and measuring interpersonal and group relationships.

concepts.label: Software
concepts.title: Software
concepts.definition: Sequential operating programs and data which instruct the functioning of a digital computer.

concepts.label: Psychiatric Somatic Therapies
concepts.title: Psychiatric Somatic Therapies
concepts.definition: The biologic treatment of mental disorders (e.g., ELECTROCONVULSIVE THERAPY), in contrast with psychotherapy. (Stone, American Psychiatric Glossary, 1988, p159)

concepts.label: Somatoform Disorders
concepts.title: Somatoform Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders having the presence of physical symptoms that suggest a general medical condition but that are not fully explained by another medical condition, by the direct effects of a substance, or by another mental disorder. The MEDICALLY UNEXPLAINED SYMPTOMS must cause clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning. In contrast to FACTITIOUS DISORDERS and MALINGERING, the physical symptoms are not under voluntary control. (APA, DSM-V)

concepts.label: Somatosensory Cortex
concepts.title: Somatosensory Cortex
concepts.definition: Area of the parietal lobe concerned with receiving sensations such as movement, pain, pressure, position, temperature, touch, and vibration. It lies posterior to the central sulcus.

concepts.label: Somatostatin
concepts.title: Somatostatin
concepts.definition: A 14-amino acid peptide named for its ability to inhibit pituitary GROWTH HORMONE release, also called somatotropin release-inhibiting factor. It is expressed in the central and peripheral nervous systems, the gut, and other organs. SRIF can also inhibit the release of THYROID-STIMULATING HORMONE; PROLACTIN; INSULIN; and GLUCAGON besides acting as a neurotransmitter and neuromodulator. In a number of species including humans, there is an additional form of somatostatin, SRIF-28 with a 14-amino acid extension at the N-terminal.

concepts.label: Somnambulism
concepts.title: Somnambulism
concepts.definition: A parasomnia characterized by a partial arousal that occurs during stage IV of non-REM sleep. Affected individuals exhibit semipurposeful behaviors such as ambulation and are difficult to fully awaken. Children are primarily affected, with a peak age range of 4-6 years.

concepts.label: Sound Localization
concepts.title: Sound Localization
concepts.definition: Ability to determine the specific location of a sound source.

concepts.label: Space Perception
concepts.title: Space Perception
concepts.definition: The awareness of the spatial properties of objects; includes physical space.

concepts.label: Space-Time Clustering
concepts.title: Space-Time Clustering
concepts.definition: A statistically significant excess of cases of a disease, occurring within a limited space-time continuum.

concepts.label: Spasm
concepts.title: Spasm
concepts.definition: An involuntary contraction of a muscle or group of muscles. Spasms may involve SKELETAL MUSCLE or SMOOTH MUSCLE.

concepts.label: Spasms, Infantile
concepts.title: Spasms, Infantile
concepts.definition: An epileptic syndrome characterized by the triad of infantile spasms, hypsarrhythmia, and arrest of psychomotor development at seizure onset. The majority present between 3-12 months of age, with spasms consisting of combinations of brief flexor or extensor movements of the head, trunk, and limbs. The condition is divided into two forms: cryptogenic (idiopathic) and symptomatic (secondary to a known disease process such as intrauterine infections; nervous system abnormalities; BRAIN DISEASES, METABOLIC, INBORN; prematurity; perinatal asphyxia; TUBEROUS SCLEROSIS; etc.). (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, pp744-8)

concepts.label: Spatial Behavior
concepts.title: Spatial Behavior
concepts.definition: Reactions of an individual or groups of individuals with relation to the immediate surrounding area including the animate or inanimate objects within that area.

concepts.label: Spectrum Analysis
concepts.title: Spectrum Analysis
concepts.definition: The measurement of the amplitude of the components of a complex waveform throughout the frequency range of the waveform. (McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

concepts.label: Speech
concepts.title: Speech
concepts.definition: Communication through a system of conventional vocal symbols.

concepts.label: Speech Acoustics
concepts.title: Speech Acoustics
concepts.definition: The acoustic aspects of speech in terms of frequency, intensity, and time.

concepts.label: Speech Disorders
concepts.title: Speech Disorders
concepts.definition: Acquired or developmental conditions marked by an impaired ability to comprehend or generate spoken forms of language.

concepts.label: Speech Intelligibility
concepts.title: Speech Intelligibility
concepts.definition: Ability to make speech sounds that are recognizable.

concepts.label: Speech Perception
concepts.title: Speech Perception
concepts.definition: The process whereby an utterance is decoded into a representation in terms of linguistic units (sequences of phonetic segments which combine to form lexical and grammatical morphemes).

concepts.label: Speech Production Measurement
concepts.title: Speech Production Measurement
concepts.definition: Measurement of parameters of the speech product such as vocal tone, loudness, pitch, voice quality, articulation, resonance, phonation, phonetic structure and prosody.

concepts.label: Sphingolipidoses
concepts.title: Sphingolipidoses
concepts.definition: A group of inherited metabolic disorders characterized by the intralysosomal accumulation of SPHINGOLIPIDS primarily in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM and to a variable degree in the visceral organs. They are classified by the enzyme defect in the degradation pathway and the substrate accumulation (or storage). Clinical features vary in subtypes but neurodegeneration is a common sign.

concepts.label: Sphingolipids
concepts.title: Sphingolipids
concepts.definition: A class of membrane lipids that have a polar head and two nonpolar tails. They are composed of one molecule of the long-chain amino alcohol sphingosine (4-sphingenine) or one of its derivatives, one molecule of a long-chain acid, a polar head alcohol and sometimes phosphoric acid in diester linkage at the polar head group. (Lehninger et al, Principles of Biochemistry, 2nd ed)

concepts.label: Sphingomyelin Phosphodiesterase
concepts.title: Sphingomyelin Phosphodiesterase
concepts.definition: An enzyme that catalyzes the hydrolysis of sphingomyelin to ceramide (N-acylsphingosine) plus choline phosphate. A defect in this enzyme leads to NIEMANN-PICK DISEASE. EC 3.1.4.12.

concepts.label: Spinal Cord
concepts.title: Spinal Cord
concepts.definition: A cylindrical column of tissue that lies within the vertebral canal. It is composed of WHITE MATTER and GRAY MATTER.

concepts.label: Spinal Cord Compression
concepts.title: Spinal Cord Compression
concepts.definition: Acute and chronic conditions characterized by external mechanical compression of the SPINAL CORD due to extramedullary neoplasm; EPIDURAL ABSCESS; SPINAL FRACTURES; bony deformities of the vertebral bodies; and other conditions. Clinical manifestations vary with the anatomic site of the lesion and may include localized pain, weakness, sensory loss, incontinence, and impotence.

concepts.label: Spinal Cord Diseases
concepts.title: Spinal Cord Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathologic conditions which feature SPINAL CORD damage or dysfunction, including disorders involving the meninges and perimeningeal spaces surrounding the spinal cord. Traumatic injuries, vascular diseases, infections, and inflammatory/autoimmune processes may affect the spinal cord.

concepts.label: Spinal Cord Injuries
concepts.title: Spinal Cord Injuries
concepts.definition: Penetrating and non-penetrating injuries to the spinal cord resulting from traumatic external forces (e.g., WOUNDS, GUNSHOT; WHIPLASH INJURIES; etc.).

concepts.label: Spinal Cord Neoplasms
concepts.title: Spinal Cord Neoplasms
concepts.definition: Benign and malignant neoplasms which occur within the substance of the spinal cord (intramedullary neoplasms) or in the space between the dura and spinal cord (intradural extramedullary neoplasms). The majority of intramedullary spinal tumors are primary CNS neoplasms including ASTROCYTOMA; EPENDYMOMA; and LIPOMA. Intramedullary neoplasms are often associated with SYRINGOMYELIA. The most frequent histologic types of intradural-extramedullary tumors are MENINGIOMA and NEUROFIBROMA.

concepts.label: Spinal Diseases
concepts.title: Spinal Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases involving the SPINE.

concepts.label: Spinal Nerve Roots
concepts.title: Spinal Nerve Roots
concepts.definition: Paired bundles of NERVE FIBERS entering and leaving the SPINAL CORD at each segment. The dorsal and ventral nerve roots join to form the mixed segmental spinal nerves. The dorsal roots are generally afferent, formed by the central projections of the spinal (dorsal root) ganglia sensory cells, and the ventral roots are efferent, comprising the axons of spinal motor and PREGANGLIONIC AUTONOMIC FIBERS.

concepts.label: Spinal Nerves
concepts.title: Spinal Nerves
concepts.definition: The 31 paired peripheral nerves formed by the union of the dorsal and ventral spinal roots from each spinal cord segment. The spinal nerve plexuses and the spinal roots are also included.

concepts.label: Spinocerebellar Degenerations
concepts.title: Spinocerebellar Degenerations
concepts.definition: A heterogenous group of degenerative syndromes marked by progressive cerebellar dysfunction either in isolation or combined with other neurologic manifestations. Sporadic and inherited subtypes occur. Inheritance patterns include autosomal dominant, autosomal recessive, and X-linked.

concepts.label: Spinothalamic Tracts
concepts.title: Spinothalamic Tracts
concepts.definition: A bundle of NERVE FIBERS connecting each posterior horn of the spinal cord to the opposite side of the THALAMUS, carrying information about pain, temperature, and touch. It is one of two major routes by which afferent spinal NERVE FIBERS carrying sensations of somaesthesis are transmitted to the THALAMUS.

concepts.label: Spiral Ganglion
concepts.title: Spiral Ganglion
concepts.definition: The sensory ganglion of the COCHLEAR NERVE. The cells of the spiral ganglion send fibers peripherally to the cochlear hair cells and centrally to the COCHLEAR NUCLEI of the BRAIN STEM.

concepts.label: Spirochaetales Infections
concepts.title: Spirochaetales Infections
concepts.definition: Infections with bacteria of the order SPIROCHAETALES.

concepts.label: Splanchnic Nerves
concepts.title: Splanchnic Nerves
concepts.definition: The major nerves supplying sympathetic innervation to the abdomen. The greater, lesser, and lowest (or smallest) splanchnic nerves are formed by preganglionic fibers from the spinal cord which pass through the paravertebral ganglia and then to the celiac ganglia and plexuses. The lumbar splanchnic nerves carry fibers which pass through the lumbar paravertebral ganglia to the mesenteric and hypogastric ganglia.

concepts.label: Sports
concepts.title: Sports
concepts.definition: Activities or games, usually involving physical effort or skill. Reasons for engagement in sports include pleasure, competition, and/or financial reward.

concepts.label: Sports Medicine
concepts.title: Sports Medicine
concepts.definition: The field of medicine concerned with physical fitness and the diagnosis and treatment of injuries sustained in exercise and sports activities.

concepts.label: Sprains and Strains
concepts.title: Sprains and Strains
concepts.definition: A collective term for muscle and ligament injuries without dislocation or fracture. A sprain is a joint injury in which some of the fibers of a supporting ligament are ruptured but the continuity of the ligament remains intact. A strain is an overstretching or overexertion of some part of the musculature.

concepts.label: Cortical Spreading Depression
concepts.title: Cortical Spreading Depression
concepts.definition: The decrease in neuronal activity (related to a decrease in metabolic demand) extending from the site of cortical stimulation. It is believed to be responsible for the decrease in cerebral blood flow that accompanies the aura of MIGRAINE WITH AURA. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Stanford-Binet Test
concepts.title: Stanford-Binet Test
concepts.definition: An individual intelligence test designed primarily for school children to predict school performance and the ability to adjust to everyday demands.

concepts.label: Reflex, Startle
concepts.title: Reflex, Startle
concepts.definition: A complex involuntary response to an unexpected strong stimulus. The reaction involves physical movement away from the stimulus, MUSCLE CONTRACTION and limb flexion, BLINKING, and changes in HEART RATE, BLOOD PRESSURE, and RESPIRATION.

concepts.label: Starvation
concepts.title: Starvation
concepts.definition: Lengthy and continuous deprivation of food. (Stedman, 25th ed)

concepts.label: Statistics as Topic
concepts.title: Statistics as Topic
concepts.definition: Works about the science and art of collecting, summarizing, and analyzing data that are subject to random variation.

concepts.label: Status Epilepticus
concepts.title: Status Epilepticus
concepts.definition: A prolonged seizure or seizures repeated frequently enough to prevent recovery between episodes occurring over a period of 20-30 minutes. The most common subtype is generalized tonic-clonic status epilepticus, a potentially fatal condition associated with neuronal injury and respiratory and metabolic dysfunction. Nonconvulsive forms include petit mal status and complex partial status, which may manifest as behavioral disturbances. Simple partial status epilepticus consists of persistent motor, sensory, or autonomic seizures that do not impair cognition (see also EPILEPSIA PARTIALIS CONTINUA). Subclinical status epilepticus generally refers to seizures occurring in an unresponsive or comatose individual in the absence of overt signs of seizure activity. (From N Engl J Med 1998 Apr 2;338(14):970-6; Neurologia 1997 Dec;12 Suppl 6:25-30)

concepts.label: Stellate Ganglion
concepts.title: Stellate Ganglion
concepts.definition: A paravertebral sympathetic ganglion formed by the fusion of the inferior cervical and first thoracic ganglia.

concepts.label: Stem Cells
concepts.title: Stem Cells
concepts.definition: Relatively undifferentiated cells that retain the ability to divide and proliferate throughout postnatal life to provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

concepts.label: Stereognosis
concepts.title: Stereognosis
concepts.definition: Perception of shape and form of objects by TOUCH and KINESTHESIS, via tactile stimuli.

concepts.label: Stereotyped Behavior
concepts.title: Stereotyped Behavior
concepts.definition: Relatively invariant mode of behavior elicited or determined by a particular situation; may be verbal, postural, or expressive.

concepts.label: Stereotyping
concepts.title: Stereotyping
concepts.definition: An oversimplified perception or conception especially of persons, social groups, etc.

concepts.label: Steroids
concepts.title: Steroids
concepts.definition: A group of polycyclic compounds closely related biochemically to TERPENES. They include cholesterol, numerous hormones, precursors of certain vitamins, bile acids, alcohols (STEROLS), and certain natural drugs and poisons. Steroids have a common nucleus, a fused, reduced 17-carbon atom ring system, cyclopentanoperhydrophenanthrene. Most steroids also have two methyl groups and an aliphatic side-chain attached to the nucleus. (From Hawley's Condensed Chemical Dictionary, 11th ed)

concepts.label: Stochastic Processes
concepts.title: Stochastic Processes
concepts.definition: Processes that incorporate some element of randomness, used particularly to refer to a time series of random variables.

concepts.label: Stomatognathic System
concepts.title: Stomatognathic System
concepts.definition: The mouth, teeth, jaws, pharynx, and related structures as they relate to mastication, deglutition, and speech.

concepts.label: Strabismus
concepts.title: Strabismus
concepts.definition: Misalignment of the visual axes of the eyes. In comitant strabismus the degree of ocular misalignment does not vary with the direction of gaze. In noncomitant strabismus the degree of misalignment varies depending on direction of gaze or which eye is fixating on the target. (Miller, Walsh & Hoyt's Clinical Neuro-Ophthalmology, 4th ed, p641)

concepts.label: Illicit Drugs
concepts.title: Illicit Drugs
concepts.definition: Drugs that are manufactured, obtained, or sold illegally. They include prescription drugs obtained or sold without prescription and non-prescription drugs. Illicit drugs are widely distributed, tend to be grossly impure and may cause unexpected toxicity.

concepts.label: Streptococcal Infections
concepts.title: Streptococcal Infections
concepts.definition: Infections with bacteria of the genus STREPTOCOCCUS.

concepts.label: Stress Disorders, Post-Traumatic
concepts.title: Stress Disorders, Post-Traumatic
concepts.definition: A class of traumatic stress disorders with symptoms that last more than one month.

concepts.label: Stress, Psychological
concepts.title: Stress, Psychological
concepts.definition: Stress wherein emotional factors predominate.

concepts.label: Student Dropouts
concepts.title: Student Dropouts
concepts.definition: Individuals who leave school, secondary or college, prior to completion of specified curriculum requirements.

concepts.label: Students
concepts.title: Students
concepts.definition: Individuals enrolled in a school or formal educational program.

concepts.label: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
concepts.title: Sturge-Weber Syndrome
concepts.definition: A non-inherited congenital condition with vascular and neurological abnormalities. It is characterized by facial vascular nevi (PORT-WINE STAIN), and capillary angiomatosis of intracranial membranes (MENINGES; CHOROID). Neurological features include EPILEPSY; cognitive deficits; GLAUCOMA; and visual defects.

concepts.label: Stuttering
concepts.title: Stuttering
concepts.definition: A disturbance in the normal fluency and time patterning of speech that is inappropriate for the individual's age. This disturbance is characterized by frequent repetitions or prolongations of sounds or syllables. Various other types of speech dysfluencies may also be involved including interjections, broken words, audible or silent blocking, circumlocutions, words produced with an excess of physical tension, and monosyllabic whole word repetitions. Stuttering may occur as a developmental condition in childhood or as an acquired disorder which may be associated with BRAIN INFARCTIONS and other BRAIN DISEASES. (From DSM-IV, 1994)

concepts.label: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis
concepts.title: Subacute Sclerosing Panencephalitis
concepts.definition: A rare, slowly progressive encephalitis caused by chronic infection with the MEASLES VIRUS. The condition occurs primarily in children and young adults, approximately 2-8 years after the initial infection. A gradual decline in intellectual abilities and behavioral alterations are followed by progressive MYOCLONUS; MUSCLE SPASTICITY; SEIZURES; DEMENTIA; autonomic dysfunction; and ATAXIA. DEATH usually occurs 1-3 years after disease onset. Pathologic features include perivascular cuffing, eosinophilic cytoplasmic inclusions, neurophagia, and fibrous gliosis. It is caused by the SSPE virus, which is a defective variant of MEASLES VIRUS. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp767-8)

concepts.label: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
concepts.title: Subarachnoid Hemorrhage
concepts.definition: Bleeding into the intracranial or spinal SUBARACHNOID SPACE, most resulting from INTRACRANIAL ANEURYSM rupture. It can occur after traumatic injuries (SUBARACHNOID HEMORRHAGE, TRAUMATIC). Clinical features include HEADACHE; NAUSEA; VOMITING, nuchal rigidity, variable neurological deficits and reduced mental status.

concepts.label: Subarachnoid Space
concepts.title: Subarachnoid Space
concepts.definition: The space between the arachnoid membrane and PIA MATER, filled with CEREBROSPINAL FLUID. It contains large blood vessels that supply the BRAIN and SPINAL CORD.

concepts.label: Subcellular Fractions
concepts.title: Subcellular Fractions
concepts.definition: Components of a cell produced by various separation techniques which, though they disrupt the delicate anatomy of a cell, preserve the structure and physiology of its functioning constituents for biochemical and ultrastructural analysis. (From Alberts et al., Molecular Biology of the Cell, 2d ed, p163)

concepts.label: Subclavian Steal Syndrome
concepts.title: Subclavian Steal Syndrome
concepts.definition: A clinically significant reduction in blood supply to the BRAIN STEM and CEREBELLUM (i.e., VERTEBROBASILAR INSUFFICIENCY) resulting from reversal of blood flow through the VERTEBRAL ARTERY from occlusion or stenosis of the proximal subclavian or brachiocephalic artery. Common symptoms include VERTIGO; SYNCOPE; and INTERMITTENT CLAUDICATION of the involved upper extremity. Subclavian steal may also occur in asymptomatic individuals. (From J Cardiovasc Surg 1994;35(1):11-4; Acta Neurol Scand 1994;90(3):174-8)

concepts.label: Subcommissural Organ
concepts.title: Subcommissural Organ
concepts.definition: Ependymal derivative located at the junction of the THIRD VENTRICLE and the CEREBRAL AQUEDUCT; and the SOMATOSTATIN SECRETING CELLS.

concepts.label: Subdural Effusion
concepts.title: Subdural Effusion
concepts.definition: Leakage and accumulation of CEREBROSPINAL FLUID in the subdural space which may be associated with an infectious process; CRANIOCEREBRAL TRAUMA; BRAIN NEOPLASMS; INTRACRANIAL HYPOTENSION; and other conditions.

concepts.label: Empyema, Subdural
concepts.title: Empyema, Subdural
concepts.definition: An intracranial or rarely intraspinal suppurative process invading the space between the inner surface of the DURA MATER and the outer surface of the ARACHNOID.

concepts.label: Subdural Space
concepts.title: Subdural Space
concepts.definition: Potential cavity which separates the ARACHNOID MATER from the DURA MATER.

concepts.label: Subfornical Organ
concepts.title: Subfornical Organ
concepts.definition: A structure, situated close to the intraventricular foramen, which induces DRINKING BEHAVIOR after stimulation with ANGIOTENSIN II.

concepts.label: Sublimation, Psychological
concepts.title: Sublimation, Psychological
concepts.definition: A defense mechanism through which unacceptable impulses and instinctive urges are diverted into personally and socially acceptable channels; e.g., aggression may be diverted through sports activities.

concepts.label: Subliminal Stimulation
concepts.title: Subliminal Stimulation
concepts.definition: Stimulation at an intensity below that where a differentiated response can be elicited.

concepts.label: Submucous Plexus
concepts.title: Submucous Plexus
concepts.definition: One of two ganglionated neural networks which together form the enteric nervous system. The submucous (Meissner's) plexus is in the connective tissue of the submucosa. Its neurons innervate the epithelium, blood vessels, endocrine cells, other submucosal ganglia, and myenteric ganglia, and play an important role in regulating ion and water transport. (From FASEB J 1989;3:127-38)

concepts.label: Substance Withdrawal Syndrome
concepts.title: Substance Withdrawal Syndrome
concepts.definition: Physiological and psychological symptoms associated with withdrawal from the use of a drug after prolonged administration or habituation. The concept includes withdrawal from smoking or drinking, as well as withdrawal from an administered drug.

concepts.label: Substantia Gelatinosa
concepts.title: Substantia Gelatinosa
concepts.definition: Gelatinous-appearing material in the dorsal horn of the spinal cord, consisting chiefly of Golgi type II neurons and some larger nerve cells.

concepts.label: Substantia Innominata
concepts.title: Substantia Innominata
concepts.definition: Tissue in the BASAL FOREBRAIN inferior to the anterior perforated substance, and anterior to the GLOBUS PALLIDUS and ansa lenticularis. It contains the BASAL NUCLEUS OF MEYNERT.

concepts.label: Substantia Nigra
concepts.title: Substantia Nigra
concepts.definition: The black substance in the ventral midbrain or the nucleus of cells containing the black substance. These cells produce DOPAMINE, an important neurotransmitter in regulation of the sensorimotor system and mood. The dark colored MELANIN is a by-product of dopamine synthesis.

concepts.label: Sucking Behavior
concepts.title: Sucking Behavior
concepts.definition: Any suction exerted by the mouth; response of the mammalian infant to draw milk from the breast. Includes sucking on inanimate objects. Not to be used for thumb sucking, which is indexed under fingersucking.

concepts.label: Suggestion
concepts.title: Suggestion
concepts.definition: The uncritical acceptance of an idea or plan of action.

concepts.label: Suicide
concepts.title: Suicide
concepts.definition: The act of killing oneself.

concepts.label: Suicide, Attempted
concepts.title: Suicide, Attempted
concepts.definition: The unsuccessful attempt to kill oneself.

concepts.label: Sulfatases
concepts.title: Sulfatases
concepts.definition: A class of enzymes that catalyze the hydrolysis of sulfate ESTERS.

concepts.label: Superego
concepts.title: Superego
concepts.definition: The component of the personality associated with ethics, standards, and self-criticism - the conscience. It is derived mainly from identification with parents and parent substitutes.

concepts.label: Superior Colliculi
concepts.title: Superior Colliculi
concepts.definition: The anterior pair of the quadrigeminal bodies which coordinate the general behavioral orienting responses to visual stimuli, such as whole-body turning, and reaching.

concepts.label: Superoxide Dismutase
concepts.title: Superoxide Dismutase
concepts.definition: An oxidoreductase that catalyzes the reaction between SUPEROXIDES and hydrogen to yield molecular oxygen and hydrogen peroxide. The enzyme protects the cell against dangerous levels of superoxide.

concepts.label: Supination
concepts.title: Supination
concepts.definition: Applies to movements of the forearm in turning the palm forward or upward. When referring to the foot, a combination of adduction and inversion movements of the foot.

concepts.label: Suppuration
concepts.title: Suppuration
concepts.definition: A pathologic process consisting in the formation of pus.

concepts.label: Suprachiasmatic Nucleus
concepts.title: Suprachiasmatic Nucleus
concepts.definition: An ovoid densely packed collection of small cells of the anterior hypothalamus lying close to the midline in a shallow impression of the OPTIC CHIASM.

concepts.label: Supranuclear Palsy, Progressive
concepts.title: Supranuclear Palsy, Progressive
concepts.definition: A degenerative disease of the central nervous system characterized by balance difficulties; OCULAR MOTILITY DISORDERS (supranuclear ophthalmoplegia); DYSARTHRIA; swallowing difficulties; and axial DYSTONIA. Onset is usually in the fifth decade and disease progression occurs over several years. Pathologic findings include neurofibrillary degeneration and neuronal loss in the dorsal MESENCEPHALON; SUBTHALAMIC NUCLEUS; RED NUCLEUS; pallidum; dentate nucleus; and vestibular nuclei. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp1076-7)

concepts.label: Supraoptic Nucleus
concepts.title: Supraoptic Nucleus
concepts.definition: Hypothalamic nucleus overlying the beginning of the OPTIC TRACT.

concepts.label: Sural Nerve
concepts.title: Sural Nerve
concepts.definition: A branch of the tibial nerve which supplies sensory innervation to parts of the lower leg and foot.

concepts.label: Cardiovascular Surgical Procedures
concepts.title: Cardiovascular Surgical Procedures
concepts.definition: Surgery performed on the heart or blood vessels.

concepts.label: Endocrine Surgical Procedures
concepts.title: Endocrine Surgical Procedures
concepts.definition: Surgery performed on any endocrine gland.

concepts.label: Surgical Procedures, Operative
concepts.title: Surgical Procedures, Operative
concepts.definition: Operations carried out for the correction of deformities and defects, repair of injuries, and diagnosis and cure of certain diseases. (Taber, 18th ed.).

concepts.label: Oral Surgical Procedures, Preprosthetic
concepts.title: Oral Surgical Procedures, Preprosthetic
concepts.definition: Surgery necessary for a denture to rest on a firm base, free from marked osseous protuberances or undercuts, and devoid of interfering muscle attachments, excess mucoperiosteum, hyperplasias, and fibrous or papillary growths.

concepts.label: Urogenital Surgical Procedures
concepts.title: Urogenital Surgical Procedures
concepts.definition: Surgery performed on the urinary tract or its organs and on the male or female genitalia.

concepts.label: Gestational Carriers
concepts.title: Gestational Carriers
concepts.definition: Females who allow themselves to be impregnated with the understanding that the offspring are to be given over to the parents who have commissioned the surrogate.

concepts.label: Sweat Gland Diseases
concepts.title: Sweat Gland Diseases
concepts.definition: Diseases of the SWEAT GLANDS.

concepts.label: Sweating, Gustatory
concepts.title: Sweating, Gustatory
concepts.definition: An autonomic disorder characterized by excessive sweating of the forehead, upper lip, perioral region, or sternum subsequent to gustatory stimuli. The auriculotemporal syndrome features facial flushing or sweating limited to the distribution of the auriculotemporal nerve and may develop after trauma to the parotid gland, in association with PAROTID NEOPLASMS, or following their surgical removal. (From Ann Neurol 1997 Dec;42(6):973-5)

concepts.label: Swimming
concepts.title: Swimming
concepts.definition: An activity in which the body is propelled through water by specific movement of the arms and/or the legs. Swimming as propulsion through water by the movement of limbs, tail, or fins of animals is often studied as a form of PHYSICAL EXERTION or endurance.

concepts.label: Symbolism
concepts.title: Symbolism
concepts.definition: A concept that stands for or suggests something else by reason of its relationship, association, convention, or resemblance. The symbolism may be mental or a visible sign or representation. (From Webster, 3d ed)

concepts.label: Sympathectomy
concepts.title: Sympathectomy
concepts.definition: The removal or interruption of some part of the sympathetic nervous system for therapeutic or research purposes.

concepts.label: Sympathetic Nervous System
concepts.title: Sympathetic Nervous System
concepts.definition: The thoracolumbar division of the autonomic nervous system. Sympathetic preganglionic fibers originate in neurons of the intermediolateral column of the spinal cord and project to the paravertebral and prevertebral ganglia, which in turn project to target organs. The sympathetic nervous system mediates the body's response to stressful situations, i.e., the fight or flight reactions. It often acts reciprocally to the parasympathetic system.

concepts.label: Sympatholytics
concepts.title: Sympatholytics
concepts.definition: Drugs that inhibit the actions of the sympathetic nervous system by any mechanism. The most common of these are the ADRENERGIC ANTAGONISTS and drugs that deplete norepinephrine or reduce the release of transmitters from adrenergic postganglionic terminals (see ADRENERGIC AGENTS). Drugs that act in the central nervous system to reduce sympathetic activity (e.g., centrally acting alpha-2 adrenergic agonists, see ADRENERGIC ALPHA-AGONISTS) are included here.

concepts.label: Sympathomimetics
concepts.title: Sympathomimetics
concepts.definition: Drugs that mimic the effects of stimulating postganglionic adrenergic sympathetic nerves. Included here are drugs that directly stimulate adrenergic receptors and drugs that act indirectly by provoking the release of adrenergic transmitters.

concepts.label: Pathological Conditions, Signs and Symptoms
concepts.title: Pathological Conditions, Signs and Symptoms
concepts.definition: Abnormal anatomical or physiological conditions and objective or subjective manifestations of disease, not classified as disease or syndrome.

concepts.label: Synapses
concepts.title: Synapses
concepts.definition: Specialized junctions at which a neuron communicates with a target cell. At classical synapses, a neuron's presynaptic terminal releases a chemical transmitter stored in synaptic vesicles which diffuses across a narrow synaptic cleft and activates receptors on the postsynaptic membrane of the target cell. The target may be a dendrite, cell body, or axon of another neuron, or a specialized region of a muscle or secretory cell. Neurons may also communicate via direct electrical coupling with ELECTRICAL SYNAPSES. Several other non-synaptic chemical or electric signal transmitting processes occur via extracellular mediated interactions.

concepts.label: Synaptic Membranes
