Plasma glucose concentration is critical to survival for it is the predominant fuel for the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

concepts.label: Data Compression
concepts.title: Data Compression
concepts.definition: Information application based on a variety of coding methods to minimize the amount of data to be stored, retrieved, or transmitted. Data compression can be applied to various forms of data, such as images and signals. It is used to reduce costs and increase efficiency in the maintenance of large volumes of data.

concepts.label: Pedunculopontine Tegmental Nucleus
concepts.title: Pedunculopontine Tegmental Nucleus
concepts.definition: Dense collection of cells in the caudal pontomesencephalic tegmentum known to play a role in the functional organization of the BASAL GANGLIA and in the modulation of the thalamocortical neuronal system.

concepts.label: Complex Mixtures
concepts.title: Complex Mixtures
concepts.definition: Mixtures of many components in inexact proportions, usually natural, such as PLANT EXTRACTS; VENOMS; and MANURE. These are distinguished from DRUG COMBINATIONS which have only a few components in definite proportions.

concepts.label: Molecular Mechanisms of Pharmacological Action
concepts.title: Molecular Mechanisms of Pharmacological Action
concepts.definition: Pharmacological activities at the molecular level of DRUGS and other exogenous compounds that are used to treat DISEASES and affect normal BIOCHEMISTRY.

concepts.label: Physiological Effects of Drugs
concepts.title: Physiological Effects of Drugs
concepts.definition: Activities which affect organs and systemic functions without regard to a particular disease.

concepts.label: Therapeutic Uses
concepts.title: Therapeutic Uses
concepts.definition: Uses of chemicals which affect the course of conditions, diseases, syndromes or pathology to benefit the health of an individual.

concepts.label: Metalloproteases
concepts.title: Metalloproteases
concepts.definition: Proteases which use a metal, normally ZINC, in the catalytic mechanism. This group of enzymes is inactivated by metal CHELATORS.

concepts.label: Enzymes and Coenzymes
concepts.title: Enzymes and Coenzymes
concepts.definition: Biological catalysts and their cofactors.

concepts.label: Refusal to Participate
concepts.title: Refusal to Participate
concepts.definition: Refusal to take part in activities or procedures that are requested or expected of an individual. This may include refusal by HEALTH PERSONNEL to participate in specific medical procedures or refusal by PATIENTS or members of the public to take part in clinical trials or health promotion programs.

concepts.label: Hearing Loss, Unilateral
concepts.title: Hearing Loss, Unilateral
concepts.definition: Partial or complete hearing loss in one ear.

concepts.label: Hearing Loss, Mixed Conductive-Sensorineural
concepts.title: Hearing Loss, Mixed Conductive-Sensorineural
concepts.definition: Hearing loss due to damage or impairment of both the conductive elements (HEARING LOSS, CONDUCTIVE) and the sensorineural elements (HEARING LOSS, SENSORINEURAL) of the ear.

concepts.label: Passeriformes
concepts.title: Passeriformes
concepts.definition: A widely distributed order of perching BIRDS, including more than half of all bird species.

concepts.label: Hypertension, Pregnancy-Induced
concepts.title: Hypertension, Pregnancy-Induced
concepts.definition: A condition in PREGNANT PEOPLE with elevated systolic (>140 mm Hg) and diastolic (>90 mm Hg) blood pressure on at least two occasions 6 h apart. HYPERTENSION complicates 8-10% of all pregnancies, generally after 20 weeks of gestation. Gestational hypertension can be divided into several broad categories according to the complexity and associated symptoms, such as EDEMA; PROTEINURIA; SEIZURES; abnormalities in BLOOD COAGULATION and liver functions.

concepts.label: Freezing Reaction, Cataleptic
concepts.title: Freezing Reaction, Cataleptic
concepts.definition: An induced response to threatening stimuli characterized by the cessation of body movements, except for those that are involved with BREATHING, and the maintenance of an immobile POSTURE.

concepts.label: Immobility Response, Tonic
concepts.title: Immobility Response, Tonic
concepts.definition: An induced response to threatening stimuli characterized by complete loss of muscle strength.

concepts.label: Neuroepithelial Bodies
concepts.title: Neuroepithelial Bodies
concepts.definition: Innervated clusters of NEUROEPITHELIAL CELLS found in the LUNGS. They act as airway OXYGEN sensors, releasing regulatory PEPTIDES and SEROTONIN in response to HYPOXIA.

concepts.label: Neuroepithelial Cells
concepts.title: Neuroepithelial Cells
concepts.definition: Cells of epithelial origin possessing specialized sensory functions. They include cells that are found in the TASTE BUDS; OLFACTORY MUCOSA; COCHLEA; and NEUROEPITHELIAL BODIES.

concepts.label: CADASIL
concepts.title: CADASIL
concepts.definition: A familial, cerebral arteriopathy mapped to chromosome 19q12, and characterized by the presence of granular deposits in small CEREBRAL ARTERIES producing ischemic STROKE; PSEUDOBULBAR PALSY; and multiple subcortical infarcts (CEREBRAL INFARCTION). CADASIL is an acronym for Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy. CADASIL differs from BINSWANGER DISEASE by the presence of MIGRAINE WITH AURA and usually by the lack of history of arterial HYPERTENSION. (From Bradley et al, Neurology in Clinical Practice, 2000, p1146)
aliases: Cerebral Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy
Cerebral Autosomal Dominant Arteriopathy with Subcortical Infarcts and Leukoencephalopathy

concepts.label: Synkinesis
concepts.title: Synkinesis
concepts.definition: An involuntary movement accompanying a volitional movement. It often refers to facial movements that accompany FACIAL PARALYSIS.

concepts.label: Hematoma, Subdural, Intracranial
concepts.title: Hematoma, Subdural, Intracranial
concepts.definition: Accumulation of blood in the SUBDURAL SPACE over the CEREBRAL HEMISPHERE.

concepts.label: Pattern Recognition, Physiological
concepts.title: Pattern Recognition, Physiological
concepts.definition: The analysis of a critical number of sensory stimuli or facts (the pattern) by physiological processes such as vision (PATTERN RECOGNITION, VISUAL), touch, or hearing.

concepts.label: Macromolecular Substances
concepts.title: Macromolecular Substances
concepts.definition: Compounds and molecular complexes that consist of very large numbers of atoms and are generally over 500 kDa in size. In biological systems macromolecular substances usually can be visualized using ELECTRON MICROSCOPY and are distinguished from ORGANELLES by the lack of a membrane structure.

concepts.label: Multiprotein Complexes
concepts.title: Multiprotein Complexes
concepts.definition: Macromolecular complexes formed from the association of defined protein subunits.

concepts.label: Unsafe Sex
concepts.title: Unsafe Sex
concepts.definition: Sexual behaviors which are high-risk for contracting SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES or for producing PREGNANCY.

concepts.label: Pituitary ACTH Hypersecretion
concepts.title: Pituitary ACTH Hypersecretion
concepts.definition: A disease of the PITUITARY GLAND characterized by the excess amount of ADRENOCORTICOTROPIC HORMONE secreted. This leads to hypersecretion of cortisol (HYDROCORTISONE) by the ADRENAL GLANDS resulting in CUSHING SYNDROME.

concepts.label: Intracellular Signaling Peptides and Proteins
concepts.title: Intracellular Signaling Peptides and Proteins
concepts.definition: Proteins and peptides that are involved in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION within the cell. Included here are peptides and proteins that regulate the activity of TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS and cellular processes in response to signals from CELL SURFACE RECEPTORS. Intracellular signaling peptide and proteins may be part of an enzymatic signaling cascade or act through binding to and modifying the action of other signaling factors.

concepts.label: Informatics
concepts.title: Informatics
concepts.definition: The field of information science concerned with the analysis and dissemination of data through the application of computers.

concepts.label: Hepatic Insufficiency
concepts.title: Hepatic Insufficiency
concepts.definition: Conditions in which the LIVER functions fall below the normal ranges. Severe hepatic insufficiency may cause LIVER FAILURE or DEATH. Treatment may include LIVER TRANSPLANTATION.

concepts.label: Growth and Development
concepts.title: Growth and Development
concepts.definition: The series of changes to the shape, size, components, and functions of an individual organism that occur over time as the organism progresses from its initial form to full size and maturity.

concepts.label: Diabetes Complications
concepts.title: Diabetes Complications
concepts.definition: Conditions or pathological processes associated with the disease of diabetes mellitus. Due to the impaired control of BLOOD GLUCOSE level in diabetic patients, pathological processes develop in numerous tissues and organs including the EYE, the KIDNEY, the BLOOD VESSELS, and the NERVE TISSUE.

concepts.label: Labor Pain
concepts.title: Labor Pain
concepts.definition: Pain associated with OBSTETRIC LABOR in CHILDBIRTH. It is caused primarily by UTERINE CONTRACTION as well as pressure on the CERVIX; BLADDER; and the GASTROINTESTINAL TRACT. Labor pain mostly occurs in the ABDOMEN; the GROIN; and the BACK.

concepts.label: Dystrophin-Associated Proteins
concepts.title: Dystrophin-Associated Proteins
concepts.definition: A group of proteins that associate with DYSTROPHIN at the CELL MEMBRANE to form the DYSTROPHIN-ASSOCIATED PROTEIN COMPLEX.

concepts.label: Dystroglycans
concepts.title: Dystroglycans
concepts.definition: Dystrophin-associated proteins that play role in the formation of a transmembrane link between laminin-2 and DYSTROPHIN. Both the alpha and the beta subtypes of dystroglycan originate via POST-TRANSLATIONAL PROTEIN PROCESSING of a single precursor protein.

concepts.label: Sphingolipid Activator Proteins
concepts.title: Sphingolipid Activator Proteins
concepts.definition: A family of glycoprotein cofactors that are required for the efficient catabolization of SPHINGOLIPIDS by specific acid hydrolases such as GLUCOSYLCERAMIDASE; GALACTOCEREBROSIDASE; BETA-N-ACETYLHEXOSAMINIDASE; and CEREBROSIDE-SULFATASE.

concepts.label: Dendritic Spines
concepts.title: Dendritic Spines
concepts.definition: Spiny processes on DENDRITES, each of which receives excitatory input from one nerve ending (NERVE ENDINGS). They are commonly found on PURKINJE CELLS and PYRAMIDAL CELLS.

concepts.label: Speech Recognition Software
concepts.title: Speech Recognition Software
concepts.definition: Software capable of recognizing dictation and transcribing the spoken words into written text.

concepts.label: Muscular Dystrophies, Limb-Girdle
concepts.title: Muscular Dystrophies, Limb-Girdle
concepts.definition: A heterogenous group of inherited muscular dystrophy that can be autosomal dominant or autosomal recessive. There are many forms (called LGMDs) involving genes encoding muscle membrane proteins such as the sarcoglycan (SARCOGLYCANS) complex that interacts with DYSTROPHIN. The disease is characterized by progressing wasting and weakness of the proximal muscles of arms and legs around the HIPS and SHOULDERS (the pelvic and shoulder girdles).

concepts.label: G(M2) Activator Protein
concepts.title: G(M2) Activator Protein
concepts.definition: An essential cofactor for the degradation of G(M2)GANGLIOSIDE by lysosomal BETA-N-ACETYLHEXOSAMINIDASES. Genetic mutations resulting in loss of G(M2) activator protein are one of the causes of TAY-SACHS DISEASE, AB VARIANT.

concepts.label: Tay-Sachs Disease, AB Variant
concepts.title: Tay-Sachs Disease, AB Variant
concepts.definition: A progressive neurodegenerative disorder that begins with muscle weakness, then progresses to startle reaction, retardation and seizures. It is characterized by the accumulation of G(M2) GANGLIOSIDE in neurons that is caused by a lack of G(M2) ACTIVATOR PROTEIN function. The AB variant designation refers to the increase of both HEXOSAMINIDASE A and HEXOSAMINIDASE B in tissues that lack of G(M2) activator protein.

concepts.label: Distal Myopathies
concepts.title: Distal Myopathies
concepts.definition: A heterogeneous group of genetic disorders characterized by progressive MUSCULAR ATROPHY and MUSCLE WEAKNESS beginning in the hands, the legs, or the feet. Most are adult-onset autosomal dominant forms. Others are autosomal recessive.

concepts.label: Blood-Nerve Barrier
concepts.title: Blood-Nerve Barrier
concepts.definition: The barrier between the perineurium of PERIPHERAL NERVES and the endothelium (ENDOTHELIUM, VASCULAR) of endoneurial CAPILLARIES. The perineurium acts as a diffusion barrier, but ion permeability at the blood-nerve barrier is still higher than at the BLOOD-BRAIN BARRIER.

concepts.label: Nomograms
concepts.title: Nomograms
concepts.definition: Graphical representation of a statistical model containing scales for calculating the prognostic weight of a value for each individual variable. Nomograms are instruments that can be used to predict outcomes using specific clinical parameters. They use ALGORITHMS that incorporate several variables to calculate the predicted probability that a patient will achieve a particular clinical endpoint.

concepts.label: Postpartum Period
concepts.title: Postpartum Period
concepts.definition: In females, the period that is shortly after giving birth (PARTURITION).

concepts.label: Growth Hormone-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma
concepts.title: Growth Hormone-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma
concepts.definition: A pituitary tumor that secretes GROWTH HORMONE. In humans, excess HUMAN GROWTH HORMONE leads to ACROMEGALY.

concepts.label: ACTH-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma
concepts.title: ACTH-Secreting Pituitary Adenoma
concepts.definition: A pituitary adenoma which secretes ADRENOCORTICOTROPIN, leading to CUSHING DISEASE.

concepts.label: DNA Repair-Deficiency Disorders
concepts.title: DNA Repair-Deficiency Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders resulting from defective DNA REPAIR processes or the associated cellular responses to DNA DAMAGE.

concepts.label: Membrane Transport Modulators
concepts.title: Membrane Transport Modulators
concepts.definition: Agents that affect ION PUMPS; ION CHANNELS; ABC TRANSPORTERS; and other MEMBRANE TRANSPORT PROTEINS.

concepts.label: Bone Density Conservation Agents
concepts.title: Bone Density Conservation Agents
concepts.definition: Agents that inhibit BONE RESORPTION and/or favor BONE MINERALIZATION and BONE REGENERATION. They are used to heal BONE FRACTURES and to treat METABOLIC BONE DISEASES such as OSTEOPOROSIS.

concepts.label: Dyslipidemias
concepts.title: Dyslipidemias
concepts.definition: Abnormalities in the serum levels of LIPIDS, including overproduction or deficiency. Abnormal serum lipid profiles may include high total CHOLESTEROL, high TRIGLYCERIDES, low HIGH DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN CHOLESTEROL, and elevated LOW DENSITY LIPOPROTEIN CHOLESTEROL.

concepts.label: Overweight
concepts.title: Overweight
concepts.definition: A status with BODY WEIGHT that is above certain standards. In the scale of BODY MASS INDEX, overweight is defined as having a BMI of 25.0-29.9 kg/m2. Overweight may or may not be due to increases in body fat (ADIPOSE TISSUE), hence overweight does not equal over fat.

concepts.label: Neurotransmitter Transport Proteins
concepts.title: Neurotransmitter Transport Proteins
concepts.definition: Membrane transport proteins found predominately in NEURONS and neuroendocrine cells that facilitate neurotransmitter transport. They include two distinct families of proteins that transport NEUROTRANSMITTERS across the PLASMA MEMBRANE and that transport NEUROTRANSMITTERS into SECRETORY VESICLES.

concepts.label: Plasma Membrane Neurotransmitter Transport Proteins
concepts.title: Plasma Membrane Neurotransmitter Transport Proteins
concepts.definition: A family of neurotransmitter transporter proteins that facilitate NEUROTRANSMITTER reuptake into PRESYNAPTIC TERMINALS. They may play a role in regulating the intensity and duration of neurotransmission.

concepts.label: GABA Plasma Membrane Transport Proteins
concepts.title: GABA Plasma Membrane Transport Proteins
concepts.definition: A family of plasma membrane neurotransmitter transporter proteins that regulates extracellular levels of the inhibitory neurotransmitter GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID. They differ from GABA RECEPTORS, which signal cellular responses to GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID. They control GABA reuptake into PRESYNAPTIC TERMINALS in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM through high-affinity sodium-dependent transport.
aliases: Gamma Aminobutyric Acid Plasma Membrane Transport Proteins
Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid Plasma Membrane Transport Proteins

concepts.label: Glycine Plasma Membrane Transport Proteins
concepts.title: Glycine Plasma Membrane Transport Proteins
concepts.definition: A family of sodium chloride-dependent neurotransmitter symporters that transport the amino acid GLYCINE. They differ from GLYCINE RECEPTORS, which signal cellular responses to GLYCINE. They are located primarily on the PLASMA MEMBRANE of NEURONS; GLIAL CELLS; EPITHELIAL CELLS; and RED BLOOD CELLS where they remove inhibitory neurotransmitter glycine from the EXTRACELLULAR SPACE.

concepts.label: Receptors, Dopamine D3
concepts.title: Receptors, Dopamine D3
concepts.definition: A subtype of dopamine D2 receptors that are highly expressed in the LIMBIC SYSTEM of the brain.

concepts.label: Receptors, Dopamine D4
concepts.title: Receptors, Dopamine D4
concepts.definition: A subtype of dopamine D2 receptors that has high affinity for the antipsychotic CLOZAPINE.

concepts.label: Receptors, Dopamine D5
concepts.title: Receptors, Dopamine D5
concepts.definition: A subtype of dopamine D1 receptors that has higher affinity for DOPAMINE and differentially couples to GTP-BINDING PROTEINS.

concepts.label: Fractures, Bone
concepts.title: Fractures, Bone
concepts.definition: Breaks in bones.

concepts.label: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
concepts.title: Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation
concepts.definition: A technique that involves the use of electrical coils on the head to generate a brief magnetic field which reaches the CEREBRAL CORTEX. It is coupled with ELECTROMYOGRAPHY response detection to assess cortical excitability by the threshold required to induce MOTOR EVOKED POTENTIALS. This method is also used for BRAIN MAPPING, to study NEUROPHYSIOLOGY, and as a substitute for ELECTROCONVULSIVE THERAPY for treating DEPRESSION. Induction of SEIZURES limits its clinical usage.

concepts.label: SUNCT Syndrome
concepts.title: SUNCT Syndrome
concepts.definition: A primary headache disorder that is characterized by frequent short-lasting, unilateral, neuralgiform pain attacks in the ocular area, with CONJUNCTIVA fluid-filling and tearing. SUNCT syndrome is usually resistant to treatment.

concepts.label: Split-Brain Procedure
concepts.title: Split-Brain Procedure
concepts.definition: Complete severing of the CORPUS CALLOSUM. In humans it is usually performed to treat medically intractable, multifocal EPILEPSY. EXPERIMENTAL ANIMAL MODELS of split brain preparations are used in research.

concepts.label: Oxidoreductases Acting on CH-NH2 Group Donors
concepts.title: Oxidoreductases Acting on CH-NH2 Group Donors
concepts.definition: Enzymes catalyzing the dehydrogenation of or oxidation of compounds containing primary amines.
aliases: Oxidoreductases Acting on CH NH2 Group Donors

concepts.label: Catarrhini
concepts.title: Catarrhini
concepts.definition: An infraorder of PRIMATES comprised of the families CERCOPITHECIDAE (old world monkeys); HYLOBATIDAE (siamangs and GIBBONS); and HOMINIDAE (great apes and HUMANS). With the exception of humans, they all live exclusively in Africa and Asia.

concepts.label: Murinae
concepts.title: Murinae
concepts.definition: A subfamily in the family MURIDAE, comprising the Old World MICE and RATS.

concepts.label: Receptors, Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase-Activating Polypeptide
concepts.title: Receptors, Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase-Activating Polypeptide
concepts.definition: A family of G-protein-coupled receptors that share significant homology with GLUCAGON RECEPTORS. They bind PITUITARY ADENYLATE CYCLASE ACTIVATING POLYPEPTIDE with high affinity and trigger intracellular changes that influence the behavior of CELLS.
aliases: Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase Activating Peptide Receptor
Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase Activating Peptide Receptors
Receptors, Pituitary Adenylate Cyclase Activating Polypeptide

concepts.label: Retinal Bipolar Cells
concepts.title: Retinal Bipolar Cells
concepts.definition: INTERNEURONS of the vertebrate RETINA containing two processes. They receive inputs from the RETINAL PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS and send outputs to the RETINAL GANGLION CELLS. The bipolar cells also make lateral connections in the retina with the RETINAL HORIZONTAL CELLS and with the AMACRINE CELLS.

concepts.label: Retinal Horizontal Cells
concepts.title: Retinal Horizontal Cells
concepts.definition: NEURONS in the inner nuclear layer of the RETINA that synapse with both the RETINAL PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS and the RETINAL BIPOLAR CELLS, as well as other horizontal cells. The horizontal cells modulate the sensory signal.

concepts.label: Headache Disorders, Primary
concepts.title: Headache Disorders, Primary
concepts.definition: Conditions in which the primary symptom is HEADACHE and the headache cannot be attributed to any known causes.

concepts.label: Headache Disorders, Secondary
concepts.title: Headache Disorders, Secondary
concepts.definition: Conditions with HEADACHE symptom that can be attributed to a variety of causes including BRAIN VASCULAR DISORDERS; WOUNDS AND INJURIES; INFECTION; drug use or its withdrawal.

concepts.label: Post-Traumatic Headache
concepts.title: Post-Traumatic Headache
concepts.definition: Secondary headache attributed to TRAUMA of the HEAD and/or the NECK.

concepts.label: Post-Dural Puncture Headache
concepts.title: Post-Dural Puncture Headache
concepts.definition: A secondary headache disorder attributed to low CEREBROSPINAL FLUID pressure caused by SPINAL PUNCTURE, usually after dural or lumbar puncture.

concepts.label: Paroxysmal Hemicrania
concepts.title: Paroxysmal Hemicrania
concepts.definition: A primary headache disorder that is similar to the CLUSTER HEADACHE with unilateral head pain, but differs by its multiple short severe attacks. It is usually seen in females, and may be responsive to non-steroidal-anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS).

concepts.label: Trigeminal Autonomic Cephalalgias
concepts.title: Trigeminal Autonomic Cephalalgias
concepts.definition: Primary headache disorders that show symptoms caused by the activation of the AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM of the TRIGEMINAL NERVE. These autonomic features include redness and tearing of the EYE, nasal congestion or discharge, facial SWEATING and other symptoms. Most subgroups show unilateral cranial PAIN.

concepts.label: Dependent Ambulation
concepts.title: Dependent Ambulation
concepts.definition: To move about or walk on foot with the use of aids.

concepts.label: Mobility Limitation
concepts.title: Mobility Limitation
concepts.definition: Difficulty in walking from place to place.

concepts.label: Mice
concepts.title: Mice
concepts.definition: The common name for the genus Mus.

concepts.label: Aquaporin 4
concepts.title: Aquaporin 4
concepts.definition: Aquaporin 4 is the major water-selective channel in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM of mammals.

concepts.label: Neuralgia, Postherpetic
concepts.title: Neuralgia, Postherpetic
concepts.definition: Pain in nerves, frequently involving facial SKIN, resulting from the activation the latent varicella-zoster virus (HERPESVIRUS 3, HUMAN). The two forms of the condition preceding the pain are HERPES ZOSTER OTICUS; and HERPES ZOSTER OPHTHALMICUS. Following the healing of the rashes and blisters, the pain sometimes persists.

concepts.label: Synucleins
concepts.title: Synucleins
concepts.definition: A family of homologous proteins of low MOLECULAR WEIGHT that are predominately expressed in the BRAIN and that have been implicated in a variety of human diseases. They were originally isolated from CHOLINERGIC FIBERS of TORPEDO.

concepts.label: alpha-Synuclein
concepts.title: alpha-Synuclein
concepts.definition: A synuclein that is a major component of LEWY BODIES and plays a role in SYNUCLEINOPATHIES, neurodegeneration and neuroprotection.
aliases: Non AB Component of AD Amyloid Protein
Non-AB Component of AD Amyloid Protein

concepts.label: Bulimia Nervosa
concepts.title: Bulimia Nervosa
concepts.definition: An eating disorder that is characterized by a cycle of binge eating (BULIMIA or bingeing) followed by inappropriate acts (purging) to avert weight gain. Purging methods often include self-induced VOMITING, use of LAXATIVES or DIURETICS, excessive exercise, and FASTING.

concepts.label: Vaginismus
concepts.title: Vaginismus
concepts.definition: Recurrent or persistent involuntary SPASM of the outer muscles of the VAGINA, occurring during vaginal penetration.

concepts.label: Glycogen Storage Disease Type IIb
concepts.title: Glycogen Storage Disease Type IIb
concepts.definition: An X-linked dominant multisystem disorder resulting in cardiomyopathy, myopathy and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY. It is caused by mutation in the gene encoding LYSOSOMAL-ASSOCIATED MEMBRANE PROTEIN 2.
aliases: Glycogen Storage Disease Limited to the Heart
Lysosomal Glycogen Storage Disease with Normal Acid Maltase
Lysosomal Glycogen Storage Disease without Acid Maltase Deficiency
Vacuolar Cardiomyopathy and Myopathy, X linked
X Linked Vacuolar Cardiomyopathy and Myopathy

concepts.label: Genes, Neoplasm
concepts.title: Genes, Neoplasm
concepts.definition: Genes whose abnormal expression, or MUTATION are associated with the development, growth, or progression of NEOPLASMS.

concepts.label: Usher Syndromes
concepts.title: Usher Syndromes
concepts.definition: Autosomal recessive hereditary disorders characterized by congenital SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS and RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA. Genetically and symptomatically heterogeneous, clinical classes include type I, type II, and type III. Their severity, age of onset of retinitis pigmentosa and the degree of vestibular dysfunction are variable.

concepts.label: Lipid Metabolism Disorders
concepts.title: Lipid Metabolism Disorders
concepts.definition: Pathological conditions resulting from abnormal anabolism or catabolism of lipids in the body.

concepts.label: Hypoalphalipoproteinemias
concepts.title: Hypoalphalipoproteinemias
concepts.definition: Conditions with abnormally low levels of ALPHA-LIPOPROTEINS (high-density lipoproteins) in the blood. Hypoalphalipoproteinemia can be associated with mutations in genes encoding APOLIPOPROTEIN A-I; LECITHIN CHOLESTEROL ACYLTRANSFERASE; and ATP-BINDING CASSETTE TRANSPORTERS.

concepts.label: Sulfatidosis
concepts.title: Sulfatidosis
concepts.definition: A group of inherited metabolic disorders characterized by the intralysosomal accumulation of sulfur-containing lipids (SULFATIDES), including SULFOGLYCOSPHINGOLIPIDS normally found in the MYELIN SHEATH of the brain. These disorders are caused by defective degradative enzymes leading to substrate accumulation (or storage).

concepts.label: Multiple Sulfatase Deficiency Disease
concepts.title: Multiple Sulfatase Deficiency Disease
concepts.definition: An inherited metabolic disorder characterized by the intralysosomal accumulation of sulfur-containing lipids (sulfatides) and MUCOPOLYSACCHARIDES. Excess levels of both substrates are present in urine. This is a disorder of multiple sulfatase (arylsulfatases A, B, and C) deficiency which is caused by the mutation of sulfatase-modifying factor-1. Neurological deterioration is rapid.

concepts.label: Niemann-Pick Disease, Type A
concepts.title: Niemann-Pick Disease, Type A
concepts.definition: The classic infantile form of Niemann-Pick Disease, caused by mutation in SPHINGOMYELIN PHOSPHODIESTERASE. It is characterized by accumulation of SPHINGOMYELINS in the cells of the MONONUCLEAR PHAGOCYTE SYSTEM and other cell throughout the body leading to cell death. Clinical signs include JAUNDICE, hepatosplenomegaly, and severe brain damage.
aliases: Niemann Pick Disease, Acute Neuronopathic Form
Niemann Pick Disease, Acute Neurovisceral Form

concepts.label: Niemann-Pick Disease, Type B
concepts.title: Niemann-Pick Disease, Type B
concepts.definition: An allelic disorder of TYPE A NIEMANN-PICK DISEASE, a late-onset form. It is also caused by mutation in SPHINGOMYELIN PHOSPHODIESTERASE but clinical signs involve only visceral organs (non-neuropathic type).
aliases: Niemann Pick Disease, Non Neuronopathic Type

concepts.label: Niemann-Pick Disease, Type C
concepts.title: Niemann-Pick Disease, Type C
concepts.definition: An autosomal recessive lipid storage disorder that is characterized by accumulation of CHOLESTEROL and SPHINGOMYELINS in cells of the VISCERA and the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. Type C (or C1) and type D are allelic disorders caused by mutation of the NPC1 gene, which encodes  a protein that mediates intracellular cholesterol transport from LYSOSOMES. Clinical signs include hepatosplenomegaly and chronic neurological symptoms. Type D is a variant in people with a Nova Scotia ancestry.
aliases: Neurovisceral Storage Disease with Vertical Supranuclear Ophthalmoplegia
Niemann Pick Disease with Cholesterol Esterification Block
Niemann Pick Disease without Sphingomyelinase Deficiency
Niemann Pick Disease, Chronic Neuronopathic Form
Niemann-Pick Disease with Cholesterol Esterification Block

concepts.label: Muscle Stretching Exercises
concepts.title: Muscle Stretching Exercises
concepts.definition: Exercises that stretch the muscle fibers with the aim to increase muscle-tendon FLEXIBILITY, improve RANGE OF MOTION or musculoskeletal function, and prevent injuries. There are various types of stretching techniques including active, passive (relaxed), static, dynamic (gentle), ballistic (forced), isometric, and others.

concepts.label: Pinch Strength
concepts.title: Pinch Strength
concepts.definition: Force exerted when using the index finger and the thumb. It is a test for determining maximum voluntary contraction force.

concepts.label: Mating Preference, Animal
concepts.title: Mating Preference, Animal
concepts.definition: The selection or choice of sexual partner in animals. Often this reproductive preference is based on traits in the potential mate, such as coloration, size, or behavioral boldness. If the chosen ones are genetically different from the rejected ones, then NATURAL SELECTION is occurring.

concepts.label: Particulate Matter
concepts.title: Particulate Matter
concepts.definition: Particles of any solid substance, generally under 30 microns in size, often noted as PM30. There is special concern with PM1 which can get down to PULMONARY ALVEOLI and induce MACROPHAGE ACTIVATION and PHAGOCYTOSIS leading to FOREIGN BODY REACTION and LUNG DISEASES.

concepts.label: Corticotrophs
concepts.title: Corticotrophs
concepts.definition: Anterior pituitary cells that produce ADRENOCORTICOTROPHIC HORMONE.

concepts.label: Gonadotrophs
concepts.title: Gonadotrophs
concepts.definition: Anterior pituitary cells that can produce both FOLLICLE STIMULATING HORMONE and LUTEINIZING HORMONE.

concepts.label: Lactotrophs
concepts.title: Lactotrophs
concepts.definition: Anterior pituitary cells that produce PROLACTIN.

concepts.label: Somatotrophs
concepts.title: Somatotrophs
concepts.definition: Anterior pituitary cells which produce GROWTH HORMONE.

concepts.label: Thyrotrophs
concepts.title: Thyrotrophs
concepts.definition: Anterior pituitary cells that produce THYROID-STIMULATING HORMONE.

concepts.label: Pituitary Gland, Intermediate
concepts.title: Pituitary Gland, Intermediate
concepts.definition: The intermediate lobe of the pituitary gland. It shows considerable size variation among the species, small in humans, and large in amphibians and lower vertebrates. This lobe produces mainly MELANOCYTE-STIMULATING HORMONES and other peptides from post-translational processing of pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC).

concepts.label: Melanotrophs
concepts.title: Melanotrophs
concepts.definition: Neuroendocrine cells in the INTERMEDIATE LOBE OF PITUITARY. They produce MELANOCYTE STIMULATING HORMONES and other peptides from the post-translational processing of pro-opiomelanocortin (POMC).

concepts.label: Female Urogenital Diseases
concepts.title: Female Urogenital Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes of the female URINARY TRACT and the reproductive system (GENITALIA, FEMALE).

concepts.label: Male Urogenital Diseases
concepts.title: Male Urogenital Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes of the male URINARY TRACT and the reproductive system (GENITALIA, MALE).

concepts.label: Subacute Combined Degeneration
concepts.title: Subacute Combined Degeneration
concepts.definition: A neuropathy due to VITAMIN B 12 DEFICIENCY or to excessive NITROUS OXIDE inhalation. It is associated with overproduction of the myelinolytic TUMOR NECROSIS FACTOR-ALPHA.

concepts.label: Pyomyositis
concepts.title: Pyomyositis
concepts.definition: An intramuscular suppuration of the large skeletal muscle groups. It is associated with INFECTION such as STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS and PYODERMA. It was known as a tropical disease but is increasing among the immunocompromised (IMMUNOCOMPROMISED HOST). Symptoms include muscle pain, FEVER, and leucocytosis. It has been diagnosed by MRI SCANS.

concepts.label: Refsum Disease, Infantile
concepts.title: Refsum Disease, Infantile
concepts.definition: An early onset form of phytanic acid storage disease with clinical and biochemical signs different from those of REFSUM DISEASE. Features include MENTAL RETARDATION; SENSORINEURAL HEARING LOSS; OSTEOPOROSIS; and severe liver damage. It can be caused by mutation in a number of genes encoding proteins involving in the biogenesis or assembly of PEROXISOMES.
aliases: Infantile Form of Phytanic Acid Storage Disease

concepts.label: Tarlov Cysts
concepts.title: Tarlov Cysts
concepts.definition: Perineurial cysts commonly found in the SACRAL REGION. They arise from the PERINEURIUM membrane within the SPINAL NERVE ROOTS. The distinctive feature of the cysts is the presence of spinal nerve root fibers within the cyst wall, or the cyst cavity itself.

concepts.label: Tool Use Behavior
concepts.title: Tool Use Behavior
concepts.definition: Modifying, carrying, or manipulating an item external to itself by an animal, before using it to effect a change on the environment or itself (from Beck, Animal Tool Behavior, 1980).

concepts.label: Nocturnal Enuresis
concepts.title: Nocturnal Enuresis
concepts.definition: Involuntary discharge of URINE during sleep at night after expected age of completed development of urinary control.

concepts.label: Diurnal Enuresis
concepts.title: Diurnal Enuresis
concepts.definition: Involuntary discharge of URINE during the daytime while one is awake.

concepts.label: Kaplan-Meier Estimate
concepts.title: Kaplan-Meier Estimate
concepts.definition: A nonparametric method of compiling LIFE TABLES or survival tables. It combines calculated probabilities of survival and estimates to allow for observations occurring beyond a measurement threshold, which are assumed to occur randomly. Time intervals are defined as ending each time an event occurs and are therefore unequal. (From Last, A Dictionary of Epidemiology, 1995)

concepts.label: High Vocal Center
concepts.title: High Vocal Center
concepts.definition: Nucleus in the NEOSTRIATUM of bird brains that sends signals for song production and receives auditory input. In some adult SONGBIRDS, research has shown that the size of this nucleus changes seasonally and that it exhibits neurogenesis.

concepts.label: Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome
concepts.title: Hand-Arm Vibration Syndrome
concepts.definition: An occupational disorder resulting from prolonged exposure to vibration, affecting the fingers, hands, and forearms. It occurs in workers who regularly use vibrating tools such as jackhammers, power chain saws, riveters, etc. Symptoms include episodic finger blanching, NUMBNESS, tingling, and loss of nerve sensitivity.

concepts.label: Inhibitory Postsynaptic Potentials
concepts.title: Inhibitory Postsynaptic Potentials
concepts.definition: Hyperpolarization of membrane potentials at the SYNAPTIC MEMBRANES of target neurons during NEUROTRANSMISSION. They are local changes which diminish responsiveness to excitatory signals.

concepts.label: Channelopathies
concepts.title: Channelopathies
concepts.definition: A variety of neuromuscular conditions resulting from MUTATIONS in ION CHANNELS manifesting as episodes of EPILEPSY; HEADACHE DISORDERS; and DYSKINESIAS.

concepts.label: Eye Movement Measurements
concepts.title: Eye Movement Measurements
concepts.definition: Methods and procedures for recording EYE MOVEMENTS.

concepts.label: Proteinase Inhibitory Proteins, Secretory
concepts.title: Proteinase Inhibitory Proteins, Secretory
concepts.definition: Peptides and proteins found in BODILY SECRETIONS and BODY FLUIDS that are PROTEASE INHIBITORS. They play a role in INFLAMMATION, tissue repair and innate immunity (IMMUNITY, INNATE) by inhibiting endogenous proteinases such as those produced by LEUKOCYTES and exogenous proteases such as those produced by invading microorganisms.

concepts.label: Opsoclonus-Myoclonus Syndrome
concepts.title: Opsoclonus-Myoclonus Syndrome
concepts.definition: A neurological condition that is characterized by uncontrolled rapid irregular movements of the eye (OPSOCLONUS) and the muscle (MYOCLONUS) causing unsteady, trembling gait. It is also known as dancing eyes-dancing feet syndrome and is often associated with neoplasms, viral infections, or autoimmune disorders involving the nervous system.

concepts.label: Muscle Strength
concepts.title: Muscle Strength
concepts.definition: The amount of force generated by MUSCLE CONTRACTION. Muscle strength can be measured during isometric, isotonic, or isokinetic contraction, either manually or using a device such as a MUSCLE STRENGTH DYNAMOMETER.

concepts.label: Arthrometry, Articular
concepts.title: Arthrometry, Articular
concepts.definition: Measurements of joint flexibility (RANGE OF MOTION, ARTICULAR), usually by employing an angle-measuring device (arthrometer). Arthrometry is used to measure ligamentous laxity and stability. It is often used to evaluate the outcome of ANTERIOR CRUCIATE LIGAMENT replacement surgery.

concepts.label: Referred Pain
concepts.title: Referred Pain
concepts.definition: A type of pain that is perceived in an area away from the site where the pain arises, such as facial pain caused by lesion of the VAGUS NERVE, or throat problem generating referred pain in the ear.

concepts.label: Stupor
concepts.title: Stupor
concepts.definition: A state of reduced sensibility and response to stimuli which is distinguished from COMA in that the person can be aroused by vigorous and repeated stimulation. The person is still conscious and can make voluntary movements. It can be induced by CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM AGENTS. The word derives from Latin stupere and is related to stunned, stupid, dazed or LETHARGY.

concepts.label: Lethargy
concepts.title: Lethargy
concepts.definition: A general state of sluggishness, listless, or uninterested, with being tired, and having difficulty concentrating and doing simple tasks. It may be related to DEPRESSION or DRUG ADDICTION.

concepts.label: Female Athlete Triad Syndrome
concepts.title: Female Athlete Triad Syndrome
concepts.definition: A condition of competitive female athletes in which there are interrelated problems of feeding and eating disorders; AMENORRHEA; and OSTEOPOROSIS.

concepts.label: Metabolic Networks and Pathways
concepts.title: Metabolic Networks and Pathways
concepts.definition: Complex sets of enzymatic reactions connected to each other via their product and substrate metabolites.

concepts.label: Nevus, Sebaceous of Jadassohn
concepts.title: Nevus, Sebaceous of Jadassohn
concepts.definition: A syndrome characterized by lesions occurring on the face, scalp, or neck which consist of congenital hypoplastic malformations of cutaneous structures and which over time undergo verrucous hyperplasia. Additionally it is associated with neurological symptoms and skeletal, ophthalmological, urogenital, and cardiovascular abnormalities.

concepts.label: Cerebrum
concepts.title: Cerebrum
concepts.definition: Derived from TELENCEPHALON, cerebrum is composed of a right and a left hemisphere. Each contains an outer cerebral cortex and a subcortical basal ganglia. The cerebrum includes all parts within the skull except the MEDULLA OBLONGATA, the PONS, and the CEREBELLUM. Cerebral functions include sensorimotor, emotional, and intellectual activities.

concepts.label: Myelencephalon
concepts.title: Myelencephalon
concepts.definition: The most posterior portion of the hindbrain from which MEDULLA OBLONGATA is derived.

concepts.label: Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome
concepts.title: Posterior Leukoencephalopathy Syndrome
concepts.definition: A condition that is characterized by HEADACHE; SEIZURES; and visual loss with edema in the posterior aspects of the CEREBRAL HEMISPHERES, such as the BRAIN STEM. Generally, lesions involve the white matter (nerve fibers) but occasionally the grey matter (nerve cell bodies).

concepts.label: Deaf-Blind Disorders
concepts.title: Deaf-Blind Disorders
concepts.definition: The absence of both hearing and vision.

concepts.label: Mevalonate Kinase Deficiency
concepts.title: Mevalonate Kinase Deficiency
concepts.definition: Autosomal recessive disorder caused by mutations in the mevalonate kinase gene. Because of the mutations cholesterol biosynthesis is disrupted and MEVALONIC ACID accumulates. It is characterized by a range of symptoms, including dysmorphic FACIES, psychomotor retardation, CATARACT, hepatosplenomegaly, CEREBELLAR ATAXIA, elevated IMMUNOGLOBULIN D, and recurrent febrile crises with FEVER; LYMPHADENOPATHY; ARTHRALGIA; EDEMA; and rash.

concepts.label: Vascular Malformations
concepts.title: Vascular Malformations
concepts.definition: A spectrum of congenital, inherited, or acquired abnormalities in BLOOD VESSELS that can adversely affect the normal blood flow in ARTERIES or VEINS. Most are congenital defects such as abnormal communications between blood vessels (fistula), shunting of arterial blood directly into veins bypassing the CAPILLARIES (arteriovenous malformations), formation of large dilated blood blood-filled vessels (cavernous angioma), and swollen capillaries (capillary telangiectases). In rare cases, vascular malformations can result from trauma or diseases.

concepts.label: Vein of Galen Malformations
concepts.title: Vein of Galen Malformations
concepts.definition: Congenital arteriovenous malformation involving the VEIN OF GALEN, a large deep vein at the base of the brain. The rush of arterial blood directly into the vein of Galen, without passing through the CAPILLARIES, can overwhelm the heart and lead to CONGESTIVE HEART FAILURE.

concepts.label: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group II
concepts.title: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group II
concepts.definition: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal CELL MIGRATION in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes COBBLESTONE LISSENCEPHALY and PERIVENTRICULAR NODULAR HETEROTOPIA.
aliases: Malformations Due to Abnormal Neuronal Migration
Malformations Secondary to Abnormal Neuronal Migration

concepts.label: Lissencephaly
concepts.title: Lissencephaly
concepts.definition: A smooth brain malformation of the CEREBRAL CORTEX resulting from the abnormal location of developing neurons during corticogenesis. It is characterized by an absence of normal convoluted indentations on the surface of the brain (agyria), or fewer and shallower indentations (pachygryia). There is a reduced number of cortical layers, typically 4 instead of 6, resulting in a thickened cortex, and reduced cerebral white matter that is a reversal of the normal ratio of cerebral white matter to cortex.

concepts.label: Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia
concepts.title: Periventricular Nodular Heterotopia
concepts.definition: A disorder resulting from a defect in the pattern of neuronal migration in which ectopic collections of neurons lie along the lateral ventricles of the brain or just beneath, contiguously or in isolated patches.

concepts.label: Malformations of Cortical Development
concepts.title: Malformations of Cortical Development
concepts.definition: Abnormalities in the development of the CEREBRAL CORTEX. These include malformations arising from abnormal neuronal and glial CELL PROLIFERATION or APOPTOSIS (Group I); abnormal neuronal migration (Group II); and abnormal establishment of cortical organization (Group III). Many INBORN METABOLIC BRAIN DISORDERS affecting CNS formation are often associated with cortical malformations. They are common causes of EPILEPSY and developmental delay.

concepts.label: Classical Lissencephalies and Subcortical Band Heterotopias
concepts.title: Classical Lissencephalies and Subcortical Band Heterotopias
concepts.definition: Disorders comprising a spectrum of brain malformations representing the paradigm of a diffuse neuronal migration disorder. They result in cognitive impairment; SEIZURES; and HYPOTONIA or spasticity. Mutations of two genes, LIS1, the gene for the non-catalytic subunit of PLATELET-ACTIVATING FACTOR ACETYLHYDROLASE IB; and DCX or XLIS, the gene for doublecortin, have been identified as the most common causes of disorders in this spectrum. Additional variants of classical (Type I) lissencephaly have been linked to RELN, the gene for reelin, and ARX, the gene for aristaless related homeobox protein. (From Leventer, R.J., et al, Mol Med Today. 2000 Jul;6(7):277-84 and Barkovich, A.J., et al, Neurology. 2005 Dec 27;65(12):1873-87.)

concepts.label: Cobblestone Lissencephaly
concepts.title: Cobblestone Lissencephaly
concepts.definition: The smooth pebbled appearance of the CEREBRAL CORTEX with a thickened cortex and reduced and abnormal white matter, which results from migration of heterotopic neurons beyond the marginal zone into the leptomeninges through gaps in the external BASEMENT MEMBRANE. There is also enlarged ventricles, underdeveloped BRAINSTEM and cerebellum, and absence of the CORPUS CALLOSUM. These abnormalities occur as a syndrome without other birth defects (cobblestone complex) or in other syndromes associated with congenital MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY, often involving the eye, such as the Walker-Warburg Syndrome, Fukuyama congenital muscular dystrophy, and muscle-eye-brain disease.

concepts.label: Marchiafava-Bignami Disease
concepts.title: Marchiafava-Bignami Disease
concepts.definition: A neurodegenerative condition that is characterized by demyelination or necrosis of the CORPUS CALLOSUM. Symptoms include DEPRESSION; PARANOIA; DEMENTIA; SEIZURES; and ATAXIA which can progress to COMA and death in a few months. Marchiafava-Bignami syndrome is seen often in alcoholics but has been found in non-alcoholics as well.

concepts.label: Cell Transdifferentiation
concepts.title: Cell Transdifferentiation
concepts.definition: A naturally occurring phenomenon where terminally differentiated cells dedifferentiate to the point where they can switch CELL LINEAGES. The cells then differentiate into other cell types.

concepts.label: Electrical Synapses
concepts.title: Electrical Synapses
concepts.definition: Specialized junctions between NEURONS which connect the cytoplasm of one neuron to another allowing direct passage of an ion current.

concepts.label: Vulvar Vestibulitis
concepts.title: Vulvar Vestibulitis
concepts.definition: Inflammation of the vulvar vestibular region at the entrance of the VAGINA, generally involving surface mucosa and submucosal vestibular glands. It is characterized by ERYTHEMA and chronic recurrent pain in this area.

concepts.label: Attentional Blink
concepts.title: Attentional Blink
concepts.definition: Temporary visual deficit or impaired visual processing occurring in a rapid serial visual presentation task. After a person identifies the first of two visual targets, the ability to detect the second target is impaired for the next few hundred milliseconds. This phenomenon is called attentional blink.

concepts.label: Adult Survivors of Child Abuse
concepts.title: Adult Survivors of Child Abuse
concepts.definition: Persons who were child victims of violence and abuse including physical, sexual, or emotional maltreatment.

concepts.label: Family Conflict
concepts.title: Family Conflict
concepts.definition: Struggle or disagreement between parents, parent and child or other members of a family.

concepts.label: Neuroacanthocytosis
concepts.title: Neuroacanthocytosis
concepts.definition: An inherited autosomal disorder that is characterized by neurodegeneration; orofacial and buccal DYSKINESIAS; CHOREA; and thorny-looking red cells (ACANTHOCYTES). This disorder is due to mutations of chorein which is important in protein trafficking and is encoded by Vps13a on chromosome 9q21.

concepts.label: Consumer Health Information
concepts.title: Consumer Health Information
concepts.definition: Information intended for potential users of medical and healthcare services. There is an emphasis on self-care and preventive approaches as well as information for community-wide dissemination and use.

concepts.label: Protein Interaction Domains and Motifs
concepts.title: Protein Interaction Domains and Motifs
concepts.definition: Protein modules with conserved ligand-binding surfaces which mediate specific interaction functions in SIGNAL TRANSDUCTION PATHWAYS and the specific BINDING SITES of their cognate protein LIGANDS.

concepts.label: Ecotoxicology
concepts.title: Ecotoxicology
concepts.definition: The study of ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTION and the toxic effects of ENVIRONMENTAL POLLUTANTS on the ECOSYSTEM. The term was coined by Truhaut in 1969.

concepts.label: Muscle, Striated
concepts.title: Muscle, Striated
concepts.definition: One of two types of muscle in the body, characterized by the array of bands observed under microscope. Striated muscles can be divided into two subtypes: the CARDIAC MUSCLE and the SKELETAL MUSCLE.

concepts.label: Histamine H3 Antagonists
concepts.title: Histamine H3 Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that selectively bind to but do not activate HISTAMINE H3 RECEPTORS. They have been used to correct SLEEP WAKE DISORDERS and MEMORY DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Cardiac Electrophysiology
concepts.title: Cardiac Electrophysiology
concepts.definition: The study of the electrical activity and characteristics of the HEART; MYOCARDIUM; and CARDIOMYOCYTES.

concepts.label: Athletic Performance
concepts.title: Athletic Performance
concepts.definition: Carrying out of specific physical routines or procedures by one who is trained or skilled in physical activity. Performance is influenced by a combination of physiological, psychological, and socio-cultural factors.

concepts.label: Primary Dysautonomias
concepts.title: Primary Dysautonomias
concepts.definition: Disorders of the AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM occurring as a primary condition. Manifestations can involve any or all body systems but commonly affect the BLOOD PRESSURE and HEART RATE.

concepts.label: Pure Autonomic Failure
concepts.title: Pure Autonomic Failure
concepts.definition: A degenerative disease of the AUTONOMIC NERVOUS SYSTEM that is characterized by idiopathic ORTHOSTATIC HYPOTENSION and a greatly reduced level of CATECHOLAMINES. No other neurological deficits are present.

concepts.label: Orthostatic Intolerance
concepts.title: Orthostatic Intolerance
concepts.definition: Symptoms of cerebral hypoperfusion or autonomic overaction which develop while the subject is standing, but are relieved on recumbency. Types of this include NEUROCARDIOGENIC SYNCOPE; POSTURAL ORTHOSTATIC TACHYCARDIA SYNDROME; and neurogenic ORTHOSTATIC HYPOTENSION. (From Noseworthy, JH., Neurological Therapeutics Principles and Practice, 2007, p2575-2576)

concepts.label: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome
concepts.title: Postural Orthostatic Tachycardia Syndrome
concepts.definition: A syndrome of ORTHOSTATIC INTOLERANCE combined with excessive upright TACHYCARDIA, and usually without associated ORTHOSTATIC HYPOTENSION. All variants have in common an excessively reduced venous return to the heart (central HYPOVOLEMIA) while upright.

concepts.label: Pallister-Hall Syndrome
concepts.title: Pallister-Hall Syndrome
concepts.definition: A pleiotropic disorder of human development that comprises hypothalamic HAMARTOMA; central and postaxial POLYDACTYLY; bifid EPIGLOTTIS; ANAL ATRESIA; and renal and other abnormalities. This disorder is associated with FRAMESHIFT MUTATIONS in the GLI3 gene which encodes the GLI3 protein, a KRUPPEL-LIKE TRANSCRIPTION FACTORS family member.
aliases: Hypothalamic Hamartoblastoma, Hypopituitarism, Imperforate Anus, and Postaxial Polydactyly

concepts.label: Resistance Training
concepts.title: Resistance Training
concepts.definition: A type of strength-building exercise program that requires the body muscle to exert a force against some form of resistance, such as weight, stretch bands, water, or immovable objects. Resistance exercise is a combination of static and dynamic contractions involving shortening and lengthening of skeletal muscles.

concepts.label: Periodontal Atrophy
concepts.title: Periodontal Atrophy
concepts.definition: Degradation or wasting of the PERIODONTIUM tissues that may involve the gum (GINGIVA), the alveolar bone (ALVEOLAR PROCESS), the DENTAL CEMENTUM, or the PERIODONTAL LIGAMENT.

concepts.label: Endocrine Cells
concepts.title: Endocrine Cells
concepts.definition: Secretory cells of the ductless glands. They secrete HORMONES directly into the blood circulation (internal secretion) to be carried to the target cells. The secreted chemicals can be PEPTIDES; STEROIDS; NEUROPEPTIDES; or BIOGENIC AMINES.

concepts.label: Medication Adherence
concepts.title: Medication Adherence
concepts.definition: Voluntary cooperation of the patient in taking drugs or medicine as prescribed. This includes timing, dosage, and frequency.

concepts.label: Sensory Gating
concepts.title: Sensory Gating
concepts.definition: The ability of the BRAIN to suppress neuronal responses to external sensory inputs, such as auditory and visual stimuli. Sensory filtering (or gating) allows humans to block out irrelevant, meaningless, or redundant stimuli.

concepts.label: Dysphonia
concepts.title: Dysphonia
concepts.definition: Difficulty and/or pain in PHONATION or speaking.

concepts.label: Retinal Photoreceptor Cell Inner Segment
concepts.title: Retinal Photoreceptor Cell Inner Segment
concepts.definition: The inner portion of a retinal rod or a cone photoreceptor cell, situated between the PHOTORECEPTOR CONNECTING CILIUM and the synapse with the adjacent neurons (RETINAL BIPOLAR CELLS; RETINAL HORIZONTAL CELLS). The inner segment contains the cell body, the nucleus, the mitochondria, and apparatus for protein synthesis.

concepts.label: Photoreceptor Connecting Cilium
concepts.title: Photoreceptor Connecting Cilium
concepts.definition: The bridge between the inner and the outer segments of a retinal rod or a cone photoreceptor cell. Through it, proteins synthesized in the inner segment are transported to the outer segment.

concepts.label: Retinal Photoreceptor Cell Outer Segment
concepts.title: Retinal Photoreceptor Cell Outer Segment
concepts.definition: The light sensitive outer portion of a retinal rod or a cone photoreceptor cell. The outer segment contains a stack of disk membranes laden with photoreceptive pigments (RETINAL PIGMENTS). The outer segment is connected to the inner segment by a PHOTORECEPTOR CONNECTING CILIUM.

concepts.label: Color Vision
concepts.title: Color Vision
concepts.definition: Function of the human eye that is used in bright illumination or in daylight (at photopic intensities). Photopic vision is performed by the three types of RETINAL CONE PHOTORECEPTORS with varied peak absorption wavelengths in the color spectrum (from violet to red, 400 - 700 nm).

concepts.label: Night Vision
concepts.title: Night Vision
concepts.definition: Function of the human eye that is used in dim illumination (scotopic intensities) or at nighttime. Scotopic vision is performed by RETINAL ROD PHOTORECEPTORS with high sensitivity to light and peak absorption wavelength at 507 nm near the blue end of the spectrum.

concepts.label: Mesopic Vision
concepts.title: Mesopic Vision
concepts.definition: The function of the eye that is used in the intermediate level of illumination (mesopic intensities) where both the RETINAL ROD PHOTORECEPTORS and the RETINAL CONE PHOTORECEPTORS are active in processing light input simultaneously.

concepts.label: Rod-Cone Interaction
concepts.title: Rod-Cone Interaction
concepts.definition: Reciprocal action of two vertebrate photoreceptor cells (RODS AND CONES). Rod-cone interaction occurs during MESOPIC VISION in which both rods and cones are active in light transduction to the VISUAL CORTEX. Such interaction can influence visual sensitivity and luminous efficiency.

concepts.label: Cystatin B
concepts.title: Cystatin B
concepts.definition: An intracellular cystatin subtype that is found in a broad variety of cell types. It is a cytosolic enzyme inhibitor that protects the cell against the proteolytic action of lysosomal enzymes such as CATHEPSINS.

concepts.label: Retinal Neurons
concepts.title: Retinal Neurons
concepts.definition: Nerve cells of the RETINA in the pathway of transmitting light signals to the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. They include the outer layer of PHOTORECEPTOR CELLS, the intermediate layer of RETINAL BIPOLAR CELLS and AMACRINE CELLS, and the internal layer of RETINAL GANGLION CELLS.

concepts.label: Multilevel Analysis
concepts.title: Multilevel Analysis
concepts.definition: The statistical manipulation of hierarchically and non-hierarchically nested data. It includes clustered data, such as a sample of subjects within a group of schools. Prevalent in the social, behavioral sciences, and biomedical sciences, both linear and nonlinear regression models are applied.

concepts.label: Synaptic Potentials
concepts.title: Synaptic Potentials
concepts.definition: The voltages across pre- or post-SYNAPTIC MEMBRANES.

concepts.label: Miniature Postsynaptic Potentials
concepts.title: Miniature Postsynaptic Potentials
concepts.definition: Postsynaptic potentials generated from a release of neurotransmitters from a presynaptic nerve terminal in the absence of an ACTION POTENTIAL. They may be m.e.p.p.s (miniature EXCITATORY POSTSYNAPTIC POTENTIALS) or m.i.p.p.s (miniature INHIBITORY POSTSYNAPTIC POTENTIALS).

concepts.label: Neurogenesis
concepts.title: Neurogenesis
concepts.definition: Formation of NEURONS which involves the differentiation and division of STEM CELLS in which one or both of the daughter cells become neurons.

concepts.label: Resilience, Psychological
concepts.title: Resilience, Psychological
concepts.definition: The human ability to adapt in the face of tragedy, trauma, adversity, hardship, and ongoing significant life stressors.

concepts.label: Bulbo-Spinal Atrophy, X-Linked
concepts.title: Bulbo-Spinal Atrophy, X-Linked
concepts.definition: An X-linked recessive form of spinal muscular atrophy. It is due to a mutation of the gene encoding the ANDROGEN RECEPTOR.
aliases: Kennedy Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy
Spinal And Bulbar Muscular Atrophy, X Linked 1
Spinal And Bulbar Muscular Atrophy, X-Linked 1
X Linked Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy
X-Linked Spinal and Bulbar Muscular Atrophy

concepts.label: Morgellons Disease
concepts.title: Morgellons Disease
concepts.definition: An unexplained illness which is characterized by skin manifestations including non-healing lesions, itching, and the appearance of fibers.

concepts.label: Light Signal Transduction
concepts.title: Light Signal Transduction
concepts.definition: The conversion of absorbed light energy into molecular signals.

concepts.label: Farber Lipogranulomatosis
concepts.title: Farber Lipogranulomatosis
concepts.definition: A sphingolipidosis subtype that is characterized by the histological appearance of granulomatous deposits in tissues. It results from the accumulation of CERAMIDES in various tissues due to an inherited deficiency of ACID CERAMIDASE.

concepts.label: Physical Phenomena
concepts.title: Physical Phenomena
concepts.definition: The entities of matter and energy, and the processes, principles, properties, and relationships describing their nature and interactions.

concepts.label: Biophysical Phenomena
concepts.title: Biophysical Phenomena
concepts.definition: The physical characteristics and processes of biological systems.

concepts.label: Mechanical Phenomena
concepts.title: Mechanical Phenomena
concepts.definition: The properties and processes of materials that affect their behavior under force.

concepts.label: Chemical Phenomena
concepts.title: Chemical Phenomena
concepts.definition: The composition, structure, conformation, and properties of atoms and molecules, and their reaction and interaction processes.

concepts.label: Genetic Phenomena
concepts.title: Genetic Phenomena
concepts.definition: The biological processes, properties, and objects that are involved in maintaining, expressing, and transmitting from one organism to another, genetically encoded traits.

concepts.label: Electrical Equipment and Supplies
concepts.title: Electrical Equipment and Supplies
concepts.definition: Apparatus and instruments that generate and operate with ELECTRICITY, and their electrical components.

concepts.label: Optical Phenomena
concepts.title: Optical Phenomena
concepts.definition: LIGHT, its processes and properties, and the characteristics of materials interacting with it.

concepts.label: Orbital Myositis
concepts.title: Orbital Myositis
concepts.definition: Inflammation of the extraocular muscle of the eye. It is characterized by swelling which can lead to ischemia, fibrosis, or ORBITAL PSEUDOTUMOR.

concepts.label: Immune System Phenomena
concepts.title: Immune System Phenomena
concepts.definition: The characteristic properties and processes involved in IMMUNITY and an organism's immune response.

concepts.label: Mathematical Concepts
concepts.title: Mathematical Concepts
concepts.definition: Numeric or quantitative entities, descriptions, properties, relationships, operations, and events.

concepts.label: Ecological and Environmental Phenomena
concepts.title: Ecological and Environmental Phenomena
concepts.definition: Ecological and environmental entities, characteristics, properties, relationships and processes.

concepts.label: Acrocallosal Syndrome
concepts.title: Acrocallosal Syndrome
concepts.definition: Autosomal recessive syndrome characterized by hypogenesis or agenesis of CORPUS CALLOSUM. Clinical features include MENTAL RETARDATION; CRANIOFACIAL ABNORMALITIES; digital malformations, and growth retardation.
aliases: Hallux Duplication, Postaxial Polydactyly, and Absence of Corpus Callosum

concepts.label: Musculoskeletal and Neural Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Musculoskeletal and Neural Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: Properties, and processes of the MUSCULOSKELETAL SYSTEM and the NERVOUS SYSTEM or their parts.

concepts.label: Digestive System and Oral Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Digestive System and Oral Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: Properties and processes of the DIGESTIVE SYSTEM and DENTITION as a whole or of any of its parts.
aliases: Digestive System and Oral Physiological Concepts
Digestive System and Oral Physiological Phenomenon

concepts.label: Olfactory Perception
concepts.title: Olfactory Perception
concepts.definition: The process by which the nature and meaning of olfactory stimuli, such as odors, are recognized and interpreted by the brain.

concepts.label: Taste Perception
concepts.title: Taste Perception
concepts.definition: The process by which the nature and meaning of gustatory stimuli are recognized and interpreted by the brain. The five basic classes of taste perception are salty, sweet, bitter, sour and umami.

concepts.label: Touch Perception
concepts.title: Touch Perception
concepts.definition: The process by which the nature and meaning of tactile stimuli are recognized and interpreted by the brain, such as realizing the characteristics or name of an object being touched.

concepts.label: Reproductive Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Reproductive Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: Physiological processes, factors, properties and characteristics pertaining to REPRODUCTION.

concepts.label: Electrophysiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Electrophysiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: The electrical properties, characteristics of living organisms, and the processes of organisms or their parts that are involved in generating and responding to electricity.

concepts.label: Meningeal Carcinomatosis
concepts.title: Meningeal Carcinomatosis
concepts.definition: Primary or secondary neoplasm in the ARACHNOID or SUBARACHNOID SPACE. It appears as a diffuse fibrotic thickening of the MENINGES associated with variable degrees of inflammation.

concepts.label: Stalking
concepts.title: Stalking
concepts.definition: Course of conduct directed at a specific person that involves repeated (two or more occasions) visual or physical proximity, nonconsensual communication, or verbal, written, or implied threats, or a combination thereof, that would cause a reasonable person fear.

concepts.label: Illness Behavior
concepts.title: Illness Behavior
concepts.definition: Coordinate set of non-specific behavioral responses to non-psychiatric illness. These may include loss of APPETITE or LIBIDO; disinterest in ACTIVITIES OF DAILY LIVING; or withdrawal from social interaction.

concepts.label: Wandering Behavior
concepts.title: Wandering Behavior
concepts.definition: Moving oneself through space while confused or otherwise cognitively impaired. Patterns include akathisia, exhibiting neuroleptic-induced pacing and restlessness; exit seekers who are often newly admitted institution residents who try to open locked exit doors; self-stimulators who perform other activities such as turning doorknobs, in addition to continuous pacing; and modelers who shadow other pacers.

concepts.label: Integumentary System Physiological Phenomena
concepts.title: Integumentary System Physiological Phenomena
concepts.definition: The properties and relationships and biological processes that characterize the nature and function of the SKIN and its appendages.

concepts.label: Sleep Phase Chronotherapy
concepts.title: Sleep Phase Chronotherapy
concepts.definition: A progressive advance or delay of bedtime until the desired bedtime is achieved.

concepts.label: Climatic Processes
concepts.title: Climatic Processes
concepts.definition: Characteristic events occurring in the ATMOSPHERE during the interactions and transformation of various atmospheric components and conditions.

concepts.label: Magnetic Field Therapy
concepts.title: Magnetic Field Therapy
concepts.definition: The magnetic stimulation of specific target tissues or areas of the body for therapeutic purposes via the application of magnetic fields generated by MAGNETS or ELECTROMAGNETS.

concepts.label: Sarcopenia
concepts.title: Sarcopenia
concepts.definition: Progressive decline in muscle mass due to aging which results in decreased functional capacity of muscles.

concepts.label: Cogan Syndrome
concepts.title: Cogan Syndrome
concepts.definition: A condition consisting of inflammatory eye disease usually presenting as interstitial KERATITIS, vestibuloauditory dysfunction, and large- to medium-vessel vasculitis.

concepts.label: Microscopic Polyangiitis
concepts.title: Microscopic Polyangiitis
concepts.definition: A primary systemic vasculitis of small- and some medium-sized vessels. It is characterized by a tropism for kidneys and lungs, positive association with anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCA), and a paucity of immunoglobulin deposits in vessel walls.

concepts.label: Susac Syndrome
concepts.title: Susac Syndrome
concepts.definition: A rare disorder consisting of microangiopathy of brain, retina, and inner ear ARTERIOLES. It is characterized by the clinical triad of encephalopathy, BRANCH RETINAL ARTERY OCCLUSION and VERTIGO/hearing loss.

concepts.label: Diffuse Neurofibrillary Tangles with Calcification
concepts.title: Diffuse Neurofibrillary Tangles with Calcification
concepts.definition: A form of presenile DEMENTIA characterized by cortical dementia, NEUROFIBRILLARY TANGLES without SENILE PLAQUES, Fahr's type CALCINOSIS, and ATROPHY in frontotemporal or TEMPORAL LOBE.

concepts.label: Piriformis Muscle Syndrome
concepts.title: Piriformis Muscle Syndrome
concepts.definition: A chronic PELVIC PAIN characterized by pain deep in the buttock that may radiate to posterior aspects of the leg. It is caused by the piriformis muscle compressing or irritating the SCIATIC NERVE due to trauma, hypertrophy, inflammation or anatomic variations.

concepts.label: Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
concepts.title: Intervertebral Disc Degeneration
concepts.definition: Degenerative changes in the INTERVERTEBRAL DISC due to aging or structural damage, especially to the vertebral end-plates.

concepts.label: Alien Limb Phenomenon
concepts.title: Alien Limb Phenomenon
concepts.definition: An apraxia characterized by the affected limb having involuntary, autonomous, and seemingly purposeful behaviors that are perceived as being controlled by an external force. Often the affected limb interferes with the actions of the normal limb. Symptoms develop from lesions in the CORPUS CALLOSUM or medial frontal cortex caused by stroke, infarction, and neurodegenerative diseases (e.g., CREUTZFELDT-JAKOB SYNDROME, corticobasal degeneration).

concepts.label: Molecular Dynamics Simulation
concepts.title: Molecular Dynamics Simulation
concepts.definition: A computer simulation developed to study the motion of molecules over a period of time.

concepts.label: Equine-Assisted Therapy
concepts.title: Equine-Assisted Therapy
concepts.definition: Therapy assisted by the use of a horse and/or its movement, including equine-assisted psychotherapy, horseback riding, and hippotherapy.

concepts.label: Feedback, Sensory
concepts.title: Feedback, Sensory
concepts.definition: A mechanism of communicating one's own sensory system information about a task, movement or skill.

concepts.label: Diffusion Tensor Imaging
concepts.title: Diffusion Tensor Imaging
concepts.definition: The use of diffusion ANISOTROPY data from diffusion magnetic resonance imaging results to construct images based on the direction of the faster diffusing molecules.

concepts.label: Executive Function
concepts.title: Executive Function
concepts.definition: A set of cognitive functions that controls complex, goal-directed thought and behavior. Executive function involves multiple domains, such as CONCEPT FORMATION, goal management, cognitive flexibility, INHIBITION control, and WORKING MEMORY. Impaired executive function is seen in a range of disorders, e.g., SCHIZOPHRENIA; and ADHD.

concepts.label: Theory of Mind
concepts.title: Theory of Mind
concepts.definition: The ability to attribute mental states (e.g., beliefs, desires, feelings, intentions, thoughts, etc.) to self and to others, allowing an individual to understand and infer behavior on the basis of the mental states. Difference or deficit in theory of mind is associated with ASPERGER SYNDROME; AUTISTIC DISORDER; and SCHIZOPHRENIA, etc.

concepts.label: Emotional Intelligence
concepts.title: Emotional Intelligence
concepts.definition: The ability to understand and manage emotions and to use emotional knowledge to enhance thought and deal effectively with tasks. Components of emotional intelligence include empathy, self-motivation, self-awareness, self-regulation, and social skill. Emotional intelligence is a measurement of one's ability to socialize or relate to others.

concepts.label: Colloid Cysts
concepts.title: Colloid Cysts
concepts.definition: Benign, congenital, neuroepithelial cysts that are typically filled with a viscous mucus. They usually arise in the anterior portion of the THIRD VENTRICLE between the fornices.

concepts.label: Knee-Chest Position
concepts.title: Knee-Chest Position
concepts.definition: The posture of an individual supported by the knees and chest resting on a table.

concepts.label: Animal Assisted Therapy
concepts.title: Animal Assisted Therapy
concepts.definition: The use of live animals as a means of therapy.

concepts.label: Earth Sciences
concepts.title: Earth Sciences
concepts.definition: Fields of science encompassing studies and research from the disciplines of PHYSICS; CHEMISTRY; BIOLOGICAL SCIENCES; and MATHEMATICS; that are related to the planet EARTH. Subfields include atmospheric chemistry; CLIMATOLOGY; ENVIRONMENTAL SCIENCES; GEOGRAPHY; GEOLOGY; geophysics; METEOROLOGY; OCEANOGRAPHY; PALEONTOLOGY; mineralogy; and seismology.

concepts.label: Position-Specific Scoring Matrices
concepts.title: Position-Specific Scoring Matrices
concepts.definition: Tabular numerical representations of sequence motifs displaying their variability as likelihood values for each possible residue at each position in a sequence. Position-specific scoring matrices (PSSMs) are calculated from position frequency matrices.

concepts.label: CA1 Region, Hippocampal
concepts.title: CA1 Region, Hippocampal
concepts.definition: One of four subsections of the hippocampus described by Lorente de No, located furthest from the DENTATE GYRUS.

concepts.label: Systemic Vasculitis
concepts.title: Systemic Vasculitis
concepts.definition: A heterogeneous group of diseases characterized by inflammation and necrosis of the blood vessel walls.

concepts.label: Anti-Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody-Associated Vasculitis
concepts.title: Anti-Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody-Associated Vasculitis
concepts.definition: Group of systemic vasculitis with a strong association with ANCA. The disorders are characterized by necrotizing inflammation of small and medium size vessels, with little or no immune-complex deposits in vessel walls.
aliases: Anti Neutrophil Cytoplasmic Antibody Associated Vasculitis

concepts.label: CA2 Region, Hippocampal
concepts.title: CA2 Region, Hippocampal
concepts.definition: A subsection of the hippocampus, described by Lorente de No, that is located between the HIPPOCAMPUS CA1 FIELD and the HIPPOCAMPUS CA3 FIELD.

concepts.label: CA3 Region, Hippocampal
concepts.title: CA3 Region, Hippocampal
concepts.definition: A subsection of the hippocampus, described by Lorente de No, that is located between the HIPPOCAMPUS CA2 FIELD and the DENTATE GYRUS.

concepts.label: Hereditary Autoinflammatory Diseases
concepts.title: Hereditary Autoinflammatory Diseases
concepts.definition: Hereditary inflammation conditions, characterized by recurrent episodes of systemic inflammation. Common symptoms include recurrent fever, rash, arthritis, fatigue, and secondary AMYLOIDOSIS. Hereditary autoinflammatory diseases are associated with mutations in genes involved in regulation of normal inflammatory process and are not caused by AUTOANTIBODIES, or antigen specific T-LYMPHOCYTES.

concepts.label: Biometric Identification
concepts.title: Biometric Identification
concepts.definition: A method of differentiating individuals based on the analysis of qualitative or quantitative biological traits or patterns. Biometric identification, which has applications in forensics and identity theft prevention, includes DNA profiles or DNA FINGERPRINTS; FINGERPRINTS; AUTOMATED FACIAL RECOGNITION; IRIS scan; RETINA scan; hand geometry; vascular patterns; automated VOICE pattern recognition; ultrasound of fingers; and X-RAYS.

concepts.label: Immunomodulation
concepts.title: Immunomodulation
concepts.definition: Alteration of the immune system or of an immune response by agents that activate or suppress its function. This can include IMMUNIZATION or administration of immunomodulatory drugs. Immunomodulation can also encompass non-therapeutic alteration of the immune system effected by endogenous or exogenous substances.

concepts.label: Giant Axonal Neuropathy
concepts.title: Giant Axonal Neuropathy
concepts.definition: Rare autosomal recessive disorder of INTERMEDIATE FILAMENT PROTEINS. The disease is caused by mutations in the gene that codes gigaxonin protein. The mutations result in disorganization of axonal NEUROFILAMENT PROTEINS, formation of the characteristic giant axons, and progressive neuropathy. The clinical features of the disease include early-onset progressive peripheral motor and sensory neuropathies often associated with central nervous system involvement (INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, seizures, DYSMETRIA, and CONGENITAL NYSTAGMUS).

concepts.label: Alstrom Syndrome
concepts.title: Alstrom Syndrome
concepts.definition: Rare autosomal recessive disease characterized by multiple organ dysfunction. The key clinical features include retinal degeneration (NYSTAGMUS, PATHOLOGIC; RETINITIS PIGMENTOSA; and eventual blindness), childhood obesity, sensorineural hearing loss, and normal mental development. Endocrinologic complications include TYPE 2 DIABETES MELLITUS; HYPERINSULINEMIA; ACANTHOSIS NIGRICANS; HYPOTHYROIDISM; and progressive renal and hepatic failures. The disease is caused by mutations in the ALMS1 gene.

concepts.label: Leukoencephalopathies
concepts.title: Leukoencephalopathies
concepts.definition: Any of various diseases affecting the white matter of the central nervous system.

concepts.label: Urea Cycle Disorders, Inborn
concepts.title: Urea Cycle Disorders, Inborn
concepts.definition: Rare congenital metabolism disorders of the urea cycle. The disorders are due to mutations that result in complete (neonatal onset) or partial (childhood or adult onset) inactivity of an enzyme, involved in the urea cycle. Neonatal onset results in clinical features that include irritability, vomiting, lethargy, seizures, NEONATAL HYPOTONIA; RESPIRATORY ALKALOSIS; HYPERAMMONEMIA; coma, and death. Survivors of the neonatal onset and childhood/adult onset disorders share common risks for ENCEPHALOPATHIES, METABOLIC, INBORN; and RESPIRATORY ALKALOSIS due to HYPERAMMONEMIA.

concepts.label: Argininosuccinic Aciduria
concepts.title: Argininosuccinic Aciduria
concepts.definition: Rare autosomal recessive disorder of the urea cycle which leads to the accumulation of argininosuccinic acid in body fluids and severe HYPERAMMONEMIA. Clinical features of the neonatal onset of the disorder include poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, seizures, tachypnea, coma, and death. Later onset results in milder set of clinical features including vomiting, failure to thrive, irritability, behavioral problems, or psychomotor retardation. Mutations in the ARGININOSUCCINATE LYASE gene cause the disorder.
aliases: Inborn Error of Urea Synthesis, Arginino Succinic Type
Urea Cycle Disorder, Arginino Succinase Type

concepts.label: Biostatistics
concepts.title: Biostatistics
