concepts.definition: The application of STATISTICS to biological systems and organisms involving the retrieval or collection, analysis, reduction, and interpretation of qualitative and quantitative data.

concepts.label: Renal Colic
concepts.title: Renal Colic
concepts.definition: A severe intermittent and spasmodic pain in the lower back radiating to the groin, scrotum, and labia which is most commonly caused by a kidney stone (RENAL CALCULUS) passing through the URETER or by other urinary track blockage. It is often associated with nausea, vomiting, fever, restlessness, dull pain, frequent urination, and HEMATURIA.

concepts.label: Contrecoup Injury
concepts.title: Contrecoup Injury
concepts.definition: An injury in which the damage is located on the opposite side of the primary impact site. A blow to the back of head which results in contrecoup injury to the frontal lobes of the brain is the most common type.

concepts.label: Patient Positioning
concepts.title: Patient Positioning
concepts.definition: Moving a patient into a specific position or POSTURE to facilitate examination, surgery, or for therapeutic purposes.

concepts.label: Eukaryota
concepts.title: Eukaryota
concepts.definition: One of the three domains of life (the others being BACTERIA and ARCHAEA), also called Eukarya. These are organisms whose cells are enclosed in membranes and possess a nucleus. They comprise almost all multicellular and many unicellular organisms, and are traditionally divided into groups (sometimes called kingdoms) including ANIMALS; PLANTS; FUNGI; and various algae and other taxa that were previously part of the old kingdom Protista.

concepts.label: Binge-Eating Disorder
concepts.title: Binge-Eating Disorder
concepts.definition: A disorder associated with three or more of the following: eating until feeling uncomfortably full; eating large amounts of food when not physically hungry; eating much more rapidly than normal; eating alone due to embarrassment; feeling of disgust, DEPRESSION, or guilt after overeating. Criteria includes occurrence on average, at least 2 days a week for 6 months. The binge eating is not associated with the regular use of inappropriate compensatory behavior (i.e. purging, excessive exercise, etc.) and does not co-occur exclusively with BULIMIA NERVOSA or ANOREXIA NERVOSA. (From DSM-IV, 1994)

concepts.label: Excitation Contraction Coupling
concepts.title: Excitation Contraction Coupling
concepts.definition: A process fundamental to muscle physiology whereby an electrical stimulus or action potential triggers a myocyte to depolarize and contract. This mechanical muscle contraction response is regulated by entry of calcium ions into the cell.

concepts.label: Bioengineering
concepts.title: Bioengineering
concepts.definition: The application of engineering principles and methods to living organisms or biological systems.

concepts.label: Molecular Imaging
concepts.title: Molecular Imaging
concepts.definition: The use of molecularly targeted imaging probes to localize and/or monitor biochemical and cellular processes via various imaging modalities that include RADIONUCLIDE IMAGING; ULTRASONOGRAPHY; MAGNETIC RESONANCE IMAGING; FLUORESCENCE IMAGING; and MICROSCOPY.

concepts.label: Cervical Rib
concepts.title: Cervical Rib
concepts.definition: A supernumerary rib developing from an abnormal enlargement of the costal element of the C7 vertebra. This anomaly is found in 1-2% of the population and can put pressure on adjacent structures causing CERVICAL RIB SYNDROME; THORACIC OUTLET SYNDROME; or other conditions.

concepts.label: Corneal Perforation
concepts.title: Corneal Perforation
concepts.definition: A puncture or hole through the CORNEAL STROMA resulting from various diseases or trauma.

concepts.label: Proteostasis Deficiencies
concepts.title: Proteostasis Deficiencies
concepts.definition: Disorders caused by imbalances in the PROTEIN HOMEOSTASIS network - synthesis, folding, and transport of proteins; post-translational modifications; and degradation or clearance of misfolded proteins.

concepts.label: Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing
concepts.title: Eye Movement Desensitization Reprocessing
concepts.definition: A technique that induces the processing of disturbing memories and experiences, by stimulating neural mechanisms that are similar to those activated during REM sleep. The technique consists of eye movements following side-to-side movements of the index and middle fingers, or the alternate tapping of the hands on the knees. This procedure triggers the processing of information, thus facilitating the connection of neural networks.

concepts.label: Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration
concepts.title: Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration
concepts.definition: Heterogeneous group of neurodegenerative disorders characterized by frontal and temporal lobe atrophy associated with neuronal loss, gliosis, and dementia. Patients exhibit progressive changes in social, behavioral, and/or language function. Multiple subtypes or forms are recognized based on presence or absence of TAU PROTEIN inclusions. FTLD includes three clinical syndromes: FRONTOTEMPORAL DEMENTIA, semantic dementia, and PRIMARY PROGRESSIVE NONFLUENT APHASIA.

concepts.label: TDP-43 Proteinopathies
concepts.title: TDP-43 Proteinopathies
concepts.definition: Diseases characterized by the presence of abnormally phosphorylated, ubiquitinated, and cleaved DNA-binding protein TDP-43 in affected brain and spinal cord. Inclusions of the pathologic protein in neurons and glia, without the presence of AMYLOID, is the major feature of these conditions, thus making these proteinopathies distinct from most other neurogenerative disorders in which protein misfolding leads to brain amyloidosis. Both frontotemporal lobar degeneration and AMYOTROPHIC LATERAL SCLEROSIS exhibit this common method of pathogenesis and thus they may represent two extremes of a continuous clinicopathological spectrum of one disease.

concepts.label: Primary Progressive Nonfluent Aphasia
concepts.title: Primary Progressive Nonfluent Aphasia
concepts.definition: A form of frontotemporal lobar degeneration and a progressive form of dementia characterized by motor speech impairment and AGRAMMATISM, with relative sparing of single word comprehension and semantic memory.

concepts.label: Frontotemporal Dementia
concepts.title: Frontotemporal Dementia
concepts.definition: The most common clinical form of FRONTOTEMPORAL LOBAR DEGENERATION, this dementia presents with personality and behavioral changes often associated with disinhibition, apathy, and lack of insight.
aliases: Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration With Ubiquitin Positive Inclusions
Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration With Ubiquitin-Positive Inclusions
Multiple System Tauopathy with Presenile Dementia

concepts.label: Pleasure
concepts.title: Pleasure
concepts.definition: Sensation of enjoyment or gratification.

concepts.label: Sedentary Behavior
concepts.title: Sedentary Behavior
concepts.definition: Behaviors during waking hours that have low energy expenditure and are often performed in a sitting or reclining POSTURE.

concepts.label: Stroop Test
concepts.title: Stroop Test
concepts.definition: Timed test in which the subject must read a list of words or identify colors presented with varying instructions and different degrees of distraction. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary. 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Body Dysmorphic Disorders
concepts.title: Body Dysmorphic Disorders
concepts.definition: Preoccupations with appearance or self-image causing significant distress or impairment in important areas of functioning.

concepts.label: Propensity Score
concepts.title: Propensity Score
concepts.definition: Conditional probability of exposure to a treatment given observed covariates.

concepts.label: Health Literacy
concepts.title: Health Literacy
concepts.definition: Degree to which individuals have the capacity to obtain, process, and understand basic health information and services needed to make appropriate health decisions.

concepts.label: Data Mining
concepts.title: Data Mining
concepts.definition: Use of sophisticated analysis tools to sort through, organize, examine, and combine large sets of information.

concepts.label: Information Seeking Behavior
concepts.title: Information Seeking Behavior
concepts.definition: How information is gathered in personal, academic or work environments and the resources used.

concepts.label: Femininity
concepts.title: Femininity
concepts.definition: Female-associated sex-specific social roles and behaviors unrelated to biologic function.

concepts.label: Masculinity
concepts.title: Masculinity
concepts.definition: Male-associated sex-specific social roles and behaviors unrelated to biologic function.

concepts.label: Limit of Detection
concepts.title: Limit of Detection
concepts.definition: Concentration or quantity that is derived from the smallest measure that can be detected with reasonable certainty for a given analytical procedure.

concepts.label: Climate Change
concepts.title: Climate Change
concepts.definition: Any significant change in measures of climate (such as temperature, precipitation, or wind) lasting for an extended period (decades or longer). It may result from natural factors such as changes in the sun's intensity, natural processes within the climate system such as changes in ocean circulation, or human activities.

concepts.label: Criminals
concepts.title: Criminals
concepts.definition: Persons who have committed a crime or have been convicted of a crime.

concepts.label: Early Termination of Clinical Trials
concepts.title: Early Termination of Clinical Trials
concepts.definition: Earlier than planned termination of clinical trials.

concepts.label: Patient Preference
concepts.title: Patient Preference
concepts.definition: Individual's expression of desirability or value of one course of action, outcome, or selection in contrast to others.

concepts.label: Precision Medicine
concepts.title: Precision Medicine
concepts.definition: Clinical, therapeutic and diagnostic approaches to optimal disease management based on individual variations in a patient's genetic profile.

concepts.label: Social Stigma
concepts.title: Social Stigma
concepts.definition: A perceived attribute that is deeply discrediting and is considered to be a violation of social norms.

concepts.label: Apathy
concepts.title: Apathy
concepts.definition: Lack of emotion or emotional expression; a disorder of motivation that persists over time.

concepts.label: Memory, Long-Term
concepts.title: Memory, Long-Term
concepts.definition: Remembrance of information from 3 or more years previously.

concepts.label: Post-Exercise Hypotension
concepts.title: Post-Exercise Hypotension
concepts.definition: Transient reduction in blood pressure levels immediately after exercises that lasts 2-12 hours. The reduction varies but is typically 5-20 mm Hg when compared to pre-exercise levels. It exists both in normotensive and hypertensive individuals and may play a role in excercise related PHYSIOLOGIC ADAPTATION.

concepts.label: Pets
concepts.title: Pets
concepts.definition: Animals kept by humans for companionship and enjoyment, as opposed to DOMESTIC ANIMALS such as livestock or farm animals, which are kept for economic reasons.

concepts.label: Gender-Affirming Procedures
concepts.title: Gender-Affirming Procedures
concepts.definition: Clinical treatments used to change the physiological sexual characteristics of an individual.

concepts.label: Gender-Affirming Surgery
concepts.title: Gender-Affirming Surgery
concepts.definition: Surgical procedure(s) by which a person's physical appearance and functional abilities are changed to align with their identified gender.

concepts.label: Optic Flow
concepts.title: Optic Flow
concepts.definition: The continuous visual field seen by a subject through space and time.

concepts.label: Reflex, Righting
concepts.title: Reflex, Righting
concepts.definition: The instinctive tendency (or ability) to assume a normal position of the body in space when it has been displaced.

concepts.label: Post-Synaptic Density
concepts.title: Post-Synaptic Density
concepts.definition: Cytoskeleton specialization at the cytoplasmic side of postsynaptic membrane in SYNAPSES. It is involved in neuronal signaling and NEURONAL PLASTICITY and comprised of GLUTAMATE RECEPTORS; scaffolding molecules (e.g., PSD95, PSD93), and other proteins (e.g., CaCMKII).

concepts.label: Inappropriate Prescribing
concepts.title: Inappropriate Prescribing
concepts.definition: The practice of administering medications in a manner that poses more risk than benefit, particularly where safer alternatives exist.

concepts.label: Millon Clinical Multiaxial Inventory
concepts.title: Millon Clinical Multiaxial Inventory
concepts.definition: A psychological test consisting of true/false items. It is used as a diagnostic screening or clinical assessment of adults who evidence problematic emotional and interpersonal symptoms or who are undergoing PSYCHOTHERAPY or a psychodiagnostic evaluation.

concepts.label: Multifactor Dimensionality Reduction
concepts.title: Multifactor Dimensionality Reduction
concepts.definition: A statistical tool for detecting and modeling gene-gene interactions. It is a non-parametric and model-free approach.

concepts.label: Neuropsychiatry
concepts.title: Neuropsychiatry
concepts.definition: A subfield of psychiatry that emphasizes the somatic substructure on which mental operations and emotions are based, and the functional or organic disturbances of the central nervous system that give rise to, contribute to, or are associated with mental and emotional disorders. (From Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 8th ed.)

concepts.label: Wavelet Analysis
concepts.title: Wavelet Analysis
concepts.definition: Signal and data processing method that uses decomposition of wavelets to approximate, estimate, or compress signals with finite time and frequency domains. It represents a signal or data in terms of a fast decaying wavelet series from the original prototype wavelet, called the mother wavelet. This mathematical algorithm has been adopted widely in biomedical disciplines for data and signal processing in noise removal and audio/image compression (e.g., EEG and MRI).

concepts.label: Sarcoglycanopathies
concepts.title: Sarcoglycanopathies
concepts.definition: Deficiencies or mutations in the genes for the SARCOGLYCAN COMPLEX subunits. A variety of phenotypes are associated with these mutations including a subgroup of autosomal recessive limb girdle muscular dystrophies, cardiomyopathies, and respiratory deficiency.

concepts.label: Amyloidogenic Proteins
concepts.title: Amyloidogenic Proteins
concepts.definition: Proteins that form the core of amyloid fibrils. For example, the core of amyloid A is formed from amyloid A protein, also known as serum amyloid A protein or SAA protein.

concepts.label: Cognitive Reserve
concepts.title: Cognitive Reserve
concepts.definition: Capacity that enables an individual to cope with and/or recover from the impact of a neural injury or a psychotic episode.

concepts.label: Protease Nexins
concepts.title: Protease Nexins
concepts.definition: Extracellular protease inhibitors that are secreted from FIBROBLASTS. They form a covalent complex with SERINE PROTEASES and can mediate their cellular internalization and degradation.

concepts.label: Brain Waves
concepts.title: Brain Waves
concepts.definition: Wave-like oscillations of electric potential between parts of the brain recorded by EEG.

concepts.label: Electroencephalography Phase Synchronization
concepts.title: Electroencephalography Phase Synchronization
concepts.definition: Adjustment of BRAIN WAVES from two or more neuronal groups within or across a brain structure (e.g., cortical and limbic brain structures) to become uniform in EEG oscillation patterns in response to a stimulus. It is interpreted as a brain integration sign during many processes such as learning, memory, and perception and involves reciprocal neural connections.

concepts.label: Catastrophization
concepts.title: Catastrophization
concepts.definition: Cognitive and emotional processes encompassing magnification of pain-related stimuli, feelings of helplessness, and a generally pessimistic orientation.

concepts.label: Bullying
concepts.title: Bullying
concepts.definition: Aggressive behavior by a more powerful party that results in physical harm to or emotional distress of the victim.

concepts.label: Ligand-Gated Ion Channels
concepts.title: Ligand-Gated Ion Channels
concepts.definition: A subclass of ion channels that open or close in response to the binding of specific LIGANDS.

concepts.label: Eye Pain
concepts.title: Eye Pain
concepts.definition: A dull or sharp painful sensation associated with the outer or inner structures of the eyeball, having different causes.

concepts.label: Biota
concepts.title: Biota
concepts.definition: The spectrum of different living organisms inhabiting a particular region, habitat, or biotope.

concepts.label: Emmetropia
concepts.title: Emmetropia
concepts.definition: The condition of where images are correctly brought to a focus on the retina.

concepts.label: Cysteine Loop Ligand-Gated Ion Channel Receptors
concepts.title: Cysteine Loop Ligand-Gated Ion Channel Receptors
concepts.definition: A subfamily of ligand-gated ion channel receptors that share a characteristic loop which is formed by a disulfide bond between two CYSTEINE residues. These receptors typically contain five subunits with the cysteine-loop occurring near an N-terminal extracellular domain.
aliases: Cysteine Loop Ligand Gated Ion Channel Receptor
Cysteine Loop Ligand Gated Ion Channel Receptors
Cysteine Loop Ligand-Gated Ion Channel Receptor

concepts.label: Receptors, Ionotropic Glutamate
concepts.title: Receptors, Ionotropic Glutamate
concepts.definition: A class of ligand-gated ion channel receptors that have specificity for GLUTAMATE. They are distinct from METABOTROPIC GLUTAMATE RECEPTORS which act through a G-protein-coupled mechanism.

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2X
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2X
concepts.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2 receptors that signal by means of a ligand-gated ion channel. They are comprised of three P2X subunits which can be identical (homotrimeric form) or dissimilar (heterotrimeric form).

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y
concepts.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2 receptors whose signaling is coupled through a G-PROTEIN signaling mechanism.

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y1
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y1
concepts.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2Y receptors that have a preference for ATP and ADP. The activated P2Y1 receptor signals through the G-PROTEIN-coupled activation of PHOSPHOLIPASE C and mobilization of intracellular CALCIUM.

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y2
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y2
concepts.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2Y receptors that have a preference for ATP and UTP. The activated P2Y2 receptor acts through a G-PROTEIN-coupled PHOSPHATIDYLINOSITOL and intracellular CALCIUM SIGNALING pathway.

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2X1
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2X1
concepts.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor found at sympathetically innervated SMOOTH MUSCLE. It may play a functional role regulating the juxtoglomerular apparatus of the KIDNEY.
aliases: Purinergic Receptor P2X, Ligand-Gated Ion Channel, 1

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2X2
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2X2
concepts.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor involved in sensory signaling of TASTE PERCEPTION, chemoreception, visceral distension and NEUROPATHIC PAIN. The receptor comprises three P2X2 subunits. The P2X2 subunits also have been found associated with P2X3 RECEPTOR subunits in a heterotrimeric receptor variant.
aliases: Purinergic Receptor P2X, Ligand-Gated Ion Channel, 2

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2X3
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2X3
concepts.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor involved in sensory signaling of TASTE PERCEPTION, chemoreception, visceral distension, and NEUROPATHIC PAIN. The receptor comprises three P2X3 subunits. The P2X3 subunits are also associated with P2X2 RECEPTOR subunits in a heterotrimeric receptor variant.
aliases: Purinergic Receptor P2X, Ligand-Gated Ion Channel, 3

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2X5
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2X5
concepts.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor found at high levels in the BRAIN and IMMUNE SYSTEM.
aliases: Purinergic Receptor P2X, Ligand-Gated Ion Channel, 5

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2X7
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2X7
concepts.definition: A purinergic P2X neurotransmitter receptor that plays a role in pain sensation signaling and regulation of inflammatory processes.
aliases: Purinergic Receptor P2X, Ligand-Gated Ion Channel, 7

concepts.label: Disorder of Sex Development, 46,XY
concepts.title: Disorder of Sex Development, 46,XY
concepts.definition: Congenital conditions in individuals with a male karyotype, in which the development of the gonadal or anatomical sex is atypical.

concepts.label: Walker-Warburg Syndrome
concepts.title: Walker-Warburg Syndrome
concepts.definition: Rare autosomal recessive lissencephaly type 2 associated with congenital MUSCULAR DYSTROPHY and eye anomalies (e.g., RETINAL DETACHMENT; CATARACT; MICROPHTHALMOS). It is often associated with additional brain malformations such as HYDROCEPHALY and cerebellar hypoplasia and is the most severe form of the group of related syndromes (alpha-dystroglycanopathies) with common congenital abnormalities in the brain, eye and muscle development.

concepts.label: Smith-Magenis Syndrome
concepts.title: Smith-Magenis Syndrome
concepts.definition: Complex neurobehavioral disorder characterized by distinctive facial features (FACIES), developmental delay and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY. Behavioral phenotypes include sleep disturbance, maladaptive, self-injurious and attention-seeking behaviors. The sleep disturbance is linked to an abnormal circadian secretion pattern of MELATONIN. The syndrome is associated with de novo deletion or mutation and HAPLOINSUFFICIENCY of the retinoic acid-induced 1 protein on chromosome 17p11.2.

concepts.label: Retinal Dystrophies
concepts.title: Retinal Dystrophies
concepts.definition: A group of disorders involving predominantly the posterior portion of the ocular fundus, due to degeneration in the sensory layer of the RETINA; RETINAL PIGMENT EPITHELIUM; BRUCH MEMBRANE; CHOROID; or a combination of these tissues.

concepts.label: Pentalogy of Cantrell
concepts.title: Pentalogy of Cantrell
concepts.definition: Rare congenital deformity syndrome characterized by a combination of five anomalies as a result of neural tube defect. The five anomalies are a midline supraumbilical abdominal wall defect (e.g., OMPHALOCELE), a lower STERNUM defect, a congenital intracardiac defect, an anterior DIAPHRAGM defect, and a diaphragmatic PERICARDIUM defect (e.g., PERICARDIAL EFFUSION). Variants with incomplete and variable combinations of the defects are known. ECTOPIA CORDIS; CLEFT LIP; and CLEFT PALATE are often associated with the syndrome.

concepts.label: Aicardi Syndrome
concepts.title: Aicardi Syndrome
concepts.definition: A rare genetic disorder characterized by partial or complete absence of the CORPUS CALLOSUM, resulting in infantile spasms, MENTAL RETARDATION, and lesions of the RETINA or OPTIC NERVE.
aliases: Agenesis of Corpus Callosum with Chorioretinal Abnormality
Agenesis of Corpus Callosum with Infantile Spasms and Ocular Abnormalities
Corpus Callosum, Agenesis Of, With Chorioretinal Abnormality

concepts.label: Inhalant Abuse
concepts.title: Inhalant Abuse
concepts.definition: Illicit use of chemicals and products whose vapors can be inhaled to produce a rapid mind-altering effect. Inhalants include aerosols, gases, and volatile solvents that are often inhaled repeatedly to achieve the short-lived intoxicating effect.

concepts.label: Cerebral Ventriculitis
concepts.title: Cerebral Ventriculitis
concepts.definition: Inflammation of CEREBRAL VENTRICLES.

concepts.label: Visual Field Tests
concepts.title: Visual Field Tests
concepts.definition: Method of measuring and mapping the scope of vision, from central to peripheral of each eye.

concepts.label: Horticultural Therapy
concepts.title: Horticultural Therapy
concepts.definition: A therapeutic approach in which the engagement of a person in gardening and plant-based activities are utilized in improving an individual's social, emotional, educational, psychological, and physical well-being.

concepts.label: Megalencephaly
concepts.title: Megalencephaly
concepts.definition: A congenital abnormality in which the occipitofrontal circumference is greater than two standard deviations above the mean for a given age. It is associated with HYDROCEPHALUS; SUBDURAL EFFUSION; ARACHNOID CYSTS; or is part of a genetic condition (e.g., ALEXANDER DISEASE; SOTOS SYNDROME).

concepts.label: Spinal Cord Regeneration
concepts.title: Spinal Cord Regeneration
concepts.definition: Repair of the damaged neuron function after SPINAL CORD INJURY or SPINAL CORD DISEASES.

concepts.label: Adrenergic alpha-1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic alpha-1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC ALPHA-1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic alpha-2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic alpha-2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC ALPHA-2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC BETA-1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds bind to and activate ADRENERGIC BETA-2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-3 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-3 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate ADRENERGIC BETA-3 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic alpha-1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic alpha-1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC ALPHA-1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic alpha-2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic alpha-2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC ALPHA-2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC BETA-1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC BETA-2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adrenergic beta-3 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adrenergic beta-3 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of ADRENERGIC BETA-3 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Coronary-Subclavian Steal Syndrome
concepts.title: Coronary-Subclavian Steal Syndrome
concepts.definition: A complication of INTERNAL MAMMARY-CORONARY ARTERY ANASTOMOSIS whereby an occlusion or stenosis of the proximal SUBCLAVIAN ARTERY causes a reversal of the blood flow away from the CORONARY CIRCULATION, through the grafted INTERNAL MAMMARY ARTERY (internal thoracic artery), and back to the distal subclavian distribution.

concepts.label: CHARGE Syndrome
concepts.title: CHARGE Syndrome
concepts.definition: Rare disease characterized by COLOBOMA; CHOANAL ATRESIA; and abnormal SEMICIRCULAR CANALS. Mutations in CHD7 protein resulting in disturbed neural crest development are associated with CHARGE Syndrome.
aliases: CHARGE Association--Coloboma, Heart Anomaly, Choanal Atresia, Retardation, Genital and Ear Anomalies
Coloboma, Heart Anomaly, Choanal Atresia, Retardation, Genital and Ear Anomalies

concepts.label: Pain Perception
concepts.title: Pain Perception
concepts.definition: The process by which PAIN is recognized and interpreted by the brain.

concepts.label: Neurofeedback
concepts.title: Neurofeedback
concepts.definition: A technique to self-regulate brain activities provided as a feedback in order to better control or enhance one's own performance, control or function. This is done by trying to bring brain activities into a range associated with a desired brain function or status.

concepts.label: GABA-A Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: GABA-A Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate GABA-A RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: GABA-B Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: GABA-B Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that bind to and activate GABA-B RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: GABA-A Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: GABA-A Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate GABA-A RECEPTORS thereby blocking the actions of endogenous or exogenous GABA-A RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

concepts.label: GABA-B Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: GABA-B Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate GABA-B RECEPTORS thereby blocking the actions of endogenous or exogenous GABA-B RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

concepts.label: GABA Uptake Inhibitors
concepts.title: GABA Uptake Inhibitors
concepts.definition: Compounds that suppress or block the plasma membrane transport of GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID by GABA PLASMA MEMBRANE TRANSPORT PROTEINS.
aliases: Gamma Aminobutyric Acid Plasma Membrane Transport Inhibitor
Gamma Aminobutyric Acid Plasma Membrane Transport Inhibitors
Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid Plasma Membrane Transport Inhibitor
Gamma-Aminobutyric Acid Plasma Membrane Transport Inhibitors

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT1 RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for one or more of the specific 5-HT1 receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT2 RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for one or more of the specific 5-HT2 receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT3 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT3 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT3 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT4 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT4 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Endogenous compounds and drugs that specifically stimulate SEROTONIN 5-HT4 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT1 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN 5-HT1 RECEPTOR AGONISTS. Included under this heading are antagonists for one or more of the specific 5-HT1 receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT2 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN or SEROTONIN 5-HT2 RECEPTOR AGONISTS. Included under this heading are antagonists for one or more specific 5-HT2 receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT3 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT3 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT3 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN or SEROTONIN 5-HT3 RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

concepts.label: Serotonin 5-HT4 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Serotonin 5-HT4 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to but do not activate SEROTONIN 5-HT4 RECEPTORS, thereby blocking the actions of SEROTONIN or SEROTONIN RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2X4
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2X4
concepts.definition: A widely distributed purinergic P2X receptor subtype that plays a role in pain sensation. P2X4 receptors found on MICROGLIA cells may also play a role in the mediation of allodynia-related NEUROPATHIC PAIN.
aliases: Purinergic Receptor P2X, Ligand-Gated Ion Channel, 4

concepts.label: Purinergic Agents
concepts.title: Purinergic Agents
concepts.definition: Compounds that act on PURINERGIC RECEPTORS or influence the synthesis, storage, uptake, metabolism, or release of purinergic transmitters.

concepts.label: Purinergic P1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adenosine A1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adenosine A1 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate ADENOSINE A1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adenosine A2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adenosine A2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that selectively bind to and activate ADENOSINE A2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adenosine A3 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Adenosine A3 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that selectively bind to and activate ADENOSINE A3 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Purinergic P2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P2 Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Purinergic P2X Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P2X Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P2X RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for specific P2X receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Purinergic P2Y Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P2Y Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and stimulate PURINERGIC P2Y RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are agonists for specific P2Y receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Purinergic Agonists
concepts.title: Purinergic Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and activate PURINERGIC RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Purinergic Antagonists
concepts.title: Purinergic Antagonists
concepts.definition: Drugs that bind to and block the activation of PURINERGIC RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Purinergic P1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adenosine A1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adenosine A1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of ADENOSINE A1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adenosine A2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adenosine A2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that selectively bind to and block the activation of ADENOSINE A2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Adenosine A3 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Adenosine A3 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that selectively bind to and block the activation of ADENOSINE A3 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Purinergic P2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Purinergic P2X Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P2X Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P2X RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are antagonists for specific P2X receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Purinergic P2Y Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Purinergic P2Y Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that bind to and block the stimulation of PURINERGIC P2Y RECEPTORS. Included under this heading are antagonists for specific P2Y receptor subtypes.

concepts.label: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome
concepts.title: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome
concepts.definition: SKELETAL MUSCLE pain and tenderness along the posteromedial TIBIA resulting from exercise such as running and other physical activity.

concepts.label: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y12
concepts.title: Receptors, Purinergic P2Y12
concepts.definition: A subclass of purinergic P2Y receptors that have a preference for ADP binding and are coupled to GTP-BINDING PROTEIN ALPHA SUBUNIT, GI. The P2Y12 purinergic receptors are found in PLATELETS where they play an important role regulating PLATELET ACTIVATION.

concepts.label: Neural Stem Cells
concepts.title: Neural Stem Cells
concepts.definition: Self-renewing cells that generate the main phenotypes of the nervous system in both the embryo and adult. Neural stem cells are precursors to both NEURONS and NEUROGLIA.

concepts.label: Organs at Risk
concepts.title: Organs at Risk
concepts.definition: Organs which might be damaged during exposure to a toxin or to some form of therapy. It most frequently refers to healthy organs located in the radiation field during radiation therapy.

concepts.label: Information Literacy
concepts.title: Information Literacy
concepts.definition: The ability to recognize when information is needed and to locate, evaluate, and use the needed information effectively.

concepts.label: Drug-Seeking Behavior
concepts.title: Drug-Seeking Behavior
concepts.definition: Activities performed to obtain licit or illicit substances.

concepts.label: Suicidal Ideation
concepts.title: Suicidal Ideation
concepts.definition: A risk factor for suicide attempts and completions, it is the most common of all suicidal behavior, but only a minority of ideators engage in overt self-harm.

concepts.label: Diagnostic Self Evaluation
concepts.title: Diagnostic Self Evaluation
concepts.definition: A self-evaluation of health status.

concepts.label: Anticipation, Psychological
concepts.title: Anticipation, Psychological
concepts.definition: The ability to foresee what is likely to happen on the basis of past experience. It is largely a frontal lobe function.

concepts.label: Learning Curve
concepts.title: Learning Curve
concepts.definition: The course of learning of an individual or a group. It is a measure of performance plotted over time.

concepts.label: HIV Serosorting
concepts.title: HIV Serosorting
concepts.definition: The practice of making choices about SEXUAL PARTNERS based on their HIV status.

concepts.label: Mirror Neurons
concepts.title: Mirror Neurons
concepts.definition: Neurons that fire when an animal acts or observes the same action of another thus coding the motor response. They were originally discovered in the premotor and parietal cortex of the monkey and studies have shown that neurons that have a similar mechanism are present in humans. Mirror neurons are theorized to be related to social cognition.

concepts.label: Nociception
concepts.title: Nociception
concepts.definition: Sensing of noxious mechanical, thermal or chemical stimuli by NOCICEPTORS. It is the sensory component of visceral and tissue pain (NOCICEPTIVE PAIN).

concepts.label: Nociceptive Pain
concepts.title: Nociceptive Pain
concepts.definition: Dull or sharp aching pain caused by stimulated NOCICEPTORS due to tissue injury, inflammation or diseases. It can be divided into somatic or tissue pain and VISCERAL PAIN.

concepts.label: Postsynaptic Potential Summation
concepts.title: Postsynaptic Potential Summation
concepts.definition: Physiological integration of multiple SYNAPTIC POTENTIAL signals to reach the threshold and initiate postsynaptic ACTION POTENTIALS. In spatial summation stimulations from additional synaptic junctions are recruited to generate s response. In temporal summation succeeding stimuli signals are summed up to reach the threshold. The postsynaptic potentials can be either excitatory or inhibitory (EPSP or IPSP).

concepts.label: Reflex, Trigeminocardiac
concepts.title: Reflex, Trigeminocardiac
concepts.definition: Sudden occurrence of BRADYCARDIA or HEART ARREST induced by manipulations of the MAXILLARY NERVE AND MANDIBULAR NERVE during a craniomaxillofacial or oral surgery. It is the maxillary and mandibular variants of OCULOCARDIAC REFLEX.

concepts.label: Dopaminergic Neurons
concepts.title: Dopaminergic Neurons
concepts.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is DOPAMINE.

concepts.label: Serotonergic Neurons
concepts.title: Serotonergic Neurons
concepts.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is SEROTONIN.

concepts.label: Cholinergic Neurons
concepts.title: Cholinergic Neurons
concepts.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is ACETYLCHOLINE.

concepts.label: GABAergic Neurons
concepts.title: GABAergic Neurons
concepts.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is GAMMA-AMINOBUTYRIC ACID.

concepts.label: Adrenergic Neurons
concepts.title: Adrenergic Neurons
concepts.definition: Neurons whose primary neurotransmitter is EPINEPHRINE.

concepts.label: Central Nervous System Sensitization
concepts.title: Central Nervous System Sensitization
concepts.definition: An increased response to stimulation that is mediated by amplification of signaling in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM (CNS).

concepts.label: Cerebral Small Vessel Diseases
concepts.title: Cerebral Small Vessel Diseases
concepts.definition: Pathological processes or diseases where cerebral MICROVESSELS show abnormalities. They are often associated with aging, hypertension and risk factors for lacunar infarcts (see LACUNAR INFARCTION); LEUKOARAIOSIS; and CEREBRAL HEMORRHAGE.

concepts.label: Peripheral Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Peripheral Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Injuries to the PERIPHERAL NERVES.

concepts.label: Chronic Pain
concepts.title: Chronic Pain
concepts.definition: Aching sensation that persists for more than a few months. It may or may not be associated with trauma or disease, and may persist after the initial injury has healed. Its localization, character, and timing are more vague than with acute pain.

concepts.label: Musculoskeletal Pain
concepts.title: Musculoskeletal Pain
concepts.definition: Discomfort stemming from muscles, LIGAMENTS, tendons, and bones.

concepts.label: Mastodynia
concepts.title: Mastodynia
concepts.definition: Pain in the breast generally classified as cyclical (associated with menstrual periods), or noncyclical, i.e. originating from the breast or nearby muscles or joints, ranging from minor discomfort to severely incapacitating.

concepts.label: Plyometric Exercise
concepts.title: Plyometric Exercise
concepts.definition: Exercises in which muscles are repeatedly and rapidly stretched, followed by shortening, concentric MUSCLE CONTRACTION (e.g. jumping and rebounding). They are designed to exert maximal force in minimal time by increasing STRETCH REFLEX.

concepts.label: Breakthrough Pain
concepts.title: Breakthrough Pain
concepts.definition: Acute pain that comes on rapidly despite the use of pain medication.

concepts.label: Stroke, Lacunar
concepts.title: Stroke, Lacunar
concepts.definition: Stroke caused by lacunar infarction or other small vessel diseases of the brain. It features hemiparesis (see PARESIS), hemisensory, or hemisensory motor loss.

concepts.label: Anhedonia
concepts.title: Anhedonia
concepts.definition: Inability to experience pleasure due to impairment or dysfunction of normal psychological and neurobiological mechanisms. It is a symptom of many PSYCHOTIC DISORDERS (e.g., DEPRESSIVE DISORDER, MAJOR; and SCHIZOPHRENIA).

concepts.label: Stereocilia
concepts.title: Stereocilia
concepts.definition: Mechanosensing organelles of hair cells which respond to fluid motion or fluid pressure changes. They have various functions in many different animals, but are primarily used in hearing.

concepts.label: Polydipsia
concepts.title: Polydipsia
concepts.definition: Excessive thirst manifested by excessive fluid intake. It is characteristic of many diseases such as DIABETES MELLITUS; DIABETES INSIPIDUS; and NEPHROGENIC DIABETES INSIPIDUS. The condition may be psychogenic in origin.

concepts.label: Polydipsia, Psychogenic
concepts.title: Polydipsia, Psychogenic
concepts.definition: A clinical disorder characterized by excessive fluid intake (polydipsia); HYPONATREMIA; and POLYURIA in SCHIZOPHRENIA and other psychiatric disorders. Impaired water metabolism in psychogenic polydipsia can result in WATER INTOXICATION.

concepts.label: Signal-To-Noise Ratio
concepts.title: Signal-To-Noise Ratio
concepts.definition: The comparison of the quantity of meaningful data to the irrelevant or incorrect data.

concepts.label: Acute Pain
concepts.title: Acute Pain
concepts.definition: Intensely discomforting, distressful, or agonizing sensation associated with trauma or disease, with well-defined location, character, and timing.

concepts.label: Neuroimaging
concepts.title: Neuroimaging
concepts.definition: Non-invasive methods of visualizing the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM, especially the brain, by various imaging modalities.

concepts.label: Functional Neuroimaging
concepts.title: Functional Neuroimaging
concepts.definition: Methods for visualizing REGIONAL BLOOD FLOW, metabolic, electrical, or other physiological activities in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM using various imaging modalities.

concepts.label: Genotyping Techniques
concepts.title: Genotyping Techniques
concepts.definition: Methods used to determine individuals' specific ALLELES or SNPS (single nucleotide polymorphisms).

concepts.label: Protein Interaction Maps
concepts.title: Protein Interaction Maps
concepts.definition: Graphs representing sets of measurable, non-covalent physical contacts with specific PROTEINS in living organisms or in cells.

concepts.label: Magnetometry
concepts.title: Magnetometry
concepts.definition: The measurement of various aspects of MAGNETIC FIELDS.

concepts.label: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis
concepts.title: Anti-N-Methyl-D-Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis
concepts.definition: Disorder characterized by symptoms of CATATONIA; HYPOVENTILATION; DYSKINESIAS; ENCEPHALITIS; and SEIZURES followed by a reduced CONSCIOUSNESS. It is often followed by a viral-like prodrome. Many cases are self-limiting and respond well to IMMUNOMODULATORY THERAPIES against the NMDA RECEPTORS antibodies.
aliases: Anti N Methyl D Aspartate Receptor Encephalitis

concepts.label: Anthropology, Medical
concepts.title: Anthropology, Medical
concepts.definition: Field of social science that is concerned with differences between human groups as related to health status and beliefs.

concepts.label: Herbivory
concepts.title: Herbivory
concepts.definition: The act of feeding on plants by animals.

concepts.label: Carnivory
concepts.title: Carnivory
concepts.definition: The consumption of animal flesh.

concepts.label: Ophthalmoplegic Migraine
concepts.title: Ophthalmoplegic Migraine
concepts.definition: Childhood-onset of recurrent headaches with an oculomotor cranial nerve palsy. Typically, ABDUCENS NERVE; OCULOMOTOR NERVE; and TROCHLEAR NERVE are involved with DIPLOPIA and BLEPHAROPTOSIS.

concepts.label: Pudendal Nerve
concepts.title: Pudendal Nerve
concepts.definition: A nerve which originates in the sacral spinal cord (S2 to S4) and innervates the PERINEUM, the external GENITALIA, the external ANAL SPHINCTER and the external urethral sphincter. It has three major branches: the perineal nerve, inferior anal nerves, and the dorsal nerve of penis or clitoris.

concepts.label: Pudendal Neuralgia
concepts.title: Pudendal Neuralgia
concepts.definition: Pain associated with a damaged PUDENDAL NERVE. Clinical features may include positional pain with sitting in the perineal and genital areas, sexual dysfunction and FECAL INCONTINENCE and URINARY INCONTINENCE.

concepts.label: Sense of Coherence
concepts.title: Sense of Coherence
concepts.definition: A view of the world and the individual's environment as comprehensible, manageable, and meaningful, claiming that the way people view their life has a positive influence on their health.

concepts.label: Dyscalculia
concepts.title: Dyscalculia
concepts.definition: Impaired ability in numerical concepts. These inabilities arise as a result of primary neurological lesion, are syndromic (e.g., GERSTMANN SYNDROME ) or acquired due to brain damage.

concepts.label: Fetal Globulins
concepts.title: Fetal Globulins
concepts.definition: Specialized proteins that are preferentially expressed during FETAL DEVELOPMENT.

concepts.label: Social Networking
concepts.title: Social Networking
concepts.definition: Individuals connected by family, work or other interests. It also includes connectivity facilitated by computer-based communications.

concepts.label: Neoplasm Grading
concepts.title: Neoplasm Grading
concepts.definition: Methods which attempt to express in replicable terms the level of CELL DIFFERENTIATION in neoplasms as increasing ANAPLASIA correlates with the aggressiveness of the neoplasm.

concepts.label: Performance Anxiety
concepts.title: Performance Anxiety
concepts.definition: Anxiety related to the execution of a task. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 9th ed.)

concepts.label: Cognitive Dysfunction
concepts.title: Cognitive Dysfunction
concepts.definition: Diminished or impaired mental and/or intellectual function.

concepts.label: Hoarding
concepts.title: Hoarding
concepts.definition: A persistent difficulty discarding or parting with possessions.

concepts.label: Repetition Priming
concepts.title: Repetition Priming
concepts.definition: A type of procedural memory manifested as a change in the ability to identify an item as a result of a previous encounter with the item or stimuli.

concepts.label: Economics, Behavioral
concepts.title: Economics, Behavioral
concepts.definition: The combined discipline of psychology and economics that investigates what happens in markets in which some of the agents display human limitations and complications.

concepts.label: Agenesis of Corpus Callosum
concepts.title: Agenesis of Corpus Callosum
concepts.definition: Birth defect that results in a partial or complete absence of the CORPUS CALLOSUM. It may be isolated or a part of a syndrome (e.g., AICARDI'S SYNDROME; ACROCALLOSAL SYNDROME; ANDERMANN SYNDROME; and HOLOPROSENCEPHALY). Clinical manifestations include neuromotor skill impairment and INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY of variable severity.

concepts.label: Breast Milk Expression
concepts.title: Breast Milk Expression
concepts.definition: The act of evacuating BREAST MILK by hand or with a pump.

concepts.label: Memory, Episodic
concepts.title: Memory, Episodic
concepts.definition: Type of declarative memory, consisting of personal memory in contrast to general knowledge.

concepts.label: Depressive Disorder, Treatment-Resistant
concepts.title: Depressive Disorder, Treatment-Resistant
concepts.definition: Failure to respond to two or more trials of antidepressant monotherapy or failure to respond to four or more trials of different antidepressant therapies. (Campbell's Psychiatric Dictionary, 9th ed.)

concepts.label: Olfactory Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Olfactory Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the OLFACTORY NERVE. It may result in various olfactory dysfunction including a complete loss of smell.

concepts.label: Oculomotor Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Oculomotor Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the OCULOMOTOR NERVE. This may result in various eye movement dysfunction.

concepts.label: Trigeminal Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Trigeminal Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the TRIGEMINAL NERVE. It may result in extreme pain, abnormal sensation in the areas the nerve innervates on face, jaw, gums and tongue and can cause difficulties with speech and chewing. It is sometimes associated with various dental treatments.

concepts.label: Lingual Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Lingual Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the LINGUAL NERVE. It may be a complication following dental treatments.

concepts.label: Vagus Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Vagus Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the VAGUS NERVE. Because the vagus nerve innervates multiple organs, injuries in the nerve fibers may result in any gastrointestinal organ dysfunction downstream of the injury site.

concepts.label: Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the LARYNGEAL NERVE.

concepts.label: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Recurrent Laryngeal Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the RECURRENT LARYNGEAL NERVE that may result in vocal cord dysfunction.

concepts.label: Accessory Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Accessory Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the ACCESSORY NERVE. Damage to the nerve may produce weakness in head rotation and shoulder elevation.

concepts.label: Hypoglossal Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Hypoglossal Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the HYPOGLOSSAL NERVE.

concepts.label: Trochlear Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Trochlear Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the TROCHLEAR NERVE.

concepts.label: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Vestibulocochlear Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the VESTIBULOCOCHLEAR NERVE.

concepts.label: Glossopharyngeal Nerve Injuries
concepts.title: Glossopharyngeal Nerve Injuries
concepts.definition: Traumatic injuries to the GLOSSOPHARYNGEAL NERVE.

concepts.label: Forgiveness
concepts.title: Forgiveness
concepts.definition: Excusing or pardoning for an offense or release of anger or resentment.

concepts.label: Numbers Needed To Treat
concepts.title: Numbers Needed To Treat
concepts.definition: Number of patients who need to be treated in order to prevent one additional bad outcome. It is the inverse of Absolute Risk Reduction.

concepts.label: Tobacco Use Cessation Devices
concepts.title: Tobacco Use Cessation Devices
concepts.definition: Devices or delivery systems used to aid in ending a TOBACCO habit.

concepts.label: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channels
concepts.title: Voltage-Gated Sodium Channels
concepts.definition: A family of membrane proteins that selectively conduct SODIUM ions due to changes in the TRANSMEMBRANE POTENTIAL DIFFERENCE. They typically have a multimeric structure with a core alpha subunit that defines the sodium channel subtype and several beta subunits that modulate sodium channel activity.

concepts.label: Premature Ejaculation
concepts.title: Premature Ejaculation
concepts.definition: The emission of SEMEN and seminal fluid during the act of preparation for sexual intercourse, i.e. before there is penetration, or shortly after penetration.

concepts.label: Alice in Wonderland Syndrome
concepts.title: Alice in Wonderland Syndrome
concepts.definition: Neurological condition characterized by disturbances in VISUAL PERCEPTION, most often of BODY SCHEMA, TIME PERCEPTION and HALLUCINATIONS. It is associated with MIGRAINE, infections (e.g., INFECTIOUS MONONUCLEOSIS), FEVER, EPILEPSY, and other neurological and psychiatric disorders.

concepts.label: Molecular Docking Simulation
concepts.title: Molecular Docking Simulation
concepts.definition: A computer simulation technique that is used to model the interaction between two molecules. Typically the docking simulation measures the interactions of a small molecule or ligand with a part of a larger molecule such as a protein.

concepts.label: Databases, Chemical
concepts.title: Databases, Chemical
concepts.definition: Databases devoted to knowledge about specific chemicals.

concepts.label: Spatial Analysis
concepts.title: Spatial Analysis
concepts.definition: Investigative techniques which measure the topological, geometric, and or geographic properties of the entities studied.

concepts.label: Spatio-Temporal Analysis
concepts.title: Spatio-Temporal Analysis
concepts.definition: Techniques which study entities using their topological, geometric, or geographic properties and include the dimension of time in the analysis.

concepts.label: Geographic Mapping
concepts.title: Geographic Mapping
concepts.definition: Creating a representation of areas of the earth or other celestial bodies, for the purpose of visualizing spatial distributions of various information.

concepts.label: Geography, Medical
concepts.title: Geography, Medical
concepts.definition: The area of medicine concerned with the effects on health and disease due to geographic factors such as CLIMATE, environmental conditions, and geographic location.

concepts.label: Optogenetics
concepts.title: Optogenetics
concepts.definition: The combination of genetic and optical methods in controlling specific events with temporal precision in targeted cells of a functioning intact biological system.

concepts.label: Motivational Interviewing
concepts.title: Motivational Interviewing
concepts.definition: It is a client-centered, directive method for eliciting intrinsic motivation to change using open-ended questions, reflective listening, and decisional balancing. This nonjudgmental, nonconfrontational interviewing style is designed to minimize a patient's resistance to change by creating an interaction that supports open discussion of risky or problem behavior.

concepts.label: Social Marginalization
concepts.title: Social Marginalization
concepts.definition: Individuals or groups, excluded from participation in the economic, social, and political activities of membership in a community.

concepts.label: Narrative Therapy
concepts.title: Narrative Therapy
concepts.definition: A form of PSYCHOTHERAPY that centers on the individuals as the experts in their own lives and views problems as separate from people. It is assumed that people have many skills, competencies, beliefs, values, commitments, and abilities that will assist them to reduce the influence of problems in their lives.

concepts.label: NAV1.1 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
concepts.title: NAV1.1 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
concepts.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype that is predominantly expressed in the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM. Defects in the SCN1A gene which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel are associated with DRAVET SYNDROME, generalized epilepsy with febrile seizures plus, type 2 (GEFS+2), and familial hemiplegic migraine type 3.

concepts.label: NAV1.4 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
concepts.title: NAV1.4 Voltage-Gated Sodium Channel
concepts.definition: A voltage-gated sodium channel subtype that mediates the sodium ion PERMEABILITY of SKELETAL MYOCYTES. Defects in the SCN4A gene, which codes for the alpha subunit of this sodium channel, are associated with several MYOTONIC DISORDERS.

concepts.label: Drug Overdose
concepts.title: Drug Overdose
concepts.definition: Accidental or deliberate use of a medication or street drug in excess of normal dosage.

concepts.label: Transgender Persons
concepts.title: Transgender Persons
concepts.definition: Persons having a sense of persistent identification with, and expression of, gender-coded behaviors not typically associated with one's anatomical sex at birth, with or without a desire to undergo GENDER-AFFIRMING PROCEDURES.

concepts.label: Connectome
concepts.title: Connectome
concepts.definition: A comprehensive map of the physical interconnections of an organism's neural networks. This modular organization of neuronal architecture is believed to underlie disease mechanisms and the biological development of the CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

concepts.label: Animal Distribution
concepts.title: Animal Distribution
concepts.definition: A process by which animals in various forms and stages of development are physically distributed through time and space.

concepts.label: Pneumorrhachis
concepts.title: Pneumorrhachis
concepts.definition: Presence of air or gas within the spinal canal cavity (EPIDURAL SPACE; or SUBARACHNOID SPACE). It may result from traumatic injuries, emphysema, infection and other conditions. It can also develop as a complication of various SURGICAL PROCEDURES (e.g., MYELOGRAPHY).

concepts.label: Central Pattern Generators
concepts.title: Central Pattern Generators
concepts.definition: Networks of nerve cells that control the firing patterns of MOTOR NEURONS to produce rhythmic movements such as MASTICATION; WALKING; SWIMMING; RESPIRATION; and PERISTALSIS.

concepts.label: Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy
concepts.title: Virtual Reality Exposure Therapy
concepts.definition: Treatment technique in a virtual environment which allows the participant to experience a sense of presence in an immersive, computer-generated, three-dimensional, interactive environment that minimizes avoidance behavior and facilitates emotional involvement. (from Curr Psychiatry Rep (2010) 12:298)

concepts.label: Cannabinoid Receptor Modulators
concepts.title: Cannabinoid Receptor Modulators
concepts.definition: Compounds that interact with and modulate the activity of CANNABINOID RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Cannabinoid Receptor Agonists
concepts.title: Cannabinoid Receptor Agonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that interact with and stimulate the activity of CANNABINOID RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Cannabinoid Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Cannabinoid Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of CANNABINOID RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Endocannabinoids
concepts.title: Endocannabinoids
concepts.definition: Fatty acid derivatives that have specificity for CANNABINOID RECEPTORS. They are structurally distinct from CANNABINOIDS and were originally discovered as a group of endogenous CANNABINOID RECEPTOR AGONISTS.

concepts.label: Binge Drinking
concepts.title: Binge Drinking
concepts.definition: Drinking an excessive amount of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES in a short period of time.

concepts.label: Prescription Drug Misuse
concepts.title: Prescription Drug Misuse
concepts.definition: Improper use of prescription drugs or medications outside the intended purpose, scope, or guidelines for use.
aliases: Non Medical Use of Prescription Drugs

concepts.label: Racism
concepts.title: Racism
concepts.definition: Differential treatment or unequal access to opportunities, based on group membership such as origin or ethnicity.

concepts.label: Ageism
concepts.title: Ageism
concepts.definition: Biased behaviors or attitudes, differential treatment, unequal access to social participation or opportunities based on age.

concepts.label: Sexism
concepts.title: Sexism
concepts.definition: Prejudice or discrimination based on gender or behavior or attitudes that foster stereotyped social roles based on gender.

concepts.label: Social Discrimination
concepts.title: Social Discrimination
concepts.definition: Differential or prejudicial group behavior toward others by virtue of their group membership.

concepts.label: Homophobia
concepts.title: Homophobia
concepts.definition: Differential treatment or unequal access to opportunities or services based on perceived homosexual preference or orientation.

concepts.label: Delusional Parasitosis
concepts.title: Delusional Parasitosis
concepts.definition: A delusional disorder of belief in infestation by insects or other parasites. This FORMICATION is typically accompanied by dermatological manifestation such as PRURITUS that may lead to self-mutilation in order to remove the perceived parasites. It can be either primary or secondary to a somatic or psychiatric condition.

concepts.label: Myalgia
concepts.title: Myalgia
concepts.definition: Painful sensation in the muscles.

concepts.label: Ependymoglial Cells
concepts.title: Ependymoglial Cells
concepts.definition: The macroglial cells of EPENDYMA. They are characterized by bipolar cell body shape and processes that contact BASAL LAMINA around blood vessels and/or the PIA MATER and the CEREBRAL VENTRICLES. Muller cells of the RETINA are included based on similar microenvironmental contacts and morphology.

concepts.label: Warm-Up Exercise
concepts.title: Warm-Up Exercise
concepts.definition: Physical activities done to prepare the body for more intense physical activities.

concepts.label: Human Coprophagia
concepts.title: Human Coprophagia
concepts.definition: A rare aberrant human behavior involving consumption of excrement.

concepts.label: Nodding Syndrome
concepts.title: Nodding Syndrome
concepts.definition: Unexplained neurologic condition characterized by episodes of atonic seizures, convulsions or staring spells with further cognitive decline.

concepts.label: Microbiota
concepts.title: Microbiota
concepts.definition: The full collection of microbes (bacteria, fungi, virus, etc.) that naturally exist within a particular biological niche such as an organism, soil, a body of water, etc.

concepts.label: Type B Personality
concepts.title: Type B Personality
concepts.definition: Behavior pattern characterized by a generally calm and even-tempered demeanor. Emotionally, such personality types show less frequent irritation, anger, hostility, and aggression than Type A individuals. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 223)

concepts.label: Type D Personality
concepts.title: Type D Personality
concepts.definition: Behavior pattern characterized by negative emotionality, an inability to express emotions, and social isolation, which has been linked to greater cardiovascular disease and increased mortality. (from International Encyclopedia of the Social Sciences, 2008, p. 217)

concepts.label: Chemically-Induced Disorders
concepts.title: Chemically-Induced Disorders
concepts.definition: Disorders caused by the intentional or unintentional ingestion or exposure to chemical substances such as PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS; NOXAE; and PESTICIDES.

concepts.label: Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
concepts.title: Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
concepts.definition: Disorders that result from the intended use of PHARMACEUTICAL PREPARATIONS. Included in this heading are a broad variety of chemically-induced adverse conditions due to toxicity, DRUG INTERACTIONS, and metabolic effects of pharmaceuticals.
aliases: Drug Related Side Effects and Adverse Reaction
Drug Related Side Effects and Adverse Reactions
Drug-Related Side Effects and Adverse Reaction

concepts.label: Tobacco Use
concepts.title: Tobacco Use
concepts.definition: Use of TOBACCO (Nicotiana tabacum L) and TOBACCO PRODUCTS.

concepts.label: Gasotransmitters
concepts.title: Gasotransmitters
concepts.definition: Endogenously produced lipid-soluble gaseous molecules which function as neurotransmitters and signal mediators targeting ION CHANNELS and transporters.

concepts.label: Orexin Receptors
concepts.title: Orexin Receptors
concepts.definition: G-protein-coupled NEUROPEPTIDE RECEPTORS that have specificity for OREXINS and play a role in appetite control, and sleep-wake cycles. Two principle receptor types exist, each having a specificity for OREXIN A and OREXIN B peptide subtypes.

concepts.label: Receptor, Metabotropic Glutamate 5
concepts.title: Receptor, Metabotropic Glutamate 5
concepts.definition: A type I G protein-coupled receptor mostly expressed post-synaptic pyramidal cells of the cortex and CENTRAL NERVOUS SYSTEM.

concepts.label: alpha7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
concepts.title: alpha7 Nicotinic Acetylcholine Receptor
concepts.definition: A member of the NICOTINIC ACETYLCHOLINE RECEPTOR subfamily of the LIGAND-GATED ION CHANNEL family. It consists entirely of pentameric α7 subunits expressed in the CNS, autonomic nervous system, vascular system, lymphocytes and spleen.

concepts.label: Cool-Down Exercise
concepts.title: Cool-Down Exercise
concepts.definition: Tapering-off physical activity from vigorous to light, to gradually return the body to pre-exercise condition and metabolic state.

concepts.label: Vocal Cord Dysfunction
concepts.title: Vocal Cord Dysfunction
concepts.definition: A disorder characterized by an intermittent abnormal VOCAL CORDS movement toward the midline during inspiration or expiration resulting in upper AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION.

concepts.label: Neurokinin-1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Neurokinin-1 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds that inhibit or block the activity of NEUROKININ-1 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Veterinary Sports Medicine
concepts.title: Veterinary Sports Medicine
concepts.definition: The field of veterinary medicine concerned with PHYSICAL FITNESS of animals in sports (horse racing, dog racing, etc.) and the diagnosis and treatment of sports injuries in animals.

concepts.label: Physical Conditioning, Human
concepts.title: Physical Conditioning, Human
concepts.definition: Diet modification and physical exercise to improve the ability to carry out daily tasks and perform physical activities.

concepts.label: Anticholinergic Syndrome
concepts.title: Anticholinergic Syndrome
concepts.definition: Adverse drug effects associated with CHOLINERGIC ANTAGONISTS. Clinical features include TACHYCARDIA; HYPERTHERMIA; MYDRIASIS, dry skin and dry mucous membranes, decreased bowel sounds and urinary retention in peripheral anticholinergic syndrome; and HALLUCINATIONS; PSYCHOSES; SEIZURES; and COMA in central anticholinergic syndrome.

concepts.label: Alcohol Abstinence
concepts.title: Alcohol Abstinence
concepts.definition: Non-consumption of ALCOHOLIC BEVERAGES.

concepts.label: Mindfulness
concepts.title: Mindfulness
concepts.definition: A psychological state of awareness, the practices that promote this awareness, a mode of processing information and a character trait. As a therapy mindfulness is defined as a moment-to-moment awareness of one's experience without judgment and as a state and not a trait.

concepts.label: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
concepts.title: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
concepts.definition: Contextually focused form of cognitive behavioral psychotherapy that uses MINDFULNESS and behavioral activation to increase patients' psychological flexibility in areas such as ability to engage in values-based, positive behaviors while experiencing difficult thoughts, emotions, or sensations.

concepts.label: Teach-Back Communication
concepts.title: Teach-Back Communication
concepts.definition: Providing the patient, family or others information, and then allowing them to take an action or restate the information in their own words. The clinician prefaces communications with a statement framed to show the clinician has the burden of effective communication rather than the patient.

concepts.label: Psychotherapy, Psychodynamic
concepts.title: Psychotherapy, Psychodynamic
concepts.definition: Forms of PSYCHOTHERAPY falling within or deriving from the psychoanalytic tradition, that view individuals as reacting to unconscious forces (e.g., motivation, drive), that focus on processes of change and development, and that place a premium on self understanding and making meaning of what is unconscious.

concepts.label: Social Determinants of Health
concepts.title: Social Determinants of Health
concepts.definition: The circumstances in which people are born, grow up, live, work, and age, as well as the systems put in place to deal with illness. These circumstances are in turn shaped by a wider set of forces: economics, social policies, and politics (htt[已隐藏本地路径]

concepts.label: Hope
concepts.title: Hope
concepts.definition: Belief in a positive outcome.

concepts.label: Acetylcholine Release Inhibitors
concepts.title: Acetylcholine Release Inhibitors
concepts.definition: Compounds that block release of the neurotransmitter ACETYLCHOLINE.

concepts.label: Dopamine D2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.title: Dopamine D2 Receptor Antagonists
concepts.definition: Compounds and drugs that bind to and inhibit or block the activation of DOPAMINE D2 RECEPTORS.

concepts.label: Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy
concepts.title: Sepsis-Associated Encephalopathy
concepts.definition: Acute neurological dysfunction during severe SEPSIS in the absence of direct brain infection characterized by systemic inflammation and BLOOD BRAIN BARRIER perturbation.

concepts.label: Corneal Injuries
concepts.title: Corneal Injuries
concepts.definition: Damage or trauma inflicted to the CORNEA by external means.

concepts.label: Circuit-Based Exercise
concepts.title: Circuit-Based Exercise
concepts.definition: Alternating sets of exercise that work out different muscle groups and that also alternate between aerobic and anaerobic exercises, which, when combined together, offer an overall program to improve strength, stamina, balance, or functioning.

concepts.label: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder
concepts.title: Premenstrual Dysphoric Disorder
concepts.definition: A condition in which a woman suffers from severe depression, irritability, and tension before MENSTRUATION. Premenstrual dysphoric disorder (PMDD) may involve a wide range of physical or emotional symptoms, which are more severe and debilitating than those seen with premenstrual syndrome (PMS), and which include at least one mood-related symptom. Symptoms usually stop when, or shortly after, menstruation begins.

concepts.label: Diving Reflex
concepts.title: Diving Reflex
concepts.definition: BREATH HOLDING; VASOCONSTRICTION; and a drop in HEART RATE in response to submersion of the face in cold water.

concepts.label: Absorption, Physiological
concepts.title: Absorption, Physiological
concepts.definition: Uptake of substances by the body, tissues, or cells. The uptake may occur by various forms of BIOLOGICAL TRANSPORT or by simple DIFFUSION.

concepts.label: Intramuscular Absorption
concepts.title: Intramuscular Absorption
concepts.definition: Uptake of substances via muscle tissue.

concepts.label: Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak
concepts.title: Cerebrospinal Fluid Leak
concepts.definition: Discharge of cerebrospinal fluid through a hole through the skull bone most commonly draining from the nose (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID RHINORRHEA) or the ear (CEREBROSPINAL FLUID OTORRHEA).

concepts.label: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
concepts.title: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
concepts.definition: Idiopathic recurrent VERTIGO associated with POSITIONAL NYSTAGMUS. It is associated with a vestibular loss most often with OTOCONIA dislodge but without other neurological or auditory signs. Unlike in LABYRINTHITIS and VESTIBULAR NEURONITIS, inflammation in the ear is not observed.

concepts.label: Myotonin-Protein Kinase
concepts.title: Myotonin-Protein Kinase
concepts.definition: Serine/threonine protein kinase responsible for various SKELETAL MUSCLE functions; HEART CONDUCTION SYSTEM activity; calcium HOMEOSTASIS; calcium uptake by SARCOPLASMIC RETICULUM and SYNAPTIC PLASTICITY. It is encoded by the DMPK gene and its abnormal EXPANDED TRINUCLEOTIDE REPEAT of CTG in the 3'-UTR is associated with MYOTONIC DYSTROPHY 1.

concepts.label: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group I
concepts.title: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group I
concepts.definition: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal neuronal and glial CELL PROLIFERATION or APOPTOSIS in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes congenital MICROCEPHALIES; MICROLISSENCEPHALIES, megalencephalies, HEMIMEGALENCEPHALIES and cortical dysplasias with balloon cells.
aliases: Malformations Due to Abnormal Neuronal and Glial Proliferation or Apoptosis
Malformations Secondary to Abnormal Neuronal and Glial Proliferation or Apoptosis

concepts.label: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group III
concepts.title: Malformations of Cortical Development, Group III
concepts.definition: Cortical malformations secondary to abnormal cortical maturation after CELL MIGRATION in NEUROGENESIS. This group includes injury to the cortex during later stages of cortical development such as POLYMICROGYRIA and focal cortical dysplasias.
aliases: Malformations Due to Abnormal Postmigrational Development
Malformations Secondary to Abnormal Postmigrational Development

concepts.label: Hemimegalencephaly
concepts.title: Hemimegalencephaly
concepts.definition: Rare MALFORMATIONS OF CORTICAL DEVELOPMENT, GROUP I characterized by the enlargement of one side of the brain. It is associated with seizures, partial paralysis, and mental retardation.

concepts.label: Polymicrogyria
concepts.title: Polymicrogyria
concepts.definition: Heterogeneous disorders of cortical malformation characterized by excessive and small fused gyri and shallow sulci of the CORTEX with abnormal cortical lamination. It is considered a malformation secondary to abnormal post-migrational development of the neurons during cerebral cortical development and is associated with EPILEPSY and learning difficulties.

concepts.label: Schizencephaly
concepts.title: Schizencephaly
concepts.definition: Cortical malformations characterized by grey matter-lined cleft or cyst that extends from the EPENDYMA often to the PIA MATER outer surface. The grey matter that lines the cleft is often POLYMICROGYRIA. It is associated with developmental delay, motor disturbance and seizures.

concepts.label: Porencephaly
concepts.title: Porencephaly
concepts.definition: Cortical malformations characterized by white matter-lined cleft or cyst associated with ISCHEMIA and hemorrhagic insults. Symptoms include delayed growth and development, HYPOTONIA; SEIZURES; SPASTIC HEMIPLEGIA and MACROCEPHALY; MICROCEPHALY; or HYDROCEPHALUS. Mutations in the genes encoding COLLAGEN TYPE IV are associated with familial types.

concepts.label: Broca Area
concepts.title: Broca Area
concepts.definition: Functional neuroanatomical region of the inferior frontal gyrus consisting of pars opercularis and pars triangularis. It is important in SPEECH and LANGUAGE production. Injuries to Broca area are associated with BROCA APHASIA and APRAXIA.

concepts.label: Limbic Lobe
concepts.title: Limbic Lobe
concepts.definition: The medial surface of the cerebral hemisphere around the brain stem.

concepts.label: Lennox Gastaut Syndrome
concepts.title: Lennox Gastaut Syndrome
concepts.definition: A childhood-onset epilepsy syndrome.

concepts.label: Delay Discounting
concepts.title: Delay Discounting
concepts.definition: The tendency to devalue an outcome as a function of its temporal delay or probability of achievement. It can be evaluated in a psychological paradigm that involves the choice between receiving a smaller immediate reward or a larger delayed reward, and may be used to provide a measure of impulsive behavior.

concepts.label: Xenophobia
concepts.title: Xenophobia
concepts.definition: Intense or irrational dislike or fear of anything that is strange or foreign, particularly of people who are strangers or foreigners. It is an attitudinal orientation of hostility against non-natives in a given population that includes attitudes, prejudices and behavior that reject, exclude or vilify persons, based on the perception that they are outsiders or foreigners to the community, society or national identity.

concepts.label: Prepulse Inhibition
concepts.title: Prepulse Inhibition
